Title: What Are the Most Useful Browser Extensions for Odoo Developers?
Content:
Useful Browser Extensions For Odoo Developers

Are you using Odoo for your business operations but missing something? Or perhaps you're wondering how to make the most of Odoo’s powerful features? The answer could lie in exploring useful extensions for Odoo.

These extensions are designed to enhance Odoo's existing functionality, allowing you to customize the system to suit your unique business needs. Whether you’re looking to enhance accounting processes, automate workflows, or improve customer relations, there's likely an extension that can take your Odoo experience to the next level.

But which extensions should you prioritize?

This post will explore some of the most useful Odoo extensions and how they can enhance your business operations.

1. Odoo Debug - Amy Greenfelder

This extension is a Breakthrough if you toggle between normal and debug modes in Odoo instead of manually clicking through the settings With Amy Greenfelder's Odoo Debug plugin, you can quickly switch between debug mode and normal mode in Odoo using keyboard shortcuts and mouse clicks. The debug mode can be accessed by clicking on the extension with your mouse. The debug with assets mode will be activated by double-clicking.  

What It Does:

Instantly Switch Modes: Flip between debug and normal modes without breaking your workflow.

Keyboard Shortcuts:

  • Ctrl + . for debug mode.
  • Ctrl +. + . (Hold Ctrl and press. twice) for debugging with assets mode.

Customizable: If you have a preferred shortcut, you can change it to suit your needs.

You can modify your keyboard shortcut from Settings > Extension > Keyboard shortcuts (located at the bottom).

This extension will save you much time if you're digging through Odoo's settings or troubleshooting.

2. Owl devtools – Odoo

If you're a developer working with Odoo’s modern Owl framework, you’ve probably encountered some debugging difficulties. This extension is a huge help.

What It Does:

  • Component Breakdown: View detailed info about the components on the page.
  • Easy Detection: You’ll know if Owl is loaded in the current tab. If the extension icon is flipped upside down, Owl isn’t active.
  • Super Helpful for Debugging: Perfect for developers looking to see deeper into the technical side of Odoo.

If you're working with the Owl framework, this extension is worth checking out.

  • Developers can use this extension to debug applications that use the Owl JS framework by providing visual information about the structure of the components, their contents, and their lifecycle.
  • When we click on the owl icon, an info popup will open, letting us know whether the owl is loaded in the current tab. We can also get this from the extension icon; if flipped upside-down, the owl is not loaded in the active tab.
  • Documentation: https://github.com/odoo/owl/blob/master/doc/tools/devtools_guide.md

3. OdooTerminal – Tardo

Sometimes, a command-line interface is the best way to get things done. The OdooTerminal extension adds a terminal directly to your browser, letting you run commands like viewing records, searching, creating, or even deleting stuff without leaving the page.

What it holds:

Command-Line Interface: Type in commands directly to interact with your Odoo data.

Helpful List of Commands: Type help to see a list of all available commands.

Fast Operations: Perform tasks quickly without going through menus.

  • This extension offers an Odoo terminal where we can type commands for various functions, such as viewing, searching, creating and deleting records, reloading, etc.
  • We can view all commands about various operations by opening this terminal and typing the "help" command.

If you like using the terminal efficiently, this extension brings all those capabilities into your browser.

4. Odoo Database Manager – Michell Stuttgart 

Managing multiple databases in Odoo can get confusing, especially when you need to switch between them quickly. The Odoo Database Manager extension makes accessing the Database Selector and Manager pages easy with a click or keyboard shortcut.

  • This extension provides easy access to the Database Selector and Manager Odoo webpages. It can be navigated using both mouse and keyboard.

Mouse Control:

  • Single-click redirects to the database selector.
  • Double-click redirects to the database manager page.

Keyboard Shortcuts:

  • For the database selector page, Press Ctrl + M.
  • Press Ctrl + M + M for the database manager page.

If you work with multiple Odoo instances or databases, this extension simplifies jumping between them.

5. Odoo Utility – Droggol 

If you frequently need to access Odoo's forum, documentation, or App Store, the Odoo Utility extension is a huge time-saver. It gives you quick shortcuts to these essential pages, plus some cool customization options to make it look even easier.

  •  This extension offers convenient shortcuts to Odoo Forum, Documentation, Runbot, App Store, and more, saving us valuable time.
  • In this extension wizard, By clicking on the settings icon, we can configure various options like navigation buttons for swift navigation and toggle between light/dark themes.

It Also Had:

Quick Links: Direct access to Odoo’s forum, docs, Runbot, App Store, and more.

Customizable: You can tweak the extension settings to add buttons for faster navigation or toggle between light and dark themes.

Saves Time: Instead of hunting for these pages, they’re right at your fingertips.

That is a great extension for anyone frequently jumping between Odoo resources.

More than just Convenient:

There you have it! These browser extensions are more than just convenient; they help you save time and increase productivity while using Odoo. Whether you’re debugging code, managing databases, or simply going through Odoo faster, these tools make your experience smoother and more efficient.

Title: How to Dynamically Execute Python Code When a Form Loads in Odoo 18
Content:
Python has become one of the most popular programming languages due to its simplicity, versatility, and ease of integration into various platforms. In Odoo, Python is central to customizing the platform and automating tasks, making it more efficient for businesses to personalize their systems to meet specific needs.

But what happens when you need a form in Odoo to load dynamically based on the user, their role, or any specific condition? This is where the get_views() method in Odoo 18 comes into play.

In this post, we’ll explore how to execute Python code when a form is loaded, making the Odoo experience more dynamic and personalized.

Executing Python Code When a Form Loads in Odoo 18

In earlier versions of Odoo, developers commonly used the fields_view_get() method to execute Python logic whenever a form was loaded. This method dynamically customised views by altering their structure or injecting specific logic. However, starting from Odoo 16, this method was deprecated, and the get_views() method was introduced to achieve the same functionality with enhanced flexibility.

With get_views(), developers can now handle multiple view types, form, tree, and kanban, at once and apply more conditional logic efficiently.

Why Switch to get_views() Method?

Odoo’s evolution from fields_view_get() to get_views() was driven by the need to provide a more robust and modular approach to view management. The get_views() method allows developers to:

  1. Multiple Views at Once: With a single override, you can modify a form, tree, kanban, or any view simultaneously.
  2. Conditional Logic: This allows for more robust customization, customizing views depending on user roles, departments, or custom fields.
  3. Better Performance: get_views() improves Performance, especially when working with large datasets, by reducing unnecessary calls and enhancing flexibility.

Using get_views() is essential for ensuring that your customizations are not only forward-compatible with Odoo’s updates but also cleaner and more efficient.

Overview of get_views()

The get_views() method is a powerful feature introduced in Odoo 16 and further refined in Odoo 18. It is designed to help developers dynamically customize views based on specific conditions, whether it's a form, tree, kanban, or any other view type. 

The get_views() method is invoked when a model’s views are loaded. You can override this method in your model to inject custom Python logic and dynamically modify the view based on certain conditions.

By overriding get_views(), you can tap into Odoo’s best architecture and create a more intuitive and context-sensitive user experience.

				
					Method Signature:
def get_views(self, views, options=None):
    # Custom logic
    return super().get_views(views, options)

Implementing Get_views() in Odoo 18

Now that we understand the basics of the get_views() method. Let’s walk through an example where we customize a form view dynamically based on the user’s branch.

Use Case: Show/Hide Fields Based on User’s Branch

In many businesses, different branches or departments may require distinct sets of information. For instance, a field may need to be visible to users from one branch but hidden from others. In this example, we'll show or hide a specific field on the form depending on the branch the logged-in user is associated with.

This is a perfect use case for get_views(), as it allows us to conditionally adjust the form's layout as it’s being loaded without requiring users to refresh the page or interact with complex UI elements.

				
					from odoo import models, fields, api
class CustomModel(models.Model):
    _name = 'custom.model'
    _description = 'Custom Model Example'
    name = fields.Char(string="Name")
    branch_specific_field = fields.Char(string="Branch Specific Field")
    @api.model
    def get_views(self, views, options=None):
        res = super(CustomModel, self).get_views(views, options)
        # Get the current user's branch
        user_branch = self.env.user.branch_id
        # Check if the current view is a form view
        if views.get('form'):
            arch = res['views']['form']['arch']
            # Modify the form view dynamically based on the branch
            if user_branch.code == 'BRANCH_01':
                # Add or modify the XML to include a specific field
                arch = arch.replace('<field name="name"/>',
                                    '<field name="name"/><field name="branch_specific_field"/>')
            res['views']['form']['arch'] = arch
        return res

How the code works : 

    1. Override get_views(): We override the method in our model to inject custom logic when the views are loaded.
    2. Access the User’s Branch: Using self.env.user.branch_id, we fetch the current user’s branch.
    3. Modify the Form View: We dynamically update the form view to include or exclude specific fields based on the branch.

    The arch variable represents the XML structure of the form view. It defines the layout and fields displayed to the user, which we modify dynamically based on the user's branch.

    Advantages of get_views()

      1. Dynamic View Customization: Custom views dynamically based on user roles, conditions, or preferences.
      2. Improved Performance: Fetch and modify multiple views in a single call.
      3. Future-Proof: Aligns with Odoo’s modern architecture, ensuring compatibility with newer versions.
      4. Modularity and maintainability enable easier management and updating of customizations in large-scale Odoo projects.

      Best Practices for Using get_views()

        1. Avoid Overloading the Method: Only apply the logic necessary for view customization. Complex logic can slow down the view rendering.
        2. Test Thoroughly: Since get_views() is invoked every time a view is loaded, ensure your modifications don’t introduce errors or conflicts.
        3. Use Modular Logic: Keep your modifications modular and reusable.

        We can conclude like:

        The get_views() method in Odoo 18 offers a powerful way to execute Python code when forms (or other views) are loaded. While it replaces the deprecated fields_view_get() method, it provides enhanced functionality, enabling developers to handle multiple views simultaneously.

        By Utilizing get_views(), you can create dynamic and user-specific experiences in your Odoo applications. Whether you need to conditionally display fields, add new elements, or transform views, this method equips you with the tools to achieve it effectively.

        With Odoo’s continuous evolution, adopting modern practices like get_views() ensures that your customizations remain compatible with future versions.
        Happy coding!

Title: How To Load JS Function In Menu Item Click In Odoo 18
Content:
Odoo integrates both Python and JavaScript to offer complete functionality. Python is responsible for backend logic, while JavaScript enhances the user interface and client-side interactions. In this blog, we'll explore how to load a JavaScript function upon clicking a menu item in Odoo 18.

To begin, 

Create the Menu Item (menu.xml): Define a menu item in an XML file that triggers the JavaScript function when clicked.

				
					menu.xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
<odoo>
<menuitem id="menu_load_js" action="load_js_code" name="Load JS"/>
</odoo>

Define the Action (actions.xml):
Create a client action in an XML file corresponding to the menu item. This Action will specify the tag that links to the JavaScript function.

				
					actions.xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
<odoo>
<record id="load_js_code" model="ir.actions.client">
<field name="name">Load JS Code</field>
<field name="tag">js_code</field>
</record>
</odoo>

Implement the JavaScript Function (script.js): Write the JavaScript code executed when the Action is triggered. This script imports necessary modules, registers the Action, and defines the execution function.

				
					script.js
/** @odoo-module **/
import { registry } from "@web/core/registry";
const actionRegistry = registry.category("actions");
const loadJsAction = async (env,context) => {
// Custom JS Code Here
console.log('JS File Loaded === Custom Script Will Execute Here',env,context);
window.alert('Sidmec Technologies Pvt Ltd');
};
actionRegistry.add("js_code", loadJsAction);

Configure the Manifest File (__manifest__.py): Update the manifest file to include the JavaScript file in the backend assets and reference the XML files.

				
					__manifest__.py
'assets': {
'web.assets_backend': [
'module_name/static/src/js/script.js',
],

Title: What Are the Most Common Errors in Odoo & How to Fix It?
Content:
Odoo is a strong open-source ERP platform that helps businesses streamline their operations. However, like any complex system, it's prone to occasional errors. Whether installing modules, configuring settings, or running day-to-day operations, error messages can pop up anytime, causing frustration and delays.

This guide covers some of the most common errors in Odoo, their causes, and actionable solutions to help you quickly get your system back on track. Whether you're a beginner or an experienced Odoo developer, these troubleshooting tips will save you time and effort.

In development, errors and exceptions are inevitable and need proper handling to work the code efficiently. In Odoo, errors and exceptions occur while installing, configuring, developing, or doing day-to-day operations.

This blog explores some of the most common Odoo errors and provides practical solutions to address them effectively.

Let’s check the type of errors, their causes, and solutions.

1. Database Connection Error

Symptom

You encounter the following error message:

psycopg2.OperationalError: 

could not connect to server: 

Connection refused

Cause

This error occurs when Odoo cannot connect to the PostgreSQL database. It often happens because of incorrect database credentials or if PostgreSQL is not running on the server.

Solution

    • Ensure PostgreSQL is installed and running:

sudo systemctl start postgresql

    • Verify the database configuration in the odoo.conf file. Confirm the correct db_host, db_user, and db_password are specified.

2. Missing Dependency Errors

Symptom

You see errors related to missing Python packages, such as:

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'some_package'

Cause

Odoo relies on specific Python libraries to function. This error indicates that one or more of these required packages are missing from your system.

Solution

    • Identify the missing package from the error message.
    • Install the required package using pip:

pip install some_package

    • For a complete dependency installation, run:

pip install -r requirements.txt

3. QWeb Template Errors

Symptom

You encounter an error message like:

QWebException: 'template_id' is not defined

Cause

That occurs when Odoo cannot find the specified QWeb template in your XML view, either because the template is missing or incorrectly defined.

Solution

    • Verify the template ID exists in the XML files.
    • Check the file paths and ensure all related files are loaded in the __manifest__.py file.
    • Restart the Odoo server and update the module:

./odoo-bin -u your_module_name

4. Module Installation Errors

Symptom

Module installation can fails with errors like:

ValidationError: Field(s)

Cause

This error typically occurs due to missing fields, mismatched dependencies, or incorrect configurations in the __manifest__.py file.

Solution

    • Verify that all dependencies in __manifest__.py are installed.
    • Confirm all fields and models exist before adding them to views.
    • Restart Odoo and attempt reinstallation.

5. Odoo Server Not Starting

Symptom

When attempting to start the Odoo server, you see:

Error: Address already in use

Cause

Another process is using the default port (8069), preventing Odoo from binding.

Solution

    • Identify and terminate the conflicting process:

sudo netstat -tuln | grep 8069

sudo kill -9 <process_id>

    • Change the port in the odoo.conf file:

xmlrpc_port = 8070

6. Website or Portal Errors

Symptom

Users see a blank page or encounter routing issues on the website.

Cause

That could be due to a misconfigured controller or routing conflicts in your module.

Solution

Verify that the controllers are correctly defined in your module’s controllers.py file.

Ensure the route paths are unique and match the expected URLs.

Clear the cache to force Odoo to reload website data:

./odoo-bin -u website

7. Import Errors

Symptom

An error occurs while importing data, such as:

ValueError: Wrong value for field 'field_name': some_value

Cause

This error happens when the imported data doesn’t match the field's expected format or value constraints.

Solution

    • Verify the data file for errors. Ensure the column names match Odoo’s field names.
    • Validate the data using a smaller sample to identify problematic rows.
    • Use the Import Preview feature in Odoo to test mappings.

8. Access Control Errors

Symptom

Users encounter the following error:

AccessError: You are not allowed to access this document. Please contact your administrator.

Cause

This error occurs when users lack access rights or record rules to view the document.

Solution

    • Go to Settings > Users & Companies > Users and ensure the user has the correct permissions.
    • Review and update access control lists (ACLs) in the module’s security folder.
    • Test changes by refreshing user access rights:

./odoo-bin -u your_module_name

9. View Inheritance Issues

Symptom

The Odoo interface fails to load, showing an error like:

Element '<xpath>' cannot be located in parent view

Cause

This error happens when an XPath expression in the XML file cannot find the element it intends to modify in the parent view.

Solution

    • Verify the XPath syntax and ensure it matches the structure of the parent view.
    • Check the view IDs referenced in the inherit_id field.
    • Restart the server and update the module to reflect changes.

10. Session Expired Errors

Symptom

Users are logged out frequently with a "Session Expired" message.

Cause

This may occur due to improper session settings or excessive server load.

Solution

Increase the session timeout in the odoo.conf file:
session_timeout = 3600

    • Optimize server resources to handle traffic better.

Final Thoughts

While Odoo’s flexibility makes it an excellent platform, errors are inevitable, especially in complex systems. Understanding the causes and solutions to these common errors will help you troubleshoot efficiently and keep your Odoo instance running smoothly.

Remember to update your environment, check for system optimizations regularly, and follow best practices for error handling. If you need help with a tricky Odoo issue that wasn’t covered here, leave a comment below, and let’s solve it together!

Also, Share this guide with your team!

When developing modules in Odoo, hooks are essential tools that allow developers to perform custom operations at specific points in a module's lifecycle. Understanding Hooks in Odoo 18

Hooks in Odoo 18 act as entry points that allow custom code to execute during various stages of a module's lifecycle. They enable developers to:

Title: How to Manage Split Delivery Orders in Odoo 18 Sales?
Content:
Why You Need to Manage Split Delivery Orders in Odoo 18 Sales

Have you ever faced a situation where your customer placed a big order, but only some of the items were in stock? You probably wanted to send whatever was available right away and deliver the rest later. That's where the ability to manage split delivery orders in Odoo 18 Sales becomes very helpful. In today's fast-moving business world, customers expect fast service, even if their order isn't fully ready.

Odoo 18 makes this process very smooth. With its innovative features, you can easily handle Odoo 18 split delivery orders, manage backorders, and make sure your customers stay happy. Whether you're selling products online or handling logistics for a warehouse, understanding how to use the Odoo sales module's delivery splitting feature can significantly simplify your workflow.

In this blog, you'll learn everything from how to enable split delivery, how Odoo partial shipment management works, to how to track and process backorders. We'll also explore how Odoo 18 logistics features and Odoo delivery order management help you stay in control of every shipment. And we'll keep it all simple, no complex words, just the way you talk to your teammates or clients every day.

Let's dig in and see how easy it is to manage split delivery orders in Odoo 18 Sales.

Odoo 18 Split Delivery Orders – What Does It Mean?

When a customer places an order, you usually try to ship everything in one go. But sometimes, some products are out of stock. That's where Odoo 18 split delivery orders come into play. It means breaking the delivery into parts, shipping the available products first and sending the rest later.

This benefits you in two ways: you avoid keeping your customer waiting, and you prevent your warehouse from being blocked by pending orders. It's a win-win.

For example, imagine a customer ordered 10 phones and five chargers, but you only have six phones in stock. Instead of delaying the whole order, you send the six phones right away. Later, when the other four phones and the chargers arrive, you send them in the second delivery. This whole thing is handled smoothly with Odoo sales order split delivery.

Odoo 18 does all this without making things confusing. You don't need extra software or add-ons; use the options already inside the system.

How Odoo Sales Module Delivery Splitting Works in Real Life

To use the Odoo sales module delivery splitting, you just need to follow some simple steps. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you.

Go to your Sales module.

Click on New.

Select the Customer, I’ll choose Alexa Laza.

Click on Add a Product and choose the product. My Customer, Alexa Laza, wants the product Black Embroidered t-shirt.

After selecting the size & quantity, click on Confirm.

Then, I’ll set the quantity to 6 and click on the Confirm button.

Now, click on the Delivery smart button to deliver the product.

Here, you can find the demand & quantity of the product. We need to split the order, which means changing the product amount. So, now I'll set the quantity to 3. Go to the Settings icon and click on the Split option.

As shown in the screenshot above, before selecting the Split option, we had 6 units in Demand and 3 units in Quantity. However, after clicking on the Split option, both Demand and Quantity display as 3 units. Now, click on Validate. 

We just successfully split the order and then went back to the quotation.

Click on the Delivery button.

Here, you can find other deliveries that have been created. If you want to proceed with the delivery using the remaining quantity, you can do so by clicking Validate. So, let’s choose the other one.

Click on the Validate.

Then go back by clicking on the Transfers.

As shown in the screenshot below, we successfully split and delivered the item to the customer & Odoo marked it as Done.

So, that’s how you can smoothly manage split delivery orders in the Odoo 18 sales module.

Odoo Partial Shipment Management – Keep Your Orders Moving

One of the best things about Odoo is how it handles partial shipments. When you're working with a big order, and only part of it is ready, Odoo gives you the option to ship now and create a backorder.

Once you validate the delivery of the available items, Odoo asks, "Do you want to create a backorder for the remaining products?" If you click "Yes," the system will schedule another delivery for the rest. This is called Odoo 18 backorder processing, and it's built right into the flow.

You don't have to worry about missed deliveries, lost orders, or confusing paperwork. Everything is tracked neatly. The system even updates the sales order with both delivery statuses. So, you know exactly what went out, what's left, and when it's going to be delivered.

Odoo 18 Backorder Processing – Never Miss a Delivery

Backorders might sound scary, but in Odoo 18, they are super easy to manage. When you choose to create a backorder, Odoo saves the remaining items in a new delivery order and sets it up for you.

You can view both deliveries in the system. One will show as "Done," and the other as "Waiting" or "Ready." You can even make changes to the second delivery, such as adding notes, changing the date, or updating product quantities.

This is a huge help for businesses that deal with large or complex orders. With Odoo 18 backorder processing, nothing slips through the cracks.

Let's say you're selling laptops and accessories. A customer places an order for:

  • 5 laptops
  • 10 laptop bags

You only have three laptops and six bags in stock. When you confirm the sales order, Odoo will:

  • Create a delivery order for three laptops and six bags
  • Automatically create a backorder for two laptops and four bags

You deliver the first batch now and the second batch later. This is precisely how Odoo sales order split delivery makes your life easier.

Your warehouse knows what to send, your customer is happy to get what's available, and your system tracks everything.

Odoo 18 Logistics Features – Smart Tools That Help You Every Day

  • Manual editing: You can manually adjust the delivery if needed.
  • Reports: Odoo provides comprehensive delivery reports that give you the whole picture.

All of these Odoo 18 logistics features work together to make your delivery order management smooth and stress-free.

You can go to your Delivery Orders dashboard and see:

  • Which orders are done?
  • Which ones are waiting?
  • Which ones are late?
  • Which ones are split?

You can click on each delivery and see full details. Odoo also links everything together: sales orders, invoices, deliveries, and stock movements. That way, you're never lost.

This is how Odoo delivery order management gives you peace of mind.

Why You Should Manage Split Delivery Orders in Odoo 18 Sales

Still wondering why you should care about managing split delivery orders in Odoo Sales? Here's why:

  • You deliver faster: No need to wait for the whole order to be ready.
  • You keep customers happy by sending available items early.
  • You reduce errors: No manual entries. Odoo handles it all.
  • You save time: Everything is automated from split to backorder.

You don't need special training or tools to follow the steps; you'll be managing Odoo 18 split delivery orders like a professional. With strong support from Odoo sales module delivery splitting, Odoo partial shipment management, and Odoo 18 backorder processing, you're always in control.

Title: How to Set Up the Bill Control Policy in Odoo 18 Purchase?
Content:
Managing vendor bills and purchase orders effectively is critical for any business, and Odoo 18 makes this process smooth with its robust Bill Control Policy in Odoo 18 Purchase. Whether you need to set up invoicing based on received goods or ordered quantities, understanding the configuration process can save time and reduce errors.

What if I told you there’s a hidden superpower in Odoo 18 that could change your vendor billing from a chaotic mess into a finely tuned symphony? Sounds like magic, right? Stick around because this guide is packed with all the juicy details you didn’t even know you needed. Spoiler alert: By the end, you’ll be ready to conquer Odoo 18 purchase configuration like a pro.

Why You Need the Bill Control Policy in Odoo 18 Purchase

Accurate and timely billing is crucial in the fast-paced world of business. Odoo 18 simplifies this process with its dynamic Bill Control Policy in Odoo 18 Purchase. This policy allows companies to dictate when vendor bills are generated based on the quantities ordered or received.

With the Odoo 18 bill control policy, organizations gain better control over their financial workflows, ensuring vendor bills align with actual procurement activities. It integrates flawlessly with the Odoo 18 purchase invoicing settings, making the billing process efficient, accurate, and automated.

The Odoo 18 purchase configuration enables businesses to choose between ordered vs. received billing, ensuring flexibility to meet different operational needs. By understanding the nuances of Odoo 18 vendor bill management, companies can reduce errors, save time, and improve supplier relationships.

What is the Bill Control Policy in Odoo 18?

The Bill Control Policy in Odoo 18 Purchase is a configurable setting that determines how and when vendor bills are created for purchases. It offers two primary options:

Based on Ordered Quantities

Vendor bills are generated based on the quantities specified in the purchase order, irrespective of whether the goods have been received.

Based on Received Quantities

Vendor bills are created only for the quantities of items that have been physically received.

This policy directly influences how companies handle Odoo 18 purchase order billing, ensuring invoicing aligns with operational realities.

Key Benefits of the Odoo 18 Bill Control Policy

Flexibility in Billing

The ability to choose between ordered vs. received billing allows businesses to adapt their billing practices to their procurement strategies.

Enhanced Vendor Bill Management

With updated Odoo 18 vendor bill management, businesses can efficiently track and process vendor invoices, minimizing disputes and delays.

Improved Financial Accuracy

The Odoo 18 purchase invoicing settings link billing to actual transactions, ensuring that your financial records reflect reality and reducing the risk of overpayments or underpayments.

All-in-one Integration

The Odoo 18 purchase configuration integrates with modules like Inventory and Accounting, creating a cohesive workflow from purchase order to payment.

Reduced Operational Errors

Clear and consistent billing policies help eliminate errors in Odoo 18 purchase order billing, fostering better supplier relationships.

Step-by-Step Guide to Setting Up the Bill Control Policy in Odoo 18 Purchase

Ensure the Purchase module is installed and active before setting up the Odoo 18 bill control policy.  

Go to the Purchase module from the main dashboard.

Click on Configuration in the menu and select Settings.

Locate the Bill Control Policy section under the Invoicing tab.

Select one of the following options:

  • Based on Ordered Quantities: Bills are generated once the purchase order is confirmed.
  • Based on Received Quantities: Bills are generated only after receiving goods.

Click Save to apply the changes.

Let me show you how this works. To do so, go to the Products Menu and click Products.

So, I am choosing two products: Bacon Burger & Bagel.

Based on Received Quantities

First, click on Bacon Burger and go to the Purchase Tab. Here, you have vendor bills, which are on received quantity. So, we know Bacon Burger is for the received quantity.

Next, open the second product, which is the Bagel. Then go to the Purchase Tab to choose On Ordered Quantities. So, we know the Bagel is for the ordered quantity.

We have given two products: Bacon Burger, which has the control policy received quantities, and Bagel, which has the control policy ordered quantities. Now, go to the Orders menu and select Requests for Quotation.

Click on New.

Select the Vendor and click on Add a Product.

First, I am going to check Bacon Burger, so select Bacon Burger as a product and click on Confirm.

Confirm the Order.

As you can see in the screenshot below, the Create Bill button is not active yet. You can only create the bill after receiving the product. Now, click on the Receive Products button.

Click on Validate.

Go back to the Purchase order.

Then you can create the bill by clicking on Create Bill.

Mention the bill date and click on Confirm.

Click on Pay.

Next, click on the Create Payment.

Now, you can see it’s in payment state. That’s how you can create an RFQ (Request for Quotation) for a product with a bill control policy on received quantities.

Based on Ordered Quantities

Now, let’s create another one for Received Quantities. Choose the vendor, add the product, and click on Confirm.

After confirming the order, you can see the Received Products button and Create Bill are active here. In the previous case, the bill creation was not active because you can create the bill only after receiving the products. So, bill creation is possible here; just click on Create Bill.

Add the bill date and click Confirm.

Click on Pay.

Then, Create Payment.

So, it's possible before receiving the product in ordered quantities control policy.

Payment is also made; if you click on return, you can ‘‘Receive the Product’’ and complete the procedure.

Click on Validate. Now, everything is done, so that’s how you deal with two control policies.

What Happened if We Add Two Products in the Same RFQ?

Are you wondering, "What happens if we add two products to the same RFQ?" Let’s create a new RFQ with two products and see what happens.

First, choose the Vendor and add two products, then click on Confirm Order.

Now, you can see that creating a bill is possible; just click ‘‘Create Bill’’.

As shown in the screenshot below, only Bagel is here because Bagel has the control policy, which is ordered quantity. Odoo gives the highest priority to the control policy on ordered quantities. That’s why we are able to create a bill for Bagel and not for Bacon Burger because Bacon Burger is in the control policy for received quantities. Now, click on Confirm after specifying the bill date.

Click on Pay.

And Create Payment.

That’s all about the Bagel because the Bagel has the ordered quantity as a control policy. Let’s go back by clicking on the above purchase order number.

And Receive the Products.

Validate the product.

That’s in the done stage, let’s go back.

So, as you can see in the screenshot below, the Create Bill option is active now; just click on "Create Bill."

Now, you can see it is a bill for Bacon Burger. Add the bill date and click on Confirm. So, once you receive the product, you are able to create a bill for it with the control policy received quantities.

Click on Pay.

Then, Create Payment.

So, if you check the priority of the control policies, ordered quantities have the highest priority, followed by received quantities, because only after receiving the product can you create the bill.

Basically, that’s how you can deal with the Bill Control Policy. By effectively utilizing the bill control policy in Odoo 18, you can strengthen your financial management and protect your organization’s assets.

Real-Life Applications of Odoo 18 Bill Control Policy

Scenario 1: Based on Ordered Quantities

A wholesale distributor orders bulk goods and needs to pay vendors upon order confirmation. Setting the Odoo 18 bill control policy to "Based on Ordered Quantities" generates the vendor bill immediately, facilitating timely payments.

Title: What are the Differences Between Odoo Community vs Odoo Enterprise?
Content:
Understanding Odoo Community vs Odoo Enterprise

If you're exploring Odoo for your business, you’re probably aware of the two primary versions available: Odoo COMMUNITY and Odoo ENTERPRISE. Both are powerful ERP solutions, but understanding their key differences is essential to making the right choice for your business.

Let's clarify from the start: Odoo Community vs Odoo Enterprise is not just a technical comparison. It’s a decision that will affect how your business runs, the tools you’ll have at your disposal, the level of support you’ll get, and, of course, the cost.

So, why should you care about these differences? Imagine having a system that can update your processes, manage your inventory, and even help you with accounting. That sounds great, right? But, should you opt for the free, open-source Odoo Community or go all-in with the feature-rich Odoo Enterprise?

In this post, we will get deep into the Odoo Community features and Odoo Enterprise features, uncover Odoo Community's limitations, and explore Odoo Enterprise's benefits. That will help you determine which option suits your business needs better.

Odoo Community Features: What’s Available for Free?

Let’s start with the basics: Odoo Community is the open-source version of Odoo. And yes, it’s free. But, before you get too excited, remember that free doesn’t always mean everything you need is included.

1. Core Modules: The Essentials

With Odoo Community, you’ll have access to the core modules that many businesses need, like:

  1. Inventory Management
  2. Sales
  3. Accounting
  4. And Basic Purchasing.

These modules provide all the essential functionality you need to run a small business smoothly.

So, if you’re running a small business or a startup, this might be a good starting point. The modules are user-friendly and give you just enough to get by without overwhelming you with extra features.

2. Open-Source Freedom

Odoo Community is open-source, so you can access and modify the code. That could be a massive plus if you’re tech-savvy (or have an excellent developer team). You can customize the system to meet your business needs - without paying a dime for licensing.

3. Limited Integrations

You’ll notice its limited integration options when using Odoo Community. Sure, it plays nice with a few essential third-party apps, but it’s not as extensive as Odoo Enterprise regarding integrations with advanced tools. That might be a dealbreaker for some businesses, especially if you rely on multiple software systems.

4. No Mobile App Support

Odoo Community doesn’t include access to dedicated mobile apps. That might seem small, but this could be a significant limitation if you have employees who need to access Odoo on the go. The mobile aspect is something that Odoo Enterprise handles beautifully, making it a must-have for businesses with a lot of remote or travelling staff.

5. Odoo Community Limitations

While the Odoo Community is powerful, it does have its limitations:

  1. Lack of Advanced Features:

    Critical features like automated workflows, detailed reporting, and advanced integrations are absent.

  2. Limited Support:

    No official support leaves you reliant on the community and forums.

  3. No Studio Tool:

    The ability to customize applications using the Odoo Studio tool is only available in Odoo Enterprise.

  4. Restricted Scalability:

    Suitable for small-scale operations but lacks tools for scaling as businesses grow.

Who Should Choose Odoo Community Support?

Odoo Community is ideal for:

  1. Startups with tight budgets.
  2. Small businesses with basic operational needs.
  3. Companies with in-house IT teams for support and customization.

Odoo Enterprise Features: The Full Package

Now, let's turn the spotlight to Odoo Enterprise - the paid version of the system. Odoo Enterprise is where all the bells and whistles are; if you need something more robust, this is the version you’ll want.

1. Extensive Modules for Every Need

Unlike the Community version, Odoo Enterprise has an extensive library of modules.

You’ve got everything like:

  1. Project Management
  2. Human Resources
  3. Marketing
  4. eCommerce, and more.

If your business needs specific functionality, Odoo Enterprise has you covered with dedicated modules designed to grow with your company.

The beauty of this is that you only pay for the modules you need. You can scale up or down based on your changing business needs without worrying about being stuck with unnecessary features.

2. Dedicated Mobile App for On-the-Go Access

One of the innovations of Odoo Enterprise is the mobile app. Imagine managing your sales, inventory, or even customer relationships while on the go. It’s a huge advantage for businesses that require flexibility and mobility. With the mobile app, your team can access Odoo’s functionality anytime, anywhere, allowing them to be productive no matter where they are.

3. Regular Software Updates and Bug Fixesa

Keeping your system up to date is essential for maintaining security and functionality. With Odoo Enterprise, you’ll receive regular software updates, ensuring that your ERP system is always running on the latest version, with bug fixes and security patches. Title: How to Set Asset Model & Automation in Odoo 18 Accounting?
Content:
Managing your company's assets, from machines and vehicles to office equipment, is no small feat. If you're using spreadsheets or outdated systems, you probably know how time-consuming and prone to errors this process can be. That's where Odoo 18 asset management comes into play.

Trust me, this will make your life a whole lot easier!

What Exactly Are Asset Models in Odoo 18 Accounting?

Think of Asset Models as Your Assets' Blueprint

An asset model is a template for your assets. It tells Odoo how to handle different assets in your system, whether an office computer, a fleet vehicle, or heavy machinery. This model outlines essential information such as:

  • How to calculate depreciation (straight-line, declining balance, or custom rules)
  • Which accounts should be impacted when you buy, depreciate, or sell the asset
  • How to categorize your assets for better reporting and tracking

In short, asset models in Odoo 18 fixed asset management act like a blueprint for everything your asset will go through in its lifecycle.

How to Perform Odoo 18 Accounting Setup

Setting up an asset model is simpler than you think. Follow these steps to get started:

Go to the Accounting Module: Open your Odoo 18 dashboard and head straight to the Accounting module.

Find the Configuration Menu: Under the “Configuration” section, click on Asset Models.

Create a New Asset Model: Click the “New” button to define a new asset model.

Enter the following details:

  • Asset Category: Define whether this asset is machinery, office equipment, etc.
  • Depreciation Method: Choose how depreciation will be calculated (e.g., straight-line, declining balance).
  • Depreciation Frequency: Set whether depreciation happens monthly, yearly, etc.
  • Accounting Entries: Choose which accounts should be used for acquisition, depreciation, and disposal.
  • Save and Use It: Once you’re done, save your model. When you acquire an asset in this category, Odoo will automatically use the model’s rules.

Odoo 18 Accounting Automation

No More Manual Tracking!

Automation is the real magic behind Odoo 18 accounting automation. Instead of manually tracking each asset's depreciation, creating journal entries, or even worrying about tax implications, Odoo automatically does it all for you.

Let's break down what's possible when you set up automation for your assets in Odoo 18:

  • Automated Depreciation:

    Odoo calculates depreciation based on the rules you've set in the asset model. Whether you need straight-line depreciation or a custom method, Odoo covers you.

  • Automatic Journal Entries:

    When you acquire or dispose of assets, Odoo posts the appropriate journal entries without you having to lift a finger.

  • Tax Compliance:

    Odoo ensures that all asset-related transactions comply with tax regulations, reducing the risk of errors in your financial reports.

By automating these processes, you'll save time and ensure that everything stays accurate and compliant.

How to Set Up Asset Automation in Odoo 18

Here’s how to configure asset automation in Odoo 18 to update your accounting tasks:

1. Enable Asset Automation Features:

In the Accounting module, go to Configuration and ensure the asset automation options are turned on. That includes automation for depreciation, journal entries, and asset reports.

2. Link Your Asset Models to Automation Rules:

Each time you create an asset model, ensure it’s linked to its corresponding automation rules. For example, if you have different types of assets (office equipment vs. vehicles), set up distinct rules for depreciation frequency or journal entries.

3. Use Tags for Better Organization:

Tags help group assets based on characteristics like department or type (e.g., IT assets, office assets). That makes automation even smoother by letting you apply different depreciation or accounting rules depending on the asset category.

4. Schedule Actions for Depreciation:

Odoo 18 allows you to schedule recurring actions. Set up scheduled depreciation calculations so that Odoo automatically handles them without you having to input entries each month manually.

Why You'll Love Odoo 18 Asset Automation

No more waiting until the end of the quarter to manually calculate depreciation. Odoo does this in real-time, updating your financial reports and balance sheets as assets depreciate.

Tax season doesn't need to be stressful. With Odoo 18 asset models and automation, tax reporting for your assets is as easy as clicking a button. Odoo ensures that everything is accounted for in your financial statements, reducing the risk of errors when filing your taxes.

Best Practices for Using Odoo 18 Fixed Asset Management

Title: What Are the Work Center Parameters in Odoo 18 Manufacturing?

Understanding the Core Function of Odoo Manufacturing Work Centers

Some of the key Odoo work center parameters you’ll configure include things like:

  • Capacity:

    This defines how much work each work center can handle simultaneously, which is crucial for balancing production flow.

  • Work Center Efficiency

  • Machine Hours:

    How long does it take for a machine to complete a specific task? That can impact scheduling and throughput.

These parameters are customizable, and you must adjust them based on your operations to get the best results.

A work center is considered fully productive when it can:

  •       Receive work orders
  •       Have the components necessary to process work orders
  •       Operate within the expected duration of the work order it is processing

  • Time Efficiency: Determines how quickly tasks are completed.

Cost Per Hour: Helps calculate production costs.

Next, configure the work center efficiency. This will let you track how much the work center produces compared to what you expect. You can use this data by Odoo Implementation to improve if a work center is not performing up to standard.

Step 4: Add Machine Hours and Operational Hours

Lastly, you’ll want to input machine hours, which are how long it takes to complete a specific task. 

That is crucial for planning your production schedule. Also, define the operational hours for each work center so that you know when each part of your factory is up and running.

What Are Units of Measure in Odoo 18?

Before we discuss the specifics of configuring and managing units, let's examine the units of measure in Odoo 18.

In Managing Product Sales in Different Units in Odoo 18, a unit of measure quantifies your products for sales and inventory. For example, if you sell fabric, you might buy it in rolls but sell it by the meter. Alternatively, you could sell in bulk (like purchasing a box of items) but sell them individually. Odoo 18 allows you to track products in these different units easily.

Types of Units of Measure in Odoo 18

There are typically two types of units you'll be dealing with:

  • Purchase Unit of Measure:

    This is where you purchase or stock your products. Depending on how you buy the item, it could be anything from a kilogram (kg) to a box of 12 units.

  • Sales Unit of Measure:

    This is how you sell your product to customers. For example, you may buy products by weight (e.g., kilograms) but sell them in pieces or boxes.

The beauty of Managing Product Sales in Different Units in Odoo 18 is that it allows you to set these units separately for each product. This units-of-measure setup ensures that inventory is tracked accurately and conversions between units happen automatically when you make sales or purchases. That prevents mistakes like accidentally selling 10 kilograms instead of 10 boxes.

How to Set Up Units of Measure in Odoo 18

In Odoo 18, the Units of Measure (UoM) system is critical, especially for businesses that handle products sold and purchased in different quantities or units. Let's break it down Product Sales in Different Units in Odoo 18 step-by-step so you can set it up without any confusion:

Step 1: Access the Inventory Module

To begin, you must go to the Inventory module within Odoo 18.

From the main dashboard, Go to Configuration and select Units of Measure.

That will open up the page where you can create and manage your units.

Step 2: Create New Units

In the Units of Measure section, you can either edit the existing units or add new ones.

To add a new unit, click on New.

And then:

  • Name the Unit: This could be "Box," "Kilogram," "Piece," "Liter," or any unit that makes sense for your product.
  • Category: Choose the category that best fits the unit. For example, if it's a measurement, you'd select "Weight." If it's volume, you'd choose "Volume."
  • Reference Unit: This is the base unit to which all other units will convert. For instance, if your reference unit is Kilograms, all different units, such as grams, pounds, etc., will be based on this standard.

Once you've filled in the details, click Save. You can now use this unit across your products.

Step 3: Assign Units of Measure to Products

Now that you've set up your Product Sales in Different Units in Odoo 18, it's time to assign them to products:

  1. Go to the Products section in the Inventory module.

2. Select a product you want to edit.

3. Under the Inventory tab, look for the Unit of Measure field.

4. For the purchase, select the unit you use to receive the product (e.g., box, kilogram, etc.).

5. For the Sales, choose the unit where you sell the product (e.g., pieces, boxes).

That's it! Odooautomatically manages the conversion between these units whenever you purchase or sell.

3. Select your customer and add products to the order.

    4. Odoo will automatically show the Sales Unit you've set up for each product.

For example, if you buy product A in boxes but sell it individually, you'll see "Pieces" as the sales unit while your inventory is tracked in "Boxes."

Step 2: Automating Conversions

The great thing about Odoo is that it automatically handles conversions between your purchase and sales units. So, if you purchased Product A in boxes but the customer orders it in pieces, Odoo will calculate the number of pieces in one box and adjust the order accordingly.

You don't need to figure out conversions manually. Odoo does it for you!

Step 3: Invoicing and Delivery

Step 4: Real-Time Inventory Updates

When a sale is completed, Odoo automatically updates your inventory levels. The stock of Product A decreases based on the sales units, and Odoo keeps everything in sync.

Improved Efficiency

Title: How to Identify the Margin From Sales Orders Using Odoo 18?
Content:
Understanding Margin from sales orders Analysis

Understanding your profit margins is paramount for sustainable growth in today's competitive business landscape. Margin from sales orders analysis allows businesses to track and optimise their sales profitability effectively. This powerful ERP solution will enable users to calculate margins accurately, ensuring that every sales order contributes positively to the bottom line. This article will explore how to calculate margins in Odoo 18, delve into Odoo 18 sales order profitability tracking, and provide insights on margin tracking in Odoo 18 sales orders.

Why Margin Tracking is Essential

Understanding Profitability

Profitability is a crucial indicator of business health. Tracking margins helps businesses understand which products or services are generating profit and which are not. Odoo 18 ERP profit margin calculation features enable companies to analyze sales orders effectively, ensuring decision-makers have the information they need to make informed choices.

Enhancing Decision-Making

With accurate margin data, businesses can make strategic decisions regarding pricing, product offerings, and sales strategies. This analysis can lead to improved profitability and optimized resource allocation.

How to Calculate Margins in Odoo 18

Step-by-Step Process

To conduct Odoo 18 sales margin analysis, follow these steps:

Access the Sales Module: Log into your Odoo 18 account 

and Direct to the Sales module. This is where you will manage all sales orders and customer information.

Create or Select a Sales Order: You can create or select a new or existing one. Ensure all relevant details, including product prices and quantities, are correctly entered.

Input Cost Prices: For accurate margin calculation, it's essential to input the cost prices of the products sold. This can be done by editing the product information in the Inventory module. Make sure that the cost price reflects the actual expense incurred.

Calculate the Margin: Once the sales order is complete, Odoo 18 will automatically calculate the margin based on the formula:

Margin= Selling Price−Cost Price Margin=Selling Price−Cost Price

This calculation provides insights into the profitability of each sale.

Review the Profitability Report: After calculating the margin, you can generate a profitability report. This report summarises the sales, costs, and margins, providing a comprehensive view of your sales performance.

Utilizing Odoo 18 Sales Management Features

Sales Tracking

Odoo 18 offers a range of sales management features that enhance margin tracking capabilities. These include:

Real-Time Data Analysis: Odoo provides real-time insights into sales performance, allowing businesses to respond quickly to market changes.

Customisable Reports: Users can create customised reports focusing on specific products, sales teams, or periods, making it easier to identify trends and opportunities.

Integration with Inventory Management: Integrating sales and inventory modules ensures that cost prices are always up-to-date, facilitating accurate margin calculations.

Monitoring Sales Order Profitability

Odoo 18 sales order profitability tracking is critical for businesses aiming to optimise their sales processes. By monitoring profitability on a per-order basis, companies can identify which products or services are underperforming and adjust their strategies accordingly.

Identifying Sales Margins in Odoo 18 ERP

Key Metrics to Monitor

To effectively analyse sales margins in Odoo 18, consider monitoring the following key metrics:

Gross Margin: This is the difference between sales revenue and the cost of goods sold (COGS). It provides a high-level view of profitability.

Net Margin: This metric accounts for all expenses, including operating costs, taxes, and interest. It offers a more comprehensive view of overall profitability.

    This method applies a higher depreciation in the earlier years of an asset's life and decreases over time. That is typically used for assets that lose value quickly, such as computers.

  3. Manual Depreciation:

    Odoo also allows you to enter depreciation values manually.

You can set the depreciation method for each asset category, which will automatically apply to all assets within that category.

Important Point: Why Set Depreciation in Months Instead of Years?

Reporting > Depreciation Schedule

  1. Asset Details:
    • Asset name or description (e.g., Laptop).
    • Purchase price or cost.
    • Date of purchase.
    • Useful life (e.g., 5 years).
    • Residual value (value at the end of the useful life).
  2. Depreciation Method:
    • The chosen method (e.g., straight-line, declining balance).
  3. Periods:
    • Timeframes for depreciation (e.g., months or years).
  4. Calculation:
    • Amount depreciated each period.
    • Accumulated depreciation (total depreciation up to a certain point).
    • Net book value (remaining value of the asset after depreciation).

Title: How to Install Odoo 17 on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
Content:
Install Odoo 17 on Ubuntu

Odoo is a comprehensive, open-source Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system that integrates all aspects of business management into one platform. This tutorial will help you:

  • Install Odoo 17 on Ubuntu server.
  • Configure PostgreSQL as the database backend.
  • Set up Odoo to run as a service for automatic startup on reboot.
  • Access Odoo via the web interface for easy setup and management.

Whether you're a system administrator, developer, or business owner new to Odoo, this guide on How to Install Odoo 17 on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS will walk you through the essential steps to get your instance up and running.

Log in to the Ubuntu Server via SSH

To begin Connect to your server using SSH:

				
					ssh username@IP_Address -p Port_number

Example:

				
					ssh root@127.0.0.1 -p 22

Step 2: Update Your Server

Before Install Odoo 17 on Ubuntu make sure your system is up-to-date.

				
					sudo apt-get update -y
 sudo apt-get upgrade -y

Step 3: Secure Your Server

For enhanced security, it’s recommended to install Fail2Ban to protect your server from brute-force SSH attacks. 

				
					 sudo apt-get install openssh-server fail2ban -y

Now, Start and enable Fail2Ban:

				
					sudo systemctl start fail2ban
sudo systemctl enable fail2ban

To verify that Fail2Ban is running:

				
					sudo systemctl status fail2ban

Step 4: Create a System User for Odoo

For security reasons, Create a dedicated system user for Odoo:

				
					sudo adduser --system --home=/opt/odoo17 --group odoo17

Step 5: Install Required Packages and Libraries

To install the necessary libraries and development tools, run the following:

				
					sudo apt-get install -y python3-pip python3-dev libxml2-dev libxslt1-dev zlib1g-dev libsasl2-dev libldap2-dev build-essential libssl-dev libffi-dev libmysqlclient-dev libjpeg-dev libpq-dev

Step 6: Install Web Dependencies

Odoo uses Node.js for some web dependencies, so install them as follows:

				
					sudo apt-get install -y npm
sudo ln -s /usr/bin/nodejs /usr/bin/node
sudo npm install -g less less-plugin-clean-css
sudo apt-get install -y node-less

Step 7: Install and Configure PostgreSQL

Odoo requires PostgreSQL to store data. Install PostgreSQL and set up an Odoo user: 

				
					 sudo apt-get install postgresql -y

Create an Odoo PostgreSQL user:

				
					 sudo su postgres
 createuser --createdb --username postgres --no-createrole --no-superuser --pwprompt odoo17

Grant superuser privileges to this user:

				
					 psql -c "ALTER USER odoo17 WITH SUPERUSER;"

exit

Step 8: Get Odoo 17 Community from GitHub

Now, install Git and clone the Odoo 17 repository: 

				
					sudo apt-get install git -y

Switch to the odoo17 user and Clone the Odoo repository:  

				
					sudo su - odoo17 -s /bin/bash
git clone https://www.github.com/odoo/odoo --depth 1 --branch 17.0 --single-branch .
exit

Step 9: Install Python Dependencies

Now, install all the required Python dependencies for Odoo:

				
					sudo pip3 install -r /opt/odoo17/requirements.txt

You may encounter issues with gevent, greenlet, python-ldap, and psycopg2. To resolve this, manually install them:

				
					sudo pip3 install gevent greenlet python-ldap psycopg2-binary psycopg2

Step 10: Install Wkhtmltopdf for PDF Reports

To generate PDF reports, Odoo requires Wkhtmltopdf. Install it by running:

				
					sudo wget 
https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/releases/download/0.12.5/wkhtmltox_0.12.5-1.bionic_amd64.deb
				
			
				
					sudo dpkg -i wkhtmltox_0.12.5-1.bionic_amd64.deb
sudo apt install -f -y

Step 11: Configure the Odoo Configuration File

Create the configuration file for Odoo:

				
					sudo nano /etc/odoo17.conf

Add the following content (update the password and other settings as needed):

				
					[options]
admin_passwd = admin
db_host = localhost
db_port = 5432
db_user = odoo17
db_password = password
addons_path = /opt/odoo17/addons
logfile = /var/log/odoo17/odoo.log

Set the necessary file permissions: 

				
					sudo chown odoo17: /etc/odoo17.conf
sudo chmod 640 /etc/odoo17.conf
sudo mkdir /var/log/odoo17
sudo chown odoo17:root /var/log/odoo17

Step 12: Create an Odoo Service File

Create a systemd service file to manage the Odoo service:

				
					sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/odoo17.service

Add the following content:

				
					[Unit]
Description=Odoo17
Documentation=http://www.odoo.com
[Service]
Type=simple
User=odoo17
ExecStart=/opt/odoo17/odoo-bin -c /etc/odoo17.conf
[Install]
WantedBy=default.target

Set the correct permissions for the service file:

				
					sudo chmod 755 /etc/systemd/system/odoo17.service
sudo chown root: /etc/systemd/system/odoo17.service

Step 13: Start Odoo 17

Start the Odoo service:

				
					sudo systemctl start odoo17.service

Check the status of the Odoo service:

				
					sudo systemctl status odoo17.service

Enable Odoo to start on boot:

				
					sudo systemctl enable odoo17.service

Step 14: Access Odoo 17

Open your browser and visit:

				
					http://:8069

You should now see the Odoo setup page, where you can configure your database and start using Odoo.

You’ve successfully installed Odoo 17

Understanding Odoo Database Management

Efficient database management allows for smooth business operations and helps in testing new functionalities without disrupting production data.

Odoo Database Back Up

Taking a backup in Odoo from the frontend involves a few steps.

  • Log in to your Odoo instance using your IP address.
  •  ip-address/web/database/manager
  •  eg:- 123.456.78.9:8089/web/database/manager

2. Click on Backup

Select the database you want to back up. If you have multiple databases, ensure you select the correct one.

3. Enter the Credentials

Enter the master password and Select "zip(includes fiestore)" from the drop down menu.

4. Click in back up and the download begins

Click on the backup option, and the download process will automatically start without any additional steps or confirmation required.

Database Restoring

  • Log in to your Odoo instance using your IP-address.
  • ip-address/web/database/manager
  • eg:- 123.456.78.9:8089/web/database/manager 

2. Click on Restore Database

3. Enter the Credentials

  • Provide the master password in the field provided.
  • Click on choose file and select the database zip file.
  • Provide a new name for the data base under 'Database Name' tab.
  • Untick the Nutralize tab.
  • Select the 'This database is a copy' from the check box list.

After adding all the credentials, click on continue, and restoring begins. Please wait for the restoration to be completed.

How to Duplicate an Odoo Database

How to Delete an Odoo Database

Regular updates ensure security patches and improved functionality.

 sudo apt-get upgrade -y

sudo systemctl enable fail2ban

Step 5: Install PostgreSQL

sudo su - postgres
createuser --createdb --username postgres --no-createrole --superuser --pwprompt odoo18
exit

Step 6: Create a System User for Odoo

					sudo adduser --system --home=/opt/odoo18 --group odoo18

Step 7: Clone Odoo 18 from GitHub

Clone the Odoo 18 repository to your server:

				
					sudo su - odoo18
git clone https://www.github.com/odoo/odoo --depth 1 --branch 18.0 --single-branch .
exit

This ensures that your system has the latest version of Odoo 18.

Step 8: Install Python Packages

Install Python packages globally (without using a virtual environment):

				
					sudo pip3 install -r /opt/odoo18/requirements.txt

Or 

Create and activate a Python virtual environment for Odoo 18:

				
					sudo python3 -m venv /opt/odoo18/venv
				
			
				
					sudo -s
cd /opt/odoo18/
source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

				
			
				
					sudo wget
https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/releases/download/0.12.5/wkhtmltox_0.12.5-1.bionic_amd64.deb sudo dpkg -i
wkhtmltox_0.12.5-1.bionic_amd64.deb sudo apt-get install -y 
xfonts-75dpi sudo apt install -f
deactivate

Step 9:Create Odoo Configuration File

Create the Odoo configuration file /etc/odoo18.conf:

				
					sudo nano /etc/odoo18.conf

Add the following content:

				
					ini
[options]
   ; This is the password that allows database operations:
   ; admin_passwd = admin
   db_host = localhost

   addons_path = /opt/odoo18/addons

Set File Permissions:

Change the ownership and permissions of the configuration file:

				
					sudo chown odoo18: /etc/odoo18.conf
sudo chmod 640 /etc/odoo18.conf

Create a Log Directory:

Create a directory for storing Odoo logs:

sudo chown odoo18:root /var/log/odoo

Step 10: Create the Service File

Create a new systemd service file for Odoo:

				
					sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/odoo18.service

Add the following configuration:

Description=Odoo18
Documentation=http://www.odoo.com

# Ubuntu/Debian convention:
Type=simple
User=odoo18
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /opt/odoo18/odoo-bin -c /etc/odoo18.conf

sudo chown root: /etc/systemd/system/odoo18.service

Step 11: Start Odoo Service

Step 12: Enable Odoo Service at Boot

Imagine  instead of manually monitoring stock levels or remembering when to reorder products, Odoo  automatically places orders based on set parameters. Not only will that save time, but it will also help manage inventory more effectively, cutting operational costs while assuring customers their products will always be available in stock.

Here's why reordering rules can benefit your business:

Odoo 18 Inventory Automation:

The system takes over once you set up the rules. It’s like having an employee dedicated to ensuring your stock never runs out.

Odoo 18 Automatic Replenishment:

The system generates purchase orders automatically whenever your stock reaches a predetermined reorder point.

Odoo 18 Inventory Optimization:

With proper setup, Odoo ensures you maintain just the right amount of stock, optimizing storage space and capital.

Setting Up Reordering Rules in Odoo 18: The Easy Way

Are you ready to implement Odoo 18 reordering rules in your system? 

It’s much simpler than you think, and I’ll walk you through it by step.

Step 1: Access the Inventory Module

First things first: Go to the Inventory Module in Odoo

Once there, look for the "Reordering Rules" option under the Product. That is where all the work happens.

Step 2: Create a New Reordering Rule

Click on the “Create” button to set up a new rule.

You’ll need to fill in key details about the product for which you’re creating the rule. Here’s what you’ll define:

Product Name:

Write the name of the item or product.

Warehouse:

Choose the go down or warehouse where the rule applies.  

Minimum Stock Level:

Think of it as your safety net. That is the minimum number of units you want in stock before triggering a restock.

With this on hand, we have 16, and the forecasted amount is 18, and the maximum we need is 40; that's why we have to order 22 more.

Step 3: Set Reorder Points

Next, you’ll set your Reorder Points.

That tells Odoo when it’s time to reorder. For instance, the system automatically generates a purchase order for more items if your reorder point is 10 and your stock level drops to 10 or lower.

Step 4: Lead Time and Odoo 18 Minimum Stock Rules

Then specify Lead Time (how long a supplier takes to deliver the product) and Maximum Stock (the highest level of stock you want to keep). These factors are essential for balancing demand and supply.

Step 5: Activate the Rule

After everything’s set up, hit save and activate the rule. You’re done! Odoo will now track the inventory and place orders automatically once stock levels reach the minimum threshold.

You must periodically review or check your Odoo reordering rules to ensure they match your company's current needs. For example, if a product suddenly becomes a best-seller, you should adjust the reorder point to keep up with demand.

Title: How to Automatically Sync Product Template Field Updates to Product Variants in Odoo 18?
Content:
Managing product variants in Odoo can sometimes feel overwhelming, especially for newcomers unfamiliar with its structure. At its core, Odoo’s product management system, it's common to encounter scenarios where changes made at the Product Template (product.template) level must be reflected automatically in its corresponding Product Variants (product.product). This is especially important in systems with complex product configurations or when maintaining data consistency across variants.

In this blog post, we’ll explore how to automate the synchronization of field updates from the product template to its related Product Variants in Odoo, ensuring your data stays consistent without manual intervention.

Why Sync Fields Between Product Template and Variants?

Odoo separates product data into two models:

  • Product.template:

    The shared attributes (like name, category, type) for all variants of a product.

  • product.product:

    The specific variants of that product (each with its own combination of attributes).

By default, not every field is automatically synchronized between these models. Manual intervention or automation is needed to maintain consistency if you introduce custom fields or require specific fields to propagate from templates to variants.

For instance, if you’ve added a custom field such as "Part Number" or "Description," it’s essential for these fields to stay consistent across all related product variants. Without automation, this can be a time-consuming and error-prone process.

How to Automatically Sync a Field from Product Template to Product Variants in odoo:

When we introduce custom fields such as part number or description, we may want them to stay in sync with the product template and Product Variants in Odoo - both when creating a product and updating existing records.

Below is a robust implementation that automatically syncs fields between product.template and product.product, using context flags to prevent infinite recursion.

Sync Field Updates from Variant to Template

				
					from odoo import api, fields, models, _
class ProductProduct(models.Model):
   _inherit = 'product.product'
   _inherits = {'product.template': 'product_tmpl_id'}
   part_number = fields.Char(string="Part Number")
   product_description = fields.Char(string="Description")
   @api.model
   def create(self, vals):
       # Sync part_number from product.template if product_tmpl_id is provided
       template_id = vals.get('product_tmpl_id')
       if template_id:
           template = self.env['product.template'].browse(template_id)
           vals['part_number'] = template.part_number
           vals['product_description'] = template.product_description
       return super(ProductProduct, self).create(vals)
   def write(self, vals):
       if 'part_number' in vals:
           self.mapped('product_tmpl_id').with_context(skip_part_number_sync=True).write({'part_number': vals['part_number']})
       if 'product_description' in vals:
           self.mapped('product_tmpl_id').with_context(skip_product_description_sync=True).write({'product_description': vals['product_description']})
       return super(ProductProduct, self).write(vals)

Sync Fields on Product Variant Creation 

				
					from odoo import api, fields, models, _
class ProductTemplate(models.Model):
   _inherit = 'product.template'
   part_number = fields.Char(string="Part Number")
   product_description = fields.Char(string='Description')
   def write(self, vals):
       # Avoid recursion by using a context flag
       res = super(ProductTemplate, self).write(vals)
       if not self.env.context.get('skip_part_number_sync') and 'part_number' in vals:
           for template in self:
               template.product_variant_ids.with_context(skip_part_number_sync=True).write({'part_number': vals['part_number']})
       if 'product_description' in vals and not self.env.context.get('skip_product_description_sync'):
           for template in self:
               template.product_variant_ids.with_context(skip_product_description_sync=True).write({'product_description': vals['product_description']})
       return res

Visual Representation of the Workflow

By implementing this workflow, you can ensure a consistent data structure that aligns with your operational needs, whether managing a small inventory or an extensive catalog.

Key Benefits of This Approach

  • Bi-directional Synchronization:

    Ensures updates flow smoothly between templates and variants.

  • Prevents Recursion:

    Uses context flags to avoid infinite loops during synchronization.

  • Data Consistency:

    Maintains uniformity in product data across all records.

  • Universal Application:

    Supports manual UI updates and programmatic changes (via XML-RPC, imports, or automation).

  • Time-Saving Automation:

    Reduces the need for manual updates, freeing up time for more critical tasks.

Practical Applications in Real-World Scenarios

Consider a retail business managing a catalog of clothing items. Like a t-shirt, each product has multiple variants based on size and color. By implementing this synchronization:

  • Updating the "Material" or "Style" field in the product template automatically updates all related variants.
  • Reduces errors in product descriptions across platforms.
  • Ensures consistency for customers viewing the catalog online or in-store.

This automation helps eliminate repetitive tasks, allowing your team to focus on strategic priorities rather than data correction.

The Road to Efficient Product Management

Implementing this solution can simplify your product management process and reduce the chances of errors caused by manual data updates. Whether adding custom fields or managing large product catalogues, this approach ensures your data stays consistent across all templates and product variants in Odoo.
