Title: How to Customize Access Rights in Odoo 18 Using Python Code?
Content:
In any business, managing user access to critical data and operations is not just a best practice - it's essential. Odoo 18, with its highly customizable ERP framework, encourages businesses to fine-tune user access rights. Whether safeguarding sensitive information or streamlining workflows, configuring user permissions ensures your system is secure and efficient.

But how do you ensure the right people access the correct data without overwhelming them with unnecessary privileges? The answer lies in Odoo’s powerful access control mechanisms. This blog takes you step-by-step through customizing user access rights in Odoo 18 using Python code. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced developer, this guide will show you how to create user groups, enforce model-level restrictions, and apply record rules that adapt to your unique business needs.

By the end of this blog, you’ll understand how to control access precisely and why this customisation is an innovation for your organisation’s security and productivity.

Why Access Rights Matter

Access rights in Odoo 18 define what a user can see, create, edit, or delete in the system. Properly managing access rights:

  • Protects sensitive information.
  • Automate workflows by showing users only relevant data.
  • Prevents accidental or unauthorized modifications.
  • Ensures compliance with organizational policies.

Utilising Odoo’s tools - Access Control Lists (ACLs), record rules, and Python overrides - allows you to achieve fine-grained control over user access.

1. Create Custom User Groups

The first step in customizing access rights in Odoo 18 is defining user groups. Groups represent roles within your organization, such as "Custom Manager" or "Custom User."

				
					security/user_groups.xml
       
           Custom Manager
       
           Custom User

What it does:

  • This defines two groups: Custom Manager and Custom User.
  • These groups will later be used to restrict access.

2. Restrict Access with ACLs

Access Control Lists (ACLs) allow you to define permissions at the model level. You can control whether a group can read, create, write, or delete records for a specific model.

				
					security/ir.model.access.csv
id,name,model_id:id,group_id:id,perm_read,perm_write,perm_create,perm_unlink
user_restrict.access_user_restriction,access_user_restriction,user_restrict.model_user_restriction,user_restrict.group_custom_manager,1,1,1,1
user_restrict.access_user_restriction,access_user_restriction,user_restrict.model_user_restriction,user_restrict.group_custom_user,1,0,0,0

Explanation:

  • Custom Managers can read, write, create, and delete records.
  • Custom Users can only read records (no editing, creating, or deleting).

3. Apply Record Rules

To restrict users from accessing specific records, define record rules in an XML file:

				
					
security/record_rules.xml
       
           Custom User: Only See Own Records
           [('user_id', '=', user.id)]

Explanation:

  • Users in the Custom User group can only see records they created.

  • Custom Managers: This rule does not restrict them.

4. Restrict Access in Python Code

Sometimes, you may want to enforce additional restrictions at the model level. You can override the create, write, and unlink methods in your model.

				
					from odoo import models, fields, api
from odoo.exceptions import AccessError
class UserRestriction(models.Model):
   _name = 'user.restriction'
   _description = 'UserRestriction'
   name = fields.Char(string="Name", required=True)
   user_id = fields.Many2one('res.users', string="Owner", default=lambda self: self.env.user)
   @api.model
   def create(self, vals):
       if not self.env.user.has_group('user_restrict.group_custom_manager'):
           raise AccessError("Only managers can create records.")
       return super(UserRestriction, self).create(vals)
   def write(self, vals):
       if not self.env.user.has_group('user_restrict.group_custom_manager'):
           raise AccessError("Only managers can edit records.")
       return super(UserRestriction, self).write(vals)
   def unlink(self):
       if not self.env.user.has_group('user_restrict.group_custom_manager'):
           raise AccessError("Only managers can delete records.")
       return super(UserRestriction, self).unlink()
class SaleOrder(models.Model):
   _inherit = 'sale.order'
   def unlink(self):
       if not self.env.user.has_group('user_restrict.group_custom_manager'):
           raise AccessError("You are not allowed to delete quotations.")
       return super(SaleOrder, self).unlink()

Explanation:

  • Users in the Custom User group cannot create, edit, or delete records.
  • If a user lacks the Custom Manager role, they will see an AccessError.

5. Testing Access Rights

After implementing the above changes, it’s essential to test them:

  1. Log in as a Custom User:

    • Verify that you can only view records you own.

    • Confirm you cannot create, edit, or delete records.

  2. Log in as a Custom Manager:

    • Ensure you have full access to all records and functionality.

  3. Test Boundary Cases:

    • Attempt unauthorized actions to confirm that restrictions work as intended.

Best Practices for Managing Access Rights in Odoo 18

  • Plan Ahead:

    Before customizing access rights, map out the roles and permissions needed for your organization.

  • Keep Security Files Organized:

    To maintain clarity, use separate XML files for groups, ACLs, and record rules.

  • Test in a Development Environment:

    Always test changes in a non-production environment to avoid disrupting operations.

  • Document Your Changes:

    Keep detailed documentation for future reference or debugging.

Customizing Access Rights in Odoo 18

Customizing access rights in Odoo 18 is more than just a technical exercise - it’s a strategic decision that shapes how efficiently your team collaborates and how securely your data is handled. Utilizing Python to create user groups, enforce model restrictions, and apply record-level rules encourages your business to operate smarter and safer.

As you refine these settings, always keep your organizational goals and workflows in mind. A well-configured access system doesn't just protect - it enables.

With Odoo 18, you manage permissions and build a foundation for secure, updated success.

Title: Enhancing User Authentication Security in Flutter with Firebase
Content:
Firebase Authentication offers easy integration with Flutter through its well-documented SDKs, significantly reducing development time. Developers can quickly add authentication features without building complex backend systems, making Firebase an efficient choice for handling user authentication in mobile applications. With minimal setup, Firebase Auth flawlessly integrates into Flutter apps, allowing developers to focus on building engaging user experiences.

How to Implement Firebase Authentication in your Flutter Application: A Step-by-Step Guide

Create a Flutter Project

Open your terminal or IDE (like Android Studio or Visual Studio Code) and run the following command in terminal to create a new Flutter project:

  • flutter create you_project_name
  • Flutter create firebase-login

Set Up a Firebase Project

  • Sign to Firebase.
  • SignIn the Firebase console ,click add Project (or Create a project), and enter a name for your Firebase project(for example, “firebase-login).
  • Click through the project creation options. If prompted, accept the Firebase terms. Skip setting up Google Analytics because you won't be using Analytics for this app.
  • Once your Firebase project is ready, you must register your Flutter app (both for Android and iOS, if needed).

Enable email sign-in for Firebase Authentication

The app that you're building uses Firebase Authentication to allow your users to sign in to your app. It also allows new users to register from the Flutter application.To allow users to sign in to the web app, you'll first use the Email/Password sign-in method. Later, you'll add the Google Sign-In method.

  • In the Firebase console, expand the Build menu in the left panel.
  • Click Authentication, click the Get Started button, then the Sign-in method tab Click Email/Password in the Sign-in providers list, set the Enable switch to the on position, and then click Save.

Register Your Flutter App with Firebase

For Android:

  • In the Firebase Console, click on the Android icon to register your app.
  • Enter your Android package name. You can find it in your Flutter project at android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml under the package attribute.
  • Download the google-services.json file and place it in your Flutter project’s android/app directory.

For iOS:

  • Click on the iOS icon in the Firebase Console.
  • Enter your iOS bundle identifier. You can find it in your Flutter project at ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj under the PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER setting.
  • Download the GoogleService-Info.plist file and place it in your Flutter project’s ios/Runner directory.

Open ios/Runner.xcworkspace in Xcode and ensure the GoogleService-Info.plist is included in your app’s build.

Install Firebase Packages

Add the necessary Firebase packages to your pubspec.yaml file, including firebase_core and firebase_auth, then run flutter pub get:

Title: How to Prevent Duplicate Invoice Numbers in Odoo 18
Content:
Boosting Odoo Data Integrity with Python Constraints

Data integrity is crucial for maintaining accurate business records in Odoo. Maintaining reliable data in Odoo is helpful and the cornerstone for wise company decision-making.  But when mistakes pass through the system?  One effective method of enforcing data rules is to implement Python constraints.  These behind-the-scenes protections ensure that the data entered into your Odoo system is consistent, dependable, and free from frequent errors.  

At Netilligence, we will show you how to simplify your procedures, why they are so successful, and how to use them. In this guide, you'll learn how to create a Python constraint to prevent duplicate invoice numbers in Odoo, ensuring data consistency. Ultimately, you will realise how much peace of mind this tiny reasoning can provide for your Odoo configuration.

What Are Python Constraints in Odoo?

Python constraints are custom rules written in Python to validate data before it's saved in the database. They are defined using the _constraints attribute or by overriding the create() and write() methods.

How to Prevent Duplicate Invoice Numbers

Preventing duplicate invoice numbers is paramount for maintaining accurate financial records. In Odoo, you can set up unique constraints or use Python code to ensure that each invoice number is distinct. This avoids confusion, keeps your accounting clean, and prevents costly errors.

Let’s create a constraint that restricts users from creating invoices with duplicate invoice numbers.

Step 1: Define the Python Constraint

We'll inherit the account.move model (used for invoices) and add a constraint.

Python Code:

				
					from odoo import models, fields, api
from odoo.exceptions import ValidationError
class AccountMove(models.Model):
   _inherit = 'account.move'
   invoice_number = fields.Char(string='Invoice Number', required=True)
   @api.constrains('invoice_number')
   def _check_invoice_number_unique(self):
       for record in self:
           if self.search_count([
               ('invoice_number', '=', record.invoice_number),
               ('id', '!=', record.id)
           ]):
               raise ValidationError(f"Invoice number '{record.invoice_number}' already exists!")

Step 2: Add the Field to the View

Enriching Data Accuracy with Python Constraints in Odoo

By implementing Python constraints, you can effectively prevent data entry errors and ensure consistent records in your Odoo database. This flexible approach can be applied to various models and fields, making it a powerful tool for maintaining data integrity.

Title: How to Upload Images & Files in Flutter and Store Them in Odoo Backend?
Content:
In the age of smartphones and mobile apps, uploading images and files has become a common feature in many applications. Whether you’re developing an e-commerce app where users must upload profile pictures, invoices, or receipts or perhaps a logistics app where documents must be submitted for verification, handling file uploads is crucial. But how do you make this process seamless for your users, and how do you store those files in a backend system that’s both reliable and scalable?

In this blog post, we’ll walk you through handling file uploads in a Flutter app and securely storing them in an Odoo backend. Don’t worry if you’re new to either Flutter or Odoo - this guide is designed to be beginner-friendly and approachable.

The Importance of File Uploads in Modern Apps

File uploads are essential for modern apps - users must submit documents, images, or other files that must be stored safely. For example, in an e-commerce app, users might need to upload product images, invoices, or delivery receipts. For logistics, uploaded documents might include shipping labels or proof of delivery. Flutter, the framework used for building natively compiled mobile, web, and desktop applications from a single codebase, makes handling these tasks relatively simple.

Meanwhile, Odoo, an open-source ERP system, provides an easy-to-use backend for storing and managing such files. With its robust API, Odoo allows you to store images, documents, and other files, all while keeping everything neatly organized.

In this tutorial, we’ll guide you step by step through:

  1. Setting up the Flutter project for file uploads.
  2. Using the Flutter app to select images and files.
  3. Sending files to Odoo backend using their REST API.
  4. Handling the server's response and displaying uploaded files within the Flutter app.

So whether you're a beginner or a developer looking to add this functionality, you’ll find everything you need here.

1. Setting up the flutter project

Before headfirst into file uploads, let's set up a Flutter project. If you haven’t already created one, you can do so by running:

				
					Add the required dependencies in pubspec.yaml
				
			
				
					dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter
  # The following adds the Cupertino Icons font to your application.
  # Use with the CupertinoIcons class for iOS style icons.
  cupertino_icons: ^1.0.6
  get: ^4.7.2
  hive_flutter: ^1.1.0
  file_picker: ^10.1.2
  image_picker: ^1.1.2
  dio: ^5.8.0+1

2. Selecting images and files in Flutter

In this step, we’ll allow users to select files (images or documents) from their devices. We'll use the image_picker package for pictures and the file_picker package for documents.

Start by creating a service file called file_picker_service.dart, where we'll implement methods for picking files.

				
					Create a service file file_picker_service.dart
				
			
				
					import 'dart:io';
import 'package:file_picker/file_picker.dart';
import 'package:image_picker/image_picker.dart';
class FilePickerService {
  static Future<File?> pickImage() async {
    final ImagePicker picker = ImagePicker();
    final XFile? image = await picker.pickImage(source: ImageSource.gallery);
    if (image != null) {
      return File(image.path);
    }
    return null;
  }
  static Future<File?> pickFile() async {
    FilePickerResult? result = await FilePicker.platform.pickFiles();
    if (result != null && result.files.single.path != null) {
      return File(result.files.single.path!);
    }
    return null;
  }
}

In this service, we have two methods:

  • pickImage() allows the user to choose an image from their device’s gallery.
  • pickFile() lets the user select any file (such as PDFs or Word documents).

Now, we’ve got a service that lets users select files or images - easy enough, right?

3. Sending them to Odoo’s REST API

Once a file is selected, we must send it to Odoo for storage. We will create an API call to Odoo’s backend using the http package.

				
					Create odoo_upload_service.dart to handle file uploads.
				
			
				
					import 'dart:io';
import 'package:dio/dio.dart';
class OdooUploadService {
  final String baseUrl = "https://your-odoo-instance.com";
  final String uploadEndpoint = "/web/dataset/call_kw/your.model/create";
  Future<void> uploadFile(File file, String fileName, String accessToken) async {
    try {
      Dio dio = Dio();
      dio.options.headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer $accessToken";
      FormData formData = FormData.fromMap({
        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
        "params": {
          "model": "your.model",
          "method": "create",
          "args": [
            {
              "name": fileName,
              "file": await MultipartFile.fromFile(file.path, filename: fileName),
            }
          ],
        }
      });
      Response response = await dio.post("$baseUrl$uploadEndpoint", data: formData);
      if (response.statusCode == 200) {
        print("File uploaded successfully: ${response.data}");
      } else {
        print("Failed to upload file: ${response.data}");
      }
    } catch (e) {
      print("Upload error: $e");
    }
  }
}

In this service:

  • The uploadFile method sends a file to your Odoo instance using a multipart HTTP request.
  • We include the model (the Odoo model where the file is being uploaded) and recorded (the specific record to which the file should be attached).
  • The Authorization header includes your Odoo API key for secure access.

Replace the odooUrl and odooApiKey variables with your actual Odoo instance URL and API key.

4. Handling Odoo responses and displaying files

Once the file is successfully uploaded to Odoo, it’s time to display the results in the Flutter app. Let's create a simple UI for uploading files and showing the upload status.

  1. Implementing File Upload in the UI
				
					Create upload_screen.dart
				
			
				
					import 'dart:io';
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:get/get.dart';
import 'file_picker_service.dart';
import 'odoo_upload_service.dart';
class UploadScreen extends StatefulWidget {
  @override
  _UploadScreenState createState() => _UploadScreenState();
}
class _UploadScreenState extends State<UploadScreen> {
  File? selectedFile;
  final OdooUploadService _uploadService = OdooUploadService();
  final String accessToken = "your_odoo_access_token";
  void pickImage() async {
    File? file = await FilePickerService.pickImage();
    if (file != null) {
      setState(() {
        selectedFile = file;
      });
    }
  }
  void pickFile() async {
    File? file = await FilePickerService.pickFile();
    if (file != null) {
      setState(() {
        selectedFile = file;
      });
    }
  }
  void uploadFile() async {
    if (selectedFile != null) {
      await _uploadService.uploadFile(
          selectedFile!, "uploaded_file.png", accessToken);
      Get.snackbar("Success", "File uploaded to Odoo!");
    } else {
      Get.snackbar("Error", "Please select a file first!");
    }
  }
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: Text("Upload to Odoo")),
      body: Column(
        mainAxisAlignment: MainAxisAlignment.center,
        children: [
          selectedFile != null
              ? Image.file(selectedFile!, height: 150)
              : Text("No file selected"),
          SizedBox(height: 20),
          ElevatedButton(onPressed: pickImage, child: Text("Pick Image")),
          ElevatedButton(onPressed: pickFile, child: Text("Pick File")),
          ElevatedButton(onPressed: uploadFile, child: Text("Upload File")),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

2. Displaying Uploaded Files in Flutter

      a. If you want to fetch and display uploaded files from Odoo, modify  

				
					odoo_upload_service.dart
				
			
				
					Future<List<String>> fetchUploadedFiles(String accessToken) async {
    try {
      Dio dio = Dio();

Title: How to Add a Custom Column in Odoo 18 General Ledger?
Content:
Adding a Custom Column in Odoo 18 General Ledger

Odoo 18’s accounting module is a powerful tool for managing financial transactions and generating reports. Among its many features, the General Ledger (GL) report is essential for businesses, offering a comprehensive view of all financial entries. But what if your business requires additional details in the report that are not included by default?

Imagine being able to add a custom column to the General Ledger, displaying precisely the information you need to streamline your financial analysis. For instance, you might want to include an "Opportunity ID" to track which sales opportunities each transaction is linked to.

This guide will walk you through adding a custom column to the General Ledger in Odoo 18. Whether you’re new to Odoo or an experienced user, this step-by-step approach ensures you can easily enhance your financial reports to meet your unique business requirements. Let’s explore how to customise the Odoo 18 General Ledger and take your reporting capabilities to the next level!

How to Add a Custom Column in Odoo 18 General Ledger: A Step-by-Step Guide

Step 1: Identify the Field to Add

Before customizing your Odoo 18 General Ledger, decide on the additional information you want to display in the report. For this example, let’s say we want to add an "Opportunity ID" field to categorise the transactions.

This could be particularly useful if you want to track which opportunities each transaction is linked to, offering a more detailed view of your financial data.

Step 2: Inherit the General Ledger Model

Odoo uses a modular structure, allowing us to extend existing models without changing core files. To add a custom column to the General Ledger, we need to inherit the account.move.line model and define the new field.

Here’s how to do it:

				
					from odoo import models, fields
class AccountMoveLine(models.Model):
_inherit = 'account.move.line'
lead_reference = fields.Char("Opportunity ID", readonly=True, copy=False)
  • lead_reference is the field name that will store the "Opportunity ID."
  • "Opportunity ID" is the label displayed in the General Ledger.

Step 3: Modify the General Ledger Report (XML)

Next, we need to modify the QWeb report template for the General Ledger. This step adds the custom field to the report layout, ensuring the new column is displayed.

Find the General Ledger report template in account_reports and add  it to your custom module: 

Here, inheriting the template may not give you the desired result. So declaring the new field lead_reference like the default fields in the base code is enough, and are as follows:

				
					<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<odoo>
    <record id="account_reports.general_ledger_report" model="account.report">
        <field name="name">General Ledger</field>
        <field name="column_ids">
            <record id="general_ledger_lead_reference" model="account.report.column">
                <field name="name">Opportunity ID</field>
                <field name="expression_label">lead_reference</field>
                <field name="figure_type">string</field>
            </record>
        </field>
    </record>
</odoo>

This will add a new column at the end of the General Ledger table. You can rearrange the position of the latest or the existing column from the front end itself. 

Step 4: Modify the General Ledger Report (Python Code)

Let’s get into the Python code to customize the SQL query that fetches account move lines (AMLs). The key customisation here is adding the lead_reference custom field to the SQL query.

The following code snippet modifies the SQL query to include the new lead_reference field in the General Ledger report:

				
					class AccountGeneralLedger(models.AbstractModel):
   _inherit = 'account.general.ledger.report.handler'
   def _get_query_amls(self, report, options, expanded_account_ids, offset=0, limit=None) -> SQL:
       additional_domain = [('account_id', 'in', expanded_account_ids)] if expanded_account_ids is not None else None
       queries = []
       journal_name = self.env['account.journal']._field_to_sql('journal', 'name')
       for column_group_key, group_options in report._split_options_per_column_group(options).items():
           query = report._get_report_query(group_options, domain=additional_domain, date_scope='strict_range')
           account_alias = query.join(lhs_alias='account_move_line', lhs_column='account_id',
                                      rhs_table='account_account', rhs_column='id', link='account_id')
           account_code = self.env['account.account']._field_to_sql(account_alias, 'code', query)
           account_name = self.env['account.account']._field_to_sql(account_alias, 'name')
           account_type = self.env['account.account']._field_to_sql(account_alias, 'account_type')
           query = SQL(
               '''
               SELECT
                   account_move_line.id,
                   account_move_line.date,
                   account_move_line.date_maturity,
                   account_move_line.name,
                   account_move_line.ref,
                   account_move_line.company_id,
                   account_move_line.account_id,
                   account_move_line.payment_id,
                   account_move_line.partner_id,
                   account_move_line.currency_id,
                   account_move_line.amount_currency,
                   COALESCE(account_move_line.invoice_date, account_move_line.date) AS invoice_date,
                   %(debit_select)s                        AS debit,
                   %(credit_select)s                       AS credit,
                   %(balance_select)s                      AS balance,
                   move.name                               AS move_name,
                   company.currency_id                     AS company_currency_id,
                   partner.name                            AS partner_name,
                   move.move_type                          AS move_type,
                   %(account_code)s                        AS account_code,
                   %(account_name)s                        AS account_name,
                   %(account_type)s                        AS account_type,
                   journal.code                            AS journal_code,
                   %(journal_name)s                        AS journal_name,
                   full_rec.id                             AS full_rec_name,
                   %(column_group_key)s                    AS column_group_key,
                   account_move_line.lead_reference        AS lead_reference  -- 🔹 Added custom field
               FROM %(table_references)s
               JOIN account_move move                      ON move.id = account_move_line.move_id
               %(currency_table_join)s
               LEFT JOIN res_company company               ON company.id = account_move_line.company_id
               LEFT JOIN res_partner partner               ON partner.id = account_move_line.partner_id
               LEFT JOIN account_journal journal           ON journal.id = account_move_line.journal_id
               LEFT JOIN account_full_reconcile full_rec   ON full_rec.id = account_move_line.full_reconcile_id
               WHERE %(search_condition)s
               ORDER BY account_move_line.date, account_move_line.move_name, account_move_line.id
               ''',
               account_code=account_code,
               account_name=account_name,
               account_type=account_type,
               journal_name=journal_name,
               column_group_key=column_group_key,
               table_references=query.from_clause,
               currency_table_join=report._currency_table_aml_join(group_options),
               debit_select=report._currency_table_apply_rate(SQL("account_move_line.debit")),
               credit_select=report._currency_table_apply_rate(SQL("account_move_line.credit")),
               balance_select=report._currency_table_apply_rate(SQL("account_move_line.balance")),
               search_condition=query.where_clause,
           )
           queries.append(query)
       full_query = SQL(" UNION ALL ").join(SQL("(%s)", query) for query in queries)
       if offset:
           full_query = SQL('%s OFFSET %s ', full_query, offset)
       if limit:
           full_query = SQL('%s LIMIT %s ', full_query, limit)
       return full_query

Step 5: Update and Restart Odoo

Make sure you have updated the __init__.py  and __manifest__.py  with the python file and xml file, respectively. 

Upgrade the module and restart the server to apply changes.

Final Thoughts on Adding a Custom Column in GL

Following these steps, you have successfully added a custom column to the Odoo 18 General Ledger. This customisation allows businesses to enhance their financial reporting based on specific needs. You can further extend this by adding filters, exporting capabilities, or additional fields.

Title: Flutter State Management: GetX vs. Provider vs. Riverpod
Content:
Flutter State management is an essential part of Flutter app development. It refers to how data flows and changes within an application, ensuring that the user interface updates seamlessly when data changes. Choosing the right state management solution is crucial because it can significantly impact your app's performance, scalability, and maintainability. If you’re new to Flutter, think of state management as how your app "remembers" and "shares" data across different parts of the application.

For instance, imagine you are building a shopping app. When a user adds an item to the cart, the app needs to update the cart icon, display the updated cart total, and allow seamless navigation between screens without losing the cart data. State management plays a critical role in keeping everything synchronized and functional.

In this blog, we’ll explore and compare GetX, Provider, and Riverpod - three popular state management tools in Flutter state management. Each tool has unique features that cater to different needs, making it essential to understand them before choosing the right fit for your project.

1. Provider

Overview

Provider is one of the most popular and widely used Flutter state management solutions. Endorsed by the Flutter team, it utilises the InheritedWidget to efficiently pass state down the widget tree. Provider is simple to use and works well for managing application-level state in small to medium-sized apps. However, as the app grows in complexity, the boilerplate required can become a hurdle. It’s a great starting point for beginners due to its official support and detailed documentation.

Pros:

✅ Easy to learn and implement.

✅ Recommended by the Flutter team. 

✅ Efficient and performance-friendly.

 ✅ Works well with small to medium-sized applications.

Cons:

❌ Requires boilerplate code for ChangeNotifier classes. 

❌ Can become complex in large-scale applications.

Example:

Here is an example of using Provider to manage the state of a simple counter app:

				
					import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';
class CounterProvider extends ChangeNotifier {
 int _count = 0;
 int get count => _count;
 void increment() {
   _count++;
   notifyListeners();
 }}
void main() {
 runApp(
   MultiProvider(
     providers: [
       ChangeNotifierProvider(create: (context) => CounterProvider()),
     ],
     child: MyApp(),
   ),);}
class MyApp extends StatelessWidget {
 @override
 Widget build(BuildContext context) {
   return MaterialApp(
     debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
     home: CounterScreen(),
   );  }}
class CounterScreen extends StatelessWidget {
 @override
 Widget build(BuildContext context) {
   return Scaffold(
     appBar: AppBar(title: Text("Provider Counter App")),
     body: Center(
       child: Consumer(
         builder: (context, counter, child) => Text(
           'Count: ${counter.count}',
           style: TextStyle(fontSize: 24, fontWeight: FontWeight.bold),
         ),),),
     floatingActionButton: FloatingActionButton(
       onPressed: () => context.read().increment(),
       child: Icon(Icons.add),
     ),);}}

2. GetX

Overview

GetX is a comprehensive state management library that simplifies app development with powerful features. Besides Flutter state management, it also handles dependency injection and navigation, making it a one-stop solution for developers. GetX eliminates the need for BuildContext, which is often considered a limitation in other state management libraries. Its reactive state management approach ensures high performance and minimal code. However, GetX’s learning curve and lack of official Flutter team backing can be challenging for beginners. It's best suited for those who prefer an all-in-one solution with low boilerplate code.

Pros:

✅ No need for ChangeNotifier or BuildContext.

✅ Minimal boilerplate code. 

✅ Fast and efficient.

 ✅ Comes with built-in dependency injection and navigation handling.

Cons:

❌ Can be overwhelming for beginners. 

❌ Lacks official backing from the Flutter team.

Example:

Here is an example of using GetX to manage the state of a counter app:

				
					import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:get/get.dart';
class CounterController extends GetxController {
 var count = 0.obs;
 void increment() => count++;
}
void main() {
 runApp(GetMaterialApp(home: MyApp()));
}
class MyApp extends StatelessWidget {
 final CounterController controller = Get.put(CounterController());
 @override
 Widget build(BuildContext context) {
   return Scaffold(
     body: Center(
       child: Obx(() => Text('Count: ${controller.count}')),
     ),
     floatingActionButton: FloatingActionButton(
       onPressed: controller.increment,
       child: Icon(Icons.add),
     ),
   );
 }
}

3. Riverpod

Overview

Riverpod is a modern and robust state management library that builds upon Provider concepts. By addressing some of the Provider's limitations, Riverpod introduces a cleaner, more functional, programming-friendly approach to state management. It offers improved safety and testability by eliminating the reliance on BuildContext. This feature makes Riverpod highly flexible and scalable, particularly for large and complex applications. However, its advanced concepts make it slightly challenging for beginners. Riverpod is an excellent choice for developers looking for a forward-thinking solution, emphasising immutability and clean architecture.

Pros:

✅ More robust than Provider.

✅ Supports immutability and functional programming.

Automatic Transfers in Odoo 18 Accounting

There’s much to keep track of when managing your business monetary matters. Between moving money from one account to another, reconciling bank statements, and making sure your bills are paid, it’s easy to get swamped. Whether you’re new to Odoo 18 accounting automation or looking for ways to improve your current workflows, this blog will walk you through everything you need to know. By the end, you’ll understand how Odoo 18 automatic transfers can help you save time and run your business more efficiently.

What Are Odoo 18 Accounting Automation?

Before discussing how to set up automatic transfers in Odoo 18 accounting, let’s consider what this feature does.

At their core, automatic transfers in Odoo 18 accounting allow you to move money between different accounts without doing everything manually. This is particularly helpful if you perform transactions regularly and they also need to happen on a particular schedule or if you need to move funds between internal accounts like your savings accounts.

As instance:

  • Transferring funds between your business’s main account and your payroll account
  • Making regular payments to vendors or suppliers
  • Moving money between accounts to cover bills or other misc or significant expenses

With Odoo 18 internal transfers, you can set up these transactions to occur automatically without manually entering them every time. Odoo 18 accounting automation also comes with scheduled transfers, which means you can set up transfers on specific monthly or quarterly dates so you never miss a payment.

How to Set Up Automatic Transfers in Odoo 18 Accounting?

Now that we’ve covered what automatic transfers in Odoo 18 accounting can do let’s read how to set them up. Don’t worry if you’re not a financial expert - Odoo’s interface is simple, and setting up Odoo 18 automatic transfers is easier than you might think.

Step 1: Enable Automation Features

First, you must ensure the automation features are turned on in your Odoo 18 system. That is a simple process that’ll only take a few minutes:

  • Open the Accounting module on your Odoo 18 dashboard.
  • Go to Settings > Configuration.
  • Scroll down to the Accounting Settings section and enable the options for Automated Bank Feeds, Automated Transfers, and Scheduled Transfers.

Once all these features are enabled, you can start setting up your automatic transfers.

Step 2: Setting Up Odoo 18 Internal Transfers

One of the most common types of automatic transfers is Internal transfers. These involve moving money between accounts within your business, from your business checking account to a savings account. Here’s how to set up this:

  • Go to the Accounting & Click on Transfers.
  • Under the Transfers tab, select Internal Transfers.

Step 3: Odoo 18 Scheduled Transfers for Recurring Payments

Next, let’s talk about scheduled transfers. These automatic transfers happen at planned times, like paying rent, making tax payments, or paying other bills. To set up scheduled transfers in Odoo 18:

  • Create a New.
  • Add all the details, such as Description, period, frequency, origin account, and the account to which we want to make an automated transfer.
  • Select the Automatic Transfer option to automate this process and click on Activate.

Once this is done, Odoo will take care of the rest, ensuring that your scheduled transfers happen automatically without you needing to do anything.

Now, any time a transfer is due between these accounts, Odoo will handle it automatically, freeing you from doing it manually.

Step 4: Odoo 18 bank reconciliation

Another fantastic feature of Odoo 18 automatic transfers is the ability to reconcile your bank transactions with ease. Odoo 18 bank reconciliation is essential to keep your financial records accurate, and it’s unrealistically easy to do with Odoo. Here’s how:

  • Go to the Accounting.
  • Click on Bank Reconciliation.
  • Odoo will automatically match your bank transactions with the entries in your system.

That ensures that your accounting records stay current and match what’s in your bank account without requiring manual intervention.

Regular reviews ensure you’re not missing critical payments and that everything runs smoothly.

Just because you’ve set up automatic transfers doesn’t mean you can ignore your bank accounts entirely. Monitor your account balances regularly to avoid any overdraft situations. Odoo 18 internal transfers can help move money around between accounts. Still, keeping an eye on your balances is essential to ensure there’s always enough money to cover your automated transactions.

Odoo accounting automation is highly customisable. You can set up specific rules for different types of transfers based on factors like accounts involved, transaction amounts, or payment methods. By customising these rules to fit your business's unique needs, you can ensure that your transfers align with your financial goals.

Transparency is a significant part when it comes to financial management. Luckily, Odoo 18 automatically logs all transactions, making it easy to track the history of your transfers. You'll have all the necessary records if you need to refer back to a specific transaction or prepare for an audit.

Why Should You Trust Odoo 18 Accounting Workflows?

Despite its powerful features, Odoo 18 is incredibly user-friendly. Its clean and user-friendly interface makes it easy to navigate accounting processes, even for people who aren’t accounting experts. Whether setting up internal transfers or managing scheduled transfers, you’ll find the system easy to use.

Odoo 18 is highly flexible and scalable, so any size business could adopt it quickly. Whether you’re running a small startup or a medium-large enterprise, Odoo’s accounting automation can grow with you. It’s customisable to fit your business needs, and as your business grows, you can add more complex workflows without worrying about system limitations.

3. All-in-One Solution

Another significant benefit of using Odoo 18 is its all-in-one business management solution. It handles accounting and financial tasks and integrates with other areas of your business, such as sales, inventory, and HR. That means you can manage your entire business from one platform, creating a smooth experience for you and your team.

4. Real-Time Insights and Reporting

With Odoo 18 automatic transfers and accounting workflows, you gain real-time insights into your financial situation. The platform generates up-to-date reports, allowing you to track your business’s financial health anytime. These insights help you make informed and helpful decisions, identify problems, and improve cash flow management.

Managing your business finances doesn’t have to be complicated. With Odoo 18 automatic transfers, you can automate a significant portion of your accounting tasks and free up valuable time for other parts of your business. Whether performing internal transfers, scheduling recurring payments, or reconciling your bank statements, Odoo accounting automation offers a simple, efficient solution to keep your financial operations on track.

Common Types of Hotkeys in Odoo

Odoo hotkeys work in different views, such as ListView, Form View, Kanban View, and Search View. Let’s examine the most helpful shortcuts.

Navigation Hotkeys

Hotkey

Action

    Save the current form (same as clicking "Save").

Esc

    Close the current dialog or cancel an action.

Arrow Keys

    Move between fields, records, or menus.

Tab

    Move to the next field.

Shift + Tab

    Move to the previous field.

List View (Tree View) Hotkeys

Action

  Open the selected record in the form view.

  Select multiple records.

  Select multiple records in a range.

W

  Save changes in the editable list view (write mode).

V 

  Open the selected record in the form view.

X

  Delete the selected record.

C

  Create a new record.

Form View Hotkeys

  Save the form.

  Move to the next record.

  Move to the previous record.

  Discard changes and close the form.

  Delete the record.

Search View Hotkeys

  Focus on the search bar.

  Navigate search results.

  Apply the selected filter.

Hotkey

Action

  Open the selected record in the form view.

    Write/save changes.

  Delete the selected card.

For developers working in Odoo, hotkeys can help in debugging and customization.

Hotkey

Action

  Open developer mode.

  Open the "Create" form.

To access some advanced hotkeys, you need to enable Developer Mode. Here’s how:

Let’s practice some of the most useful hotkeys:

Example 1: Saving a Record

  1. Open any form (e.g., a Sales Order).
  2. Make changes to the form.

  1. Open a record in the list view.
  2. Press Ctrl + D to duplicate the record.

If you want to define custom hotkeys for specific actions in Odoo, you can do so using XML or JavaScript.

In this example:

  • Pressing W will trigger the Confirm button.

Pressing V will trigger the Validate button.

Title: Top 12 FAQs About Odoo Upgrades

Are You Confused About the Odoo Upgrade Process?

Is upgrading your Odoo ERP worth it? Concerned about how long an Odoo upgrade takes, what it costs, or whether your custom modules will still work? If so, you're not alone! Businesses often hesitate before upgrading, fearing downtime, compatibility issues, and unexpected costs.

This article answers the top 12 FAQs about Odoo upgrades to help you understand everything about the Odoo upgrade process: best practices, cost, time, compatibility, and benefits. Let’s dive in and clear up your doubts!

1. What Is an Odoo Upgrade?

An Odoo upgrade is moving from an older version of Odoo to a newer one. Upgrading ensures businesses benefit from new features, better security, and enhanced performance.

Types of Odoo Upgrades

Version Upgrade: Moving from an older Odoo version (e.g., Odoo 14) to a newer one (e.g., Odoo 18).

Module Upgrade: Updating specific custom or third-party modules to ensure compatibility with the new version.

Security Upgrade: Applying patches to fix vulnerabilities and keep data safe.

Upgrading Odoo is essential for businesses that want to stay competitive, improve efficiency, and leverage the latest technological advancements.

2. Why Should You Upgrade to the Latest Odoo Version?

Sticking to outdated Odoo versions might seem safe, but it can hold your business back. Here’s why upgrading is beneficial:

Key Benefits of an Odoo Upgrade

New Features & Enhancements: Every Odoo upgrade introduces new tools and automation that enhance business operations.

Better Security: Older versions are prone to vulnerabilities; upgrading ensures your system stays protected.

Improved Performance: Faster processing, reduced bugs, and optimized workflows.

Long-Term Support: Odoo stops supporting older versions after a certain period. Upgrading keeps your system relevant.

Better Integration & Compatibility: New versions improve compatibility with third-party apps and custom modules.

Is an upgrade worth it? The following section explains the best practices for upgrading Odoo to ensure a smooth transition.

3. What Are the Best Practices for a Successful Odoo Upgrade?

A well-planned Odoo upgrade minimizes risks and ensures a smooth transition. Here are some Odoo upgrade best practices to follow:

Step-by-Step Best Practices

Analyze Your Current System: Identify existing custom modules and dependencies.

Test Before Upgrading: Use a test environment to check compatibility and performance.

Backup Data: Before starting the Odoo upgrade process, always back up your database.

Check Module Compatibility: Ensure custom modules work with the new version.

Work With Experts: Partner with experienced Odoo developers to avoid errors.

Monitor Post-Upgrade Performance: Continuously check for issues and resolve them quickly.

A strategic approach reduces downtime and ensures that your business operations remain unaffected.

4. How Much Does an Odoo Upgrade Cost?

The Odoo upgrade cost varies based on several factors, including:

Factors Affecting Odoo Upgrade Cost

Odoo Version: Upgrading from an older version (e.g., Odoo 10 to Odoo 17) may be more expensive.

Custom Modules: If you have customized Odoo apps, they might need modifications for compatibility.

Number of Users: More users might mean higher costs due to additional testing and support.

Deployment Type: Cloud vs. on-premise upgrades may have different pricing structures.

Service Provider: Choosing an experienced Odoo expert might cost more but ensures a smooth upgrade.

To get an accurate estimate, consult an Odoo upgrade expert at Netilligence.

5. How Long Does an Odoo Upgrade Take?

The Odoo upgrade time depends on multiple factors, such as data size, custom modules, and testing.

Testing, debugging, and training employees can extend the timeline. Proper planning ensures a smoother and faster transition.

6. Will Custom Modules Work After an Odoo Upgrade?

One of the biggest concerns during an Odoo upgrade is whether custom modules will still function properly.

Steps to Ensure Compatibility

  • Identify all custom modules used in the current system.
  • Check if they are available in the latest Odoo version.
  • Modify or rewrite code if necessary.
  • Test everything in a staging environment before going live.

If a custom module is not compatible with the new version, developers may need to upgrade or rewrite it.

7. Is an Odoo Upgrade Mandatory?

Technically, upgrading is not mandatory. However, running an outdated Odoo version comes with risks:

  • No official support or security updates.
  • Increased chances of system crashes.
  • Lack of new features and integrations.

For long-term business growth, an Odoo upgrade is highly recommended.

Downgrading an Odoo system is complicated and not officially supported. If issues arise post-upgrade, the best approach is:

  • Restore from backups.
  • Fix compatibility issues with expert help.
  • Ensure thorough testing before upgrading.

Ignoring an Odoo upgrade can result in:

  • Security vulnerabilities.
  • Performance degradation.
  • Compatibility issues with new apps.
  • Higher maintenance costs in the long run.

Upgrading ensures stability and long-term efficiency.

A reliable partner ensures a hassle-free transition.

  • Ensures data integrity.
  • Check if any functionalities need adjustments.

Overview of the Odoo Via API Endpoint

This process allows you to automate user management efficiently, which can be a huge time-saver when integrating external applications.

Step 1: The Code Breakdown

Below is the Python code for a custom Odoo via API controller that creates users via an API call. Let’s dissect it:

1. Route Configuration

				
					class UserAPIController(http.Controller):
    @http.route('/api/create_user', type='json', auth='public', methods=['POST'], csrf=False)

  • @http.route

    This decorator defines a new HTTP route. In this case, /api/create_user will listen for incoming requests.

  • type='json'

    Specifies that the request and response should be in JSON format.

  • auth='public'

    This means the API endpoint is accessible to the public. In a production environment, ensure proper authentication is applied to protect sensitive data.

  • methods=['POST']

     Only POST requests are accepted, ensuring that data is being sent to the server.

  • csrf=False

2. Data Validation

To create Users in Odoo via API, you need data validation:

				
					def create_user(self):
    try:
        data = request.httprequest.get_json(silent=True)
        username = data.get('username')
        password = data.get('password')
        email = data.get('email')
        phone = data.get('phone')
        user_type = data.get('user_type')
        if not all([username, password, email, phone, user_type]):
             return {'status': 'error', 'message': 'Missing required fields'}

JSON Extraction

 Retrieves JSON data from the request.

Field Validation

Ensures that all mandatory fields (username, password, email, phone, user_type) are present; otherwise, it returns an error message.

3. Check Existing Users

Before creating a new user, the endpoint checks if a user with the given or provided username already exists using:

				
					existing_user = request.env['res.users'].sudo().search([('login', '=', username)], limit=1)
if existing_user:
    return {'status': 'error', 'message': 'User already exists'}

This ensures that duplicate users are not created, maintaining data integrity.

4. Determining User Group

Based on the user_type provided in the JSON request, the code assigns the new user to the correct group:

				
					 if user_type == 'internal':
    group_id = request.env.ref('base.group_user').id
elif user_type == 'portal':

elif user_type == 'public':

else:
    return {'status': 'error', 'message': 'Invalid user type'}

In Odoo, user permissions are controlled through user groups. We assign the user to the appropriate group based on the user_type provided in the JSON request (either internal, portal, or public). Each group corresponds to a set of permissions in Odoo:

  • Internal users
    (typically employees) are assigned to the group_user group.
  • Portal users
    (external customers or partners) are assigned to the group_portal group.
  • Public users
    (generic users with limited access) are assigned to the group_public group.

If an invalid user_type is received, the API will return an error message.

6. Creating the User Record

Using Odoo’s ORM, a new user is created with the specified details:

})

After validating the input and ensuring no duplicate exists, the system creates a new user in the res.users model and assigns the appropriate user group.

7. Securing the Password

For security, the user’s password is hashed before being stored:

new_user.sudo()._set_encrypted_password(uid=new_user.id, pw=hashed_password)
return {'status': 'success', 'message': 'User created successfully', 'user_id': new_user.id}

  • Updating the User Record:


    The hashed password is then set using _set_encrypted_password(), ensuring the plain text password is never stored.

8. Error Handling

The whole function is wrapped in a try-except block. Any unexpected errors are caught, and a user-friendly error message is returned.

Imagine the time saved by not manually creating users every time, especially when you can integrate external systems or apps that automatically push this data into Odoo.

This approach’ll ensure your users are created securely, no duplicates are made, and everything is neatly organised in the right groups. Plus, encrypting passwords before storing them means you’re taking extra care of your data, which is always good!

Title: How to Securely Handle Odoo Sessions in Flutter Apps?

1. Introduction to Odoo Sessions in Flutter Apps

Odoo is a powerful suite of business applications, and integrating it with Odoo sessions in Flutter apps opens up new opportunities for mobile app development. However, handling user sessions securely is critical for any app that communicates with an external system like Odoo. Secure session management ensures that users' sensitive data is protected and that only authorised individuals can access certain features.

In this guide, we'll walk you through managing Odoo sessions in Flutter app, covering key security practices and how to implement them effectively. We’ll discuss how to authenticate users, store session tokens securely, and handle authentication sessions to protect against common security risks.

Understanding Odoo Session Management

Odoo uses session-based authentication to manage user logins and API interactions. Once a user successfully logs in, Odoo issues a session ID. This session ID must be included in all subsequent API requests to maintain authentication. The Odoo Sessions in Flutter Apps ensures the user remains logged in and can access the system without re-entering credentials.

However, securely handling these Odoo sessions in Flutter Apps IDs is crucial to prevent unauthorised access and hijacking. Let’s dive into the steps to secure Odoo sessions in your Flutter app.

Why Secure Odoo Sessions in Flutter Apps?

Security is a top priority when handling user sessions in mobile apps. Here’s why securing Odoo sessions is essential:

Prevent Unauthorized Access:

Ensuring that only authenticated users can access the app's features.

Protect Sensitive User Data:

Prevent sensitive user data from being exposed.

Ensure Secure API Communication:

Secure sessions help to avoid vulnerabilities like man-in-the-middle attacks.

 

Mitigate Session Hijacking Risks:

Protecting session tokens from being intercepted by attackers.

Key Security Measures

Before looking into Flutter implementation, here are some essential security measures for handling Odoo sessions securely:

Use HTTPS for API Requests:

Always use HTTPS to encrypt data in transit, preventing interception by malicious actors.

Store Session Tokens Securely:

Avoid storing session tokens in plain text. Use secure storage mechanisms like Flutter_secure_storage.

Implement Token Expiration Handling:

Session tokens should expire after a certain period, reducing the risk of unauthorized access if a session is left open.

Log Out Inactive Users:

 Automatically log out users after a period of inactivity to mitigate the risks of unattended sessions.

Implementing Session Handling in Flutter

Now that we understand the importance of secure session management, let’s move on to how you can implement session handling in your Odoo Sessions in Flutter Apps.

2.1 Logging in to Odoo and Storing the Session

In the above code, we send a POST request to Odoo’s authentication endpoint with the user’s credentials. If successful, the session ID is retrieved and returned.

2.2 Securely Storing the Session Token

For security reasons, you should never store sensitive data like session IDs in plain text. Use flutter_secure_storage to store the session ID securely.

The SecureStorage class uses the flutter_secure_storage package to store the session token securely on the device, making it safer than storing it in SharedPreferences or other unencrypted storage locations.

3. Maintaining and Securing Odoo Sessions

Session expiration is crucial to managing sessions securely. The user should be prompted to log in again if the session expires. You can implement this by checking for errors in the API response (such as an unauthorized status) and triggering re-authentication.

Following the best practices outlined in this guide, you can ensure that your Odoo Sessions in Flutter App integrates securely with Odoo, protecting user data and session information. Here’s a quick recap:

Odoo API, you can retrieve these addresses programmatically, making it easier to integrate Odoo with external systems like CRM tools, e-commerce platforms, or other third-party services. We will explore how to fetch multiple addresses from the res.partner model using an API call in Odoo. This approach allows retrieving paginated partner addresses along with their child addresses in JSON format, making it easier to integrate with external systems.

How the get_list Method Retrieves Data from APIs and Databases

The get_list method retrieves partner addresses from the res.partner model with support for pagination and child addresses. It:

Implementing the get_list Method

1. Pagination and Filtering in Odoo Search Method

def get_list(self, domain=[], page_num=1, page_size=10):
    filter = domain
    total_rec = len(self.search(filter))
    pages_count = math.ceil(total_rec / page_size)
    offset = (page_num - 1) * page_size

        obj['email'] = o.email
        obj['phone'] = o.phone
        obj['zip'] = o.zip
        obj['is_default'] = o.is_default
        obj['address_type'] = o.address_type

3. Processing Child Addresses and Structuring the Final Response 

				
					 address_data = []
        for child in o.child_ids:

Title: How to fix the Open for Editing in Android Studio option not showing in Flutter?
Content:
If you’re a Flutter developer, you’ve probably encountered various issues while working with Android Studio, especially when integrating Flutter with the native Android module. One of the common problems that developers face is when the "Open for Editing in Android Studio" option is missing from the Tools > Flutter menu. This can be frustrating, especially when making changes or building your Android app bundle (AAB).

In this post, I’ll walk you through the steps to fix this issue, even if you’ve never encountered it. The problem is related to missing configuration files when cloning Flutter projects, but don’t worry - this guide will help you restore the missing functionality in no time. Whether you're an experienced or beginner Flutter developer, these simple steps will help you get back on track.

Why Does This Happen?

So, let's discuss the reason first. 

The answer lies in how Flutter projects are cloned. When you clone a Flutter project using Git, there’s a chance that specific project configuration files, specifically the .iml file, don’t get included in the project. This file is crucial for Android Studio to recognise the Android module of your Flutter project.

Without the .iml file, Android Studio cannot correctly load the Android module. As a result, the option to open the Android module for editing disappears from the Tools > Flutter menu.

While this ‘Open for Editing in Android Studio’ may seem complicated, but the solution is simple and requires only a few easy steps. Let’s resolve this problem.

Now, to solve this issue, we have to follow a few steps:

Step 1: Create a New Flutter Project

First, create a new Flutter project. You can do this in Android Studio by going to File > New > New Flutter Project. Follow the prompts to create a basic Flutter project. This step will give you a reference project with all the necessary files, including the .iml file.

Step 2: Go to the Android module of that new Flutter project

Once your new Flutter project is created, go to the Android module of this project. This part of the Flutter project deals with Android-specific configurations, such as Gradle files, AndroidManifest.xml, and the .iml file.

Open the Android directory in the new project. The newProjectName.iml file is in this directory. Android Studio uses this file to recognise and work with the Android module of your Flutter project.

Step 3: Find the newProjectName.iml file and copy the code inside

Next, open the .iml file in the new project. This file may contain many XML tags and project-specific information, but for our purposes, we’re interested in copying the entire content of the newProjectName.iml file.

Step 4: Create a New.iml File in Your Existing Project

Now that you have the content of the .iml file from the new project, return to your existing project where you’re experiencing the issue. Navigate to the Android directory in your existing Flutter project.

Please create a new file and name it projectname_android.iml (where project name is the name of your existing Flutter project).

Step 5: Copy and Paste the Code into the New.iml File

Once the new projectname_android.iml file is created, open it, and paste the code you copied from the new project’s .iml file. This should match the structure and configuration of the Android module for your project.

Step 6: Restart Android Studio

After saving the newly created .iml file in your existing project, restart it in Android Studio. You can also invalidate the cache by going to File > Invalidate Caches / Restart. This ensures that Android Studio reindexes the project with the updated configuration files.

That's it.

Verify the Solution

Now that you’ve completed the steps, the issue should be resolved. Here’s how you can verify:

  1. Hover your mouse over the Tools menu at the top of Android Studio.
  2. Click on Flutter from the dropdown.
  3. You should now see the option to open for editing in Android Studio.

When you select this option, Android Studio should open the Android module in a new window, allowing you to make Android-specific changes or build the AAB (Android App Bundle) file.

Why This Works

This solution for ‘Open for Editing in Android Studio’ works because the .iml file is a project configuration file that Android Studio uses to understand the structure of your Flutter project. Without it, Android Studio cannot identify the Android-specific files in the project, such as the build.gradle and AndroidManifest.xml. Creating a new .iml file and copying the content will restore the missing configuration, allowing Android Studio to recognise and work with the Android module again.

Additional Tips

  • Version Control

    If you work with version control systems like Git, include the .iml file in your repository. This will prevent issues from arising in the future when cloning or checking out different branches.

  • Android Studio Updates

    If this issue persists after these steps, ensure your Android Studio is updated to the latest version. Sometimes, bugs or glitches in older versions can also cause problems with project configuration.

  • Gradle Sync

  • If you still encounter issues after following these steps, try syncing your Gradle files again by clicking File > Sync Project with Gradle Files in Android Studio. This can help resolve any lingering configuration problems.

This easy guide will fix the 'Open for Editing in Android Studio' issue!

Fixing the “Open for Editing in Android Studio” option that is not showing in Flutter is straightforward once you understand the root cause. By creating a new Flutter project, copying the .iml file from that project, and pasting it into your existing project, you can restore the functionality and continue working without interruptions.

This blog guide will help you fix the issue and save valuable time. Feel free to comment below if you have any questions or encounter any difficulties.  

I hope it saves you time. Thanks for reading. I'll see you in the next post. Happy coding!

Title: How Can Odoo 18 Improve Manufacturing Lead Times?
Content:
Manufacturing with Odoo 18

Reducing manufacturing lead times is the integral part to stay competitive in the competitive manufacturing industry. Everyone wants to deliver high-quality products but with speed. When achieving that balance, Odoo 18 comes to the rescue like a superhero for manufacturers.

Why does it matter so much? 

Manufacturing lead time is the period between receiving an order and delivering the finished product. The faster that time is, the more products you can ship, the more revenue you generate, and the happier your customers are. 

But how do we reduce that lead time without compromising quality? 

Odoo 18 offers an advanced suite of tools that makes everything from production scheduling to inventory management incredibly efficient.

Adopting Odoo 18 for your manufacturing processes can optimise everything from production planning to supply chain management, making it one of the best solutions for improving manufacturing lead times. Ready to learn how? Let’s explore this powerful system further and see how it can streamline your operations.

What is Odoo 18 Manufacturing Lead Time, and Why Does It Matter?

Before jumping into the nitty-gritty of how Odoo 18 can improve your manufacturing lead times, let’s quickly break down what manufacturing lead time is. It’s the total time it takes for a manufacturing company to complete a product after receiving an order. That includes every production stage - from sourcing raw materials to finishing and shipping the product to the customer. And the quicker you can complete all these steps, the better it is for your business.

Reducing manufacturing lead times gives your company the flexibility to meet customer demands faster, handle fluctuating orders, and reduce costs associated with inefficiencies. That leads to improved profitability, better customer satisfaction, and enhanced competitive positioning.

Let’s discuss how Odoo 18 works wonders when reducing those lead times.

How Odoo 18 Production Scheduling Helps Optimize Lead Times

One of Odoo 18's best features is its production scheduling tools. But how does production scheduling impact manufacturing lead times? When you analyse your production schedule, you’re mapping out the most efficient way to produce and ship products, reducing unnecessary delays.

For example you're dealing with a fluctuating production load. With Odoo 18, you can quickly adjust your real-time schedules, ensuring that every machine and worker is optimally utilised. You no longer have to worry about delays or redo schedules.

How Odoo 18 Production Scheduling Can Help:

Real-time adjustments:

Imagine your crew gets an urgent order or there’s a delay from a supplier - Odoo 18 allows you to adjust the schedule instantly and ensure that production continues without a hitch.

Drag-and-drop schedule: 

Feature like drag-and-drop schedule in Odoo 18 makes adjusting production schedules quicker and more good, and it also saves time and effort.

Resource Allocation: 

Odoo 18 simplifies resource allocation and ensures uninterrupted production operations by automatically allocating workers and machines to real-time production needs, without downtime or disruptions.

By automating and updating production scheduling, Odoo 18 enables manufacturers to reduce delays and meet tight deadlines, improving overall lead time.

Odoo 18 Manufacturing Optimization: Efficiency at Every Stage

Manufacturing optimization features makes Odoo 18 stand out. Manufacturing inefficiencies often cause production delays that extend lead times; with Odoo 18, you can update workflows, identify bottlenecks, and optimise each production stage to increase efficiency and productivity.

Odoo 18 can help your company focus on speeding up product deliveries. By automating processes and eliminating repetitive manual tasks, Odoo 18 enables your employees to concentrate on what matters - the bottom line.

Here’s How Odoo 18 Helps With Manufacturing Optimization:

Work order automation:

Odoo 18 automates work order management, ensuring tasks are completed on time without manual intervention. That means you’ll never miss a step in the production process.

Task delegation:

Odoo 18's intelligent task delegation features make sure that tasks or works are assigned to the appropriate or exact people or machines at just the right moment - helping reduce downtime and accelerate manufacturing processes.

Real-time monitoring:

Odoo 18's real-time production progress tracking ensures you stay abreast of everything, enabling quick adjustments.

By optimising your manufacturing operations with Odoo 18, you can diminish the time spent dealing with inefficiencies, ultimately reducing your manufacturing lead times.

Odoo 18 Supply Chain Management: A Flow to Reduce Delays

A manufacturing process can’t run efficiently if the supply chain isn’t properly managed. Think of the supply chain as the backbone of production. Raw materials must be sourced, delivered, and stored before being used in production. Delays at any stage of the supply chain will inevitably lead to longer lead times.

Odoo 18’s supply chain management tools help you run your supply chain smoothly. They ensure that materials are always available when needed without unnecessary stockpiling or shortages.

Odoo 18 Features That Increase Supply Chain Management:

Automated procurement:

With Odoo 18, procurement processes are automated, ensuring that raw materials are ordered on time and in the correct quantity, reducing stockouts and excess inventory.

Supplier management:

Odoo 18 provides you with the tools to efficiently manage supplier relationships and track deliveries of materials to ensure timely arrival in excellent condition. 

Inventory control:

With real-time access to raw material stock levels, Odoo 18 helps prevent delays caused by untracked inventories.

When you improve your supply chain management, the production process becomes more efficient, reducing manufacturing lead times.

Odoo 18 Inventory Management: Ensuring Materials Are Always on Hand

Effective inventory management is essential for reducing manufacturing lead times. Without the right materials on hand, production delays will occur. Odoo 18’s inventory management features can help you maintain optimal stock levels, avoid stockouts, and reduce the need for manual inventory checks.

Key Inventory Features of Odoo 18:

Automated stock updates:

Odoo 18 offers automatic stock updates, providing real-time visibility into inventory levels as raw materials are consumed or received, giving you live visibility into your stock levels.

Optimised stock levels:

Our system helps ensure you consistently maintain an appropriate amount of inventory, so there are never issues of overstocking or running out mid-production.

Integrated supply chain:

Odoo 18 offers smooth integration of your supply chain, enabling you to replenish stock quickly, prevent production bottlenecks, and extend lead times more effectively.

By improving your inventory management, Odoo 18 ensures you always have the materials needed to complete production without delays, leading to faster lead times.

Odoo 18 Manufacturing Efficiency: Improving Productivity Across the Board

Finally, Odoo 18's manufacturing efficiency features make the system an innovation. The faster you can optimise every part of the manufacturing process, the quicker your lead times will become.

How Odoo 18 Maximizes Manufacturing Efficiency:

Automation of routine tasks:

 Odoo 18 automates repetitive tasks, such as production scheduling, inventory tracking, and data entry, freeing your crew to focus on high-value activities.

Cross-department collaboration:

Odoo 18's integrated design allows various departments, such as production, procurement, and inventory, to work smoothly together, ensuring an uninterrupted flow of information and faster decision-making processes.

Data-driven insights:

Odoo 18 provides powerful analytics tools that allow companies to pinpoint production bottlenecks, track production, and fine-tune strategies to increase efficiency.

By restructuring every production stage and improving overall productivity, Odoo 18 ultimately reduces manufacturing lead times.

Odoo 18 Production Planning

Odoo 18 boasts impressive enhancements for production planning, making manufacturing workflows more effective, predictable, with improved scheduling tools and automation, businesses. Businesses can modernise operations while cutting lead times and optimising resources and automation.

Key Features of Odoo 18 Production Planning:

Master Production Schedule (MPS):


Odoo 18 offers an intuitive Master Production System (MPS) that helps manufacturers plan production based on demand forecasts and replenishment rules. Companies can dynamically adjust to achieve their production goals more efficiently.

Automated Production Scheduling:


Our automated production scheduling system ensures that manufacturing orders align with available resources, workforce, and raw materials, helping prevent bottlenecks and delays that impede production.

Material Replenishment:


 Odoo 18 automatically initiates procurement or internal transfers when inventory levels fall below certain thresholds, ensuring that raw materials and components are always available when required.

Enhanced Gantt Chart & Planning Views:


With its advanced Gantt views, manufacturers can more effectively visualise work orders, deadlines, and dependencies. Zoom, drag-and-drop, and filtering functions allow greater control over production timelines.

Real-Time Collaboration & Insights:


Through integrated data sharing between departments - such as procurement, inventory and production - teams can make informed decisions that diminish the downtime and enhance coordination, while making more efficient use of resources.

Odoo 18 is the Key to Reducing Manufacturing Lead Times

Reducing manufacturing lead times isn’t just about producing faster - it’s about doing it efficiently. Odoo 18 provides the tools to update every part of your manufacturing process, from scheduling and inventory management to supply chain optimisation and efficiency upgrading. With Odoo 18, manufacturers can increase their production schedules, keep their supply chains moving smoothly, and optimise every aspect of the production cycle, leading to shorter lead times, more satisfied customers, and higher profits.

If you're looking for a comprehensive, user-friendly solution to improve your manufacturing lead times, Odoo 18 is the answer. Its combination of automation, real-time monitoring, and data-driven insights makes it the perfect tool for advancing manufacturing operations.

Title: How to Create Salary Slip for Time Sheet based-Salary Structure in the Odoo 18 Payroll Module?

In human resource management, salary slip creation is a fundamental aspect of payroll processing. The Odoo 18 Payroll Module offers a robust solution for organizations that utilize a timesheet-based salary structure. This post will lead you through the intricate process of generating a salary slip in Odoo 18, with a focus on Odoo 18 timesheet-based salary calculation. By the end of this tutorial, you will understand how to configure salary structures, generate payslips, and effectively manage payroll for hourly employees using the Odoo 18 payroll module.

What is the Odoo 18 Payroll Module?

The Odoo 18 Payroll Module is an integrated solution sketched to manage all aspects of employee compensation. This module simplifies the complexities of payroll processing, allowing businesses to handle salary calculations, deductions, and payslip generation efficiently. With its user-friendly interface and powerful features, Odoo 18 is particularly beneficial for organizations employing hourly workers, as it seamlessly integrates Odoo 18 timesheet integration with payroll.

Configuring Salary Structure in Odoo 18

Understanding Salary Structures

Before delving into the salary slip creation process, it is essential to configure a salary structure that aligns with your company's payroll policies. A salary structure defines how employee salaries are calculated, including basic pay, allowances, deductions, and bonuses.

Steps to Configure Salary Structure

  1. Navigate to Payroll Module: Access the Payroll Module in your Odoo 18 dashboard.
  1. Create a New Salary Structure: Click on the "Salary Structures" menu and select "Create." Here, you will define the various components of the salary structure.
  1. Define Salary Rules: Include salary rules in the salary structure form. These rules dictate how different components of the salary are calculated. For example, you can create rules for basic salary, overtime pay, and deductions for taxes or benefits.
  1. Assign Salary Structure to Employees: Assign the salary structure to the relevant employee contracts once it is configured. This ensures that the correct salary calculations are applied during payroll processing.

5. Save Changes: After configuring the salary structure, save your changes to implement the new settings.

How to Generate Payslip in Odoo 18

Step-by-Step Guide to Payslip Generation

Generating payslips in Odoo 18 is straightforward, especially when configuring your salary structure correctly. Here is a step-by-step guide on how to create payslips:

  1. Access the Payslip Menu: In the Payroll Module, navigate to the "Payslips" menu and select "Create."

2. Select Employee: Select the employee for whom you wish to generate the payslip. Odoo 18 allows you to filter employees based on various criteria, making it easier to locate the desired employee.

  1. Choose Payslip Period: Specify the payslip period. This is crucial for accurately reflecting the hours worked, especially for hourly employees.
  1. Add Timesheet Entries: You must enter the relevant timesheet data if the employee is paid based on timesheets. Odoo 18 supports easy integration with timesheets, allowing you to pull in hours worked directly.
  1. Validate Payslip: After entering all necessary information, validate the payslip. This step ensures that all calculations are accurate and adhere to the configured salary structure.


6. Print or Send Payslip: Once validated, you can print the payslip or email it directly to the employee.

Odoo 18 Payroll for Hourly Employees

Unique Considerations for Hourly Employees
