Understanding how to use XML effectively in Odoo can reveal limitless potential for businesses, providing an efficient and scalable solution for all your ERP needs.

Title: What is Batch Payment in Odoo 18 Accounting?
Content:
What is Batch Payment in Odoo, and How Does it Improve Financial Operations in Odoo 18

As companies manage more transactions every day, the need for reliable financial tools has grown significantly. A common question among users exploring the latest updates in Odoo is, What is batch payment in Odoo? This feature has gained attention in Odoo 18 accounting, offering a better method to handle multiple payments simultaneously. Whether you are managing supplier invoices or customer refunds, the Odoo 18 batch payment function provides a way to group and process them efficiently.

In Odoo 18 financial operations, processing each payment individually can eradicate a lot of time and increase the chances of errors. By using batch payments in Odoo accounting, companies can combine several payments into one action. This reduces repetitive work and helps keep financial records accurate. With the recent improvements in Odoo 18 accounting features, the batch payment function now supports additional filters, better control, and more compatible formats for bank exports.

The Odoo batch payment process works well with automated reconciliation tools, helping finance teams avoid manual matching. With Odoo 18 payment automation, scheduling regular batch payments and maintaining consistency in cash flow management is possible. Odoo group payments also improve communication with vendors and customers by avoiding delays caused by scattered payment schedules.

This article will explain the entire concept in detail, from understanding batch payments in Odoo accounting to how they work in Odoo 18 financial operations and why businesses are adopting Odoo 18 ERP batch payment as part of their routine payment strategy.

Understanding Odoo 18 Batch Payment in Everyday Accounting

So, what is batch payment in Odoo? It refers to combining multiple financial transactions, outgoing or incoming, into a single batch for processing. Odoo 18 accounting can be used for vendor bills, employee reimbursements, or customer refunds. Instead of going through every payment manually, you can add them to a group and take one action to process all of them.

This feature has been further enhanced with the release of the Odoo 18 ERP batch payment. Now, users can apply filters based on payment method, partner type, due date, or currency. This makes it easier to organize batches based on business needs. The straightforward process lets you control what’s paid, when, and how. As a result, many businesses now rely on batch payments in Odoo accounting for daily and monthly payment tasks.

The feature doesn’t require a complex setup. Once invoices are recorded in the system, users can direct to the batch payments area under the accounting module. There, a new batch can be created with selected payment entries. It supports different journals, making it flexible across various bank accounts and cash systems.

The Odoo Batch Payment Process from Selection to Completion

When discussing the Odoo batch payment process, it’s paramount to understand how each step works. Once you’ve identified which payments need to be grouped, you begin by creating a new batch. You select the type, either customer or vendor payment, and the payment journal. Then, you add all the relevant fees to the list.

In Odoo 18 ERP accounting features, this step has been simplified with smart filters, allowing you to locate unpaid invoices quickly. You can also filter by amount, currency, or contact. Once the batch is ready, you can validate it and create a payment file.

Odoo will sync the file directly for payment processing if your bank integration is active. If not, the file can be downloaded and uploaded manually to your bank. After the bank processes the payments, reconciliation becomes easier. 

With Odoo 18 ERP payment automation, incoming bank statements can be automatically matched with the batch, closing the loop efficiently. The Odoo batch payment process is beneficial for finance teams handling high volumes of transactions, as it simplifies tracking and reporting.

How Odoo 18 Payment Automation Supports Batch Payments

The role of automation in Odoo 18 ERP payment automation has increased significantly. With automation tools, users can prepare payment batches in advance, set them to run on specific dates, and reduce manual involvement. For example, recurring payments like salaries or supplier dues can be scheduled weekly or monthly. Once the batch is processed, Odoo automatically updates the payment status and prepares it for reconciliation.

This helps maintain cleaner records and reduces errors. Businesses using batch payments in Odoo accounting with automation tools have found the process more consistent and predictable. As a result, they can manage their cash flow with fewer disruptions.

Another advantage of Odoo 18 ERP payment automation is that it helps teams meet deadlines. Since payments can be grouped and pre-scheduled, there’s less chance of missing due dates. Combined with Odoo 18 ERP accounting features, automation ensures that payments are correctly recorded and matched accurately with invoices.

How Odoo Group Payments Improve Routine Financial Tasks

When using Odoo group payments, finance departments no longer need to address each transaction individually. Instead, multiple entries can be collected into a group and handled at once. This is useful when a business needs to pay several vendors or process many customer refunds.

Odoo 18 ERP batch payment allows customization of grouping. For example, you can group payments by bank, region, or department. This provides clarity when tracking how and where money is being sent. The grouped payments are also easier to reconcile because each batch can be matched with a specific bank statement entry.

With Odoo group payments, users can also create better records for audits. Since all payments in a batch are logged under a standard reference, it simplifies reporting and reduces confusion during financial reviews. Many companies find that using group payments in Odoo 18 financial operations leads to faster month-end closing and improved visibility.

Odoo 18 Accounting Features That Make Batch Payments More Effective

Introducing new Odoo 18 ERP accounting features has made the batch payment function more applicable across different industries. Features like multi-currency support, scheduled execution, and journal-specific payments give users more control. Companies working with international partners can now pay vendors in various currencies from a single platform.

Other new tools include better user roles and approval workflows. A batch created by one employee can be reviewed and approved by another. This layered approach ensures accuracy and avoids accidental payments. With these features, batch payments in Odoo accounting now serve operational and managerial needs.

Bank compatibility has also improved. Odoo 18 supports several formats, including SEPA, BIC, and local bank standards. This means users don’t need external software to convert payment files, and businesses can more efficiently complete the Odoo batch payment process using the built-in options.

How Batch Payments Fit into Odoo 18 Financial Operations

Odoo 18 financial operations cover all payment, reporting, reconciliation, and banking aspects. The batch payment feature ties into this structure by improving how payments are initiated and recorded. Whether supplier invoices or employee expense claims, payments can be grouped and managed through a standard interface.

By using Odoo 18 ERP batch payment, businesses can lessen the time spent on repetitive tasks and instead focus on analyzing payment trends. This is especially important in larger organizations with high payment volume. With batch records stored clearly, finance teams can generate reports faster and check for issues without reviewing individual entries.

Additionally, Odoo 18 financial operations now connect better with other modules like Purchase, Sales, and Payroll. This integration means that as invoices are generated or orders are fulfilled, payments can be grouped directly from those workflows. It eliminates the need to duplicate information or copy data between apps.

Why Batch Payment Matters in Odoo 18

To summarize, what is batch payment in Odoo? It is a method that allows users to group multiple payments for easier processing, better tracking, and more reliable reconciliation. This feature has become more advanced in Odoo 18 ERP batch payment, with added filters, automation, and support for international formats.

Using batch payments in Odoo accounting allows businesses to organize customer and vendor payments. With the help of Odoo 18 ERP payment automation, these processes require less manual effort and are completed more consistently. Odoo group payments further simplify large-scale transactions by grouping similar entries, reducing clutter in payment records.

The Odoo 18 ERP accounting features improvements support this flow, from invoice generation to payment completion. These features and the practical Odoo batch payment process contribute to a more structured and predictable financial system. As companies grow and handle more economic activities, batch payments will remain essential to Odoo 18's financial operations.

If your business needs better control over payments, reduced manual steps, and improved reporting, adopting Odoo 18 ERP batch payment is a wise decision. It aligns well with today’s financial needs and provides the tools required to manage high transaction volumes efficiently within the Odoo platform.

Title: How to Master State Management in Flutter?
Content:
Mastering State Management in Flutter: Handling API Data Efficiently (With Odoo REST API)

Why are we using state management in Flutter? Imagine creating a large-scale Flutter app with many API calls, UI screens, and components. In a usual case, these situations would be very hard to handle, but if we use state management, we can easily handle this situation. 

There are different types of state management in Flutter. You can use these state management techniques according to the situation.

These are the best options for working with api: 

Getx: Lightweight, reactive state management

Provider: Simpler apps with minimal API calls

Riverpod: Scalable and flexible state handling

Bloc (Business Logic Component): Large-scale apps with complex API interactions

This blog will focus on GetX due to its simplicity, speed, and minimal boilerplate code. Let's integrate GetX with the Odoo REST API for clean and efficient state management.

API-Driven Flutter App with GetX and Odoo

In this guide, we'll cover:

  • Setting Up Your Flutter Project with your state management  
  • Connecting Flutter to Odoo REST API
  • Managing API Data Using your state management
  • Fetching Data from Odoo Efficiently
  •  Displaying Fetched Data in your ui

Let’s dive in.

  1. Odoo uses RESTful APIs that return JSON responses. The base API URL follows this format
  2. To authenticate and fetch data, we need
    • Username (login)
    • Password (password)
  3. Create a service file api_service.dart to handle API requests
				
					class ApiService {
  final String baseUrl = "https://your-odoo-domain.com/jsonrpc";
  Future authenticate(String username, String password, String db) async {
    final response = await http.post(
      Uri.parse(baseUrl),
      headers: {"Content-Type": "application/json"},
      body: jsonEncode({
        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
        "method": "call",
        "params": {
          "service": "common",
          "method": "authenticate",
          "args": [db, username, password, {}]
        }
      }),
    );
    final data = jsonDecode(response.body);
    return data["result"]; // Returns user ID if successful
  }

3. Managing API Data Using GetX

Create a Controller to Handle API Calls.

				
					import 'package:get/get.dart';
import 'api_services.dart';
class AuthController extends GetxController {
  final ApiService _apiService = ApiService();
  var isAuthenticated = false.obs;
  var userId = 0.obs;
  Future login(String username, String password, String db) async {

4. Fetching Data from Odoo Efficiently

Update api_service.dart

				
					Future<List> getCustomers(int userId, String db) async {
    final response = await http.post(
      Uri.parse(baseUrl),
      headers: {"Content-Type": "application/json"},
      body: jsonEncode({
        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
        "method": "call",
        "params": {
          "service": "object",
          "method": "execute_kw",
          "args": [
            db,
            userId,
            "your_odoo_password",
            "res.partner",
            "search_read",
            [],
            {
              "fields": ["name", "email"]
            }
          ]
        }
      }),
    );
    final data = jsonDecode(response.body);
    return data["result"];
  }

5. Displaying Fetched Data in UI

Create a Customer Controller to manage API calls

				
					import 'package:get/get.dart';
import 'api_services.dart';
class CustomerController extends GetxController {
  final ApiService _apiService = ApiService();
  var customers = [].obs;
  Future loadCustomers(int userId, String db) async {
    var result = await _apiService.getCustomers(userId, db);
    customers.value = result;
  }
}

Update customer_screen.dart

				
					import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:get/get.dart';
import 'customer_controller.dart';
class CustomerScreen extends StatelessWidget {
  CustomerScreen({super.key});
  final CustomerController controller = Get.put(CustomerController());
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: Text("Customers")),
      body: Obx(() {

With GetX and Odoo API integration, we built a clean, efficient, and reactive state management system.

Why GetX & Odoo Are a Perfect Match

By integrating GetX with Odoo REST API, we created a reactive and efficient way to manage API data in Flutter apps. GetX simplifies logic separation, smooths UI updates, and lets you handle API interactions cleanly.

Whether you're working on login systems, data fetching, or displaying lists from Odoo, GetX offers an easy learning curve and powerful performance.

This blog can act as your starting point for building scalable and dynamic Flutter apps that interact with enterprise backends like Odoo. As your app grows, you can easily extend this structure for more complex operations, permissions, and UI behaviors.

Title: How to Manage Themes in Flutter Using Firestore?
Content:
Theme Management in Flutter with Firestore

Theme management in Flutter allows developers to create visually dynamic apps with personalized user experiences. Integrating Firestore allows themes to be managed and updated remotely, enabling real-time customization. Customizing themes in Flutter using Firestore enhances user experience by allowing them to switch between Light, Dark, and Custom themes. 

In this guide, we'll learn how to implement a multi-theme selection feature in your Flutter application and persist those preferences using Firebase Firestore. The goal is to enable smooth theme switching and remote theme management for future scalability.

Covered Topics:

  1. Creating a Theme Uploader
  2. Defining Light, Dark, and Custom Themes
  3. Implementing a Theme Controller
  4. Implementing Theme Switching in main.dart
  5. Firebase Firestore Structure for Theme Storage

Why Multi-Theme Selection?

Multi-theme selection enhances user experience by allowing them to personalize the app's appearance. It is beneficial for providing light and dark modes or custom themes based on brand colours.

Steps to Implement Multi-Theme Selection in Flutter

Add Dependencies

To get started first, install the required dependencies in pubspec.yaml:

				
					dependencies:
 flutter:
   sdk: flutter
 cupertino_icons: ^1.0.6
 firebase_core: ^3.5.0

Step 1: Creating a Theme Uploader

We need to store theme configurations in Firebase Firestore for remote management.

Structure Firebase Firestore: 

 Firestore structure for "themes" collection

				
					themes (Collection)
 ├── light (Document)
 │     ├── bodyBgColorTop: "#FFFFFF"
 │     ├── bodyBgColorBottom: "#F5F5F5"
 │     ├── appBarIconsColor: "#000000"
 │     └── avatarBgColor: "#E0E0E0"
 ├── dark (Document)
 │     ├── bodyBgColorTop: "#121212"
 │     ├── bodyBgColorBottom: "#1E1E1E"
 │     ├── appBarIconsColor: "#FFFFFF"
 │     └── avatarBgColor: "#2C2C2C"
 └── custom (Document)
       ├── bodyBgColorTop: "#015F80"
       ├── bodyBgColorBottom: "#D0E1F9"
       ├── appBarIconsColor: "#FFFFFF"
       └── avatarBgColor: "#F2F7F9"

Uploading Themes to Firebase:

				
					import 'package:cloud_firestore/cloud_firestore.dart';
class ThemeUploader {
 static Future uploadThemes() async {
   final FirebaseFirestore firestore = FirebaseFirestore.instance;
   Map<String, Map> themes = {
     "light": {
       "bodyBgColorTop": "#FFFFFF",
       "bodyBgColorBottom": "#F5F5F5",
       "appBarIconsColor": "#000000",
       "avatarBgColor": "#E0E0E0"
     },
     "dark": {
       "bodyBgColorTop": "#121212",
       "bodyBgColorBottom": "#1E1E1E",
       "appBarIconsColor": "#FFFFFF",
       "avatarBgColor": "#2C2C2C"
     },
     "custom": {
       "bodyBgColorTop": "#015F80",
       "bodyBgColorBottom": "#D0E1F9",
       "appBarIconsColor": "#FFFFFF",
       "avatarBgColor": "#F2F7F9"
     }
   };
   try {
     for (String themeName in themes.keys) {
       await firestore.collection("themes").doc(themeName).set(themes[themeName]!);
     }
     print("Themes uploaded successfully!");
   } catch (e) {
     print("Error uploading themes: $e");
   }
 }
}

Step 2: Defining Light, Dark, and Custom Themes

Define default light and dark themes using Flutter’s ThemeData. These themes will be applied directly and serve as fallbacks if Firestore fails.

				
					import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
class AppThemes {
 static final ThemeData lightTheme = ThemeData(
   brightness: Brightness.light,
   primaryColor: Colors.white,
   scaffoldBackgroundColor: Colors.white,
   appBarTheme: AppBarTheme(color: Colors.white, iconTheme: IconThemeData(color: Colors.black)),
 );
 static final ThemeData darkTheme = ThemeData(
   brightness: Brightness.dark,
   primaryColor: Colors.black,
   scaffoldBackgroundColor: Colors.black,
   appBarTheme: AppBarTheme(color: Colors.black, iconTheme: IconThemeData(color: Colors.white)),
 );
}

Step 3: Implementing Theme Controller

The ThemeController fetches and applies themes dynamically.

				
					import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:cloud_firestore/cloud_firestore.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';
import 'app_themes.dart';
class ThemeController extends ChangeNotifier {
 ThemeData _themeData = AppThemes.lightTheme;
 ThemeData get themeData => _themeData;
 Map colors = {};
 Future fetchAndApplyTheme(String themeName) async {
   try {
     final doc = await FirebaseFirestore.instance.collection('themes').doc(themeName).get();
     if (doc.exists) {
       colors = {
         "bodyBgColorTop": _hexToColor(doc.data()!["bodyBgColorTop"] ?? "#FFFFFF"),
         "bodyBgColorBottom": _hexToColor(doc.data()!["bodyBgColorBottom"] ?? "#F5F5F5"),
         "appBarIconsColor": _hexToColor(doc.data()!["appBarIconsColor"] ?? "#000000"),
         "avatarBgColor": _hexToColor(doc.data()!["avatarBgColor"] ?? "#E0E0E0"),
       };
       notifyListeners();
     }
   } catch (e) {
     print("Failed to fetch theme: $e");
   }
 }
 static Color _hexToColor(String hexColor) {
   return Color(int.parse(hexColor.replaceAll('#', '0xFF')));
 }
}

Step 4: Implementing Theme Switching in main.dart

Modify main.dart to integrate theme switching.

				
					import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';
import 'theme_controller.dart';
void main() {
 runApp(MyApp());
}
class MyApp extends StatelessWidget {
 @override
 Widget build(BuildContext context) {
   return ChangeNotifierProvider(
     create: (context) => ThemeController(),
     child: Consumer(
       builder: (context, themeController, child) {
         return MaterialApp(
           theme: themeController.themeData,
           home: ThemeSelectionScreen(),
         );
       },
     ),
   );
 }
}

Step 5: Creating Theme Selection UI

Provide a UI for users to select between Light, Dark, or Custom themes. Each button triggers the theme fetch and applies it via the ThemeController.

				
					import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';
import 'theme_controller.dart';
class ThemeSelectionScreen extends StatelessWidget {
 @override
 Widget build(BuildContext context) {
   final themeController = Provider.of(context);
   return Scaffold(
     appBar: AppBar(title: Text("Select Theme")),
     body: Center(
       child: Column(
         mainAxisAlignment: MainAxisAlignment.center,
         children: [
           _buildThemeButton(context, "Light Theme", "light"),
           _buildThemeButton(context, "Dark Theme", "dark"),
           _buildThemeButton(context, "Custom Theme", "custom"),
         ],
       ),
     ),
   );
 }
 Widget _buildThemeButton(BuildContext context, String label, String themeName) {
   return ElevatedButton(
     onPressed: () {
       Provider.of(context, listen: false).fetchAndApplyTheme(themeName);
     },
     child: Text(label),
   );
 }
}

Enhancing Flutter Apps with Dynamic Theme Management

Multi-theme support is more than just a cosmetic upgrade; it's about giving users control over their experience. This blog demonstrated how to manage themes in Flutter with Firebase Firestore. Integrating remote theme configurations and dynamic switching makes your Flutter app more user-friendly, scalable, and adaptable to branding needs. With this approach, you can easily update themes remotely without redeploying the app, opening up endless possibilities for customization and brand identity.

Implementing multi-theme support becomes efficient and manageable with the proper structure, like Firestore, to hold theme data and provide for state management. So, let your users choose how they want their app to look and feel!

Title: How to Automate Task Assignment in Odoo Using AI Prompts?
Content:
AI Prompts by Odoo is raising the bar for intelligent business automation! In a recent demo by CEO Fabien Pinckaers, we got a sneak peek at how AI can now assign tasks automatically based on a simple prompt and user context.

This powerful new feature allows you to build intelligent workflows where Odoo reads the task name and assigns it to the most appropriate team member - just like a smart assistant would. No more manual assignment or guessing who should handle what.

Let’s explore how this works and how you can use it in your business to save time, reduce errors, and simplify your task management process.

Why AI Task Assignment Matters

In any organization, assigning the right task to the right person is crucial. But as projects grow and team sizes increase, manual assignment becomes inefficient and error-prone.

Let’s say you’re managing a project in Odoo with tasks like:

  • "Create invoice report"
  • "Review CRM lead simulation"
  • "Handle accounting integration"

Each task should go to a specialist:

  • Mitchell handles accounting.
  • Mark is the CRM/sales expert.

Traditionally, a project manager or team lead would need to assign each task manually. That’s not scalable - and it's exactly the kind of repetitive work that AI can automate.

With Odoo's AI task assignment, this step is now handled automatically, intelligently, and instantly.

Step-by-Step: AI Task Assignment

Here’s a quick walkthrough of how you can set up AI-based task assignment in Odoo using automated actions and custom AI prompts

1: Create a New Automated Action

  • Go to Settings → Automated Actions
  • Click Create and choose your model (e.g., Tasks)

2: Choose the Trigger

Set the trigger for when the AI should assign the task:

  • Example: When a task is created

3: Select “Update Record with AI”

  • Choose “Update Record” as the action type
  • Select the Assignee field
  • Use the task name/description as input context

4: Write the AI Prompts

Here’s the magic:

“Assign this task to the user best suited based on the task name. Mitchell is the product owner for accounting. Mark is the expert in sales and CRM.”

AI in Action

Once saved, when tasks are created or updated, the AI evaluates the task name and makes a smart decision.

Here’s how it worked in the demo: 

Task Name

Assigned User

Mitchell

CRM lead simulation

Mark

Sales pipeline forecast

Mark

Accounting integration sync

Mitchell

As you can see, the AI intelligently matched each task with the team member who’s best equipped to handle it - based purely on a simple prompt and the task name.

Community Buzz

The community is excited about this capability:

“Just yesterday, we had a request for CRM auto-assignment based on team roles — this is perfect!” – Lorcan Camps

“Could this even generate quotes if a lead mentions pricing interest?” – Fabio Tielen

The answer is: Yes! With this AI framework, generating quotes, prioritizing tasks, or routing leads based on context is now within reach.

Real-World Use Cases

This functionality opens the door to smarter, faster workflows across departments:

  • Customer Support:

    Auto-assign tickets based on topic or urgency

  • Sales:

    Route leads to the right salesperson based on region or interest

  • Product Teams:

    Assign dev tasks based on tags or tech stack

  • Marketing:

    Distribute content tasks by channel (e.g., social, blog, email)

With just a well-crafted AI prompts and a few minutes of setup, your team can unlock hours of saved time every week.

Getting Started with AI Automation in Odoo

Ready to try it out?

  1. Make sure AI features are enabled in your Odoo instance
  2. Create a simple project with example tasks
  3. Set up an automated action as described above
  4. Test with different prompts and refine as needed

This system isn’t just smart - it’s adaptable. You can continue to improve accuracy by expanding your prompt with more context about your team members and roles.

So why not let AI Prompts handle the busywork?

Odoo’s AI-powered task assignment is an advancement for teams looking to scale efficiently. It reduces manual workload, ensures the right person gets the right task, and opens up new possibilities for smarter business automation.

Whether you manage sales, projects, support, or product development, this feature empowers your team to work faster and more effectively.

So why not let AI handle the busywork? Start building your intelligent workflows in Odoo today and see the difference it can make.

Title: How to Set Up Odoo 18 Development Environment Using PyCharm in Ubuntu 22.04
Content:
Odoo 18 is the latest iteration of this powerful business management software, widely appreciated for its comprehensive features and its ability to simplify business operations. Using Python 3.10+ for the backend, Odoo 18 uses PostgreSQL as its database system and JavaScript for the frontend interface.

Ubuntu 22.04, a reliable Long-Term Support (LTS) release, provides a stable platform with ongoing updates and security patches for five years. The release also includes periodic updates to the Linux kernel and graphics drivers, ensuring excellent system performance and compatibility.

This guide will walk you through installing Odoo using the PyCharm IDE on Ubuntu 20.04.

Before setting up PyCharm, it's essential to install a few key libraries and packages necessary for running Odoo. We’ll also cover the installation and configuration of PostgreSQL, setting up Python environments, and managing dependencies.

Let’s explore these initial steps and ensure your system is ready for Odoo development.

Step 1: Download and Install PyCharm IDE

In this step, we will install the PyCharm Community Edition. Before proceeding, make sure your system meets the necessary requirements to ensure the IDE's smooth operation.

The following are the minimum system requirements for installing PyCharm on your computer:

System Requirements:

Requirement

Minimum

Recommended

RAM

4 GB of available RAM

8 GB of total system RAM

CPU

Any modern processor

Multi-core processor (PyCharm utilises multithreading, so that more cores will improve performance)

Disk Space

3.5 GB of free space

SSD with at least 5 GB of available space

Monitor Resolution

1024×768

1920×1080

Operating System

Officially supported 64-bit versions:

Latest 64-bit versions of Windows, macOS, or Linux (e.g., Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL)

 

- Windows 10 1809 or later

 
 

- Windows Server 2019 or later

 
 

- macOS 11.0 or later

 
 

- Any Linux distribution supporting Gnome, KDE, or Unity DE

 
 

Note: PyCharm is not supported on Linux distributions without GLIBC 2.27 or later, and pre-release versions are not supported.

 

To install PyCharm, you can download the Debian installation file from the following URL:

Downloading PyCharm Community Edition

By using the command line you can install PyCharm. To do so, open the Terminal (press Ctrl + Alt + T to launch it) and execute the following commands:

				
					sudo apt-get update 
sudo apt-get upgrade
sudo snap install pycharm-community --classic

Step 2: Installing Python 3.12

The latest Python version (3.12) is unavailable in the default Ubuntu repositories. To install this, you'll need to add an alternative repository. The dead snakes repository on Launchpad provides several Python versions, including 3.12.

  • To add the deadsnakes repository, use the given commands:
				
					sudo add-apt-repository ppa:deadsnakes/ppa 
sudo apt-get update
  • You can check the updated list of available Python packages by running the following command:
				
					apt list | grep python3.12
  • To install Python 3.12, run the following command:
				
					sudo apt-get install python3.12
  •  Use the following command to install packages for Python 3:
				
					sudo apt-get install python3.12-dev build-essential libjpeg-dev libpq-dev libjpeg8-dev libxml2-dev libssl-dev libffi-dev libmysqlclient-dev libxslt1-dev zlib1g-dev libsasl2-dev libldap2-dev liblcms2-dev

Step 3: Install the Web Dependencies

Next, you'll need to install the essential web dependencies.

				
					sudo apt-get install -y npm
sudo ln -s /usr/bin/nodejs/usr/bin/node 
sudo npm install -g less less-plugin-clean-css 
sudo apt-get install -y node-less

Step 4: Install Wkhtmltopdf

Wkhtmltopdf is required for generating Odoo reports. You can install it by running or using the below mentioned command:

				
					-> sudo wgethttps://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/releases/download/0.12.5/wkhtmltox_0.12.5-1.bionic_amd64.deb 
-> sudo dpkg -i wkhtmltox_0.12.5-1.bionic_amd64.deb

Step 5: Install PostgreSQL

Now, let's proceed with installing PostgreSQL:

				
					Sudo apt install postgresql postgresql-client

Step 6: Configure a Database User Role for Odoo Databases

Follow instructions to create a new database user. As you'll need this during creating the file for configuration you have to Set the password for this user. Remember to save the password for future reference.

				
					sudo su - postgres
createuser --createdb --username postgres --no-createrole --no-superuser --pwprompt odoo18

Next, assign superuser privileges to the newly created user.

				
					psql
ALTER USER odoo18 WITH SUPERUSER;

Finally, exit both the psql session and the Postgres user account.

				
					q
exit

Step 7: Obtain Odoo 18 Source Code

You can download the Odoo 18 Community source code directly from Odoo's GitHub repository or clone it using Git. To begin, first install Git by running the following command:

				
					sudo apt-get install git.

To use the Odoo code into an 'odoo18' directory within your directory, use the following command.

				
					git clone https://www.github.com/odoo/odoo --depth 1 --branch 18.0 --single-branch odoo18

Step 8: Open the Odoo Project in PyCharm

Open PyCharm Community Edition and navigate to the ‘Odoo18’ directory. When the project opens, you may encounter a dialog box prompting you to create a virtual environment. Please cancel this prompt since we will set up the virtual environment via the terminal.

To open the terminal, click the icon below or use the shortcut Alt+F12.

Next, execute the following commands to create a virtual environment using Python 3.12.

				
					curl -sS https://bootstrap.pypa.io/get-pip.py | python3.12
sudo apt install python3.12-venv
python3.12 -m venv your_venv_name

After off then on the terminal, you'll see that your virtual environment is now active. The terminal will show an indicator with the name of virtual environment, as shown below:

If your virtual environment doesn't activate automatically, you can manually activate it using the following command:

				
					source your_venv_name/bin/activate.

Step 9: Install Required Python Packages

Odoo relies on several Python packages specified in the requirements file in the ‘odoo18’ directory. For the installation of these packages, run the following command in the terminal:

				
					pip install -r requirements.txt

If no errors appear, you can verify that all dependencies from the requirements.txt file have been installed by running the following command:

				
					pip list

If you encounter any errors, open the requirements.txt file and install each dependency one by one using the following command:

				
					pip install requirement_name

In most cases, if packages are listed twice, you only need to install one. If one installation fails, it's typically not a problem.

Also, if any prerequisites defined with sys_platform as 'win32' fail to install, you can safely skip them.

If you encounter errors while the installation of the package "psycopg2==2.9.2; sys_platform != 'win32' and python_version <= '3.10' or psycopg2==2.9.5; python_version > '3.10' or sys_platform == 'win32'," you can use the given command to install an alternative package instead.

				
					pip install psycopg2-binary

Step 10: Create the odoo.conf File in the odoo18 Directory

To create the configuration file, right-click the Odoo18 directory, then select New -> File -> odoo.conf.

Once the odoo conf file is created, add the following code block. Be sure to update the db_password field with the password you set for the Odoo database user in the previous step.

				
					[options]
admin_passwd = admin
db_host = localhost
db_port = 5432
db_user = odoo18
db_password = your_password
addons_path = /home/user/odoo18/addons
xmlrpc_port = 8018

Also, update the addons_path value with the path to the Odoo18 addons directory. To find this path, navigate to the addons directory and press Ctrl + Shift + C to copy the current directory path. Then, paste this path into the addons_path field.

If you create a directory for your custom modules, add its path to the addons_path, separating each path with commas.

Example:

				
					addons_path = /home/user/odoo/addons, /home/user/odoo/custom_addons

Step 11: Add Python Interpreter

To set up a Python interpreter, go to Settings -> Project: odoo18 -> Python Interpreter.

When you open the specified window, no further action is required if the interpreter (Python 3.12 from the virtual environment of odoo18) is already configured. If not, select the Add Interpreter option and follow the steps below.

Step 12: Configure the Project in PyCharm

Click Edit Configurations under the Current File option to configure the project settings.

When the dialog box shown or appears, click the "+" button and select "Python" from the list.

Next, fill the fields as shown in the image below.

Name:

You can assign any name to this configuration.

Python Interpreter:

This part should automatically display the project's Python interpreter, as it was set up in the previous step.

Script-Path:

Select the odoo-bin file located in the directory of odoo18.

Parameters:

Add any necessary parameters here to run the script. The c parameter is required, and you may also need to include the configuration file as a parameter.

Working Directory:

To the project's current working directory specify the path.

Step 13: Test Run Odoo 18

The Odoo setup is now complete. To test it, click the below button to launch the project.

After this You can now test your setup by going to localhost:8018 in your browser. If all your configurations are correct, the browser will open the Odoo database management page, as shown below.

Following these steps, you can successfully set up an Odoo 18 development environment using PyCharm on Ubuntu 22.04. This environment allows you to explore the latest features of Odoo, develop custom modules, and manage business processes efficiently.

If you want guidance on installing Odoo 18 on a production server, 

check out the blog: How to Install Odoo 18 on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS Server.

Title: How to Lock Confirmed Purchase Orders in Odoo 18?
Content:
Why Lock Confirmed Purchase Orders in Odoo 18?

Imagine you’ve just confirmed a purchase order in Odoo 18, and everything seems perfect. But wait; what if someone accidentally (or intentionally) changes the order? Chaos occurs. Deliveries get delayed, budgets spiral out of control, and your procurement process becomes a nightmare. It sounds like a plot twist you didn’t sign up for, right? 

Well, here’s the good news: Odoo 18 has a superhero feature that can save the day, locking confirmed purchase orders. That’s right! With just a few clicks, you can lock down your purchase orders, ensuring no one can mess with them once they’re confirmed; no more accidental edits, no more unauthorized changes, and no more procurement fuss. 

But wait, there’s more! Locking purchase orders isn’t just about avoiding disasters; it’s about taking control of your Odoo 18 purchase order management like a pro. Imagine efficient workflows, defensible security, and audit trails so clean they’d make a detective jealous. Delighted yet? 

In this guide, we’re diving deep into how to lock confirmed purchase orders in Odoo 18, why it’s a game-changer for your business, and how it can transform your Odoo 18 procurement process. Whether you’re a seasoned Odoo user or just getting started, this is your ultimate playbook for mastering Odoo 18 purchase order locking and opening the full potential of your procurement system. 

So, buckle up and get ready to discover how to restrict purchase order edits in Odoo 18, boost your Odoo 18 purchase order security, and make your procurement process smoother than ever. Trust us, by the end of this, you’ll wonder how you ever managed without it. Let’s dive in!

Title: How Relational Fields & Widgets Unlock Odoo Visual Potential?
Content:
Welcome back to our Unlocking Odoo Visual Potential series!

In Part 1, we explored field decorations and non-relational fields - the foundation of any great Odoo interface. Now in Part 2, we’re diving deeper into Odoo’s rich framework with a spotlight on Relational Fields and Widgets - two key elements that help transform your interface into a dynamic and user-friendly environment.

Let’s explore how you can connect data smoothly and enhance interactivity in your Odoo views, giving users a smooth, visually appealing experience that’s both practical and powerful..

Relational Fields: Connecting Your Odoo visual potential to the World

Relational fields are the cornerstones of data relationships in Odoo. They allow you to connect records across different models, enabling a truly integrated and smart system. Think of relational fields as the glue that binds your application’s data into meaningful structures.

Whether you’re referencing one record, many, or setting predefined choices, Odoo offers flexible options to cover all use cases.

1. Selections & Choices:

Let users choose from a predefined list of options. Add a placeholder to guide users when no selection has been made.

Selection (selection):

Pick from a list! Use a placeholder to give users a hint when nothing is selected. It's like a friendly nudge.

Supported field types: selection

				
					  <field name="tax_id" widget="selection" placeholder="Select a tax"/>

Field type: selection

Use case: Static choices like tax types, categories, or priorities.

Radio (radio):

Choose one! Display selections as radio buttons. Use horizontal to line them up neatly. Clean and simple.

Supported field types: selection, many2one

				
					<field name="tax_id" widget="radio" options="{Select a tax}"/>

Field types: selection, many2one

Use case: Ideal for reducing clicks and clearly showing all options.

Badge Selection (selection_badge):

Select with badges! Turn selection options into stylish rectangular badges. Visual and user-friendly.

Supported field types: selection, many2one 

				
					 <field name="status" widget="selection_badge" />

Field types: selection, many2one

Use case: Perfect for status indicators or color-coded categories.

2. Many2one Relationships:

The many2one field connects a record to a single entry in another model. Think of it like assigning a customer to a sales order.

Many2one (many2one):

This is the most common relational field. Customize its behavior using attributes like:

  • can_create: Allow creating a new related record.
  • can_write: Allow editing it.
  • options: quick_create, no_create, no_create_edit, etc.
				
					Supported field types: many2one 
Attributes: can_create, can_write 
Options: quick_create, no_create, no_quick_create, no_create_edit, create_name_field, always_reload, no_open

Many2one Avatar Variants

Odoo lets you personalize the view further with avatar widgets:

  • many2one_avatar
  • many2one_avatar_user
  • many2one_avatar_employee

These widgets display user or employee images and allow for a more personalized interface, including clickable icons that open chat windows.

Many2one Avatar Employee (many2one_avatar_employee):

Display avatars for related records. Use user - and employee-specific avatars for a personal touch. Click user/employee avatars to open a chat.

Supported field types: many2one 

3. Many2many Relationships:

When you need to associate multiple records with one entry, the many2many field is your go-to. Odoo offers different widgets to make these relationships intuitive and visually pleasing.

Many2many (many2many):

Link multiple records! Use attributes like mode and domain to customize the display and filter data. It's like creating a linked list.

  • Supported field types: many2many 
  • Attributes: mode, domain 
  • Options: create_text, link, unlink

Many2many Tags (many2many_tags):

Tag it! Display many2many fields as tags. Use color_field to add color based on values. Enable tag editing with edit_tags. Organize your data visually.

  • Supported field types: many2many 
  • Options: create, color_field, no_edit_color, edit_tags 
				
					 <field name="tags" widget="many2many_tags" options="{'color_field': 'color', 'edit_tags': true}" />

Many2many Tags - Form View (form.many2many_tags), Many2many Tags - Kanban View (kanban.many2many_tags):

Tags tailored for views! Specializations of many2many_tags for form and kanban views. Edit colors on forms, and use them effectively in kanban.

Supported field types: many2many 

4. One2many Relationships:

One2many (one2many):

List related records! Display data in sub-lists or kanban views. Control creation and deletion with create and delete options. Customize the 'Add' button text with create_text.

Supported field types: one2many 

Options: create, delete, create_text

				
					 <field name="items" options="{'create_text': 'Add Item'}" />

Widgets: Visual Enhancements

Ribbon (web_ribbon):

  • Add a styled ribbon at the top-right of your form to show important status labels like “Archived,” “Draft,” or “Paid.”
  • Attributes: title, tooltip, bg-class 
				
					 <widget name="web_ribbon" title="Archived" bg_color="text-bg-danger"/>

Attributes: title, bg_color, tooltip

Use case: Instant visual status indicators in form views.

Week Days (week_days):

Select days easily! Display checkboxes for each day of the week. Perfect for scheduling or availability.

				
					<widget name="week_days" />

Take Your Odoo visual potential Experience to the Another Level

Congratulations! You now have a better understanding of  how to use Relational Fields and Widgets to build smarter, cleaner, and more intuitive interfaces in Odoo visual potential.

By mastering these tools, you can:

  • Build smooth relationships between records
  • Guide users visually with  badges, tags, and ribbons
  • Simplify user input and selection
  • Customize the experience with  avatars, colors, and placeholders

This concludes our two-part series on unlocking Odoo's visual potential. If you missed Part 1, we highly recommend checking it out to learn about field decorations, non-relational fields, and more foundational UI enhancements.

Title: How Odoo is Changing the Way We Build Custom Modules?
Content:
Odoo introduces exciting features for developers, making creating, customizing, and extending Odoo modules more efficient and robust. With its dynamic and modular framework, Odoo is changing the landscape of custom module development. Developers can now access enhanced tools, APIs, and best practices that simplify and accelerate growth. This evolution makes building scalable, maintainable, and future-ready business solutions easier. Let’s dive deeper into the key updates that are influencing the development of custom modules.

1. Best Practices for Custom Modules Development in Odoo

Odoo development is known for its flexibility, but new versions bring new ways to optimize and streamline the process. In Odoo, best practices for custom module development remain similar to previous versions, but with added improvements.

Here are a few best practices to follow when building custom modules in Odoo:

A. Plan Your Module Structure Carefully

Before you dive into coding, it's essential to plan the structure of your custom module. Odoo provides a clearer separation of concerns, making it easier to structure your module for maintainability. Keep in mind the following:

Models: Separate business logic and data management.       

Views: Define UI elements cleanly, utilizing the new XML syntax improvements.        

Security: Utilize access control lists (ACLs) and record rules to ensure proper user permissions.

B. Use Inheritance Wisely

Odoo allows module developers to extend existing functionality using inheritance. Odoo

enhances this with improved inheritance mechanisms:

Model Inheritance: Extending models with the class inheritance pattern will enable you to create more flexible and reusable modules.        

View Inheritance: Customize existing views by inheriting and modifying specific parts rather than recreating entire views.

C. Avoid Direct Modifications of Core Code

Directly modifying core Odoo code can lead to compatibility issues when upgrading to newer versions. Instead:

Use Inheritance and Extension: Extend core models or views using models. Use model inheritance rather than modifying base code.        

Leverage Addons: Ensure your custom module is built as an addon, which allows for greater flexibility and ease of upgrade.

2. New ORM Enhancements in Odoo

The Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) layer in Odoo handles the interaction between the Odoo framework and the database. With Odoo, the ORM has seen improvements that make module customization smoother and more efficient. Let’s look at these enhancements:

A. Advanced Querying Capabilities

Odoo improves how developers interact with the database, enabling advanced queries to be executed more easily and efficiently. Key enhancements include:

Improved Search Functionality: The search() method now supports more complex querying, reducing the need for raw SQL queries in custom modules. 

Optimized Filtering: Developers can now use more intuitive ways of filtering records, making retrieving data from the database easier. 

Pre-fetching of Related Data: Odoo introduces the ability to efficiently fetch related data (e.g., using many-to-one and one-to-many relationships), improving performance and reducing the number of queries executed.

B. Write and Create Performance Improvements

Odoo introduces optimized ORM methods to handle large datasets with better performance. When creating or updating records, the write() and create() methods are now much more efficient, significantly improving the performance of your custom modules, especially when handling bulk operations.

Batch Operations: When performing bulk operations, Odoo allows better batch handling to avoid loading too much data into memory at once.       

Concurrency Handling: Improved mechanisms for managing concurrent writes and avoiding race conditions in high-volume systems.

C. Enhanced Many2one/One2many Relationships

The ORM layer has been enhanced to handle relational fields such as Many2one, One2many, and Many2many more intuitively. These enhancements make it easier for developers to work with related data in custom modules:
Automatic Validation: Odoo automatically handles validation for these relationships, reducing the boilerplate code developers need to write.
Faster Updates: Updates to these related fields are now handled more efficiently, reducing the time it takes to update and save associated records.

3. Simplifying the Development Process with the New API Features

The Odoo API has always been powerful, but Odoo has several new additions and improvements that simplify the development process for custom modules. These features provide a more consistent developer experience and help speed up the development lifecycle.

A. More Efficient Fields and Data Types

Odoo introduces new field types and enhancements to existing ones, making it easier to work with complex data types in your custom modules:

New Data Types: Custom fields can now handle more advanced data types (e.g., Jsonb, Datetime, Date, Integer) that allow you to store and manipulate data more easily.         

Improved Default Values: The API now supports more flexible and dynamic default values for fields, reducing the need for manual overrides.

B. New Python Decorators and Methods

Odoo introduces new Python decorators that make coding easier and more efficient:

@api.model_create_multi: This decorator allows you to create multiple records in a single operation, significantly improving performance.        

@api.depends: Improved dependency tracking ensures that computed fields are recalculated more efficiently, reducing the need for manual triggers and improving the system's overall speed.

C. Improvements in Asynchronous Processing

With Odoo, asynchronous tasks have become more accessible, enabling developers to handle long-running operations (e.g., external API calls, bulk data processing) more effectively.

Async Methods: Methods can now be executed asynchronously, reducing the impact of long-running operations on the central system and improving user experience.         

Background Jobs: The new background job framework allows developers to schedule tasks, enabling better scalability for custom modules.

D. API Enhancements for External Integrations

Odoo has made integrating with external systems easier. Key enhancements in the API allow developers to:

  • Use RESTful APIs to connect to third-party services more easily.
  • More robust support for integrations with payment gateways, shipping services, and external CRMs.      
  • Built-in support for API rate limiting, error handling, and response parsing.

4. The Impact of Odoo Changes on Module Customization

With the improvements in ORM, the API, and best practices for module development, Odoo makes it much easier to develop high-performance, scalable, and maintainable custom modules. Some specific impacts include:

Faster Development: With more intuitive field management, better inheritance support, and optimized ORM, developers can do more in less time.        

Improved Performance: Bulk operations, smarter data management, and better query handling lead to faster modules that can more efficiently manage large datasets and complex relationships.       

Easier Maintenance: Odoo's clear structure, enhanced API, and consistent inheritance mechanisms make custom modules easier to maintain and upgrade.

Facilitating Developers with Smarter Custom Module Development in Odoo

Odoo is a game-changer for developers who are building custom modules. The new ORM features, API enhancements, and better development practices make creating powerful, high-performing modules simpler and more efficient. By leveraging these new tools and practices, you can ensure your Odoo modules are future-proof, scalable, and maintainable, allowing businesses to maximise their Odoo investment.
