Title: What Are the Best Tools and Tips for Debugging Odoo?
Content:
Debugging Odoo is a skill that every Odoo developer, beginner or seasoned, needs in their toolkit. Whether you're working on a minor customization or a complex enterprise-level solution, the ability to quickly pinpoint and resolve issues can dramatically improve the quality and reliability of your implementation.

Odoo is a powerful yet intricate platform. Thanks to its modular architecture, issues can surface in many different places, Python server logic, QWeb templates, PostgreSQL database queries, front-end JavaScript, or third-party API integrations. Without the right strategy, even a small bug can turn into hours of frustration.

In this blog, we’ll explore practical techniques, essential tools, and best practices that make debugging Odoo faster, more effective, and far less stressful.

1. Understanding the Odoo Debugging Modes

Debugging Odoo provides several built-in debug modes to help you analyze what's happening behind the scenes.

Normal Debug Mode

You can quickly enable debug mode by adding ?debug=1 at the end of your Odoo URL. This gives you access to technical fields, view architecture, and developer tools directly from the user interface.

Example:

				
					 https://yourdomain.com/web?debug=1

Developer Mode (with Assets)

This mode loads JavaScript and CSS in unminified form, which is extremely helpful when you're working on front-end customizations or fixing QWeb template rendering issues.

Activate it from the UI:

				
					Settings → Activate Developer Mode

Developer Mode (with Assets and Tests)

This is the most comprehensive mode and is best used when you need to debug automated tests or deep front-end behaviors. It includes both unminified assets and testing tools.

You can switch between debug modes using the Developer Tools dropdown in the top-right corner of Odoo once any debug mode is active.

2. Using Odoo Logs Effectively

Logs are your first line of defence when something goes wrong.

Where to Find Them

Standard Installation:

				
					/var/log/odoo/odoo-server.log

Docker Setup: Use this to view logs inside the container.

				
					docker logs <container_name>

Log Levels and How to Use Them

Odoo uses standard Python log levels:

				
					 INFO, DEBUG, WARNING, ERROR, and CRITICAL.

In development, setting the log level to DEBUG offers detailed insights:

				
					log_level = debug

Update this in your odoo.conf file to capture more granular information, especially useful when tracing custom module issues or tracking database interactions.

3. Key Tools for Debugging Odoo

Several built-in and external tools can speed up the debugging process.

Browser Developer Tools

The browser’s Developer Tools (available in Chrome, Firefox, and Edge) help you inspect:

  • HTML elements and QWeb output
  • JavaScript console errors
  • Network requests and API payloads

This is your go-to tool for front-end issues.

Odoo Shell (Odoo REPL):

Accessing the server shell with:

				
					odoo shell or python3 odoo-bin shell

PostgreSQL Logs:

Enable query logging in PostgreSQL to understand slow or complex queries affecting performance. It's beneficial when the ORM hides the underlying SQL's real complexity.

PDB (Python Debugger):

Insert breakpoints in your code using:

				
					 import pdb; pdb.set_trace()

This halts execution and lets you step through your Python code to inspect variables and trace the problem.

4. Debugging Common Odoo Issues

Interpreting Python Tracebacks

When Debugging Odoo, a server error typically includes a stack trace. Learn to read this traceback line by line. The last few lines often indicate the function or model where the error originated, allowing you to quickly pinpoint the issue.

QWeb Template Errors

Issues with XML templates can break entire views. In Developer Mode, inspect views via the UI and use browser tools to trace broken templates or incorrectly referenced fields.

Access Rights and Record Rules

Misconfigured access control is a common problem. Use Developer Mode to:

  • Check record rules and user roles
  • View the effective permissions on models.
  • Simulate user access with different roles.

External API Integration Failures

For APIs, the key to debugging odoo is isolation. Use tools like:

  • Postman: Test your endpoints independently of Odoo.
  • cURL: Lightweight CLI option for sending HTTP requests.

These help you separate the issue between Odoo code and the external service.

5. Recommended Debugging Addons and Modules

These community or built-in modules simplify your debugging workflow:

  • web_debug: Easily toggle debug modes.
  • auth_signup_disable: Quickly disable signup in staging environments for security.
  • Odoo Studio: Use Odoo Studio to inspect models and fields visually.

These add-ons are handy during the development and testing phases.

6. Advanced Debugging Tips

When you’re dealing with performance bottlenecks or hard-to-replicate bugs, advanced methods can help.

Profiling Odoo Performance (using cProfile, Pyflame, or odoo-profiler).

These tools help identify slow functions or modules dragging down your performance.

Monitoring RPC calls

  • (Especially in web apps and mobile).

For Debugging Odoo web clients or mobile apps, keep an eye on RPC (Remote Procedure Call) behavior. Use network tools to see:

  • Request/response cycles
  • Payload sizes
  • Error messages

Testing with Odoo Unit Tests

  • (writing and running tests to catch bugs early).

Odoo supports automated testing. Write tests using:

				
					from odoo.tests.common import TransactionCase

Tests can catch logic errors early and provide confidence during code changes or upgrades.

7. Best Practices for Faster Debugging

Always Use a Staging Environment

Never debug directly on production. Create a clone of your production instance for testing. This protects data and prevents disruptions to real users.

Use Version Control Effectively

Work on feature branches in Git. This keeps experiments isolated and helps you roll back if needed.

Log and Document Known Issues

Maintain a shared log of recurring problems and their resolutions. It saves time in the long run, especially for teams.

Adopt Incremental Deployment

Deploy features in smaller chunks. It makes identifying the root cause of new bugs much easier.

Ready to Debug Smarter, Not Harder?

Debugging Odoo doesn't have to be a guessing game. With the right mindset, tools, and habits, you can make it an efficient, even enjoyable part of your development workflow.

Start by enabling Developer Mode and reading logs to understand what’s happening under the hood. Use pdb and Odoo Shell for deep-dive investigations, while browser tools help you dissect front-end behavior. For performance tuning, profiling tools are your best bet, and when it comes to integrations, Postman or cURL can provide much-needed visibility.

Above all, make sure your debugging Odoo is safe, reproducible, and well-documented. The more you debug, the better you become - not just at fixing issues, but at preventing them.

Title: How to Integrate an External API with Odoo Using XML-RPC?
Content:
Integrating External API with Odoo Using XML-RPC

Integrating an External API with Odoo can open strong automation and simplify business operations. Whether you want to connect third-party apps, sync data in real time, or enhance your Odoo system’s capabilities, one of the most commonly used methods for integrating with Odoo externally is through XML-RPC, which offers a reliable way to do it. 

Odoo provides a robust API that allows external applications to interact with its database. In this guide, we’ll break down the process of integrating an external API with Odoo using XML-RPC step by step. You’ll learn to establish connections, send requests, manage responses smoothly and perform CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations using XML-RPC, even if you’re new to API integration. Ready to simplify your workflows and boost productivity? Let’s get started!

Step-by-Step Guide to Integrating an External API with Odoo Using XML-RPC

Integrating an external API with Odoo using XML-RPC covers essential steps like authentication, data retrieval, and record management. Follow the clear instructions to automate your Odoo ERP workflows and enhance system functionality.

1. Setting Up XML-RPC in Python

To interact with Odoo via XML-RPC, we use Python’s xmlrpc.client module. First, ensure you have Python installed and then import the required module:

				
					import xmlrpc.client as xmlrpclib

2. Authentication with Odoo Server

Before we can interact with any Odoo model, we need to authenticate with the Odoo server using the common endpoint.

				
					url_common = 'http://localhost:8019/xmlrpc/2/common'
db = ‘Your_db_name’
username = 'admin'
pwd = 'admin'
common = xmlrpclib.ServerProxy(url_common)
uid = common.authenticate(db, username, pwd, {})
if uid:
    print("Authentication success")
else:
    print("Authentication failed")
  • url_common: The URL for the Odoo XML-RPC common endpoint.
  • db: The database name.
  • username & pwd: Credentials for authentication.
  • uid: The unique identifier for the authenticated user. If uid is returned, authentication is successful.

3. Accessing Models and Understanding execute_kw

After authentication, we need to interact with Odoo ERP models through the object endpoint.

				
					url_object = 'http://localhost:8019/xmlrpc/2/object'
model = xmlrpclib.ServerProxy(url_object)
  • url_object: The URL for the Odoo XML-RPC object endpoint, used to interact with the models.
  • model: The proxy object that lets us perform operations on Odoo models.

Understanding execute_kw

The execute_kw method is used to call model methods remotely.

				
					Variable_name=model.execute_kw(db, uid, pwd, model_name, method_name, args, kwargs)
  • db: Database name.
  • uid: User ID obtained after authentication.
  • pwd: User password.
  • model_name: Name of the model you want to interact with (e.g., 'res.partner').
  • method_name: Method you want to call (e.g., 'search', 'read', 'create', 'write', 'unlink').
  • args: Positional arguments (usually a list).
  • kwargs: Keyword arguments (optional dictionary).

4. Searching for Records in res.partner

Once authenticated, we can interact with Odoo models. To search for records in the res.partner model, we use the search method.

				
					res_partner = model.execute_kw(db, uid, pwd, 'res.partner', 'search', [[]], {'offset': 1, 'limit': 1})
print("Search Result:", res_partner)
  • The search method retrieves records based on conditions.
  • The empty list [] means no filter is applied.
  • offset: 1 skips the first record.
  • limit: 1 returns only one record.

5. Reading Data from res.partner

To fetch details of the retrieved record(s), we use the read method.

				
					res_partner_read = model.execute_kw(db, uid, pwd, 'res.partner', 'read', [res_partner], {'fields': ['name', 'company_type', 'street', 'street2', 'city', 'vat']})
print("Read Data:", res_partner_read)
  • The read method fetches the details of the records retrieved in the search query.
  • The fields parameter specifies the fields to retrieve.

6. Counting Records Using search_count

To count the number of records in a model, use search_count.

				
					res_partner_count = model.execute_kw(db, uid, pwd, 'res.partner', 'search_count', [[['is_company', '=', True]]], {})
print("Total Companies:", res_partner_count)
  • search_count returns the total count of records matching the given criteria.
  • The filter [['is_company', '=', True]] ensures we count only companies.

7. Creating a New Record Using create

You can create a new record in Odoo using the create method.

				
					partner_id = model.execute_kw(db, uid, pwd, 'res.partner', 'create', [{
    'name': 'New Partner',
    'company_type': 'company',
    'city': 'New York'
}])
print("Created Partner ID:", partner_id)

The create method inserts a new record into the model.

8. Updating an Existing Record Using write

To update an existing record, use the write method.

				
					update_partner = model.execute_kw(db, uid, pwd, 'res.partner', 'write', [[partner_id], {'city': 'Los Angeles'}])
print("Update Status:", update_partner)

The write method updates the fields of existing records.

9. Deleting a Record Using unlink

To delete a record, use the unlink method.

				
					delete_partner = model.execute_kw(db, uid, pwd, 'res.partner', 'unlink', [[partner_id]])
print("Delete Status:", delete_partner)

The unlink method removes the record(s) with the given IDs.

Your Odoo Integration Journey Starts Here

Integrating external applications with Odoo using XML-RPC is an effective way to automate operations and synchronize data. We have covered authentication, searching, reading, counting, creating, updating, and deleting records using Python’s XML-RPC library.

With these techniques, you can extend and customize Odoo’s functionality according to your business needs, enabling more intelligent workflows, efficient data management, and smooth system connectivity.

Title: How to Create a Custom Module in Odoo 18? A Step-by-Step Guide
Content:
The open-source ERP framework Odoo 18 enables businesses to optimize their operations through the integration of  sales and inventory management and accounting and CRM applications and additional features. Odoo gives developers access to a  flexible architecture and extensive development tools which enable efficient creation of custom business applications. Learning to develop custom module in odoo 18  stands as a basic requirement for anyone who wants to become proficient in Odoo development regardless of their experience  level. This guide provides a complete walkthrough of creating a module structure and writing Python and XML files before  showing you how to install and test your module in a local Odoo 18 environment. The final  result will enable you to create business applications that fulfill your particular requirements.

Step 1: Create the Module Folder

Go to your Odoo custom addons directory and create a new folder for your module:

				
					cd ~/odoo18/custom_addons
mkdir my_custom_module

Step 2: Create the Basic Files

Inside your new module, you need to create the following files and folders:

				
					my_custom_module/
├── __init__.py
├── __manifest__.py
├── models/
│   └── __init__.py
│   └── my_model.py
├── views/
│   └── my_model_views.xml
├── security/
│   └── ir.model.access.csv

				
			
				
					File: __manifest__.py
{
	'name': 'My Custom Module',
	'version': '1.0',
	'summary': 'Simple module to demonstrate Odoo development',
	'author': 'Your Name',
	'depends': ['base'],
	'data': [
    	'security/ir.model.access.csv',
    	'views/my_model_views.xml',
	],
	'installable': True,
	'application': True,
}

Step 3: Define Your Model 

				
					File: models/__init__.py
from . import my_model
file: models/my_model.py
from odoo import models, fields
class MyModel(models.Model):
	_name = 'my.model'
	_description = 'My Custom Model'
	name = fields.Char(string='Name', required=True)
	description = fields.Text(string='Description')

Step 4: Create Views for the Model 

				
					File: views/my_model_views.xml
<odoo>
	<!-- Form View -->
	<record id="view_form_my_model" model="ir.ui.view">
    	<field name="name">my.model.form</field>
    	<field name="model">my.model</field>
    	<field name="arch" type="xml">
        	<form string="My Model">
            	<sheet>
                	<group>
                    	<field name="name"/>
                    	<field name="description"/>
                	</group>
            	</sheet>
        	</form>
    	</field>
	</record>
	<!-- List View -->
	<record id="view_tree_my_model" model="ir.ui.view">
    	<field name="name">my.model.list</field>
    	<field name="model">my.model</field>
    	<field name="arch" type="xml">
        	<list>
            	<field name="name"/>
        	</list>
    	</field>
	</record>
	<!-- Action -->
	<record id="action_my_model" model="ir.actions.act_window">
    	<field name="name">My Models</field>
    	<field name="res_model">my.model</field>
    	<field name="view_mode">list,form</field>
	</record>
	<!-- Menu -->
	<menuitem id="menu_my_custom_module_root" name="My Module"/>
	<menuitem id="menu_my_model" name="My Models" parent="menu_my_custom_module_root" action="action_my_model"/>
</odoo>

Step 5: Set Up Access Rights 

				
					File: security/ir.model.access.csv
id,name,model_id:id,group_id:id,perm_read,perm_write,perm_create,perm_unlink
access_my_model_user,access_my_model_user,model_my_model,,1,1,1,1

Step 6: Initialize Your Module 

				
					File: __init__.py
from . import models

Step 7: Install the Module in Odoo

  1. Start your Odoo 18 server:
				
					./odoo-bin -d your_database_name -u all
  1.   Go to Apps in the Odoo UI.

  2.   Click the Update Apps List (activate developer mode).

  3.   Search for your module (e.g., "My Custom Module").

  4.   Click Install.

 Result:

You should now see a new menu item in your Odoo backend called “My Module”, where you can create and view records using your custom model.

Building a Strong Foundation with Custom Module in odoo 18

Every developer working with Odoo 18 needs to learn how to create custom modules because this skill  enables them to develop tailored solutions that match specific business needs through Odoo's modular framework. The ability  to design business-specific solutions emerges from Odoo's modular structure through which you can extend its functionality.  After learning about models, views, menus and access control you can begin developing adaptable applications that smoothly connect  with other Odoo modules. The mastery of these fundamental concepts enables developers to access more complex features and  extensive customization capabilities.

Title: How Can You Optimize Gradle for Faster Android Builds in Flutter?
Content:
If you’re Android builds in Flutter, you’ve likely run into slow build times—especially during complete builds like APKs or app bundles. While Flutter’s hot reload is excellent for speeding up development, Gradle still handles the heavy lifting under the hood, and its performance directly affects your overall build speed.

In this guide, we’ll show you how to optimize your Gradle configuration to significantly reduce build times, whether you’re developing locally or preparing for a production release.

Why Gradle Configuration Matters

Gradle is the underlying build system for all Android builds, including those in Flutter. While Flutter streamlines much of the Android development process, the build performance relies heavily on Gradle configuration. Optimizing these settings can lead to significant improvements in overall efficiency.

 

Properly configuring Gradle can:

  •  Reduce build times for both debug and release modes
  •  Maximize usage of system resources during compilation
  •  Leverage caching to reuse previously compiled outputs
  •  Enhance performance in CI/CD pipelines, accelerating deployments

Best Gradle Settings for Faster Builds

Below are the most effective Gradle configurations to apply for better build performance.

1. Enable Gradle Daemon

 

The daemon keeps Gradle running in the background, avoiding expensive startup costs.

				
					android/gradle.properties:
properties
org.gradle.daemon=true
Enabled by default in newer versions, but good to confirm.

2. Use Gradle Build Caching

 

Caches outputs of tasks so that Gradle doesn’t re-run them unnecessarily.

properties

				
					org.gradle.caching=true

3. Parallel Build Execution

 

Allows Gradle to run tasks in parallel where possible.

				
					properties
org.gradle.parallel=true

4. Configure JVM Heap Size

 

Increase available memory for Gradle if you're running out or want smoother builds.

				
					properties
org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx4096m -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8
You can also add -XX:+UseParallelGC for improved garbage collection:
properties
org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx4096m -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -XX:+UseParallelGC

5. Disable Unused Transforms

 

If you’re not using Jetifier or legacy libraries:

				
					In gradle.properties:
properties
android.enableJetifier=false
 Only do this if your dependencies don’t require Jetifier!

6. Use Stable Gradle and Plugin Versions

 

Using stable versions prevents unnecessary resolution or compatibility overhead.

				
					In android/build.gradle:
groovy
classpath 'com.android.tools.build:gradle:7.4.2'
In gradle-wrapper.properties:
properties
CopyEdit
distributionUrl=https://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-7.5-all.zip
Make sure these versions are compatible.

7. Enable Only Required ABIs

 

If you're not targeting multiple architectures, limit ABI filters to reduce build time and size.

				
					groovy

Title: How to Manage Sales & Stock Movements in Odoo v18?
Content:
The sales and stock movements in Odoo v18 operate as a single integrated system. Odoo  automatically controls outgoing stock when sales occur and handles incoming stock through purchase orders and other inventory management processes.  The real-time synchronization system prevents manual errors while maintaining precise inventory levels. This guide demonstrates the process of  making sales and delivering products while showing you how to monitor both incoming and outgoing stock movements to maintain operational  efficiency between sales and inventory management.

Step 1: Create a Sales Order

To start, you need to create a Sales Order for the product(s) being sold.

  1. Go to: Sales → Orders → Quotations

  2. Click Create to start a new sales order.

  3. Select the Customer who is making the purchase.

  4. Add the Products the customer is purchasing:

    • Choose the product from the list and enter the quantity.

    • Odoo will automatically pull the price and any discounts if applicable.

  5. Once all products are added, click Confirm Sale to convert the quotation into a confirmed sales order.

This will automatically generate the Stock Move for the outgoing products, moving them from your inventory to the customer.

Step 2: Deliver the Products (Outgoing Stock)

Once the sales order is confirmed, you’ll need to process the delivery of the products.

  1. After confirming the sales order, go to the Sales Order screen.

  2. Click on Deliver to begin the delivery process.

  3. You’ll be directed to the Inventory → Operations → Transfers section, where the system has already generated the stock move.

  4. In the stock move, you’ll see the Source Location (your warehouse) and the Destination Location (the customer’s address or another location).

      5. Validate the transfer to confirm the products are being delivered, which will automatically update the stock levels.

Step 3: Check Outgoing Stock Movements

After delivering the products, it’s important to track the outgoing stock movements.

  1. Go to: Inventory → Reporting → Products Moves

  2. You’ll see all the product movements, including outgoing deliveries, with details such as:

    • Product name

    • Quantity moved

    • Source and Destination locations

    • Date and time of movement

You can filter these movements by date, product, or location to get a detailed view of your outgoing stock.

Step 4: Check Incoming Stock Movements

If you need to check the incoming stock movements, you can do so through purchase orders or inventory adjustments.

  1. Go to: Inventory → Reporting → Products Moves

  2. Filter the report by the incoming stock to view products that have been received, such as from suppliers.

You’ll see:

  • Product names

  • Quantity received

  • Source locations (e.g., supplier warehouses)

  • Date of receipt

This will help you track how much stock has been replenished and where it came from.

Step 5: Check Stock Levels After Sales

To see how your sales have affected stock levels, you can check the current stock levels.

  1. Go to: Inventory → Products
  2. Find your product and check the current stock listed in the Inventory column.

You’ll also see the Stocked Quantity for each product, which is updated automatically when sales or purchases are processed.

Seamless Sales and Inventory Management with Odoo v18

Odoo v18 provides an efficient system to handle sales operations and monitor stock movements between incoming and  outgoing stock. Odoo will automatically manage stock movements after you confirm a sales order. Odoo provides  tools to monitor stock levels and track movements which help maintain current inventory information.

By following this guide,  you’ll be able to:

> Create and confirm sales orders.

> Deliver products to customers and manage outgoing  stock.

> Check the incoming and outgoing stock movements.

> Monitor your stock levels.

This will help you stay  on top of your inventory and make informed decisions based on real-time data.

Content:

If you’re managing finances for a growing business, you know how quickly credit card transactions can pile up. Keeping those records clean, organized, and properly reconciled is essential. By the end of this article, you'll know how to configure credit cards in Odoo-18, avoid common errors and ensure that your Odoo-18 accounting credit card processes are audit-ready.

Step 1: Odoo 18 Credit Card Journal Setup - Lay the Foundation Right

The first and most important step in configuring credit cards in Odoo-18 is setting up the credit card journal. This allows your financial entries to be correctly routed and tracked.

How to Do Odoo 18 Credit Card Journal Setup:

  • Guide to Accounting >
  • Configuration > Journals.
  • Click the New button.
  • Fill in:
  1. Journal Name: Corporate Credit Card
  2. Type: Credit Card
  3. Short Code: CCARD
  4. Default Debit Account: Credit Card Expenses
  5. Default Credit Account: Credit Card Liability
  6. Select the Currency
  7. Click Save

Moving towards the dashboard, you can also check the journal you created.

Without a correct Odoo-18 credit card journal setup, your transactions might get mixed up, causing reporting inaccuracies. This configuration is the cornerstone of your Odoo-18 accounting credit card workflow.

Step 2: Handling Odoo 18 Credit Card Payments - Track Your Expenses Easily

Once the journal is created, it’s time to process Odoo-18 credit card payments. These payments may include purchases from vendors, office expenses, or subscriptions.

Steps to Record Odoo 18 Credit Card Payments:

  • Open Accounting > Customer > Payment
  • Create a bill you want to pay.
  • Click Register Payment.

Title: How to Use @api Decorators in Odoo 18 ORM?
Content:
The ORM system of Odoo has become more advanced with Odoo 18 while maintaining its powerful  capabilities. Developers who create custom modules for Odoo need to understand @api decorators because they create efficient  and future-proof code that is also clean. The decorators function as essential building blocks to create dynamic models  which operate according to your exact requirements.

This article demonstrates effective and useful methods to implement core @api  decorators including @api.depends, @api.onchange, @api.model and  @api.constrains.

The Odoo framework depends on each of these decorators for its operation. The correct implementation of  these decorators enables automated processes and user-triggered changes and data validation and additional functionality. The article demonstrates  practical applications of these decorators through real-world examples which enhance system performance and simplify logic while making maintenance easier.

 The effective use of these decorators will provide Odoo 18 developers with a substantial advantage when they  create custom applications or enhance existing ones.

1. @api.depends – Computed Fields That Stay in Sync

Use Case: Auto-calculate order total when line items change.

from odoo import models, fields, api

				
					class SaleOrder(models.Model):
   _inherit = 'sale.order'
   total_qty = fields.Float(compute='_compute_total_qty', store=True)
   @api.depends('order_line.product_uom_qty')
   def _compute_total_qty(self):
       for order in self:
           order.total_qty = sum(order.order_line.mapped('product_uom_qty'))

Tip: Always use store=True for performance if it's queried often.

2. @api.onchange – Real-Time Field Logic in Forms

Use Case: Auto-fill product price when product is selected.

class SaleOrderLine(models.Model):

				
					_inherit = 'sale.order.line'
   @api.onchange('product_id')
   def _onchange_product_id_set_price(self):
       if self.product_id:
           self.price_unit = self.product_id.lst_price

Pro Tip: Use onchange for UI-only logic. It won’t be triggered in create() or write().

3. @api.model – Model-level Operations & Custom Create Hooks

Use Case: Auto-generate a name using a sequence.

class CreditLimit(models.Model):

				
					 _name = 'credit.limit'
   name = fields.Char(string="Name", required=True, copy=False, readonly=True, default='New')
   @api.model_create_multi
   def create(self, vals_list):
       for vals in vals_list:
           if not vals.get('name') or vals['name'] == 'New':
               vals['name'] = self.env['ir.sequence'].next_by_code('credit.limit.seq') or 'CL000'
       return super().create(vals_list)

Note: @api.model_create_multi is a newer, optimized version for bulk create.

4. @api.constrains – Validation Logic That Saves Your Data

Use Case: Prevent saving if quantity is negative.

from odoo.exceptions import ValidationError

				
					class CreditLimit(models.Model):
   _name = 'credit.limit'
   quantity = fields.Float(string="Quantity")
   @api.constrains('quantity')
   def _check_quantity_positive(self):
       for record in self:
           if record.quantity < 0:
               raise ValidationError("Quantity must be positive.")

Tip: Triggers only on record save (not on form change).

5. @api.ondelete – Custom Cleanup Logic

Use Case: Prevent deletion if the record is confirmed.

				
					from odoo import models, _
from odoo.exceptions import UserError
from odoo.api import ondelete
class AccountAccount(models.Model):
   _inherit = 'account.account'
   @ondelete(at_uninstall=False)
   def _unlink_except_contains_journal_items(self):
       for account in self:
           journal_item_exists = self.env['account.move.line'].search_count(
               [('account_id', '=', account.id)], limit=1
           )
           if journal_item_exists:
               raise UserError(_('You cannot delete the account "%s" because it contains journal items.') % account.display_name)

6. @api.depends_context – React to Context Changes

@api.depends_context('lang')

				
					def _compute_description(self):
   for record in self:
       record.description = self.with_context(lang=self.env.context.get('lang'))._get_translation()

Useful for context-sensitive fields (e.g., multi-language descriptions).

Bonus Tips

  • Avoid mixing @api.onchange and @api.depends on the same method.

  • Use @api.model_create_multi for performance when overriding create().

  • Avoid triggering expensive logic inside @api.depends (like DB search calls).

  • Always consider @api.depends_context when context values are vital.

Final Thoughts: Why Mastering @api Decorators in Odoo 18 Matters

The mastery of @api decorators in Odoo 18 serves as a technical ability and strategic benefit  for Odoo developers who want to create high-quality scalable applications. The correct application of  @api.depends, @api.onchange, @api.model and @api.constrains decorators together with full  understanding enables numerous benefits which elevate your coding practice to the next level.

Your first achievement will be writing  code that is both clean and logical. The @api decorator enables automatic execution of proper actions at suitable  times thus preventing your models from becoming cluttered with manual checks and updates. The resulting codebases become  more intuitive and easier to read while maintaining better organization.

  • Product (e.g., Chair Floor Protection)
  • Quantity and Weight (e.g., 1 unit = 1 kg)
  • Under Shipping, select your preferred delivery method (e.g., UPS).

Confirm quotation and validate delivery.

Step 5: Generate Invoice Including Shipping Cost

  • Go to the order → Click Create Invoice.
  • Choose Regular Invoice.
  • You’ll see the shipping cost added as a separate line item.
  • Confirm the invoice – it will move to posted state.

Step 6: Invoice Actual Shipping Cost (Optional Method)

  • To invoice real shipping cost:
  • Create a delivery method (e.g., Standard Delivery) with unit price set to zero.
  • Create a new sales order with this delivery method.
  • Validate delivery.
  • When generating invoice, manually update shipping cost while invoice is in draft.

  • Confirm invoice – real cost will be reflected.

Link Shipping Fees to Inventory Operations

Odoo 18 inventory shipping charges are closely tied to your stock movements. When a sales order is confirmed, it generates a delivery order. Upon validation, inventory is updated, and shipping costs are finalized.

 

This connection ensures:

  • Real-time stock deduction when items are shipped
  • Visibility of shipping charges linked to inventory operations
  • Delivery costs appear in accounting alongside sales items.

This integration benefits businesses with warehousing and logistics departments, especially when shipping costs impact inventory valuation.

Automate the Odoo Shipping Cost Invoice Process

The Odoo shipping cost invoice process eliminates the need to calculate or input delivery charges manually.

What the automation covers:

  • Adds delivery cost to order at the click of a button
  • Reflects the charge in the invoice automatically
  • Syncs with real-time carrier APIs if enabled
  • Applies correct tax and accounting rules to deliver products

This workflow reduces billing errors, shortens order-to-invoice time, and ensures no shipping fees are missed during invoicing.

Best Practices for Odoo Shipping Cost Management

Efficient Odoo shipping cost management depends on innovative practices that keep data accurate and customers satisfied.

Use these tips to improve operations:

  • Create separate products for different shipping types (e.g. Standard, Express)
  • Assign default delivery methods by country or zone.
  • Set minimum order value for free shipping promotions.
  • Include tax settings for shipping lines when required.
  • Regularly update carrier rates to match actual costs.

When properly configured, the shipping charge process becomes seamless, and invoicing syncs with your logistics.

Handling Shipping Fee Invoicing with Precision

With Odoo invoicing shipping fees, every delivery line is added as a billable item, ensuring your business never misses out on recovering freight costs.

Whether you charge exact courier rates or apply a flat fee, the shipping cost line item appears clearly on the invoice. This reduces confusion, helps with audits, and improves customer communication.

Tax and accounting settings for delivery products can also be configured, making sure those charges are reported correctly in financial statements.

Setting Up Accurate Delivery Cost Logic

Your Odoo 18 delivery cost setup should reflect how your business ships goods. One-time configuration saves hours of effort later.

Checklist for setup:

  • Enable delivery methods in both Inventory and Sales apps.
  • Create delivery products with default income accounts.
  • Connect shipping carriers via API if needed.
  • Set price computation (fixed, rules, or API)
  • Activate invoicing of delivery costs.

Zone-based rules and dynamic tax setups may also be required for companies with international shipping.

Why Netilligence is the Ideal Partner

Proper setup of Odoo 18 shipping cost invoicing isn’t just about software—it’s about business logic. Netilligence works with businesses of all sizes to deliver customized Odoo solutions that reflect your operations.

What we deliver:

  • Carrier integrations
  • Custom delivery rules
  • Smart invoicing automation
  • Inventory-to-invoice syncing
  • Post-implementation support

When shipping and invoicing are aligned, your business runs better. With Netilligence, every delivery is tracked, billed, and profitable.

Final Thoughts

Managing Odoo 18 shipping cost invoicing the right way means:

  • Fewer missed charges
  • Faster invoice processing
  • Accurate financial reporting
  • Smoother logistics and customer service

By configuring delivery methods, automating cost applications, and linking everything to your inventory, shipping becomes a strength—not a complication.

Title: How to Create SMS Marketing Campaigns in Odoo 18?
Content:
Businesses operating in today's digital environment require marketing strategies that deliver direct personalized messages to reach their  customers effectively. The Odoo 18 SMS marketing platform enables businesses to connect with their audience through automated  personalized message campaigns. Odoo 18 SMS marketing provides an easy solution for startups and enterprises to create  SMS campaigns through its rich features and seamless integration capabilities.

Odoo provides both pre-designed SMS templates and  sophisticated campaign management tools which simplify the process of launching and tracking successful marketing campaigns. The following blog provides  an actionable tutorial about Odoo SMS marketing that helps businesses use Odoo 18 SMS features to improve  customer engagement and return on investment.

Why Use Odoo 18 SMS Marketing?

 The Odoo 18 SMS marketing module functions as a transformative business tool which enables organizations to establish  trust while delivering updates and achieving conversion goals. The following list explains why businesses select this tool as their  preferred choice.

> Real-time Communication: Messages are delivered and read within minutes.

> Automation Capabilities: Save  time with automated SMS workflows.

> Analytics and Tracking: Measure open rates, delivery success, and responses.

>  Integration: Connects easily with CRM, Sales, and Marketing modules.

Through Odoo 18 SMS  marketing businesses can establish a quick and personalized communication system that surpasses traditional email and notification methods to reach  their customers.

Getting Started – How to Create SMS Campaign Odoo 18 Style

 To create SMS campaign Odoo 18, follow these quick steps:

Step 1: Access SMS Marketing Module

  • Open the Odoo Dashboard.
  • Use the search bar to find "SMS Marketing".
  • The dashboard displays existing SMS campaigns by default.
  • A filter "My SMS Marketing" is already applied.
  • You can remove or add more filters based on your need.

Step 2: Create a New SMS

  • Click on the "Create" or "New" button to start a new campaign.
  • This will open a blank form for a new SMS.

Step 3: Fill in SMS Details

  • Title: Enter a subject line for your SMS (e.g., Black Friday SMS Coupon).
  • Recipient Options:
    • Choose from a Mailing List (predefined groups like Interested Customers, Newsletter Subscribers, etc.).
    • Or remove the mailing list and choose other recipient types like:
      • Application Contact
      • Event Registration
      • Journal Entry
      • Leads, etc.

Step 4: Add/Modify Filters (Optional)

  • You can modify the recipient filter.
  • Click on "Modify Filter".
  • Add new rules such as Country, and select a specific country (e.g., United States).
  • This helps to target a specific audience.

Step 5: Enter SMS Content

  • Type your SMS message content (e.g., "Get 40% OFF on all sales!").
  • Options available within the message field:
      • Insert Fields (e.g., product links, website links).
      • Emojis (e.g., 🔥, 🎉).
      • SMS Pricing Icon to preview credit cost.

Step 6: Review SMS Pricing

  • SMS pricing depends on the number of recipients and country.
  • You must purchase SMS credits in Odoo to send messages.

Step 7: Save and Send

  • Click on "Save".
  • The SMS is now ready to be scheduled or sent immediately.

Key Odoo 18 SMS Marketing Features You Must Know

 Odoo 18 SMS marketing delivers its power through its modern and advanced features. The new version  includes the following key features that distinguish it from others.

> Contact List Segmentation enables you to deliver messages  to users who match specific behavioral or geographic or demographic criteria.

> The Odoo SMS templates library provides users  with numerous pre-built templates that help speed up their campaign development process.

> The system allows users to send  SMS messages to thousands of recipients through a single click.

> The system enables users to establish automated messaging protocols  which trigger when users perform specific actions.

> The dashboard provides real-time analytics that enable users to monitor open  rates and delivery status among other metrics.

The Odoo 18 SMS marketing features provide both efficiency and  impact in your campaigns.

Customizing Odoo SMS Campaign Settings for Better Results

Every campaign requires personalization. Odoo gives you full control through its advanced Odoo SMS campaign  settings:

> A/B Testing: Try different messages to test what works.

> Send Time Optimization: Deliver messages  at times when users are most active.

> Dynamic Fields: Automatically personalize messages with customer name, order  number, etc.

> Opt-Out Options: Include an unsubscribe link for better compliance.

Fine-tuning your  Odoo SMS campaign settings ensures better deliverability, user satisfaction, and engagement.

Designing Impactful Messages with Odoo SMS Templates

Content matters. Odoo SMS templates enable you to create precise and clear effective messages quickly through the  following features:

> The system includes pre-designed templates for reminders and promotions and order confirmations and other communication  types.

> The system allows users to insert personalization tokens which include [Customer Name] and [Order  ID].

> The system allows users to save custom templates for later use.

Odoo SMS templates help  users avoid mistakes while saving time and maintaining consistent branding throughout their marketing campaigns.

Understanding Odoo 18 SMS Marketing Pricing

 Odoo provides SMS services through a credit-based pricing system. Odoo 18 SMS marketing pricing  operates as follows:

> SMS Credits: You purchase SMS credits based on your needs. Prices vary by country.

>  Usage-Based Deduction: The number of credits used for each SMS depends on the recipient's location  and message length.

> You can track your usage and billing history through your account.

Odoo’s pricing  structure works for both small and large-scale campaigns while remaining competitive across different regions.

Take Your Business Communication to the Next Level

 Odoo 18 SMS marketing functions as a powerful tool which transforms your customer communication methods. The  platform unifies speed with clarity and automation and personalization into a single system. Your Odoo SMS  campaigns will reach and convert audiences through Odoo 18 SMS features combined with optimized campaign settings and effective  template usage.

The comprehensive Odoo SMS marketing tutorial combined with your ability to create SMS campaign Odoo  18 has prepared you to launch successful campaigns with assurance. Odoo 18 SMS marketing delivers your  messages with maximum clarity during both urgent promotional campaigns and essential notification operations.

Title: How to Create & Manage Alerts in Odoo 18 Referrals
Content:
Odoo 18 referrals alerts bring a powerful edge to HR operations by enabling teams to stay updated, informed, and proactive in the recruitment process. If you're using the Odoo 18 referral module, then understanding how to configure, create, and manage alerts is vital. Whether you're aiming to boost internal referrals or streamline applicant tracking, Odoo 18 referrals alerts ensure that HR professionals and employees never miss a crucial update. With Odoo referrals alert configuration, it's easier than ever to set automated notifications that align with your hiring strategy.

When you dive into Odoo 18 to create referral alerts, you unlock new efficiencies in candidate engagement, employee participation, and hiring speed. These alerts can be configured for activities such as new referral submissions, application status changes, and reward point updates. By integrating these smart alerts into the Odoo referrals dashboard notifications, you ensure that all stakeholders—from HR managers to employees—remain aligned and informed.

This blog will guide you step-by-step through the configuration process of Odoo 18 HR alerts and how to maximize the utility of Odoo referrals management alerts. With the growing adoption of the Odoo 18 referral app alerts, mastering this functionality becomes a strategic asset for HR success.

Why Odoo 18 Referrals Alerts Are Essential for HR Success

Real-Time Updates Empower HR Teams

 The Odoo 18 referrals alerts system is designed to provide real-time notifications so that HR professionals  do not miss any important referral updates. These alerts help automate communication from referral approvals to incentive claims.

 Key Benefits:

> Instant updates on new referrals.

> Automated alerts for application status.

> Enhanced collaboration between  HR and employees.

Odoo 18 referral app alerts help you eliminate manual follow-ups and streamline candidate  pipeline tracking.

How to Create and Manage Alerts in the Odoo 18 Referrals App

Step 1: Open the Referrals App

  • Log into your Odoo dashboard.

  • Navigate to the Referrals app from the main menu.

Step 2: Locate the Alerts Section

  • On the dashboard, alerts are displayed as messages at the top.

  • These alerts can notify employees about job openings, reward updates, or other key announcements.

Note: Only users with administrator access to the Recruitment app can create and manage alerts.

Step 3: Go to Configuration > Alerts

  • Click on Configuration in the top menu.

  • Select Alerts to access the list of current alerts.

  • Here, you’ll see details like:

    • Alert text

    • Start date

    • End date

Step 4: Create a New Alert

  • Click the “New” button in the top-left corner to create a new alert.

  • Fill out the form with the following information:

    • Start date: When the alert will be visible on the dashboard.

    • End date: When the alert will stop appearing.

Example: You can set the alert to be active for two weeks starting today.

Step 5: Select Company (for Multi-Company Databases)

  • If you’re using Odoo with multiple companies, you can assign the alert to a specific company.

  • Use the dropdown menu to select the intended company.

Step 6: Add Your Alert Message

  • Enter the alert text you want to appear at the top of the Referrals dashboard.

     

Example message:
“We are hiring a Marketing Specialist! Know someone creative? Refer them today!”

Step 7: Choose the Alert Action (What Happens When Clicked)

  • Select how the alert should behave when clicked:

     

    1. Not Clickable – Just displays the message.

                2. Go to All Jobs – Directs users to the full list of job openings.

               3. Specific Web Page – Takes users to a specific URL (e.g., the job listing page).

If choosing the third option, a URL field will appear. Paste the relevant link (e.g., the Marketing Specialist job page).

Step 8: Notify Users via Email

  • To ensure employees don’t miss the alert, click “Send Mail” at the top.

     

  • All users are selected by default. You can remove any recipients as needed.

     

  • The subject and email body are pre-filled and include a link to the referrals dashboard.

     

Click “Send” once everything is reviewed.

Step 9: View the Alert on the Dashboard

  • Return to the Referrals Dashboard.
  • Your new alert should now be visible at the top for all users.

Step 10: User Dismissal of Alerts

  • Employees can dismiss the alert by clicking the "X" on the side.
  • Once dismissed, it won’t reappear—even if the user opens the app in a new session.

Step 11: User Interaction with Alerts

  • When users click the alert, they’ll be directed to the linked job posting or page.
  • They can then view and share the job details to refer candidates.

How to Manage Packages in Odoo 18 Inventory

Step 1: Manage Packages Odoo Inventory

  • Open the Inventory app.
  • Go to Configuration > Settings.
  • Find the Packages option.
  • Check the box to enable it.
  • Click Save.

Step 2: View or Create Packages

  • Go to Products > Packages (now visible after enabling).
  • Here you can:
    • View all packages.
    • See which products they contain.
    • Create a new package.

Step 3: Create or Edit a Package

  • Click New to add a new package.
  • Fill in details:

    • Package Reference
    • Package Type
    • Current Location
    • Creation Date
  • To create a custom package type, define:

    • Name
    • Size (dimensions)
    • Empty weight
    • Maximum weight

  • You can:
    • Assign barcodes for scanning.
    • Set storage category capacity.

Step 4: Create Package Types (Alternative Way)

  • Navigate to Configuration > Package Types.
  • Add package types from there as well.

Step 5: Add Products to Packages via Transfers

  • Go to Operations > Deliveries.
  • Open a delivery in "Ready" State.
  • Click the menu icon on a product line or use the "Move" smart button.
  • Under Destination Package:
    • Select an existing package or create a new one by typing a name.
  • Enter the number of units to include in the package.
  • To split quantities:

    • Click Add a line, select the product, assign another destination package, and enter the remaining quantity.

Step 6: Use "Put in Pack" Option (Optional)

  • This button groups all products in the transfer into one single package.
  • To split quantities:

Step 6: Use "Put in Pack" Option (Optional)

    • List of products.
    • Their quantities.

  • Optional Login: Combines the best of both worlds.

Proper configuration of the Odoo website checkout setup improves user experience and aligns with your business model.

The Odoo customer portal is where users access their orders, invoices, deliveries, support tickets, and more. With Odoo 18 customer portal customization, you can reflect your brand identity and add features specific to your customer needs.

  • Access controls and user rights
  • Customer communication tools

When integrated correctly, the Odoo 18 customer portal boosts trust and reduces support requests.

Enabling Odoo Guest Checkout for Frictionless Experience

While account-based checkouts offer detailed analytics, not all customers want to register. Enabling Odoo guest checkout supports faster transactions and caters to casual or first-time buyers.

Benefits of Guest Checkout:

  • Reduced cart abandonment
  • Quicker buying process
  • Ideal for flash sales or promotions

Steps to Configure Checkout Policy in Odoo 8 Website Module

Step: 1. Access the Website Settings

  • Go to the Website module.
  • Navigate to Configuration > Settings.

Step: 2. Choose a Checkout Policy

Under the Shop Checkout Process section, choose one of the following options:

  • Optional (Allows guests to checkout and later register via order confirmation email).
  • Disabled (Buy as a guest only – no registration or login required).
  • Mandatory (Sign in required – guest checkout is not allowed).

Testing Each Checkout Policy:

Step: 3 OPTIONAL Checkout Policy

  1. Set policy to Optional and Save changes.

2. Log out from the admin account.

3. Go to Shop, select an item, and add to cart.

4. Proceed to checkout without signing in.

5. Enter customer details (name, phone, email, etc.).

6. Choose a payment method and complete the payment.

7. Result: Checkout completed without account login, with an option to register later.

Step: 4 DISABLED Checkout Policy (Guest Checkout Only)

  1. Set policy to Disabled (Buy as Guest) and Save changes.

2. Again, log out from admin.

3. Visit the Shop, add an item to the cart, and go to checkout.

4. Enter the required guest information and proceed with payment.

5. Result: Only guest checkout is allowed, no login or registration required.

Step: 5 MANDATORY Checkout Policy (No Guest Checkout)

  1. Set policy to Mandatory (No Guest Checkout) and Save.

2. Create or select a customer (e.g., Doris) in Odoo backend.

3. Provide all required B2B details: address, country, state, city, zip code, tax (VAT) number.

4. Click on Grant Portal Access to send login credentials to the customer.

5. Assign an email and set a password manually (optional).

6. Log out as admin and sign in as the customer.

7. Proceed to the Shop, add a product, and go through checkout.

8. Result: Checkout only allowed after sign-in, enforcing mandatory login.

Advanced Odoo Website Checkout Configuration Tips

Fine-tuning your Odoo website checkout configuration ensures a smoother experience from cart to confirmation.

Advanced Configurations:

  • Add shipping methods and conditions.
  • Enable discount codes
  • Automate tax calculation
  • Integrate with payment gateways (Stripe, PayPal, etc.)

Combining a firm Odoo 18 checkout policy with a robust configuration ensures you minimize customer drop-offs and operational delays.

Odoo 18 Portal Access Management for B2B & Enterprise Control

If you manage B2B clients, Odoo 18 portal access management becomes essential for controlling who sees what, assigning roles, and managing user permissions.

Features Include:

  • Role-based access to documents
  • Manual or automatic user approval
  • Secure data sharing
  • Multi-user access within one client account

You can control portal access via:

Settings > Users & Companies > Portal Users

Combining access control with a well-structured Odoo 18 customer portal will streamline transparency and security.

Title: How to Manage Group Payments in Odoo 18 Accounting?
Content:
Group Payments in Odoo 18 Accounting

Managing payments efficiently is critical to a company’s financial health. Whether dealing with multiple vendors or collecting bulk payments from customers, handling transactions one at a time can be time-consuming and error-prone. That's where Group-Payments in Odoo 18 Accounting come in, allowing you to simplify your processes and completely control your accounts.

Odoo 18 introduces robust tools for group-payments, also called Odoo 18 batch payments. These features enable finance teams to manage large volumes of payments more efficiently, reduce manual entry, and automate reconciliations. Whether you’re managing Odoo 18 customer payments or Odoo 18 vendor payments, the group-payment feature ensures accuracy, speed, and clarity.

This guide explains how to manage Group-Payments in Odoo 18 Accounting, highlights key features, and shares practical implementation steps so you can make the most of your Odoo accounting system.

What are Group Payments in Odoo 18 Accounting?

Group Payments in Odoo 18 Accounting allow you to combine multiple payment entries into a single transaction. That is especially useful when paying various invoices to a single vendor or recording bulk customer payments.

Why use Group Payments?

  • Simplify payment tracking
  • Speed up reconciliation
  • Minimize transaction fees
  • Improve cash flow visibility

For example, instead of creating separate payments for each invoice, Odoo allows you to create Odoo 18 batch payments, grouping them under a single payment record for smoother processing.

Setting Up Group Payments in Odoo 18 Accounting

Before diving into group-payment operations, you must enable payment management settings.

Step 1: Enable Batch Payments

  • Go to Accounting > Configuration > Settings
  • Scroll down to Vendor Payments or Customer Payments
  • Enable the checkbox for Batch Payments
  • Click Save

Step 2: Configure Bank Journals

Ensure your bank journals are correctly set up to allow batch processing:

  • Navigate to Accounting > Configuration > Journals
  • Select your bank journal
  • Enable the “Batch Payments” option under the journal configuration

Step 3: Payment Methods

  • Make sure Manual, SEPA, or other supported payment methods are added to the journal.
  • These methods are necessary for actual fund transfers when executing Odoo 18 accounting payments

Creating Group Payments for Vendors in Odoo 18

Managing Odoo 18 vendor payments becomes a breeze with batch processing.

Step-by-Step:

  • Go to Accounting > Vendors > Batch Payments
  • Click on Create
  • Select Payment Type (e.g., Send Money)
  • Choose Bank Journal and Payment Method
  • Add payment lines by clicking Add a Line.
  • and selecting unpaid vendor bills
  • Click Validate to process the group payment.

Once the batch payment is validated, a single payment entry is created for the selected invoices, and the payment reconciliation can be done quickly.

Tip:

You can also schedule Odoo 18 group-payments ahead of time to match with supplier payment terms.

Receiving Group Payments from Customers

For companies dealing with bulk receipts, Odoo 18 customer payments via group receipts help consolidate multiple invoices into one receipt.

Step-by-Step:

  • Go to Accounting > Customers > Batch Payments
  • Select Receive Money as Payment Type
  • Choose the correct customer and payment journal.
  • Select multiple invoices and validate the group receipt

This single payment will now cover all selected invoices. Odoo automatically applies the payment to the corresponding invoices, reducing reconciliation time.

Reconciliation of Group Payments in Odoo 18 Accounting

Once a batch payment is processed, the next step is to match it with bank statements through Odoo 18 payment reconciliation.

How to Reconcile:

  • Navigate to Accounting > Reconcile
  • Import your bank statement or create one manually
  • Match the group payment with the bank entry using Odoo’s smart reconciliation tool

Odoo accounting group payment reconciliation is smooth because the system automatically detects grouped entries. It intelligently matches the amounts and references across multiple invoices.

Best Practices for Managing Group Payments

To make the most out of Group-Payments in Odoo 18 Accounting, consider the following practices:

1. Regular Review of Outstanding Invoices

Ensure all open invoices are current and included in group payments without error.

2. Use Bank Integration

Set up direct bank feeds in Odoo to simplify Odoo 18 accounting payments and real-time reconciliations.

3. Schedule Payments Based on Due Dates

Set batch payments to align with vendor terms, reducing late fees and improving relationships.

4. Segment Payments by Vendor or Project

Use tags or analytic accounts to track payment batches by project, location, or team for enhanced visibility.

5. Audit Trails and Reports

Always review Odoo 18 group-payments history through journal entries and batch reports to ensure accuracy and compliance.

Benefits of Using Group Payments in Odoo 18 Accounting

Time Efficiency

Batching payments significantly reduces the time spent on manual entry.

Accuracy in Records

Thanks to centralized group entries and validations, there is less room for error.

Enhanced Cash Flow Visibility

Real-time tracking of payables and receivables through consolidated views.

Automated Reconciliation

Fewer manual steps thanks to Odoo’s intelligent reconciliation feature.

Vendor/Customer Satisfaction

Better payment handling improves trust and partnerships with stakeholders.

Everyday Use Cases for Group Payments in Odoo 18

  • Paying multiple bills to a supplier on a fixed date
  • Receiving monthly membership or subscription fees from customers
  • Managing payroll transactions in bulk
  • Paying for bulk purchases across different departments

All these use cases are smoothly handled within Odoo 18 group-payments, reducing hassle and increasing productivity for finance teams.

Make Every Payment Count with Odoo 18

If your team is still entering payments one at a time, it’s time to upgrade. Group-Payments in Odoo 18 Accounting are designed for modern finance operations that value speed, accuracy, and strategic insight.

From simplifying bulk payments to enhancing reconciliation, Odoo 18’s features help you regain cash flow control. Whether managing Odoo 18 customer payments or coordinating large Odoo 18 vendor payments, the batch processing capabilities will change how you work.

Title: How to Access the Revenue Report in Odoo 18 Events?

  •   Pie Chart

Cumulative Line Chart

  • Insert the customized revenue report directly into a spreadsheet for further analysis or presentation.

Understanding the Revenue Report Interface

The revenue report interface in Odoo 18 is designed to provide a comprehensive view of your event's financial performance. Key components include:

  • Graph View: By default, the revenue report displays a line chart showing revenue trends.
  • Pivot View: Switch to the pivot table view for a detailed breakdown of revenues by various dimensions such as event, ticket type, or date.

  • Filters and Grouping: Use filters to narrow down data by criteria such as event type, date range, or ticket category—group data to analyze revenues by specific segments.

Customizing the Revenue Report for Deeper Insights

Leveraging the Revenue Report for Strategic Decisions

The insights gained from the Odoo 18 Events Revenue Report can inform various strategic decisions:

  • Marketing Efforts: Identify events with higher revenues to replicate successful marketing strategies.

By regularly reviewing the revenue report, you can make data-driven decisions to enhance the success of your events.

Exporting and Sharing the Revenue Report

Odoo 18 provides options to export the revenue report for sharing and further analysis:

  • Save Custom Reports: Save customized views of the report for quick access in the future.
  • Share with Team: Share the report with team members to collaborate on event planning and analysis.

Enhancing Event Management with Odoo 18 Events Revenue Report

The Odoo 18 Events Revenue Report is a powerful tool that provides valuable insights into your events' financial performance. By understanding how to access and customize this report, you can make informed decisions to improve your event strategies, optimize revenues, and ensure the success of future events.

Title: How to Manage Incoming Shipments in Odoo 18 Inventory
Content:
Managing Odoo's 18 incoming shipments efficiently is a cornerstone of effective inventory control. Whether your business handles simple receipts or complex, multi-stage warehouse processes, Odoo 18 inventory management offers powerful features to streamline every aspect of incoming logistics.

In Odoo 18, companies benefit from highly customizable warehouse configurations, including one-step, two-step, and three-step receipt processes tailored to different operational scales. Managing Odoo 18 incoming shipments has never been more intuitive or scalable, from configuring warehouses to executing precise inventory operations.

This guide covers everything you need to know about managing Odoo's 18 incoming shipments. It also explores essential aspects like Odoo 18 inventory operations, best practices, and warehouse strategies to help you get the most out of your ERP system.

In the following sections, we'll explore:

  • Step-by-step setup of receipt methods
  • Real-world scenarios for choosing between one-step, two-step, and three-step receipts
  • Tips to boost accuracy, speed, and inventory transparency

By the end, you'll master Odoo 18 incoming shipments and elevate your warehouse performance to a new level.

Setting Up Odoo 18 Warehouse Configuration for Incoming Shipments

    1. Enable:

       

      •  Storage Locations

         

      •  Multi-step Routes

         

    2. Save the settings.

       

    The first step to managing Odoo 18 incoming shipments efficiently begins with proper Odoo 18 warehouse configuration. You can define how goods should be received depending on the size and complexity of your business.

    Step-by-Step Guide: Managing Incoming Shipments in Odoo 18

     

     Step 1: Enable Required Settings
    1. Open the Inventory module in Odoo 18.

       

    2. Go to Configuration → Settings.

       

 Step 2: Configure Warehouse Receipt Process
  1. Navigate to Configuration → Warehouses.

     

  2. Open your warehouse configuration.

     

  3. In the Shipment section, under Incoming Shipments, choose:

     

    •  Three-Step (Receive → Quality → Stock)

       

Save your changes.

 Step 3: Check out all the related product moment
  1. Click on Routes smart button

       2. Select Deliver,here we can see complete Routes overview

       3. Click on any rule,where a pop-up window opnes and we can configure is more specifically

       4. To see visual representation of every steps,go to products

         5. Open any of products and inside it head over to inventory tab to check out selected routes

        6. Click on view digram link

       7. If we click on any arrow ,it will take to specific rules configuration page

 Step 4 : Create a Purchase Order
  1. Open the Purchase module.

       2. Create a new Request for Quotation (RFQ).

       3. Select a Vendor.

       4. Add a Product and set the Quantity (e.g., 10 units).

        5. Click Confirm to turn the RFQ into a Purchase Order.

 Step 5: Receive Products (Step 1 - Input)
  1. In the purchase order, click Receive Products.

       2.Validate the transfer.

       3. This moves the products into the Input Location of the warehouse.

 Step 6: Perform Quality Control (Step 2 - Quality Zone)
  1. In the PO or Inventory Overview, click on the next transfer (operation type: Quality Control).

  2. Validate the quality check.

       3. Items now move from Input to Quality Control location.

 Step 7: Move Items into Stock (Step 3 - Final Storage)
  1. Click on the next transfer (operation type: Storage).

       2. Validate the final movement.

       3. Products are now transferred to Warehouse/Stock location.

 Step 8: Verify Stock
  1. Go to Products → On Hand.
  2. Confirm that the correct number of units (e.g., 10) are now in stock.

Odoo 18 One-Step Receipt – Fast and Simple Receiving

When speed is your top priority, the Odoo 18 one-step receipt method is ideal. This setup allows goods to go directly into your warehouse’s stock location.

Ideal For

  • Small businesses

  • Startups with limited storage

  • Low-risk, frequently used items

 How It Works

  1. Vendor sends shipment.

  2. Goods are received and validated in one step.

  3. Inventory is updated immediately.

This is the most straightforward method of handling Odoo 18 incoming shipments and is perfect for businesses looking to avoid unnecessary complexity in Odoo 18 inventory operations.

Key Tip: Add barcode scanners or QR code readers to make the one-step process even faster.

Odoo 18 Two-Step Receipt – Balancing Speed and Control

For companies with moderate volume and a need for quality checks or segregation, the Odoo 18 two-step receipt model is the right balance.

Ideal For

  • Mid-sized businesses
  • Items needing preliminary checks before stocking
  • Companies requiring an input zone

How It Works

  1. Goods arrive at the warehouse.
  2. They are placed in an input location temporarily.
  3. After internal validation, goods are transferred to the stock location.

This method improves accuracy and gives teams more control over Odoo 18 incoming shipments, ensuring only validated items are added to the inventory.

Pro Tip: Automate validation rules for faster transition from input to stock using scheduled actions in Odoo 18 inventory management.

Odoo 18 Three-Step Receipt – Maximum Compliance and Accuracy

Businesses handling sensitive products like pharmaceuticals or electronics benefit greatly from the Odoo 18 three-step receipt process.

Ideal For

  • Enterprises
  • Businesses with strict compliance or quality standards
  • Perishable or regulated goods

How It Works

  1. Goods are received in the input area.
  2. Items go through quality control.
  3. Approved goods are transferred to stock.

This is the most robust method of handling Odoo 18 incoming shipments, allowing for complete control, traceability, and compliance.

Best Practice: Enable quality control checkpoints and record test results directly in Odoo for traceability and audit preparation.

Managing Odoo 18 Inventory Operations Effectively

Managing Odoo 18 inventory operations means more than just receiving goods. It includes:

  • Tracking incoming transfers
  • Batch and serial number registration
  • Automated reordering and stock alerts
  • Vendor performance tracking

Using these features alongside well-structured Odoo 18 incoming shipments processes ensures that warehouse teams have full visibility and accountability.

Key Features to Use:

  • Real-time stock reporting
  • Smart tags and filters
  • Integration with purchase and quality modules

Tip: Use dashboards and custom reports to keep leadership informed on incoming shipment trends and bottlenecks.

Best Practices for Odoo 18 Incoming Shipments

To get the most out of Odoo 18 incoming shipments, implement the following practices:

Standardize Receiving Processes

Regardless of your receipt type, ensure warehouse staff follow the same standard operation procedure for inspections and validations.

 Use Barcoding

Simplify scanning and tracking of items. Odoo 18 supports barcode integration, which speeds up Odoo 18 inventory operations.

 Train Your Staff

Even the best system fails without skilled people. Train your warehouse and procurement teams on:

  • Understanding receipt methods
  • Managing warehouse transfers
  • Using mobile inventory features

Integrate with Procurement

Ensure purchase orders automatically generate corresponding incoming shipments to reduce manual entry and errors.

Master Odoo 18 Incoming Shipments with Smart Strategies

By leveraging the right warehouse configuration and understanding when to use one-step, two-step, or three-step receipts, your business can optimize the flow of Odoo 18 incoming shipments with precision and speed.

The flexibility and depth of Odoo 18 inventory management make it a powerful tool for businesses of all sizes. From simple setups to complex operations, Odoo 18 incoming shipments can be tailored to fit your unique workflow, helping you minimize delays, eliminate errors, and boost warehouse productivity.

Take the time to properly configure your warehouse, train your team, and implement automation where possible. The results? Faster operations, better inventory accuracy, and a streamlined supply chain.

To illustrate these approaches, we’ll create a custom module where each record receives a unique reference number. Whether you’re a developer or a functional user, this guide will help you implement sequence numbers effectively.

Why Are Sequence Numbers in Odoo 18 Important?

Sequence numbers are more than identifiers; they bring structure and reliability to your data management. Here’s why they matter:

  1. Data Integrity: Prevent duplicate or missing records by ensuring each is unique and sequential.
  2. Audit Compliance: Provide a transparent tracking mechanism, which is crucial for audits and compliance.
  3. Operational Clarity: Simplify searches, streamline reporting, and improve integration processes.

Step 1: Define the Model

This step involves creating a new model in your Odoo custom module, which will represent the records you want to assign unique sequence numbers to. In this example, we’re creating a model called custom.document.

Model Structure

This Python code defines custom.document.
In Odoo, your custom create() method checks whether the name is still New when a new record is created. If so, the system knows it’s time to fetch the next number from the defined sequence.

				
					console.lfrom odoo import models, fields, api
class CustomDocument(models.Model):
	_name = 'custom.document'
	_description = 'Custom Document'
	name = fields.Char(string='Document Number', required=True, copy=False, readonly=True, default='New')
	@api.model
	def create(self, vals):
    	if vals.get('name', 'New') == 'New':
        	vals['name'] = self.env['ir.sequence'].next_by_code('custom.document') or 'New'
    	return super(CustomDocument, self).create(vals)
og( 'Code is Poetry'

Explanation:

  • Field Definition: The name field stores the unique document number.
  • Custom Create Method: When creating a new record, the method checks if the name field is set to "New." If true, it fetches the following number from the defined sequence using ir.sequence.

    Creating a Sequence in the Backend (XML)

    Let’s say we’re building a custom module and want to generate a unique number for a model called custom.document.

				
					<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<odoo>
	<data noupdate="1">
    	<record id="seq_custom_document" model="ir.sequence">
        	<field name="name">Custom Document</field>
        	<field name="code">custom.document</field>
        	<field name="prefix">CUST/</field>
        	<field name="padding">5</field>
        	<field name="number_next">1</field>
        	<field name="number_increment">1</field>
    	</record>
	</data>
</odoo>

Field Descriptions

  1. code: Must match the code used in next_by_code().
  2. prefix: E.g., “CUST” for library.
  3. padding: Number of digits (e.g., CUST/00001).
  4. number_next: Start value.
  5. number_increment: Step size.

Test the Sequence

After installing your module:

  • Go to the Custom Document menu.
  • Create a book record.
  • The NAME will auto-populate (e.g., CUST/00001, CUST/000012…).

By testing the sequence, you ensure that your implementation is functioning correctly.

Don't forget to add this file to the manifest:

				
					'data': [
	'data/sequence.xml',
],

Creating a Sequence via the Odoo UI

Odoo provides a user-friendly interface for non-technical users to create and manage sequences.

 

Access the Sequence Menu

  • Enable Developer Mode in Odoo.
  • Go to Settings > Technical > Sequences & Identifiers > Sequences

(Developer Mode must be enabled.)

Create a New Sequence

Click Create and fill in the details:

  • Name: e.g., Custom Document
  • Code: Must match your model’s sequence code (custom.document)
  • Prefix: e.g., “CUST/”
  • Padding: e.g., 5
  • Number Next: Starting value (e.g., 1)
  • Number Increment: Usually 1

Save and Apply

Once saved, any record created in custom.document will automatically receive a formatted reference number.

 

Advanced Sequence Numbers in Odoo 18 Options

Odoo’s sequence management is flexible, allowing you to implement advanced features to suit your business needs.

1. Date-Based Sub-Sequences:

You can enable date ranges to reset sequences periodically (e.g., monthly or yearly). To configure this:

  • Choose the option Use subsequences per date range in the sequence settings.
  • Set the desired interval, such as monthly or yearly.

2. Standard vs No Gap Modes

  • Standard: Gaps are allowed if numbers are skipped (common in accounting).
  • No Gap: Ensures a strict sequence without missing numbers.

With Odoo18, defining sequence numbers can be done programmatically or effortlessly through the UI. Sequences bring structure, prevent errors, and improve data management across all models. Whether creating a Library System or a complex ERP module, this feature is essential for reliable and traceable operations.

Enhancing Your Sequence Setup

Here are some additional tips to make your sequence setup even more efficient:

  1. Error Handling:

    Ensure proper handling of your custom code to manage unexpected issues.

  2. Documentation:

    Maintain detailed documentation of your sequence configurations for future reference.

  3. Customisation for Local Requirements:

    Adapt sequences to meet regional or industry-specific compliance needs, such as VAT or audit standards in the UAE.

Sequence Numbers in Odoo 18

Defining and managing sequence numbers in Odoo 18 is a smooth process that caters to developers and functional users. Whether you implement sequences programmatically or through the user interface, these unique identifiers enhance data consistency, prevent errors, and improve operational clarity.

By Utilizing Odoo’s advanced sequence options, such as date-based subsequences and no-gap modes, you can tailor your setup to meet your business's specific needs. Start creating custom sequences today and experience the benefits of structured and reliable data management in Odoo 18.
