These features are designed to help you reduce waste, improve product quality, and maintain accurate inventory data without extra manual work.

When using the manufacturing app, you'll notice how easy it is to scrap a product right in the middle of production. With just one click, the damaged product is sent to a designated scrap location. This ensures your inventory levels are always correct, and you never accidentally count unusable items as sellable stock. These features are not just for big factories; even small manufacturers can use them to keep their production clean and organized.

Understanding Odoo 17 Manufacturing Process and Scrap Handling

The Odoo 17 manufacturing process is built around efficiency and transparency. It allows you to plan, execute, and track every stage of production. But what's great is how it handles exceptions like scrap. Whether you're producing in bulk or custom orders, there's always a chance that some items will not pass inspection. That's when Odoo's scrap handling features shine.

When you mark an item as scrap during the production process, Odoo automatically moves that product to a separate scrap location. This way, you don't mix faulty items with good stock. The system also lets you record the reason for scrapping, which is essential for tracking quality issues. Over time, these insights help you reduce the number of defective items and improve your entire manufacturing flow.

How to Manage Scraping of Product in Odoo 17 Manufacturing App?

So, how do you manage scrap products in Odoo 17? The first step is to open the Manufacturing App.

Under the Operations menu, we have the option Scrap.

Here, you can view all the scrap orders that have been created. We can scrap the item during manufacturing, and we can also scrap the entire product once manufacturing is complete. This is because, during the manufacturing process, we sometimes know that specific components may be damaged or cannot be used for manufacturing purposes. In such cases, we can scrap particular components only. After manufacturing, the entire product may be damaged or unsuitable for sale so that we may scrap it entirely. So, let’s scrap the order by creating a new manufacturing order, which can be done by going to Operations > Manufacturing Orders.

Click on New.

Now, I am going to scrap the product component during the manufacturing process. So, let’s choose the Bill of Materials, which is a table. After selecting the BOM, you can view the components and work orders in the screenshot below, which will be automatically populated in the field. Click on Confirm.

Now, we need to plan the manufacturing order for the work center, so click on the Plan button.

Later on, we can start working on our manufacturing operations, starting from the assembly line and moving to one work centre. So, to do that, click on Start. As you go through the manufacturing process or plan for it, you'll notice that one of the materials is scrap. Click on the Scrap button.

Here, you can choose the material that you want to move into the Scrap. Then click on the Scrap Products.

So, one quantity is scrapped, and you can find the scrapped materials by clicking on the Scraps smart button.

Here, you can also find its reference number, date (on which the component is scrapped), the product name, as well as the quantity, source location, scrap location, and the company that has set the components as scrap.

That's how Odoo 17 makes scrap handling easy. The best part? You can even scrap products during quality checks or after they have been moved to the warehouse.

Good businesses don't just throw away bad items, they learn from them. That's precisely what Odoo 17 manufacturing scrap management helps you do. Every time you scrap an item, you can record the reason. Maybe it was damaged during packaging, or perhaps it was a supplier issue, or it failed quality inspection. Whatever the case, you now have data. And data helps you make better decisions.

You can later view reports showing the most common reasons for scrap, which employees handled the scrapped items, or which machines were involved. With this level of control, you can start reducing scrap over time, improve training for your team, or even renegotiate with suppliers if you're receiving too many faulty parts.

Every time you scrap a product, Odoo 17 automatically creates scrap orders. These are official records of what was scrapped, how much, and why. These scrap orders are not just helpful for inventory, they're essential for audits, reporting, and quality control.

Let's say your manager wants to know how many units were scrapped this month. Instead of digging through notes or spreadsheets, you can pull up scrap orders directly in Odoo. These orders also help you track trends. Are you scrapping more products this month than last month? Is one product being scrapped more than others? With Odoo 17, all this information is available in a few clicks.

Inventory accuracy is one of the most significant challenges in manufacturing. But with Odoo 17 inventory scrap, this issue is handled automatically. When a product is marked as scrap, Odoo adjusts the inventory levels immediately. No delays, no confusion.

This means your stock reports are always up to date. If you're selling products online or managing a tight warehouse, you know how important this is. Selling a product that doesn't exist because it was damaged can lead to cancelled orders and unhappy customers. With real-time scrap updates, you avoid these problems and keep your operations running smoothly.

Managing Scrap in Real Life with Odoo 17

Suppose you run a factory that makes wooden furniture. You get a shipment of wooden panels, and during cutting, your worker notices that a few of them are damaged. Using Odoo 17, the worker scrapes the damaged panels right from the work order screen. The system logs the reason, updates the inventory, and sends the panels to the scrap location.

Now imagine this happens regularly. With Odoo 17's scrap reports, you notice that 60% of damaged panels come from one supplier. You now have the proof to talk to your supplier and demand better quality or switch to someone else. This is how digital scrap management turns small actions into significant results.

Why Odoo 17 Scrap Handling Makes Business Smarter

There's a reason businesses choose Odoo over other tools; it's not just about managing processes; it's about making more intelligent decisions. With Odoo 17 scrap handling, you turn what used to be a frustrating task into a helpful learning tool.

Scrap handling helps your team work better. Instead of hiding or ignoring bad products, they know there's a clear and straightforward way to deal with them. It also helps your management team make decisions backed by real data. Whether it's quality issues, machine errors, or supplier problems, scrap data gives you the whole picture.

And when everything from manufacturing to inventory to reporting is connected in one system, there's less room for mistakes. That's the power of using Odoo 17 for your manufacturing business.

Odoo 17 Manufacturing App Features Give You the Edge

Beyond scrap handling, the Odoo 17 manufacturing app features are designed for smart, scalable growth. You can manage work orders, bill of materials, routing, subcontracting, and more. But when combined with strong scrap management, these features create a smooth flow where nothing is wasted, not time, not materials, and not opportunities.

You can even custom-make the app to fit your business. Add approval workflows for scrap actions, link scrap to maintenance requests, or set quality rules that auto-trigger scrap in specific situations. With Odoo, you're not limited, you're entrusted.

Manage Scraping of Product in Odoo the Smart Way

To wrap it all up, the ability to manage product scraping in Odoo is more than just a feature, it's a smart strategy. With tools built right into the Odoo 17 manufacturing process, you can track scrap in real time, learn from your mistakes, and improve production quality.

From scrap orders in Odoo 17 to Odoo 17 inventory scrap, every part of the system is connected, automatic, and user-friendly. Even if you're new to Odoo, you'll find the system easy to use and incredibly helpful.

Why Updating Product On-Hand Quantity in Odoo 18.2 is Essential

Managing Product On-Hand Quantity is one of the most critical tasks for any business that deals with Inventory, whether small, medium, or enterprise-level. With the latest release of Odoo 18.2, companies can perform smoother, faster, and more accurate inventory adjustments, reducing the risk of mismatches between physical stock and system records.

The Product On-Hand Quantity feature allows companies to maintain accurate stock levels, perform manual stock updates, and execute physical inventory processes without disrupting daily operations. In this blog, we will walk you through the importance of updating stock levels, explain the step-by-step process in the Odoo 18.2 inventory adjustment tutorial, and show you why Netilligence, as an Odoo Partner, is the ideal partner to help you achieve seamless inventory management.

By the end of this guide, you’ll not only know how to update your Product On-Hand Quantity but also understand the bigger picture of maintaining real-time stock visibility in Odoo 18.

What is Product On-Hand Quantity in Odoo 18.2?

The Inventory Balance represents the actual stock available in your warehouse at a given time. Unlike forecasted quantities, which consider future receipts or deliveries, the on-hand count reflects the physical inventory ready to be sold or used.

With Odoo 18.2 inventory count, businesses can easily align physical stock with the system records. This avoids stock-outs, overstocking, and unnecessary financial discrepancies.

Key advantages of managing Product On-Hand Quantity in Odoo 18.2:

  • Accurate sales availability information.
  • Reliable reporting for demand forecasting.
  • Streamlined warehouse operations.
  • Better supplier relationship management through timely reordering.

Why is Updating Product On-Hand Quantity Important?

Errors in stock management often happen due to manual counting mistakes, delays in recording movements, or miscommunication between departments. The errors will result in serious problems if not corrected.

  • Stockouts: Losing customers due to unavailability.
  • Overstocking: Wasting capital on excess Inventory.
  • Financial inaccuracy: Incorrect accounting entries.
  • Operational inefficiency: Wasted time resolving stock mismatches.

By utilizing the Odoo 18 update stock levels functionality, businesses can periodically run a physical inventory process to verify their system records. This ensures that your data is reliable for making strategic decisions.

Step-by-Step Guide to Odoo 18.2 Update On-hand Quantity

Now, let’s dive into the Odoo 18.2 inventory adjustment tutorial. Follow these steps carefully to execute an accurate update of your Inventory Balance:

Step 1 – Go to the Inventory Module

  • From the Odoo 18.2 dashboard, click on the Inventory app.

Step 2 – Select Products

  • In the Inventory module, go to Products → Products.
  • You will see a list of all products in your system.

Step 3 – Open the Product Form

  • Select the product whose stock you want to update.
  • This opens the detailed product form.

Step 4 – Update On-Hand Quantity

  • Inside the product form, click the Update Quantity button.
  • A new window will appear showing the current Inventory Balance.
  • Enter the new value for the quantity.

Step 5 – Save and Validate

  • After entering the correct number, save your changes.
  • The Inventory Balance for this product will now be updated in real-time.

Manual Stock Update vs. Physical Inventory in Odoo 18.2

It’s important to distinguish between a manual stock update and a complete physical inventory process:

  • Odoo 18.2 manual stock update: Adjust specific items quickly, for example, when receiving damaged returns or misplaced products.
  • Odoo 18.2 physical inventory process: A comprehensive stock count covering all products in a location, usually done monthly, quarterly, or annually.

The two methods modify Inventory Balance but operate at different levels according to your business requirements.

Best Practices for Managing Product On-Hand Quantity in Odoo 18.2

To maximize the benefits of Odoo’s inventory tools, follow these best practices:

  1. Perform regular Odoo 18 inventory counts by scheduling periodic counts instead of waiting for year-end adjustments.
  2. Use barcodes and scanners – Integrate Odoo with barcode scanners for faster, error-free stock counting.
  3. Train your warehouse staff – Ensure staff understand how to perform adjustments in Odoo.
  4. Audit adjustments – Regularly review who made updates and why, for better accountability.
  5. Leverage reports – Use Odoo’s reporting tools to analyze discrepancies and prevent recurring errors.

Title: Is Odoo ERP Really an All-in-One Business Solution?
Content:
Why Everyone Talks About Odoo as an All-in-One Business Solution

Every business owner has asked this question at some point: Is there really one software that can handle everything? From sales to finance, HR to inventory, and even marketing, companies usually end up using different tools for each job. The result is a mess; too many subscriptions, too much data entry, and too little visibility. That's when the idea of an all-in-one business solution starts to look attractive.

When you search for one system that does it all, Odoo always shows up in the discussion. Many call it the ultimate Odoo all-in-one business solution due to its wide range of apps. What makes it stand out is that it doesn't just give you one or two tools; it provides you with everything, all inside one connected system. The Odoo ERP features cover almost every part of a business, making it one of the most practical integrated business software platforms today.

Business leaders who want to stop managing different tools look at Odoo's flexibility. The Odoo modular ERP system enables users to start with basic functions and gradually add more capabilities as their business grows. The system operates differently from standard ERP systems because it does not need significant initial funding. The Odoo CRM ERP integration enables firms to link customer management directly to operational and financial processes, which proves challenging for most organizations to implement.

Some even compare Odoo to SAP, as both claim to cover all areas of business. The big difference? Odoo is an open-source, all-in-one ERP, making it far more accessible to small and medium-sized companies.

But the real question is: Does Odoo truly live up to the claim of being an all-in-one business solution? Let's break it down step by step.

Why Businesses Run After an All-in-One Business Solution

Think about your daily business tasks. The sales team manages leads in one app. The accounts team runs reports in another. HR tracks attendance somewhere else. And your warehouse team? They probably use spreadsheets. This setup works for a while, but as soon as you grow, the gaps start showing. Data gets lost, mistakes happen, and decisions take longer.

That's why an all-in-one business solution feels like a dream. Instead of handling ten different apps, you only log in once. Your sales team closes a deal, and the invoice is already waiting in finance. A customer buys online, and inventory is updated instantly. HR doesn't need to ask accounting about salaries; it's already in the system.

The idea that everything is connected is what makes Odoo an all-in-one business solution so appealing. Businesses want speed, accuracy, and cost savings, and they don't want to spend their energy connecting scattered tools.

Exploring Odoo ERP Features That Cover Every Part of Business

When people say Odoo is complete, they are talking about its wide range of Odoo ERP features. Unlike many other systems, Odoo doesn't just stop at finance or sales; it goes further.

The CRM and Sales side of Odoo helps track leads, monitor deals, and manage customer relationships. Once the deal is closed, the invoice is automatically created in accounting; no manual data entry.

The Accounting and Finance module supports invoicing, multi-currency, payments, and expense tracking. It provides small businesses with professional-level financial control, while large companies can manage complex accounts across multiple countries.

On the operations side, Inventory and Supply Chain management in Odoo ensures businesses know exactly what stock is available, what's coming in, and what needs to be ordered.

For manufacturers, the Manufacturing module manages work orders, production planning, and quality checks within a single platform.

Human resources are equally important, and Odoo offers HR and Payroll features. From recruitment to contracts, attendance, and payroll, everything is linked.

Even e-commerce and website management are included, which means businesses can sell online and automatically connect sales with inventory, shipping, and accounting.

This list of Odoo ERP features demonstrates why it is not just another ERP; it's a comprehensive, integrated business software platform.

How Odoo Modular ERP Makes It Flexible for All Businesses

One of the biggest reasons companies choose Odoo is its modular ERP design. You don't have to buy the whole system at once. If you're a startup, you can begin with CRM and invoicing. Once you grow, you can add HR, inventory, or even a manufacturing module.

This flexibility is priceless. Traditional ERP systems, such as SAP or Oracle, typically require a comprehensive setup from the outset. That means heavy investment, even if you don't use half the features. With Odoo, you only pay for what you actually need. That's why many small and medium businesses see Odoo as the right balance between affordability and functionality.

Integrated Business Software Odoo and Why It Matters

At the end of the day, businesses want one thing, which is connection. A sales deal shouldn't get stuck waiting for finance. HR should not be chasing accounting for payroll. And inventory data should not be buried in spreadsheets. That's the power of integrated business software Odoo.

Because Odoo is fully connected, one action automatically updates across the system. If sales close a deal, accounting sees the invoice. If a product is sold online, inventory updates instantly. If HR updates employee data, payroll is already ready.

This integration reduces errors, saves time, and provides leaders with real-time visibility into the business. And that's the true meaning of an all-in-one business solution, everything working together without friction.

Odoo CRM ERP Integration and Its Real Value

Customer data is the lifeblood of every business. But in many companies, CRM sits in one place and ERP in another. The result? Sales, marketing, and finance don't speak the same language.

With Odoo CRM ERP integration, customer data flows everywhere. A lead entered by sales moves smoothly into invoicing once the deal is closed. If the customer calls support, the service team can instantly see their purchase and payment history. Marketing campaigns can be linked directly with CRM data, so sales get warm leads instead of cold ones.

This level of integration makes Odoo not just software, but a comprehensive all-in-one business solution that connects customers with operations.

Odoo vs SAP All in One – The Ongoing Comparison

No discussion about ERP is complete without talking about Odoo vs SAP all-in-one. Both claim to cover all business needs, but there are key differences:

Cost and Licensing

SAP usually requires a high upfront investment, making it more suitable for large enterprises. Odoo, as an open-source all-in-one ERP, offers more flexibility and lower costs, especially for SMEs.

Flexibility

Odoo modular ERP allows businesses to add apps as they grow. SAP solutions are more rigid and require significant customization.

Community and Support

Odoo has an extensive, open-source community that contributes to its growth. SAP, although established, lacks the same open-source adaptability.

Many businesses find Odoo to be more user-friendly than SAP. This makes adoption easier, especially for smaller companies.

So, when businesses compare Odoo vs SAP all-in-one, many prefer Odoo for its affordability, adaptability, and simplicity.

One of the most substantial advantages of Odoo is that it is an open-source, all-in-one ERP. This provides companies with more flexibility than traditional ERP systems. They can customize the platform, add apps, or even build their own extensions.

Because Odoo is open source, it also benefits from an extensive community of developers and contributors. This keeps the system fresh with constant improvements and innovations. For businesses, it means they get access to modern tools without being locked into expensive vendor contracts.

This openness is one of the main reasons Odoo is considered the most practical all-in-one business solution today.

So, Is Odoo ERP Really an All-in-One Business Solution?

After exploring the Odoo ERP features, modular structure, CRM integration, and its comparison with SAP, the question remains: Does Odoo live up to its reputation as an all-in-one business solution?

The answer largely depends on business needs:

For SMEs, Odoo is one of the best options. It's affordable, flexible, and covers almost every function.

For large enterprises, it can be effective, but customization and professional support may be required.

For startups, Odoo's modular ERP makes it easy to start with only the essential apps and grow later.

So, yes, Odoo is indeed a strong all-in-one business solution, but businesses must plan their implementation carefully.

Why Businesses Choose Odoo All-in-One Business Solution

Nowadays, businesses prefer unified systems. They want everything under one roof. Odoo gives them precisely that. With its wide Odoo ERP features, flexible Odoo modular ERP approach, and strong Odoo CRM ERP integration, it becomes much more than just another ERP. It becomes a truly integrated business software.

When compared to Odoo and SAP, Odoo stands out as the more intelligent choice for businesses seeking affordability, flexibility, and control. And because it's an open-source all-in-one ERP, companies are not tied down by limits; they can grow and adapt the system as they please.

Title: How to Reinvoice Employee Expenses in Odoo 18 Project?
Content:
Reinvoice Employees' Expenses

 A proper system becomes essential for managing employee expenses between different projects because, without it, the process becomes complicated. Odoo 18 re-invoice employee expenses feature provides companies with a solution to simplify and automate their financial management through this important process. Odoo project expense management enables users to handle travel costs and equipment purchases, and project-related expenditures through a seamless re-invoicing process.

This article provides a comprehensive overview of Odoo 18 re-invoice employee expenses by explaining Odoo employee expense workflow, Odoo 18 project billing, Odoo expense report approval and Odoo re-invoice expenses to customers. The following section explains how to link these processes effectively under Odoo 18 expense re-invoicing features.

Understanding Odoo 18 Re-Invoice Employee Expenses Feature

 The Odoo 18 re-invoice employee expenses feature enables you to efficiently bill customers for project expenses. The system eliminates manual expense tracking and billing by automatically linking expenses to project billing.

Key Benefits:

  •  The system integrates all project-related data with timesheet records and financial accounting functions.
  •   The system enables direct billing of reimbursable expenses to customers.
  •  The system provides real-time project profitability tracking.

How to Re-invoice Expenses to Customers in Odoo 18

Step 1: Activate Analytic Accounting

  • Go to the Accounting module.
  • Click on Configuration > Settings.
  • Under the Analytics section, enable the Analytic Accounting option.
  • Click Save.

Step 2: Create Products to Re-Invoice Employee Expenses

  • Navigate to the Sales module.
  • Go to Products > Create.
  • Create First Product (Car Expense):

    • Name: Car Expense 
    • Set Product Type: Service
    • Set Invoicing Policy: Based on Delivered Quantity.
  • Enable Expense and Go to Sales smart button.
  • Set Reinvoice Expense: At Cost.
  • Assign Product Category: All Expenses.
  • Under the Accounting tab, set the Expense Account.
  • Save the product.
  • Create Second Product ( Meeting):

    • Name: Meeting
    • Set Product Type: Service.
    • Set Invoicing Policy: Based on Timesheets.
    • Enable Create on Project & Task.
    • Create a Project Template (e.g., "Odoo ").
    • Assign Product Category: All Expenses.
    • Set the Sales Price and Cost appropriately.
  • Set Reinvoice Expense: At Cost.
  • Set Unit of Measure: Hours.
  • Save the product.

Step 3: Create a Quotation

  • Go to the Sales > Orders section.
  • Click on New to create a quotation.
  • Fill in the Customer details.
  • Add the Product (e.g., Meeting) in the Order Lines.
  • Set Quantity (e.g., 8 hours).
  • Save and confirm the quotation.

Step 4: Project and Task Creation

  • After confirming, a Project and Task will be automatically generated.
  • Navigate to the Project.
  • Set Customer, Project Name, and Task Details.
  • Add timesheet entries by:
    • Logging hours.
  • Adding a description (e.g., Task Completed).

Step 5: Create an Employee Expense

  • Go to the Expenses module.
  • Click New to create a new expense.
  • Select the Category (e.g., Car expense or  Meeting).
  • Details like Name, Cost, and Quantity will auto-fill.
  • Set the Customer to Reinvoice.
  • Save the expense.

Step 6: Submit and Approve Expense

  • After saving:
    • Click Submit.
  • The expense status will change to Submitted.
  • After that Click on Approved.
  • Click Post Journal Entries to finalise and move it to the Posted state.

Step 7: Review Sale Order and Journal Entries

  • A Sale Order will be automatically created based on the expense.
  • Review:
    • Project Name.
    • Task.
    • Logged Hours.
    • Expense Details.
  • Confirm journal entries have been posted under Accounting.

Tips for Mastering Odoo 18 Expense Re-Invoicing

  • Always use analytic accounts correctly for linking expenses to projects.
  • Odoo expense report approval requires a proper approval chain to prevent miscommunication.
  • The project overview dashboard should be used to conduct regular audits of billable expenses.
  • The Odoo project expense management settings need customisation to align with your internal policies and client agreements.
  • Verify that expense products have proper revenue recognition settings when necessary.

The implementation of these practices will optimize your Odoo 18 re-invoice employee expenses process and improve cash flow management.

Odoo 18 enables you to fully control your project expenses.

Odoo 18 provides an efficient solution for employee expense management through its re-invoice employee expenses feature. Odoo enables users to track project expenses while performing customer validation for billing purposes through an efficient and transparent system.

Odoo project expense management helps you decrease administrative costs while delivering precise and timely billing to clients, which enhances their satisfaction.  These implementation steps will lead to major enhancements in your company's project financial management.

Managing shipping policies in Odoo 18 means deciding how products will be delivered, who will provide them, and what shipping costs to charge. You can create rules based on country, weight, product type, or even order value. This helps your system automatically choose the best shipping method for each order.

Instead of sending every order the same way, you can set different options. For example, use express shipping for high-value items or free shipping for orders above a certain amount. When you understand how to control and manage shipping policies in Odoo 18, you take control of your entire delivery system.

Odoo 18 Shipping Policy Best Practices That Save Time and Money

Now, let’s discuss the best ways to manage your shipping system. These Odoo 18 shipping policy best practices help you avoid mistakes and save effort.

First, always organize your shipping zones. Group countries or cities together based on how you deliver. This helps Odoo apply the proper method for each place. Next, use pricing rules based on weight or distance. This way, your shipping cost will always be accurate.

Also, add more than one delivery option for your customers. Let them choose between standard or express shipping. Give clear names like “2-Day Delivery” or “Free Delivery Above $100.” These builds trust.

The most important tip? Test your rules. Before using them on real orders, try them in a test system. Fix any issues before they affect customers.

Managing Shipping Rules in Odoo 18 Without Confusion

Managing shipping rules in Odoo 18 can initially feel tricky, but it gets easy once you understand how rules work. You can set conditions like:

  • If the weight is more than 10kg, use heavy cargo shipping
  • If the customer is from a particular country, use a special courier
  • If the order value is low, don’t offer free delivery

These shipping rules make your system smart. It knows what to do, when, and how to apply the correct method. You don’t need to do things manually anymore.

Also, keep your rules simple. Too many conditions can confuse the system and cause delays. Start small, then add more rules as your business grows.

How to Manage Shipping Policies & Picking Policies in Odoo 18: Step-by-Step Guide

In Odoo 18, managing Shipping Policies and Picking Policies helps you control how your products are delivered and prepared for shipment. It impacts how quickly and correctly your customers get their orders. This guide covers everything from creating delivery methods to deciding how and when products are picked from the warehouse.

Let’s get started!

Open the Inventory Module.

Direct to Configuration > Settings.

Under the Operations section, you can find an option called Picking Policy. This says when to start shipping. So, there are two options: the first is ‘ship products as soon as available, with back orders’, and the other one is ‘ship all products at once’. Now, let’s see how it works.

Click Products > Products.

Now, you can see all the products here. Let’s create the order.

Go to the Sales App.

When the order is placed, Odoo creates a picking order for each available product immediately. So, if a product is out of stock, a back order is created for the remaining quantity. 

Click on New.

Fill out all the details & click on Confirm. I have just set the picking policy' ship products as soon as available, with back orders'. So, even if we don't have sufficient quantities, we can create a backorder for the remaining quantities. This policy is ideal for businesses that prioritise quick fulfilment and want to ship available items promptly. It also suits customers who are willing to accept partial shipments, even if the order cannot be fulfilled immediately.

The quotation has been moved to the Sales Order state.

By clicking on the other info tab, you can also see that we have a Shipping Policy field, and here you can see that ‘as soon as available’ will be automatically configured.  

Now, move to the order lines & click on the Delivery button.

Now, you can see that the quantity demanded by the customer is 20, but we have only 11 quantities. Click on Check Availability, and we don’t have sufficient quantities in our stock. We cannot check the availability because it only updates the 11 quantities that we have in our stock.

Now, click on the Validate button to process the order.

After clicking on the validate, you can see that we can either create a backorder or no backorder. If the customer is going with no backorders, they must forget about the rest of the quantity they have made. If he creates a backorder, we simply deliver the remaining quantity to the customer once the product is returned. So, in this case, I am going to click on ‘‘Create Backorder’’.

We are currently going to deliver the 11 quantity, which is what we have in our stock. We are using a multi-step process to deliver the item. We have picked the item and now need to move it to the output location by clicking the Next Transfer smart button.

Then, click on the Validate.

By clicking the validate button, we can deliver the item directly to the customer.

Now, let’s discuss the other one, that is ‘‘Ship all products at once’’. To do this, go to the Inventory App > Configuration > Settings, change the picking policy, and then click Save.

Next, return to the Sales module and create a new sale order by clicking on New. Select the customer, add the product, and then click Confirm.

As you can see in the screenshot below, the quotation has just moved into the sales order, and we need to deliver the item to the customer by clicking on the Delivery button.

Here, you can see that it is in the waiting stage, and it is best suited for the business that prioritises complete order fulfilment and wants to ship all the items together. This policy is also ideal for the customers who expect to receive their entire order in one shipment. 

Once the product is available, the waiting status is updated to Ready. Then you can click ‘‘Validate’’ to move the item from the Ready stage to the Done stage.

So, this is the optimal picking policy depending on your business model, customer expectations and inventory management strategies. By carefully considering your business needs and customer preferences, you can select the most appropriate picking policies to optimise your order fulfilment process in Odoo.

  • Standard delivery

Odoo 18 lets you connect with real DHL, FedEx, UPS, and more couriers. The system can show real-time shipping rates based on the order details. You can also set fixed prices if you don’t want dynamic rates.

Odoo 18 delivery method rules let you choose how each delivery method works. Think of them like “if this, then that” actions.

You can say:

These rules give you complete control. You don’t have to change anything manually every time. Once your rules are set, Odoo does the work.

Make sure your rules match your real-world needs. Don’t overcomplicate them. Simple rules that solve big problems are the best kind.

Odoo brings all this together in one place. It gives you complete visibility over your logistics. You can track stock, check orders, and plan routes from your dashboard.

As your business grows, your logistics will get more complex. Odoo 18 is built to grow with you. Start small, then keep improving as you learn what works best.

Best Practices Odoo Shipping Users Swear By

These small steps lead to significant results. Your customers will get better service, and your team will work more smoothly.

Smart Shipping Starts with Odoo 18

If you want happy customers and a smooth delivery process, managing shipping policies in Odoo 18 is the way to go. From simple rules to innovative delivery options and complete logistics policy management, everything becomes easier when you use the system well.

Title: How to Install Odoo 19 on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
Content:
Installing Odoo 19 on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS is a great way to set up a powerful, open-source ERP system on a stable and secure Linux environment. Whether you’re a developer, business owner, or system administrator, this step-by-step guide will walk you through the installation process, ensuring that your Odoo instance runs smoothly on the latest Ubuntu release.

Step 1: Log in to the Ubuntu Server via SSH

To begin, log in to your server using SSH. This step allows you to access your Ubuntu server remotely:

				
					Connect to your server using SSH:
ssh username@IP_Address -p Port_number
Example:
ssh root@127.0.0.1 -p 22

Step 2: Update Your Server

Keeping your server updated is crucial for security and performance. Run the following commands to update and upgrade your system:

				
					sudo apt-get update -y
sudo apt-get upgrade -y

By ensuring your server is up-to-date, you reduce vulnerabilities and ensure compatibility with the latest packages.

Step 3: Secure Your Server

To enhance your server's security, install Fail2Ban, a tool that helps prevent SSH brute force attacks:

				
					Install fail2ban to prevent SSH attacks:
sudo apt-get install openssh-server fail2ban -y
Start and enable Fail2Ban:
sudo systemctl start fail2ban
sudo systemctl enable fail2ban
Verify Fail2Ban is running:
sudo systemctl status fail2ban

Step 4: Install Required Packages

Odoo relies on several dependencies to function properly. Install these packages using the following command:

				
					sudo apt-get install python3-pip python3-dev libxml2-dev libxslt1-dev libssl-dev libsasl2-dev libldap2-dev build-essential libjpeg8-dev liblcms2-dev libblas-dev libatlas-base-dev

These dependencies are essential for Odoo's operation and compatibility with your system.

Step 5: Install PostgreSQL

PostgreSQL is the database management system used by Odoo.  
Install PostgreSQL and create a user for Odoo:

Remember to set a strong password for the PostgreSQL user.

				
					sudo apt-get install postgresql
sudo su - postgres
createuser --createdb --username postgres --no-createrole --superuser --pwprompt odoo19
exit

Step 6: Create a System User for Odoo

Create a dedicated system user for running Odoo:

				
					sudo adduser --system --home=/opt/odoo19 --group odoo19

This step helps isolate Odoo's environment from other processes on your server.

Step 7: Clone Odoo 19 from GitHub

Clone the Odoo 19 repository to your server:

				
					sudo su - odoo19 -s /bin/bash
git clone https://www.github.com/odoo/odoo --depth 1 --branch 19.0 --single-branch .
exit

This ensures that your system has the latest version of Odoo 19.

Step 8: Install Python Packages

Create and activate a Python virtual environment for Odoo 19:

				
					sudo apt install -y python3-venv
sudo python3 -m venv /opt/odoo19/venv
cd /opt/odoo19/
source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

Install wkhtmltopdf:

				
					sudo wget https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/releases/download/0.12.5/wkhtmltox_0.12.5-1.bionic_amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i wkhtmltox_0.12.5-1.bionic_amd64.deb
sudo apt install -f
xfonts-75dpi sudo apt install -f
deactivate

Step 9:Create Odoo Configuration File

Create the Odoo configuration file /etc/odoo19.conf:

				
					sudo nano /etc/odoo19.conf

				
			
				
					Add the following content:
[options]
   ; This is the password that allows database operations:
   ; admin_passwd = admin
   db_host = localhost
   db_port = 5432
   db_user = odoo19
   db_password = 123456
   addons_path = /opt/odoo19/addons
   default_productivity_apps = True
   logfile = /var/log/odoo19/odoo.log

Set File Permissions:

Change the ownership and permissions of the configuration file:

				
					sudo chown odoo19: /etc/odoo19.conf
sudo chmod 640 /etc/odoo19.conf

Create a Log Directory:

Create a directory for storing Odoo logs:

				
					sudo mkdir /var/log/odoo19
sudo chown odoo19:root /var/log/odoo19

Step 10: Create the Service File

Create a new systemd service file for Odoo:

				
					sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/odoo19.service

Add the following configuration:

				
					[Unit]
Description=odoo19
Documentation=http://www.odoo.com
[Service]
# Ubuntu/Debian convention:
Type=simple
User=odoo19
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /opt/odoo19/odoo-bin -c /etc/odoo19.conf
[Install]
WantedBy=default.target

Set Permissions for the Service File:

Secure the service file:

				
					sudo chmod 755 /etc/systemd/system/odoo19.service
sudo chown root: /etc/systemd/system/odoo19.service

Step 11: Start Odoo Service

Start the Odoo service:

				
					sudo systemctl start odoo19.service

Step 12: Enable Odoo Service at Boot

Enable Odoo to start automatically on boot:

				
					sudo systemctl enable odoo19.service

Step 13: Access Odoo in Your Browser

Finally, open your web browser and navigate to: http://<your_domain_or_IP_address>:8069

Title: How to Manage E-Wallet in Odoo 18 Sales?
Content:
Why Managing E-Wallet in Odoo 18 Sales Matters More Than Ever

In a world where digital payment is the new norm, managing customer expectations is no longer about offering a credit card option or a cash-on-delivery checkbox. It's about flexibility, speed, and smooth user experiences. That's where the ability to manage e-wallet in Odoo becomes a real catalyst.

Enterprises gain a massive competitive advantage when they understand how to manage an e-wallet in Odoo and align it with the broader Odoo 18 sales features.

Modern consumers seek autonomy, and with Odoo e-wallet integration, they get instant, secure, and reusable digital credit. Whether running a full-scale e-commerce empire or a retail chain looking to modernize operations, knowing how to leverage Odoo payment methods, especially the digital wallet, can revolutionize how you sell and engage. Let's dive deeper into this underrated yet effective feature.

How to Manage E-Wallet in Odoo 18 Sales: A Step-by-Step Guide

At its core, the e-wallet in ERP system is not just a wallet; it's an experience enhancer. To manage an e-wallet in ERP system, you first enable it through the sales app configuration. It begins by activating "Discounts, Loyalty & Gift Cards," which opens wallet functionalities within the system. Once enabled, you can assign digital credits to customers, think gift cards, refunds, or prepaid account balances.

Now imagine this: A returning customer visits your e-commerce site and decides to buy. Instead of re-entering payment details or calculating discounts, they use their wallet balance. The transaction is quick, secure, and satisfying. That's the magic; when you manage an e-wallet in Odoo 18 sales, you're not just processing payments but building customer loyalty through ease and trust.

Step 1: Enable Wallet Features in Sales App

  • Go to Sales App in Odoo 18.
  • Click on Configuration > Settings.
  • Under the “Pricing” section, activate the checkbox for:
  • Discounts, Loyalty & Gift Cards.
  • Click Save.

This activates all features related to digital wallets including prepaid balances, loyalty programs, and gift card integration.

Step 2: Create a Wallet Product (Optional but Recommended)

Go to Sales > Products >  E-Wallet Credit

  • Click Create and name it something like eWalet.

Step 3: Assign Wallet Balance to a Customer

You can add credits to a customer’s wallet manually or through a sale/refund:

Manual Method:

  • Click on Generate eWallet.
  • Add Required Customer or otherwise the system assigns it to all customers saved in the database.
  • Click Add Balance.
  • Enter the amount and reason (e.g., refund, gift, promotion).
  • Click Confirm.

Sale-Based Method:

  • When a customer purchases a gift card or top-up, create a Sales Order using the E-Wallet Credit product.
  • Confirm and register payment. Once validated, the amount is added to the customer’s wallet.

Set Wallet Usage Rules (Optional)

You can configure conditions for wallet usage under Sales Settings or Promotions, such as:

  • Minimum purchase amount to use the wallet
  • Expiry dates on wallet credits
  • Wallet balance limits
  • Loyalty reward points are convertible to wallet credit

Bonus Tips:

  • Enable email notifications to alert customers of wallet top-ups or usage.
  • Use portal access to let customers check their wallet balance online.
  • Combine wallet with loyalty programs for long-term retention.

Its effortless alignment with your existing business operations makes it stand out. You can configure digital credit values, create personalized top-up programs, and even set expiration rules. This isn't limited to online sales; walk-in customers can also use wallets via PoS systems.

This adaptability makes it ideal for businesses with varied sales channels. Want to provide cashback for frequent buyers? Launch a loyalty program that rewards customers directly into their ERP system digital wallet. Want to encourage pre-payment for services? Offer wallet bonuses. It's all possible with ERP system e-wallet integration, no complex third-party app, and just pure ERP system magic.

Odoo E-Wallet Integration

When discussing ERP system e-wallet integration, the conversation naturally extends into real-time data sync, secure storage, and multi-platform usability. It's one thing to allow digital wallet usage and another to do it well. ERP system 18 nails this by ensuring that every wallet transaction, whether a credit or a debit, is tracked in the customer's sales history, accounting, and CRM modules.

It's smooth: Your sales representative processes an order, the customer uses wallet credits, and your backend updates all records automatically. This level of automation means fewer human errors and faster reconciliation. As businesses scale, these time and effort savings translate into serious revenue gains. The keyword here is simplicity, and ERP system payment methods are increasingly about simplifying the customer journey while allowing your teams.

Exploring Odoo 18 Sales Features That Make Digital Wallets Work Effortlessly

Many users overlook how deeply wallet functionality is tied to broader ERP system 18 sales features. It's not just about storing credits; it's about offering those credits as a dynamic payment method. From the sales quotation stage to invoicing and payment, e-wallet balances are always visible and usable. You can even send digital credits for a promotion campaign, making your sales strategy more robust and engaging.

In short, the wallet extends your business philosophy: give more, sell smarter, and retain better. Through thoughtful configuration and customer-centric usage, ERP system 18 e-wallet turns your backend process into a front-end advantage.

Odoo Payment Methods Meet the Future

Traditional payment methods are beginning to feel outdated. Customers are tired of inputting card numbers, managing OTPs, and waiting for payment confirmations. With the growing rage of digital wallets in everyday life (think Apple Pay, Google Wallet, etc.), integrating that same ease into your ERP is non-negotiable. And that's precisely what ERP system payment methods now support.

When customers use their ERP system digital wallet, they're enjoying frictionless purchasing. You're reducing cart abandonment, improving checkout times, and boosting average order value. And the backend? It keeps track of every transaction in your sales, accounting, and customer service modules. Every stakeholder benefits, from the customer to the CFO.

The management of ERP system sales payment options depends on how intelligently they're structured. Want to offer a hybrid payment where the wallet covers part of the amount and the rest is paid by card? Done. Want to create wallet recharge packages with extra credits as a bonus? Easy. This flexibility means you're never boxed into a rigid payment structure.

In practice, customers love options. Giving them control over how they pay, especially when wallet credits are involved, increases their satisfaction and likelihood of returning. It also creates a gamified shopping experience where every purchase could earn wallet rewards. With ERP system 18 sales features, this level of personalization becomes second nature, not a tech nightmare.

Reimagine Loyalty with the Odoo Digital Wallet

At this point, it's clear that the ERP system digital wallet is more than a feature; it's a loyalty engine. Unlike traditional points systems that require third-party tools or clunky integrations, ERP system’s digital wallet works natively. You define the rules, the expiration dates, the top-up methods, and even the refund workflows. Every aspect is controlled within your ERP system environment, giving you unprecedented power over your sales and marketing strategy.

Envision this scenario: A customer returns a product. Instead of refunding their card and risking customer disengagement, you refund their e-wallet, ensuring they'll return for another purchase. Or think about holiday campaigns where purchases over a certain amount earn wallet credits. The possibilities are endless, and they all contribute to better customer engagement and higher repeat purchase rates.

Grasp the Art of Managing E-Wallet in Odoo and Varying Sales

To manage e-wallets in ERP systems , it adopts a future-ready sales strategy prioritizing convenience, loyalty, and business intelligence. With ERP system 18 e-wallet, businesses now have an integrated tool that simplifies payment experiences while driving higher conversions. Add to that the beauty of ERP system e-wallet integration, and what you get is an efficient, fully traceable, and secure digital wallet environment.

The real power lies in how deeply the wallet interacts with Odoo's 18 sales features, from customer profiles to invoices and POS to eCommerce. Your ability to offer varied and flexible ERP system payment methods will define your customer retention and satisfaction strategy in the coming years. With the increasingly digital nature of commerce, implementing the ERP system digital wallet might be the most intelligent decision you'll make for your business this year.

Let your competitors keep guessing. Thanks to ERP system 18's digital wallet ecosystem, you've already opened the secret to more brilliant, faster, and more rewarding selling.

Title: How to Configure Storno Accounting in Odoo 18 Accounting?
Content:
Understanding Storno Accounting in Odoo 18

In the world of digital finance, precision is everything. For businesses using ERP systems like Odoo, the margin for error in accounting is slim. That's why the introduction of Storno Accounting in Odoo 18 is more than just a technical upgrade; it's a practical solution to one of the most common challenges in bookkeeping: clean and compliant reversal of transactions.

The word "storno" may sound unfamiliar to many. Still, in the world of accounting, especially in regions with stringent regulations, such as Germany or parts of Europe, it's a powerful concept. Storno accounting is all about reversing previously posted journal entries, not by deleting them, but by creating a mirror image with exact details, opposite amounts.

In simple terms, Storno accounting is a financial method that reverses previously recorded accounting entries using negative entries, rather than deleting or modifying the original transaction. This ensures a transparent audit trail and is often required in jurisdictions with strict accounting compliance standards. With Odoo 18, storno accounting is now flawlessly integrated into your ERP platform.

Think about the last time you had to cancel an invoice or fix an incorrect vendor bill. You likely had to create a new adjustment entry, leave some explanatory notes, and hope that the trail made sense to your auditor. That's no longer necessary with Odoo 18 reversal accounting. Instead, you click a few buttons, and an automatic storno journal entry in Odoo does the job, accurately.

This guide will walk you through the whole process of using storno in Odoo accounting, focusing on how to set up the configuration, enable storno journals, manage credit note reversals, and handle the impacts of storno entries across ledgers.

Whether you're a financial controller, accountant, or Odoo consultant, this blog will equip you with everything you need to learn storno accounting in Odoo 18.

Odoo 18 Storno Accounting: A Fresh Perspective on Financial Reversals

In the latest version, Odoo 18 storno accounting introduces a dedicated system for reversal entries that do more than "cancel" a transaction; they explain it. Instead of manually correcting values or deleting mistakes (a dangerous path in the accounting world), Storno creates an exact copy of the original entry, but with opposite signs. Think of it as a financial mirror: what was credited is now debited, and what was debited is now credited, yet the entire structure of the original remains intact. This is not only aesthetically pleasing from an accounting standpoint but also necessary for companies seeking clear audit trails and full compliance with international standards.

Odoo has always supported reversals, but this storno method takes it to the next level. Where regular reversals tend to clutter the ledger or confuse the meaning of a correction, storno clarifies it. When applied right, this method changes reversals into transparent transactions that speak for themselves. It's no wonder that more and more businesses are asking: how do we configure storno entries in Odoo 18?

Configure Storno Entries in Odoo 18 to Gain Total Control Over Mistakes

Mistakes in accounting aren't just common, they're inevitable. But how we correct them defines our professionalism. That's why configuring storno entries in your system is not just a technical stage; it's a strategic upgrade.

The process begins in Odoo's settings, under the Accounting Configuration panel. By activating the storno feature, you're enabling a structural change in how your ERP handles reversals. No more disconnected entries. No more last-minute explanations to auditors. Just accurate, automated, and visually mirrored corrections.

Once storno is activated, each journal's sales, purchases, bank, and miscellaneous can be individually set to use the storno method for reversals. This flexibility enables accounting teams to apply STORNO only when necessary.

For example, it may be ideal for correcting posted invoices but unnecessary for petty cash adjustments. That's the elegance of Odoo: you get control without complexity. And that's precisely what modern financial teams crave.

Step-by-Step Guide to Configure Storno Accounting in Odoo 18

Storno accounting is a practice that involves using negative credits and debits whenever mistakes occur in transactions. This allows for easy identification and cancellation of transactions. Storno accounting allows you to reverse the journal entries that you have created. So, let's get started and learn how to configure storno accounting in the Odoo 18 accounting module.

First, open the Accounting module from your Odoo dashboard.

Go to Configuration > Settings.

Enable the Storno Accounting feature and click on Save.

Storno accounting is a practice of using negative credit or debit. Whenever you make an error in your transaction, Storno accounting will notify you of the error by highlighting it in red and reversing the entry. Now, let's move on to the Customers > Invoices.

Create an invoice by clicking on the New button.

Fill out the Customer details, then add the product by clicking Add a Product or Line.

By clicking on the Journal Items tab, you can see that, as they are just dealing with the invoices in this case, the product will be reduced from the warehouses. We recognize the product as an asset because it is decreasing. So, whenever the asset is decreasing it will be marked under the credit side. When we just sell and alter to the customer we know we will be getting a monetization for that so in that case we are just receiving an income. In that case we know the income in the form of an asset so as asset increases it will be marked under the debit side which is clearly shown in the screenshot below.

Now, let’s click on the Confirm button and confirm the invoice.

After confirming the invoice, I realized that I had made a pricing mistake for the product. The price has just been updated, and I need to reverse the entry. To reverse the entry, click the Credit Note button.

After clicking on the credit note, a new wizard appears, and here you can provide the reason displayed on the credit note. Let's say we have an updated price. Since we're only dealing with customer invoices, the journal will auto-populate with the customer invoices. 

As shown in the screenshot below, you have two options: you can either reverse the entry or reverse it and create an invoice. I want to reverse the entry, so I'm clicking on Reverse.

After reversing the entry, you can see in the screenshot below that the entry is currently in the Draft stage. This means that a customer credit note will be in a draft state, as we have not posted it.

Now, let's move on to the Journal Items tab, where you can see that the product sale has been adjusted to -$147, as we have reversed the entry. Additionally, under the accounts receivable, there is a $-147 indication. This is due to errors in the original entry, which we have since corrected by reversing it.

Now, click on Accounting > Journal Entries.

So, under the journal entries, since we haven't posted the entry, you can remove this filtration and easily find the reversed entry.

The reverse entry is in the draft stage, so let’s Confirm the reverse entry.

After making the reversal, as shown in the screenshot below, the status will change to Paid.

Moving on to the Journal Items tab, you will find no changes in the journal item. Now, we can also manage this by reversing the entry by creating a new invoice. Let’s click again on Customers > Invoices.

Click "New" to create a new invoice. Select the new customer, fill out all the details, choose the product, and then click the "Confirm" button.

After confirming the invoice, we realized that there is an issue with the product's price. So, we need to create the credit note to reverse this. Add the reason displayed on the credit note that is ‘‘Issue in Unit Price’’ then click on ‘‘Reverse and Create Invoice’’.

Here, I can change the price from $750 to $777.

If we go to the journal items tab, you can see that the new price will be updated under the journal items. Since we haven't posted this, the price remains unchanged. Let's move on to the Accounting > Journal Entries.

In this case, we will go with a Regular Invoice. Then, click Create Draft.

And just like before, we will Confirm the invoice.

Then, click on Pay.

And click Create Payment to register the payment and complete the process.

If you go back to the Sales Orders.

You will see that we made one delivery, but we have two invoices linked to this order.

Title: What Is the Talent Pool Feature in Odoo 19 Recruitment?

Why Odoo 19 Recruitment?

With Odoo's candidate pool functionality, recruiters can organize applicants, track their journey, and nurture relationships until the right opportunity arises. This approach reduces hiring time, improves the quality of hires, and ensures that no skilled applicant slips through the cracks. Whether it’s for shortlisting, proactive talent hunting, or building an Odoo recruitment candidate tracking system, the Odoo 19 recruitment automation tools make the hiring journey smoother and more strategic.

The Odoo talent pool vs shortlist debate often comes up, but with Odoo, you don’t need to choose. You can build a rich, long-term applicant database while also maintaining shortlist-ready candidates for immediate roles. This balance makes Odoo 19 recruitment an all-in-one solution for modern hiring needs.

Understanding the Odoo 19 Talent Pool Feature

The talent pool in Odoo recruitment is a centralized place where all potential candidates, whether active applicants or passive prospects, are stored. Think of it as your personal library of future employees. Instead of losing track of applicants who weren’t a fit “right now,” you can tag, categorize, and re-engage them when the perfect opportunity opens up.

Why Businesses Need a Talent Pool in Odoo Recruitment

Modern hiring is competitive. The best candidates are often off the market in just 10 days. Without a strong Odoo 19 recruitment candidate tracking strategy, businesses risk losing top talent to competitors.

The Odoo 19 talent pool feature solves this problem by:

  • Saving Time: No need to start from scratch for every new role.
  • Boosting Candidate Quality: You only re-engage people already pre-screened.
  • Building Employer Brand: Applicants appreciate being remembered and valued.
  • Supporting Recruitment Automation: With Odoo-19, Hiring automation, communication, filtering, and follow-ups become effortless.

Step 1: Open the Recruitment App in Odoo 19

  • Log in to your Odoo-19 dashboard.
  • From the main menu, go to “Recruitment”.
  • Here you’ll find different sections like Jobs, Applications, and Talent Pool.

Step 2: Move to the Talent Pool Section

  • Inside the Recruitment app, look for the “Talent Pool” menu on the top bar.
  • Click it, and you’ll land in the Odoo-19 talent pool feature dashboard.
  • This is where you manage, track, and filter all your potential candidates.

Step 3: Add Candidates to the Talent Pool

There are multiple ways to add applicants to your talent pool in Odoo Hiring:

  1. Direct Add: Click “New” in the Talent Pool dashboard → Fill in candidate details (Name, Email, Resume, Skills).

2. From Applications: Open any applicant in the Applications tab → Click “Add to Talent Pool”.

3. Import Option: If you have many resumes, click Import to upload them in bulk into the applicant database Odoo 19.

Step 4: Organize and Categorize Candidates

With Odoo, you can manage the candidate pool. You can:

  • Assign Tags (e.g., Python Developer, Marketing, Fresh Graduate).
  • Add Stages (Screened, Interviewed, Ready to Hire).
  • Keep Notes and attach files like resumes or portfolios.
  • Create custom fields (e.g., Availability Date, Expected Salary).

This makes Odoo's Hiring candidate tracking very powerful.

Step 5: Use Odoo Talent Pool vs Shortlist

  • Talent Pool: A wide list of all potential candidates saved in the system.
  • Shortlist: A filtered group of applicants ready for a current job opening.
  • How to move a candidate from Talent Pool → Shortlist:
    1. Open the candidate profile.
    2. Click “Add to Shortlist” for the specific job position.

Step 6: Automate Candidate Tracking in Odoo 19

With Odoo-19 Hiring automation, you can:

  • Create automated email templates for follow-ups.
  • Set automated reminders for interviews.
  • Auto-assign candidates to recruiters based on role/skill.
  • Trigger nurture campaigns to keep passive candidates engaged.

Step 7: Search and Filter Your Applicant Database

The applicant database Odoo 19 grows fast, but Odoo’s smart filters make it manageable:

  • Search by Tags (e.g., Python, MBA, Sales).
  • Filter by Last Contacted Date or Stage.
  • Use the kanban view for quick candidate pipeline visualization.

Step 8: Reuse Talent Pool for Future Hiring

Instead of starting from scratch every time:

  • Revisit your talent pool in Odoo Hiring when a new job opens.
  • Select already pre-screened candidates.
  • Instantly move them to the job’s shortlist.
  • This saves time, cuts costs, and makes Hiring proactive.

Odoo manages the candidate pool function, which is designed for flexibility. Recruiters can:

  • Tag candidates based on skills, roles, or hiring stage.
  • Archive applicants without losing their data.
  • Reopen conversations anytime.
  • Search by filters like education, past applications, or interview ratings.

This system is not only efficient but also enhances Odoo Hiring candidate tracking by giving HR professionals a clear history of each applicant.

Odoo Talent Pool vs Shortlist – What’s the Difference?

A common question is whether a talent pool in Odoo Hiring is the same as a shortlist. The answer is: No, but they complement each other.

  • Talent Pool: A broad collection of potential candidates (long-term asset).
  • Shortlist: A refined set of candidates ready for immediate consideration.

With Odoo-19 Hiring, businesses don’t have to choose. They can maintain a rich applicant database in Odoo-19 while also building job-specific shortlists for urgent hiring needs. This balance ensures you are always ready, whether for tomorrow’s vacancy or next year’s growth plan.

The applicant database Odoo-19 is the backbone of strategic hiring. It’s not just a list of resumes, it’s a living, searchable, and categorized system that grows with every new application.

  3. Proactive Hiring: You can fill urgent roles faster by accessing pre-qualified candidates.
  4. Scalability: As your business grows, your database becomes more powerful.

To make this more concrete, here are real-world ways businesses use the Odoo-19 talent pool feature:

  • Niche Roles: For hard-to-fill technical positions, companies keep pipelines ready.

Understanding COD in Odoo 19 Website

What is Cash on Delivery in Odoo 19?

Cash on Delivery (COD) is a payment option that allows customers to pay for their order only when it is delivered. In the Odoo 19 Website, COD is set up as a payment acquirer, which means it functions just like online payment gateways such as PayPal or Stripe, but instead, the transaction happens offline.

When you configure COD in Odoo, it gives flexibility to customers who are hesitant to pay online. Many businesses across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East rely heavily on Odoo 19's cash on delivery setup to cater to customer preferences.

Benefits of Setting Up Cash on Delivery in Odoo 19 Website

Why Do Businesses Prefer COD on Odoo eCommerce?

Enabling the cash on delivery payment method in Odoo 19 brings multiple benefits:

  • Customer Trust: Shoppers feel safer paying for delivery.
  • Wider Reach: Many customers without cards or wallets can buy.
  • Higher Conversions: COD reduces cart abandonment on your Odoo 19 Website.
  • Flexibility: Useful for new businesses to win trust.

COD vs Online Payments – Which One Wins?

While online payments are faster, COD ensures that customers who are skeptical about online fraud still shop with confidence. By activating the Odoo 19 eCommerce COD option, you bridge the gap between traditional buying habits and modern eCommerce.

Step-by-Step Guide to Odoo 19 Cash on Delivery Setup

Step 1 – Accessing Payment Acquirers in Odoo

  • Go to your Odoo 19 Website module.
  • Navigate to Website → Configuration → Payment providers.
  • Here, you’ll find options like PayPal, Stripe, and COD.

Step 2 – Enable COD Payment on the Odoo Website

  • Locate the Cash on Delivery option in payment acquirers.
  • Switch the status from Disabled to Enabled.
  • This activates the COD module on the Odoo website for checkout.

Step 3 – Configure COD in Odoo

  • Click on COD and edit its settings.
  • Add a name (e.g., “Cash on Delivery”).
  • Define countries where COD should be available.
  • Set payment instructions like “Pay in cash when order arrives.”
  • Save and publish.

Step 4 – Set up Payment Acquirer COD Odoo 19

  • Define fees if you want to charge extra for COD orders.
  • Add conditions (for example, COD only available for orders under $500).
  • Configure journals to record COD transactions separately.

Step 5 – Testing the COD Setup in the Odoo Website

  • Visit your Odoo 19 Website store.
  • Add a product to the cart and proceed to checkout.
  • Choose Cash on Delivery as the payment method, and in any case, if you get erro,r then you have to follow a  few steps..
  • Go to: Website → Configuration → Delivery Methods
  • Open your active delivery method (e.g., Free Delivery, Standard Delivery).
  • Under “Payment Methods Allowed,” make sure Cash on Delivery is selected.
  • Now you can see the “Cas on delivery” option, select that & confirm the order.
  • Check the backend to see if the COD order is recorded correctly.

Best Practices for Managing COD Orders in Odoo 19 Website

Preventing Fake Orders

One of the challenges of COD is fake or canceled orders. Use Odoo’s automated workflows to verify customer contact details before confirming delivery.

Setting Limits on COD

Limit COD to specific regions or order values. For example, allow COD only for local deliveries under $200. This helps reduce risks.

Title: How to Create a Custom Screen in Odoo 18 PoS?
Content:
Odoo’s Point of Sale (POS) module is built on top of the OWL (Odoo Web Library) framework, which makes it highly flexible and customizable. In real-world business scenarios, you may need to extend the standard POS flow with custom screens, for example:

  • Showing additional product details.
  • Managing loyalty or rewards programs.
  • Collecting extra customer information before completing an order.

This is where custom screens come into play. In Odoo 18, creating a custom screen in POS follows a structured process that ensures flexibility without compromising on maintainability. Let’s walk through this step by step.

The Process of Adding a Custom Screen

In Odoo 18, adding a new screen to POS follows a structured process:

  1. Extend the Control Buttons to add a new button on the POS product screen.
  2. Register your custom screen in Odoo’s registry under the "pos_screens" category.
  3. Create the screen template (XML) to define its layout and design.
  4. Build the screen logic (JavaScript/OWL Component) to handle interactions, data, and navigation.
  5. Link everything together using this.pos.showScreen("CustomScreen") so the new screen can be displayed on button click.

How the Flow Works

Let’s break down what happens behind the scenes:

1. Button Click

  • User clicks your custom button in the POS product screen.
  • Button has t-on-click="() => this.onClick()".

2. onClick() Triggered

  • The patched ControlButtons class runs onClick().
  • Inside, it calls this.pos.showScreen("CustomScreen").

3. Registry Lookup

  • POS has a registry of all screens (pos_screens).
  • It searches for "CustomScreen".

4. Screen Found & Loaded

  • Your registered OWL component (CustomScreen) is matched.
  • Odoo links it with the XML template (custom_pos.CustomScreen).

5. Rendering the Screen

  • The screen layout is rendered (HTML/XML → UI).
  • User sees your custom design (message, form, table, etc.).

6. Interaction & Logic

  • Any action (buttons, inputs) inside the screen triggers your JS functions.
  • Example: closeCustomScreen() calls this.pos.closeScreen().

7. Back to Main Screen

  • Once finished, POS closes your screen.
  • User returns to the main product screen.

Basic Module Structure

Here’s how your module directory should be structured:

				
					custom_pos/
+-- static/
¦   +-- src/
¦       +-- js/
¦       ¦   +-- custom_button.js
¦       ¦   +-- custom_screen.js
¦       +-- xml/
¦           +-- custom_button.xml
¦           +-- custom_screen.xml
+-- __init__.py
+-- __manifest__.py

This clean, modular setup keeps everything organized and upgrade-safe.

Implementation Steps

Step 1: Creating the Custom Screen Template

The XML file defines the visual structure of your custom screen:

				
					
                   
This is our custom screen

In Odoo POS, XML templates define the visual structure of a screen or component, such as headings, buttons, or containers.

They act like a blueprint for the UI, ensuring the layout follows Odoo’s POS styling and is later connected to logic via JavaScript.

The t-name="custom_pos.CustomScreen" uniquely identifies this template, which will be linked to the corresponding JavaScript component so it can be displayed when triggered in the POS

Step 2: Creating the JavaScript Component

Next, we need a JavaScript component to handle the screen's logic:

				
					import { Component } from "@odoo/owl";
import { _t } from "@web/core/l10n/translation";
import { registry } from "@web/core/registry";
import { usePos } from "@point_of_sale/app/store/pos_hook";
export class CustomScreen extends Component {
   static template = "custom_pos.CustomScreen";
   setup() {
       super.setup();
       this.pos = usePos();
   }
   closeCustomScreen() {
       this.pos.closeScreen();
   }
}
registry.category("pos_screens").add("CustomScreen", CustomScreen);

This component:

  1. Extends Odoo's base Component class
  2. Specifies our XML template as its visual representation
  3. Accesses the POS store via usePos() hook
  4. Includes a method to close the screen (though not currently used in the template)
  5. Registers itself in the POS screens registry

Step 3: Adding a Custom Button to Trigger the Screen

To make our screen accessible, we'll add a button to the POS interface:

Button template (custom_button.xml):

Template Inheritance

We extend the existing point_of_sale.ControlButtons template using t-inherit with extension mode, so we can add our custom button without overriding the whole template.

XPath Targeting

The xpath expression locates the position right after the OrderlineNoteButton, ensuring our new button is inserted in the correct place.

Custom Button Definition

A new <button> element is added with a dynamic class (t-att-class="buttonClass") and an onClick() event handler linked to our JavaScript logic.

Button Content

Inside the button, we include a FontAwesome link icon (fa-link) and the text label “Custom Control Button” for clear identification.

Button JavaScript (custom_button.js)

				
					import { _t } from "@web/core/l10n/translation";
import { ConfirmationDialog } from "@web/core/confirmation_dialog/confirmation_dialog";
import { patch } from "@web/core/utils/patch";
import { ControlButtons } from "@point_of_sale/app/screens/product_screen/control_buttons/control_buttons";
patch(ControlButtons.prototype, {
   onClick() {
       // Open our custom screen
       this.pos.showScreen("CustomScreen");
   },
});

patch → Used to extend or override existing Odoo components without modifying the core code.

import { ControlButtons } → Brings in the POS Control Buttons class so we can add our custom button logic.

this.pos.showScreen("CustomScreen") → Triggers navigation to our newly registered custom screen when the button is clicked

Step 4: Adding the Manifest

We can add manifest like this:

				
					{
   'name': 'Custom POS Screen',
   'version': '18.0.1.0.0',
   'category': 'Point of Sale',
   'summary': 'Adds custom button and screen to POS',
   'description': """
This module adds a custom button to POS that opens a custom screen.
   """,
   'depends': ['point_of_sale'],
   'data': [],
   'assets': {
       'point_of_sale._assets_pos': [
           'create_custom_screen/static/src/js/custom_button.js',
           'create_custom_screen/static/src/js/custom_screen.js',
           'create_custom_screen/static/src/xml/custom_button.xml',
           'create_custom_screen/static/src/xml/custom_screen.xml',
       ],
   },
}
