Title: How to Create a Customized XLSX Report in Odoo 18?
Content:
XLSX report in Odoo 18 are a vital tool for businesses and users who want to go beyond standard reporting and create highly customized, professional Excel outputs tailored to their unique needs. If you’re someone who relies on detailed reporting for operations, finance, purchasing, or analytics, then you’re in the right place. Generating a customized XLSX report not only saves time but also ensures data is presented in a way that is clear, insightful, and aligned with your organization’s goals.

In this blog, we’ll walk you step by step through the process of building a Purchase Order XLSX Report in Odoo 18. Rather than sticking to default layouts, this tutorial focuses on showing you how to manage report design through dynamic data extraction, powerful calculations, and clean formatting techniques. By following along, you’ll see how easily raw data can be converted into polished Excel reports using Odoo’s reporting system integration and a bit of structured code development.

Whether you’re an Odoo developer, an HR or finance manager, or simply someone interested in learning the flexibility of the Odoo framework, this guide will help you take reporting to the next level. With the right approach, you’ll not only gain technical know-how but also explore the ability to deliver reports that drive better decisions and make workflows more efficient.

So, if you’ve been wondering how to transform plain reports into customized, professional XLSX documents in Odoo 18, this blog is your roadmap. 

Ready to build like a pro? Let’s get started!

What is an XLSX Report in Odoo 18?

XLSX reports in Odoo 18 use Python and the xlsxwriter module to generate Excel files. These are ideal for financial, statistical, or printable tabular data that goes beyond the limitations of Qweb.

Functional Goal

The business requirement is to generate a custom Excel report, for example, purchase orders that include:

  • Company branding (logo and name)
  • Line-by-line order details with specific formatting
  • Summary of payments, discounts, taxes, and total
  • Localized currency text

Final polished layout for download/print

Functional Users Involved

  • Procurement Officers – Generate purchase order reports quickly for tracking and record-keeping.
  • Finance Teams – Validate purchase amounts, discounts, and taxes with precise calculations.
  • Auditors – Review well-structured historical records for compliance and transparency.
  • Vendors – Receive clear, professional, and branded PO printouts for easy reference.

Custom XLSX Report in Odoo 18 (purchase order)

				
					import io
import base64
from odoo import models
class PurchaseOrderReport(models.AbstractModel):
	_name = 'report.module name.report_purchase_order_xlsx'
	_inherit = 'report.report_xlsx.abstract'
	def generate_xlsx_report(self, workbook, data, orders):
    	for doc in orders:
        	worksheet = workbook.add_worksheet('Purchase Order XLSX')

				
			
				
						# Define style Formats
        	title_format = workbook.add_format({
            	'bold': True, 'font_size': 18, 'align': 'center',
            	'bg_color': '#d0d0d0', 'border': 1
        	})
        	bg_bordered_text_format = workbook.add_format({
            	'font_size': 11, 'border': 1, 'align': 'top',
            	'bg_color': '#d0d0d0', 'bold': True
        	})
        	bordered_text_format = workbook.add_format({
            	'font_size': 11, 'border': 1, 'align': 'center'
        	})
        	right_align = workbook.add_format({
            	'border': 1, 'font_size': 11, 'align': 'right'
        	})
				
			
				
					# Add Company Logo
        	if doc.company_id.logo or doc.company_id.parent_id.logo:
            	logo_data = io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(
                	doc.company_id.parent_id.logo or doc.company_id.logo
            	))
            	worksheet.insert_image(0, 11, "company_logo.png", {
                	'image_data': logo_data, 'x_scale': 0.5, 'y_scale': 0.5
            	})

				
			
				
					# Report Title
        	worksheet.merge_range(5, 1, 6, 4, 'PURCHASE ORDER', title_format)

				
			
				
					# PO Details
        	worksheet.write(8, 1, 'PO Number:', bold_text_format)
        	worksheet.write(8, 2, doc.name, text_format)
        	worksheet.write(9, 1, 'Date:', bold_text_format)
        	worksheet.write(9, 2, doc.date_order.strftime('%d-%m-%Y'), text_format)

				
			
				
					# Table Headers
        	headers = ["No", "Part Number", "Description", "Qty", "Unit Price", "Discount", "VAT 5%", "Amount"]
        	for idx, header in enumerate(headers):
            	worksheet.write(24, idx + 1, header, bg_bordered_text_format)

				
			
				
					# Table Content
        	row = 25
        	sl_no = 1
        	total_discount = 0.0
        	for line in doc.order_line:
            	worksheet.write(row, 1, sl_no, bordered_text_format)
            	worksheet.merge_range(row, 2, row, 3, line.product_id.name or "", bordered_text_format)
            	worksheet.write(row, 10, line.product_qty, bordered_text_format)
            	worksheet.write(row, 11, f"{line.price_unit:.2f}", right_align)
            	worksheet.write(row, 12, f"{line.discount:.2f}", right_align)
            	worksheet.write(row, 13, "%.2f" % sum(line.taxes_id.mapped('amount')), right_align)
            	worksheet.merge_range(row, 14, row, 15, f"{line.price_subtotal:.2f}", right_align)
            	total_discount += line.discount
            	row += 1
            	sl_no += 1

				
			
				
					# Totals Section
        	worksheet.merge_range(row, 1, row, 11, '*** Payment', bold_left_align)
        	worksheet.merge_range(row, 12, row, 13, 'Gross:', bold_right_align)
        	worksheet.merge_range(row, 14, row, 15, f"{doc.amount_untaxed:.2f}", right_align)
        	worksheet.merge_range(row + 1, 1, row + 1, 11,
            	f"{doc.currency_id.amount_to_text(doc.amount_total)} ONLY",
            	bold_left_align)
        	worksheet.merge_range(row + 5, 12, row + 5, 13, 'Total(AED):', bold_right_align)
        	worksheet.merge_range(row + 5, 14, row + 5, 15, f"{doc.amount_total:.2f}", right_align)

				
			
				
					# Footer
        	worksheet.merge_range(row + 22, 6, row + 22, 10,
            	doc.company_id.parent_id.name or doc.company_id.name,
            	center_bold_text_format)

Register Report Action in XML

<data>
<record id="report_action_purchase_order_xlsx" model="ir.actions.report">
<field name="name">Purchase Order XLSX</field>
<field name="model">purchase.order</field>
<field name="report_type">xlsx</field>
<field name="report_name">module name.report_purchase_order_xlsx</field>
<field name="report_file">module name.report_purchase_order_xlsx</field>
<field name="print_report_name">
(object.state in ('draft', 'sent') and 'Request for Quotation - %s' % (object.name) or
'Purchase Order - %s' % (object.name))
</field>
<field name="binding_model_id" ref="purchase.model_purchase_order"/>
<field name="binding_type">report</field>
<field name="attachment_use" eval="False"/>
</record>
</data>
</odoo>

 This XML registers the report in Odoo and binds it to the purchase.order model.

Title: How to Set Up & Manage Global Discount in Odoo 18 POS?
Content:
Why Learning to Manage Global Discount in Odoo Is a Catalyst for Your Retail Strategy

If you've ever wondered how top-performing retail businesses effortlessly run promotions without confusion at the checkout counter, you're about to discover their mystery. It's not just about cutting prices or running flashy sales; it's about intelligent systems. One of the most effective tools in this domain is the ability to manage global discount in Odoo, especially in the latest Odoo 18 POS system.

Suppose your store is packed with customers during a festive weekend. Customers are lining up. Your staff is busy ringing up purchases. You need to apply a flat 15% discount to every order instantly. Do you stop the line and manually discount each item? Or do you use a single, system-wide adjustment that applies across the bill? That's precisely what the global discount in Odoo 18 enables you to do with just a tap.

This blog explores everything you need to know about setting up and managing global discounts in Odoo 18 POS, and why it's not just a "nice-to-have" but a competitive edge for modern retailers. From configuration to real-time use, and from business benefits to hidden features, we'll take you on a journey into the practical power of Odoo's POS module. 

We'll also discuss how this relates to Odoo POS pricing rules, enabling you to create sophisticated discount strategies. Stay with us because each section discovers something that might change how you run promotions forever.

How to Set Up Discount in Odoo POS Without Breaking a Sweat

When considering how to set up a discount in Odoo POS, the first thing you'll appreciate is how straightforward the system is, yet how deeply customizable it can be if needed. 

Start by enabling the Point-of-Sale module in Odoo 18.

Once it's active, head into your POS Configuration > Settings.

Use the drop down menu at the top to select the POS you want to configure. I’ll select a Bakery Shop.

Then scroll down until you find the ‘Global Discount Option’ under the Pricing Section. Tick (✔) the check box to enable it and click Save. It sounds like a small step, but this single setting opens the door to smart selling.

But setting the feature is just the beginning. The magic lies in creating a discount product, which serves as the logical placeholder that Odoo uses to track the deduction. You define it as a service item, so it doesn't affect your physical inventory. Once linked to your POS, this product becomes the tool that applies global discounts in real-time.

Let’s go back to the POS dashboard & open the Bakery Shop session. Click ‘Open Register’.

Here, you can set the opening cash balance. Then click Open Register again to launch the POS.

Let’s start by adding a few items to the cart. I’ll go ahead and add Cinnamon Roll, Blueberry Muffin, and Pain au Chocolat. Once your items are in the cart click the Actions button.

You’ll see an option called Discount. This button only appears if the global discount feature is enabled. Click on Discount.

After clicking on discount, you’ll notice the 10% default discount automatically applied but you can always change it.

Just delete the current value and enter a new one. Let’s go with 15% & click OK to apply the new discount.

As you can see in the screenshot below, we now have a new line added to the order. That’s the discount we just applied, and it covers the entire sale. Now, let’s go ahead and complete the order. First, select the Customer.

I’ll choose Abigail Peterson for this example.

Next, click on Payment.

Select the payment method, I’ll go with the cash & if the customer asks for an invoice, make sure to enable this option. Then, click Validate to confirm that transaction.

Once it’s completed, you’ll see the receipt with all the order details including the product purchased & the global discount applied.

That’s how you can set up and use the global discount feature in Odoo 18 POS. Remember, this discount applies to the entire order, not individual products.

Now, when your staff launches the POS interface and adds items to the cart, a "Discount" button appears. One tap, a simple entry, say 10%, 15% or 20% and boom: the entire order adjusts itself instantly. No more clicking on each product to enter individual discounts. No more errors or delays. This is Odoo 18 POS global discount in action, and it's beautiful in its simplicity.

Global Discount in Odoo 18: The Overlooked Feature That Changes Everything

At a glance, the global discount in Odoo 18 might seem like just another toggle in your settings, but underestimate it, and you'll miss one of the most impactful pricing tools available in Odoo's ecosystem. It's not just about cutting prices; it's about control. Control over how you position your brand, manage customer expectations, and allow your staff with the tools they need to confidently close sales.

The beauty of global discounts is in their immediacy and uniformity. Whether it's a site-wide flash sale or an end-of-day clearance push, this tool ensures every customer gets the same deal fairly, quickly, and transparently. In a world where customer loyalty hinges on speed and trust, having this level of consistency can make or break a retail business.

Odoo POS Discount Configuration: Where Smart Selling Begins

Digging deeper into Odoo POS discount configuration, you realize it's more than flipping a switch. It's where strategy meets execution. For example, do you want to allow all users to apply discounts, or just your managers? Should the system allow discounts of 5%, 10%, or up to 50%? Are these discounts before or after tax? The configuration options in Odoo 18 POS provide the level of precision you need.

And here's the kicker: Odoo's configuration doesn't just stop at how the discount is applied; it affects how it's reported. Each discount line appears as its entry in the transaction, ensuring clarity in receipts and backend reports. That means when it's time to analyze your sales at the end of the month, you know exactly how much revenue was influenced by your global discount strategies. It's not just about giving away value, it's about understanding the impact.

Odoo 18 Point of Sale Discount Setup: A Potent Tool for Modern Retailers

The Odoo 18 point of sale discount setup offers incredible flexibility for both small and large retailers. Whether you're running a cozy boutique or a chain of outlets across cities, the same system scales with you. One of the best aspects of Odoo is that it offers these robust features without requiring third-party plugins or complex custom code.

Even better, the POS discount setup is part of the broader Odoo ecosystem, which is connected to accounting, inventory, CRM, and marketing. When you apply a discount, it's not just a front-end adjustment; it flows through the financial backend, giving you an accurate picture of profit margins and tax obligations. This unified integration is what makes Odoo more than just a POS; it's an intelligent business management system.

Odoo POS Pricing Rules vs Global Discounts: What's the Difference?

This is where things get interesting. While Odoo POS pricing rules allow you to define advanced discount logic, such as offering a free item after three purchases or providing VIP customers with exceptional prices, global discounts in Odoo 18 offer a more straightforward yet compelling solution. It lets you apply a flat discount to the entire cart without worrying about which products qualify.

So, which one should you use? The real might comes in using both. Suppose your VIP customers automatically receive 10% off selected items via pricing rules, but on top of that, during a flash sale, you offer a 5% global discount across all products. The result? A layered, flexible promotional system that feels personalized to the customer and effective for the business. The key is knowing when to use Odoo POS pricing rules for precision and when to use global discounts for speed and scale.

How to Manage Global Discount in Odoo for Maximum Profit

Knowing how to manage global discounts in Odoo is not just about activating them; it's about getting them. You need to create rules for your team. Who can apply discounts? What's the maximum allowable percentage? What audit trails are in place if someone misuses the feature? Odoo 18 gives you user-level controls to assign permissions. You can restrict discount privileges to specific roles and track who applied for what, and when.

And then there's the analytics. Odoo's backend lets you track discount performance. You can compare revenue with and without discounts, evaluate the most commonly discounted products, and even spot patterns in staff behavior. This changes the global discount from a blunt tool to a surgical instrument in your pricing strategy.

By learning how to manage this feature effectively, you open the ability to test pricing models, respond to market trends, and optimize for margins, all while maintaining a smooth and friendly customer experience.

Secrets Behind the Simplicity of Odoo 18 POS Global Discount

Behind the effortless front-end operation of Odoo 18 POS, there's an intelligent architecture doing the heavy lifting. The way Odoo handles discount logic, separating it as a service item, allows for precise tracking in accounting. The clean interface conceals the complexity behind how it calculates tax, inventory valuation (which remains unchanged, as discounts don't affect quantity), and customer receipts.

And there's more: once you enable global discounts, the system automatically adapts the invoice layout, includes clear labelling on receipts, and logs it in the session reports. Every touchpoint, from cashier to finance department, remains aligned. This is what makes the Odoo 18 point of sale discount setup truly enterprise-grade.

Why You Need to Learn Odoo POS Discount Configuration Now

If you're still applying discounts manually or using outdated systems, you're not only wasting time, but you're also risking revenue and customer trust. Today's customers expect quick checkouts, transparent pricing, and smart offers. Your staff needs tools that are intuitive, fast, and consistent. As a business owner or manager, you need visibility and control.

Learning how to set up a discount in Odoo POS and manage it effectively through proper configuration enables you to gain all of these benefits. It's one of the fastest ways to modernize your sales approach without incurring significant investments.

And with the growing capabilities of Odoo, learning discount management today puts you in the perfect position to implement more complex pricing structures, loyalty systems, or even AI-based promotions in the future. It's not just about selling better today; it's about preparing your business for tomorrow.

How Odoo 18 POS Global Discount Becomes a Competitive Weapon

So now that you've seen what it can do, the only question left is: when will you start? Learning how to manage global discounts in Odoo is more than a technical exercise; it's a strategic shift. It puts your business in a position to scale promotions quickly, reduce human error, and enhance customer satisfaction with every sale.

Whether you're configuring your Odoo POS discount settings for the first time or looking to refine your Odoo POS pricing rules, there's no better time to take action. The global discount in Odoo 18 is your key to opening elegant, data-driven retail management.

And the best part? It's all built into the system you're already using, no extra tools, no additional cost, just pure Odoo management, ready when you are.

Title: How to Manage Different Customer Addresses in Odoo 18?
Content:
Why Managing Customer Addresses in Odoo 18 Is a Catalyst

Suppose running a growing business where each customer has not just one, but several addresses, one for invoicing, another for deliveries, and perhaps a few regional offices. Suddenly, you find your team making frequent mistakes, sending shipments to the wrong location or billing the wrong department. This is where the ability to manage different customer addresses in Odoo 18 becomes a real innovation. Not only does it help organize your customer data more intelligently, but it also improves your order accuracy, reduces errors, and saves time across departments.

With the release of Odoo 18, the system now supports Odoo 18 multiple addresses per customer with increased ease and flexibility. This means your sales, invoicing, and delivery processes no longer have to rely on guesswork or manual re-entry of address details. Each customer record becomes a central hub where every associated address is neatly categorized and ready for use.

What truly makes this functionality stand out is its intuitive nature. You can now configure the customer invoice address and the delivery address in Odoo 18 in just a few clicks. These aren't just data points; they are dynamic components that flow through your sales orders, invoices, delivery slips, and other related documents. This robust feature ensures that businesses, regardless of their size or industry, maintain a professional, precise, and efficient workflow.

But how does this system work internally? How can you master setting up the Odoo sales invoice delivery address without encountering errors? What role do Odoo contact address types play in this? As we delve deeper into this guide, you'll discover how all these elements come together to help you not only manage but completely optimize Odoo customer alternate addresses, turning a once-complex task into a unified process.

Manage Different Customer Addresses in Odoo 18 for Simplified Operations

When it comes to customer management, one-size-fits-all approaches no longer work. Clients today demand precise logistics, error-free invoicing, and region-specific communications. That's why being able to manage different customer addresses in Odoo 18 is not just a feature, it's a necessity. Every business, whether working in wholesale, retail, services, or manufacturing, needs to accommodate clients with multiple locations. And thanks to Odoo 18's advanced contact system, that's now easier than ever.

Odoo's design allows you to assign multiple addresses within a single customer record. Whether it's for delivery, invoicing, or other purposes, these addresses are categorized using Odoo contact address types, so they are instantly recognizable and usable in any workflow. It's a thoughtful structure that eliminates duplication and ensures your customer data is both centralized and accurate.

Once configured, you no longer need to think twice about which address to use when creating a sales order or invoice. Odoo 18 intelligently pulls the correct address based on the address type you selected when setting up your customer. The entire system becomes smarter, faster, and more reliable.

Here’s how you can easily manage different customer addresses in Odoo 18. (If you are interested in knowing how to manage customer ratings in Odoo, you can check our blog on it.)

First, we need to enable this feature. Open the Accounting App.

Go to Configuration > Settings.

Scroll down to the Customer Invoices section & enable the option called Customer Addresses then click Save.

Now, we are ready to assign different addresses to a customer. To do that, go to Customers > Customers.

Open an existing customer or create a new one. In this blog, I will use Deco Addict.

Under the Contacts & Addresses tab, you will see all the associated contacts & addresses for this customer. I have already added an invoice address. Now, let’s create a delivery address. Click the Add button.

This opens the Create Contact home, where you can select the type of address you want to add such as Invoice, Delivery, Contact, Follow-up etc. Here, I can choose Delivery Address, then add a Contact Name like ‘‘Deco’s Delivery Address’’ and fill out other details and click Save & Close.

The new address will appear under the customer’s Contact & Address tab. You can repeat this process to add more contacts & addresses. There is no limit to this. Just add as many as you need depending on your customer structure. 

Now, let’s go to the Sales App.

Create a New Quotation.

Title: What are the Different Types of Removal Strategies in Odoo 18 Inventory?
Content:
Why You Must Know the Types of Removal Strategies in Odoo 18

In the world of supply chain management and inventory, every second and every product matters. That's why businesses are rapidly turning to advanced ERP systems, such as Odoo 18, which offer more innovative, data-driven methods for managing inventory. One of the most effective features that Odoo offers is its removal strategies, a set of rules that determine how products are selected and shipped from warehouses. Understanding the types of removal strategies in Odoo 18 isn't only helpful but also essential for businesses seeking to enhance efficiency, minimize waste, and deliver the right product at the right time.

Suppose a warehouse filled with thousands of items, some nearing their expiry date, some stored deep in the racks, and some that just arrived today. How do you decide what to pick first? This is where the Odoo 18 removal strategies come into play. With options such as FIFO, LIFO, FEFO, closest location, and least packages, Odoo authorizes you to choose the best plan personalized to your business needs. Whether you're managing perishable goods, electronic equipment, or bulk shipments, knowing which strategy fits your workflow can be the catalyst.

In this blog, we will guide you through the most critical types of removal strategies in Odoo 18, explain how each one functions, when to use them, and guide on configuring the removal strategy in Odoo effectively for inventory management. We’ll also delve into the operational intelligence behind methods such as FIFO, LIFO, and FEFO, and explore how Odoo inventory can benefit from these approaches.

Additionally, we'll explore why the closest location removal strategy and the least packages removal strategy in Odoo 18 can provide a significant competitive advantage. Whether you're a warehouse manager, business owner, or Odoo consultant, this is the only topic you can't afford to skip.

FIFO LIFO FEFO Odoo Inventory

The Foundation of Smart Inventory Flow

Let’s begin with the classic trio of FIFO, LIFO, and FEFO, which form the backbone of Odoo 18 removal strategies. Each of these removal methods serves a specific business scenario, and understanding their differences helps you apply the right one when it matters most.

FIFO (First In, First Out) is the most commonly used strategy and often the default in most inventory systems, including Odoo. When using FIFO in Odoo inventory, the system automatically picks the oldest received product first. This method is ideal for fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), food and beverage, and other industries where product freshness is a top priority. By following this approach, you ensure that older items are cleared out first, reducing the risk of deadstock or expired inventory. Odoo makes it simple to apply FIFO to your warehouse by letting you configure it directly at the location level.

In contrast, LIFO (Last In, First Out) is used in industries where newer stock is preferred or where goods are stacked in a way that makes accessing older inventory more difficult. For example, in construction materials or mining equipment storage, accessing the newest stock might make more sense operationally. Odoo supports LIFO even though it's less commonly used for accounting due to regulatory restrictions in many regions. The beauty of Odoo 18's removal strategies is that you can customize them based on operational logic rather than accounting requirements.

Then comes FEFO (First Expiry, First Out), a strategy that’s not only smart but also crucial for enterprises such as those in the cosmetics, pharmaceutical, and food processing industries. When using FEFO in Odoo inventory, the system prioritizes products based on expiry dates rather than the arrival time. This is vital in regulated industries where delivering expired products could have legal or health consequences. With Odoo 18, setting up FEFO is as simple as enabling expiration tracking and assigning it as the removal strategy for specific products or locations.

So, whether it's FIFO, LIFO, or FEFO Odoo inventory, the key takeaway is that each strategy has its role, and Odoo 18 allows you to switch between them effortlessly based on real-world needs.

Odoo Closest Location Removal Strategy

Speed Meets Intelligence

Now let’s shift gears from time-based removal to location-based removal. The Odoo closest location removal strategy is a brilliant feature that enhances picking speed and warehouse efficiency. In large or multi-zone warehouses, the walking distance for warehouse operators is a significant factor. Time is money, and the further the product is from the dispatch area, the longer it takes to process an order.

Using the closest location removal strategy, Odoo 18 evaluates which bin or storage area is physically closest to the packing or shipping zone and prioritizes those locations for picking. This is ideal for operations that prioritize quick deliveries, especially in e-commerce fulfilment centers where high order volumes require speed to be critical.

Configuring this strategy in Odoo is intuitive. You assign picking rules and prioritize them based on proximity to the location. The system takes care of the rest by ensuring that products are picked from the most accessible area, minimizing travel time and boosting productivity.

Least Packages Removal Odoo 18

Smart Logistics with Fewer Boxes

Here’s another clever and often overlooked strategy for package removal in Odoo 18. In many businesses, particularly those handling bulky or packaged items, reducing the number of packages per order can result in substantial cost savings. For instance, fewer boxes mean lower shipping costs, less packaging material, and easier handling.

The least packages removal Odoo 18 strategy instructs the system to prioritize packages that contain the most significant quantity of items or are partially complete, thereby reducing the total number of packages required for an order. This can be a turning point for logistics providers and wholesalers who are continually seeking to optimize packaging and minimize waste.

Once again, Odoo makes it easy to apply. You need to assign the “least packages” method as your removal strategy for specific warehouse zones or products. The result? A more efficient packing process, lower operational costs, and a greener warehouse.

How to Configure Removal Strategy in Odoo Inventory Without Complexity

You may be wondering how to actually configure a removal strategy in Odoo inventory. Luckily, the setup process in Odoo 18 is straightforward and user-friendly, even for non-technical users.

To get started, you first need to enable multi-step routes and storage locations in the inventory settings.

This gives you the flexibility to define specific rules for picking, receiving, and internal transfers. Then, go to the “Configuration” menu and choose the locations where you want to apply the strategy.

Create a New Location.

You’ll see a drop-down menu under the removal strategy section, offering options like FIFO, LIFO, FEFO, closest location, and least packages.

However, here’s the real strength: Odoo allows you to apply different removal strategies for various products, zones, or even scenarios. Would you like to use FEFO for perishable goods and FIFO for non-perishable goods, such as electronics? You can do that. Want to apply the closest location strategy for same-day delivery items and minimize the number of packages for bulk orders? Odoo 18 supports that too.

This modular and flexible approach to configuration makes Odoo one of the best systems for managing diverse warehouse needs with precision and control.

Odoo Inventory Picking Order Strategy

More Than Just Rules

When discussing the Odoo inventory picking order strategy, it’s essential to understand that removal strategies aren’t just fixed rules; they’re part of a broader logic that governs how warehouse operations function. Odoo enables you to define routes, assign priorities, and utilize custom filters to control how picking occurs under specific conditions precisely.

For example, you can form a custom route where items from a temperature-controlled zone are picked only if the ambient zone is out of stock. Or you can configure internal transfers that automatically trigger when one zone is empty. This level of control turns the Odoo inventory picking order strategy into a smart engine that drives both efficiency and adaptability.

The more you explore, the more you realize how effective this system can be when aligned with the proper removal strategies. It’s not just about picking an item; it’s about choosing the correct item from the right place at the right time.

How Different Industries Use Odoo 18 Removal Strategies

Let’s bring theory into the real world. A pharmaceutical distributor might use FEFO to ensure that the oldest drugs (by expiration date) are shipped first, thereby protecting consumers and complying with regulations. At the same time, their general inventory may follow the FIFO method to maintain rotation.

An e-commerce warehouse that processes thousands of orders daily could rely on the closest location removal strategy to minimize picking time and increase throughput. Meanwhile, a wholesale furniture supplier may use the least packages removal strategy in Odoo 18 to optimize container loading and reduce freight costs.

All these industries share one thing: they benefit immensely from the flexibility and dominance of the types of removal strategies in Odoo 18.

Understand the Types of Removal Strategies in Odoo 18 and Take Control of Your Warehouse

If you’ve made it this far, you now understand how crucial it is to implement the right types of removal strategies in Odoo 18. From the timeless logic of FIFO, LIFO, FEFO Odoo inventory to the location-smart Odoo closest location removal strategy and cost-efficient least packages removal Odoo 18, each method has its place in building a lean, responsive, and high-performing warehouse.

Odoo 18 provides you with all the tools to easily configure and apply removal strategies in Odoo inventory, where they matter most. Whether you're looking to improve speed, reduce waste, save money, or stay compliant, the right strategy is already built into your system; you need to activate it.

Title: What Are the Different Location Types in the Odoo 18 Inventory App?
Content:
Location Types in the Odoo Inventory App

Understanding location types in the Odoo Inventory App is essential for anyone managing products, warehouses, or logistics. In Odoo 18, the Inventory module features a well-structured system of location types that help organize the movement of products within a warehouse, their arrival from suppliers, and their shipment to customers. These Odoo 18 inventory location types are designed to provide users with better control over product movements, stock levels, and storage locations.

The use of different location types that Odoo Inventory offers is not just about tracking where goods are placed. These types define the type of movement being recorded. A product coming in from a supplier, a product being produced, or a product being marked as scrap are all treated differently depending on the location type. For example, sending goods to a customer is not the same as moving them to another passageway within the same warehouse. That's why Odoo warehouse location categories help make each movement accurate and traceable.

With Odoo 18, inventory location setup allows you to define various location types, including internal storage, vendor space, customer delivery area, production location, and more. These categories help maintain data consistency and enable automated movements and reporting. When using Odoo's location types, explained through precise classification, you reduce confusion in the warehouse and ensure your inventory accurately reflects actual stock levels.

This guide covers all Odoo 18 storage location types and explains how each type works. We will also review the location type configuration in Odoo Inventory so that users can apply these concepts in their setup. By understanding these settings, you can effectively organize your storage areas, track inventory losses, manage production stock, and consistently plan movements across warehouses.

Vendor and Customer Locations in Odoo 18 Inventory Location Types

The Vendor Location is used when goods are received from a supplier. This is not a physical location in your warehouse but a virtual one used in transactions. When you receive products, Odoo considers them as coming from a vendor location and being stored in your internal warehouse. This is crucial for processing purchase orders and accurately tracking incoming products.

On the other hand, the Customer Location works in the opposite direction. When you deliver products to your clients, the stock moves from an internal location to a customer location. Just like vendor locations, customer locations are virtual and help indicate that the goods have left your warehouse and are now with the buyer. This helps maintain accurate records of what stock is still in your possession and what has been delivered.

Both vendor and customer locations are part of the Odoo 18 inventory location types and play a significant role in external product movements. These location types do not affect your internal stock valuation but help in understanding how much product has moved in or out of the business.

Internal Locations in Different Location Types of Odoo Inventory

The Internal Location is the most common type among the different location types Odoo Inventory includes. These are used to represent actual physical spaces inside your company. Examples include shelves, stockrooms, loading areas, and packing zones. Any product in your warehouse that is included in your inventory valuation must be assigned to an internal location.

You can create multiple internal locations and organize them in a hierarchical format. For instance, a warehouse may contain passageways, and each passageway may have shelves. This helps in tracking the exact physical position of products. During the Odoo 18 inventory location setup, you can also assign parent-child relationships to organize these spaces logically.

Internal locations are also used in transfers. If a product is moved from one shelf to another, the system records that movement between two internal locations. In production, raw materials may be sourced from an internal location and transported to a designated production area. These internal categories are crucial for managing daily operations and handling products effectively.

Transit Locations in Odoo Warehouse Location Categories

One of the functional Odoo warehouse location categories is the Transit Location. This location type is used when a product is being moved between warehouses or during specific delivery methods, such as drop-shipping. For example, suppose you have two warehouses in different cities and want to transfer stock from one to the other. In that case, the products will move from one internal location to a transit location before arriving at the second warehouse.

Transit locations help maintain visibility on where the stock currently is. Although it is not physically located in either of the two warehouses, it has still not been delivered. So, using this virtual location keeps the record clear. This is especially useful in multi-warehouse businesses where inter-location movements are frequent.

In Odoo 18, storage location types often utilize transit locations in conjunction with specific routes or rules. Once configured, Odoo can automatically assign a transit location during transfers, allowing you to track shipments without requiring manual updates.

Scrap and Inventory Loss Locations in Odoo 18 Inventory Location Setup

Scrap and inventory loss are two Odoo 18 inventory location types used when stock needs to be removed from the available inventory. The Scrap Location is used when products are damaged, expired, or unusable. When a product is scrapped, it is moved to this location and removed from active inventory. However, the record is still kept for reporting or auditing purposes.

The Inventory Loss Location is used when there is a difference between expected and actual stock levels. During inventory adjustments, if a product is missing or extra, the system records this change by adjusting the inventory balance accordingly, either by moving the difference to or from the inventory loss location. This makes sure that any mismatch is documented clearly.

These two types are necessary in the location type configuration of Odoo Inventory, as they ensure that your stock levels remain accurate even in the event of unexpected changes. Without these, your system may display incorrect figures, which can impact reports and purchasing decisions.

Production and Procurement Locations in Odoo Location Types Explained

For businesses involved in manufacturing, the Production Location is a crucial component of the Odoo 18 storage location types. This represents the area where production activities take place. Raw materials are moved from internal locations to the production location. Once the manufacturing is complete, the finished goods are moved out of the production area and into a storage location or delivery zone.

This type of location helps separate manufacturing processes from general storage. It also helps in tracking the usage of basic or raw materials and the output of finished products. If your company uses the Manufacturing module, setting up a production location during your Odoo 18 inventory location setup is essential.

Another location type used behind the scenes is the Procurement Location. This is not something most users interact with directly, but it is used in automated procurement rules. When stock levels drop below a certain level, Odoo may use this location type to trigger a purchase or manufacturing order. It helps connect procurement rules with actual product movement.

Both these location types are part of Odoo warehouse location categories that support advanced operations and workflows.

Using Odoo 18 Storage Location Types in Real Scenarios

Let's consider a business scenario that uses many Odoo 18 storage location types. A company receives products from multiple suppliers. These goods arrive and are recorded as moving from a vendor location into a receiving zone, which is an internal location. After quality checks, they are placed in storage racks, again represented by internal locations.

If the company assembles products, raw materials are moved into a production location. After the product is made, it is packed and stored in a dispatch zone. When an order is fulfilled, the product is transferred from the dispatch area (internal) to the customer's location. If a product becomes damaged during the process, it is relocated to the scrap area. During an inventory audit, any missing products are recorded in the location where the inventory loss occurred.

This example illustrates how each of the different location types supported by Odoo Inventory enables specific actions. Assigning the correct type to each location ensures that product tracking, accounting, and reports remain accurate and up-to-date. It also reduces the need for manual corrections and improves data reliability.

Location Type Configuration Odoo Inventory: How to Set Up in the System

To set up the location type configuration in Odoo Inventory, users must first activate certain features. In the Inventory module settings, enable "Storage Locations" and "Multi-Step Routes." This permits you to create and manage multiple location types.

Next, go to Configuration > Locations.

Here, you can create a new location by assigning it a name, selecting a parent if necessary, and specifying its location type. The options include Vendor, Customer, Internal, Transit, Production, Scrap, and Inventory Loss.

You can also apply specific rules to each location. For example, a scrap location may be excluded from valuation, or an internal location may follow a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) removal strategy. These rules facilitate daily stock management and are integral to setting up proper Odoo 18 inventory locations.

Keeping location names clear and organized helps warehouse staff understand where each product should be placed and where it will be next. For example, naming conventions like WH/Stock/ShelfA make navigation and reporting easier.

Understanding Location Types in the Odoo 18 Inventory App

The location types in the Odoo Inventory App are essential for defining how goods move across the supply chain. By utilizing all available Odoo 18 inventory location types, businesses can track product movement, enhance stock accuracy, and minimize inventory confusion. Each type, from vendor and customer to internal and production, has a specific role in daily operations.

Setting up the right different location types in Odoo Inventory ensures clear records and logical workflows. Whether it is a manufacturing unit with production locations or a retail warehouse with internal and customer locations, each business benefits from defining the correct Odoo warehouse location categories.

With the proper Odoo 18 inventory location setup, you can create a structured system for managing stock. The correct use of Odoo location types, as explained here, supports better stock control and provides reliable data. By using all relevant Odoo 18 storage location types, businesses can create clear pathways for their products from arrival to delivery.

For any organization looking to apply these settings efficiently, a proper understanding of the location type configuration in Odoo Inventory is necessary. If you are using Odoo or planning to implement it, setting up location types correctly should be one of the first steps in organizing your inventory process.

Title: How to Fix Flutter Gradle Build Failed Errors?
Content:
If you've ever Fix Flutter Gradle Build Failed Errors in the app and seen the dreaded "Gradle Build Failed" error appear in your terminal, don't worry, you're definitely not alone.

This is one of the most common roadblocks Flutter developers face when building Android projects. The frustrating part is that it can appear suddenly, even if your code was working perfectly a moment ago.

The good news? It's almost always fixable. With a few systematic checks and adjustments, you can get your Flutter project building again in no time.

In this guide, we'll walk through the most common causes of Gradle build failures and step-by-step solutions to resolve them efficiently.

Common Causes of Fix Flutter Gradle Build Failed Errors

Gradle is the build system that Fix Flutter Gradle Build Failed Errors by compiling and packaging Android apps. When it fails, the issue typically lies in configuration, compatibility, or the environment setup. Below are the most frequent causes developers encounter:

Outdated or mismatched Gradle versions 

When Flutter and Android Gradle plugin versions don't align, the build can't proceed.

Corrupted cache files 

Temporary files or cached dependencies can become corrupted, causing resource-loading issues.

Incompatible dependencies

Plugins or libraries may not be compatible with the current versions of Gradle, Kotlin, or Flutter.

Missing SDKs or build tools

If Flutter can't detect the required Android SDKs, the build process halts.

Network interruptions

Unstable connections or blocked repositories cause timeouts when Gradle attempts to download dependencies.

Misconfigured project files 

Typos or incorrect plugin versions in the build.gradle, settings. Gradle, or the gradle-wrapper.properties file, can completely halt the build.

Every developer eventually faces these issues, even experienced ones. The key to solving them is a calm, structured approach.

Steps to Fix Flutter Gradle Build Failed Errors

To fix Flutter Gradle Build Failed Errors, follow these solutions in order, starting with the simplest fixes and progressing to the more advanced ones.

1. Clean and Rebuild the Project

Sometimes, a clean build is all you need.

Open your terminal and run:

				
					flutter clean
flutter pub get
flutter build apk

2. Check Internet Connection

Ensure you have a stable internet connection. Gradle might fail while downloading dependencies.

3. Upgrade Flutter and Dependencies

Make sure you're using the latest Flutter SDK and compatible packages.

				
					flutter upgrade
flutter pub outdated
flutter pub upgrade

				
			
				
					Also, update your compileSdkVersion, targetSdkVersion, and dependencies in android/app/build.gradle.

4. Delete and Rebuild Gradle Cache

Corrupted caches can cause build failures.

				
					Delete the .gradle and build folders:
rm -rf android/.gradle
rm -rf build

5. Use a Compatible Gradle Version

Mismatched Gradle versions are another major source of build errors.

Edit your android/build.gradle file to use a stable version:

				
					dependencies {
    classpath 'com.android.tools.build:gradle:7.4.2'
}

Also, check your gradle-wrapper.properties:

				
					distributionUrl=https://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-7.5-all.zip

Make sure your Gradle version matches your Android Gradle Plugin version.

Tip: Always refer to the official Android Gradle Plugin and Gradle version compatibility table for accurate pairings.

6. Enable Multidex (If Needed)

If your project includes many dependencies or exceeds the 64K method limit, you’ll need to enable Multidex to allow more methods in your app.

In android/app/build.gradle:

				
					defaultConfig {
    ...
    multiDexEnabled true
}

And add this to dependencies:

				
					implementation 'androidx.multidex:multidex:2.0.1'

This setting helps large projects compile successfully.

You can also check our blog on “How to Implement Rating Bar in Flutter?”

7. Set JDK Version Properly

Make sure your system is using a supported Java version. Flutter supports JDK 17+ for recent versions.

You can set it manually:

				
					
export JAVA_HOME=/path/to/your/jdk

Alternatively, you can use Android Studio's built-in JDK (recommended for most setups).

Using an unsupported or older JDK often results in build script failures or “Unsupported major.minor version” to Fix Flutter Gradle Build Failed Errors.

8. Check Proguard or Shrink Resources

If you're using ProGuard, ensure that your proguard-rules.pro file isn't causing issues. You can temporarily disable minification:

				
					minifyEnabled false
shrinkResources false

Once the build succeeds, you can re-enable them and adjust your Proguard rules accordingly.

9. Use --stacktrace for More Info

Run the build with stacktrace enabled to get more details:

				
					flutter build apk --stacktrace

This prints a complete error trace in your console, showing exactly where and why the build failed.
You can search the specific error message on GitHub, Stack Overflow, or Flutter’s issue tracker to find an existing solution.

Extra Tips To Fix Flutter Gradle Build Failed Errors Environment

  • Use the latest stable channel by switching to the Flutter channel stable.
  • Avoid mixing plugin versions - update all dependencies together to maintain consistency.
  • Reinstall Android SDK if Gradle can't locate build tools or platform files.
  • Check environment variables like JAVA_HOME and ANDROID_HOME.
  • Restart Android Studio after every Gradle or plugin update.

These small housekeeping steps prevent recurring build issues and maintain a stable environment.

For best implementation and fixing easily these kind of errors you can contact Netilligence.

Your Flutter Build Should Never Fail Again

The appearance to Fix Flutter Gradle Build Failed Errors in your Flutter console during testing becomes frustrating when you are working on a new feature. The actual problem behind most build failures turns out to be less complicated than what appears at first glance.

Begin by cleaning your project and then check for Flutter updates and confirm your Gradle versions. The next step involves checking for absent SDK components and checking dependency versions and build file configurations.

Every solution you implement to Fix Flutter Gradle Build Failed Errors makes your Flutter build process more understandable while simultaneously resolving the problem.

You can find help from the Flutter community through Stack Overflow and GitHub Issues and the Flutter Dev Forums when you have exhausted all other troubleshooting options. The Flutter community maintains high activity levels because numerous users have solved identical problems.

Your Flutter development workflow will remain productive and smooth when you combine patience with persistence and the correct approach to solve Gradle Build Failed errors.

Title: How to Set Up Odoo 17 Development Environment Using Pycharm on Ubuntu 22.04
Content:
Odoo's latest update, Version 17, is renowned for its extensive features, complementing the software's capabilities in efficient business management.
In this version, backend development utilises Python 3.10 or higher, while PostgreSQL serves as the database server, and JavaScript supports the frontend development.

PyCharm on Ubuntu 22.04, a Long-Term Support (LTS) release, ensures continuous application updates and vital security patches for five years following its initial release. It also introduces new versions of the Linux kernel and enhancements to graphics drivers through regular software updates, typically issued every six months. Notably, Ubuntu 22.04 comes pre-installed with Python 3.10 as its default version.

In this blog, we will explore the utilisation of the PyCharm on Ubuntu 22.04 to establish a comprehensive Odoo 17 development.


Let's get into it.

Step 1: Download and Install the Pycharm IDE

You can install PyCharm using the following instructions.
* Open Terminal and then execute the following commands one by one:

				
					sudo apt-get update 
sudo apt-get upgrade
sudo snap install pycharm-community --classic

Step 2: Install Web Dependencies

Odoo 17 relies on several web-related dependencies to ensure the smooth functioning of its front-end and back-end components. These include Git, Python packages, and additional tools like Node.js for asset management. Here’s how to install these:

Run the following commands to install the necessary dependencies:

				
					sudo apt install -y git python3-pip python-dev python3-dev libxml2-dev libxslt1-dev zlib1g-dev libsasl2-dev libldap2-dev build-essential libssl-dev libffi-dev libmysqlclient-dev libjpeg-dev libpq-dev libjpeg8-dev liblcms2-dev libblas-dev libatlas-base-dev
sudo apt install -y npm
sudo ln -s /usr/bin/nodejs /usr/bin/node
sudo npm install -g less less-plugin-clean-css
sudo apt-get install -y node-less

Step 3: Install the wkhtmltopdf

To make the Prints and Reports, Odoo 17 necessitates a version of wkhtmltopdf that surpasses 0.12.2.
Wkhtmltopdf is utilized for converting HTML content into PDF files utilising Qt webkit.
To proceed, install the following commands:

				
					sudo wget https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/releases/download/0.12.5/wkhtmltox_0.12.5-1.bionic_amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i wkhtmltox_0.12.5-1.bionic_amd64.deb
sudo apt install -f

Moreover, are you interested in knowing how to install Odoo 18 on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS?, Then you can check our blogs on it too.

Step 4: Install PostgreSQL

Installs both the PostgreSQL server and the PostgreSQL client. If both are installed, you can skip the command below.

				
					sudo apt install postgresql postgresql-client

You will now need to create a PostgreSQL user to manage the PostgreSQL database server. In our instance, we'll create a PostgreSQL user with the same name as the system user created earlier, which is "odoo17."

				
					sudo su - postgres
createuser --createdb --username postgres --no-createrole --no-superuser --pwprompt odoo17

The username and password are required for the configuration file. Make sure you note it somewhere for configuring the file. PostgreSQL utilises a separate system user to execute tasks. To switch to this user, execute the "sudo su -postgres" command. After that, you can create a database user specifically for Odoo 17.

				
					psql
ALTER USER odoo17 WITH SUPERUSER;

Executing the above command will grant the user superuser access rights. Afterwards, it's advisable to log out of both Postgres and PSQL.

				
					q 
exit

Step 5: Get Odoo 17 Development Source Code

You can obtain the Odoo 17 development Community source code directly from Odoo's GitHub repository. Alternatively, you can clone it from Git. First, ensure you have Git installed, and then proceed by running the following commands:

				
					sudo apt-get install git

The following command will clone the Odoo code into a directory named "Odoo17" within your home directory:

				
					git clone https://www.github.com/odoo/odoo --depth 1 --branch 17.0 --single-branch odoo17

Step 6: Accessing the Odoo Project in PyCharm

We have now successfully installed PyCharm and cloned Odoo 17 development.
Now, it's time to configure Odoo17 in PyCharm.
Launch PyCharm and navigate to the Odoo 17 development directory.

NOTE:

Suppose a dialogue box appears for creating a virtual environment after the project is opened. However, since we'll be creating the virtual environment via the terminal, you can cancel it.

 To access the terminal, either click on the icon depicted below or use the shortcut Alt + F12.

 Execute the commands provided below to create a virtual environment (venv) using Python 3.10:

				
					curl -sS https://bootstrap.pypa.io/get-pip.py | python3.10
sudo apt install python3.10-venv
python3.10 -m venv your_venv_name

Close and reopen the terminal after executing the above commands to check whether the virtual environment is activated.
If activated, you can see the indicator as displaying the name of your virtual environment in parentheses.

If the previous command does not activate your virtual environment, you can utilise the following command:

				
					Source your_venv_name/bin/activate

Note: Do the next step after activating the virtual environment, ie within the virtual environment

Step 7: Installing Necessary Python Packages

You need to execute the following command in the terminal to install the necessary Python packages required by Odoo, which are listed in the "requirements.txt" file within the "Odoo17 development" directory:

				
					pip install -r requirements.txt

If you encounter any errors during the installation process, you can individually install each requirement listed in the "requirements.txt" file using the following command:

				
					pip install requirement_name

In most cases, when installing packages that are specified twice, only one of them should be installed. Therefore, even if one of them fails to install, it should not be a significant issue.

You can also check our blog on How to Install Odoo 19 on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS

Step 8: Generate the odoo.conf File in the Odoo 17 Development Directory

To create the configuration file, follow these steps:

  1. Right-click on the directory.
  2. Select "New" -> "File" -> "odoo.conf".
  3. Insert the following block into the "odoo.conf" file.
  4. Update the db_password field with the password you specified for the database user "Odoo17" in the previous step.
				
					[options]
admin_passwd = admin
db_host = localhost
db_port = 5432
db_user = odoo17
db_password = your_password
addons_path = /home/user/odoo17/addons
xmlrpc_port = 8017

To update the addons_path value with the actual path to the "Odoo 17 development" addons directory, follow these steps:

  1. Navigate to the addons directory.
  2. Press Ctrl + Shift + C to copy the path to the current directory.
  3. Replace the placeholder value in the addons_path parameter in the "odoo.conf" file with the copied path.
				
					eg: addons_path = /home/user/odoo/addons, /home/user/odoo/custom_addons

Step 9: Add Python Interpreter

Go to Settings -> Project: odoo17 -> Python Interpreter to configure a Python interpreter.

When you open the mentioned window, if the interpreter (Python 3.10 from the Odoo17 virtual environment) is already configured, no changes are necessary. However, if it's not set up, follow these steps:

Select the "Add Interpreter" option.

Navigate to the location where the Python interpreter from the Odoo17 virtual environment is located.

Choose the interpreter and confirm the selection.

Step 10: Add Project Configuration in Pycharm

To configure the settings, navigate to "Edit Configurations" under the "Current File" menu.

When the dialogue box appears, as shown below, click the "+" button and choose "Python" from the list.

Afterwards, you can fill in the fields as depicted in the image below.

Name: Provide any desired name for the configuration.

Python Interpreter: Ensure that the Python interpreter is included for this project, which should auto-populate if previously set up.

Script Path: Select the "odoo-bin" file from the "odoo17" directory.

Parameters: Add necessary parameters for script execution, including the required "-c" parameter and any additional parameters as needed. Additionally, include the path to the configuration file.

Working directory: Specify the location of the project's current working folder.

Step 11: Testing Odoo 17 Development

With Odoo's setup complete, it's time to test it out. Simply click the button below to launch the project and see it in action.

Now, you can test localhost:8017 in your web browser. If all your configurations were successful, the Odoo database management interface will open, resembling the image below.

This is how Ubuntu 22.04 users may set up an Odoo 17 Pycharm development environment.

For better implementation, you can easily contact our team as well.

Now you're set to build with Odoo 17 Development!

By following this guide, you’ve successfully set up a development environment for Odoo 17 PyCharm on Ubuntu 22.04. This environment will serve as a foundation for developing, customizing, and extending Odoo’s functionality to meet your business needs.

With this setup in place, you're now ready to explore Odoo 17's powerful features and build custom applications. 

Happy coding!

Title: How to Change UoM & Packaging in Odoo 19 Sales?
Content:
In this guide, you will learn how to change UoM and Packaging in Odoo 19 Sales, step by step. Understanding UoM and Packaging in Odoo 19 Sales is critical because it ensures your inventory, pricing, and delivery workflows stay consistent. Many businesses struggle to set the proper units of measure in Odoo 19 or to unify their UoM and packaging logic in Odoo 19. Still, with the appropriate setup, Odoo 19 offers a much more streamlined, flexible approach than earlier versions. In this article, we cover several key topics related to Odoo 19, including UoM change, packaging setup, product UoM configuration, sales packaging management, and changing product UoM in sales orders.

You'll walk away confident in configuring unified UoM and packaging Odoo 19, and you'll see how to apply those configurations to your sales orders.

Why UoM and Packaging Matter in Sales

Before steps, it's worth understanding why proper UoM and Packaging in Odoo 19 Sales is so critical:

  • If your sales orders use incorrect UoM, you risk shipping wrong quantities or mispricing orders.
  • Packaging definitions ensure that when you deliver goods, the system understands how many base units are inside a "package."
  • In Odoo 19, the packaging and UoM models are more tightly integrated so that a misconfiguration can propagate errors across inventory, purchase, and delivery.  
  • Having a correct product UoM configuration in Odoo 19 ensures your internal stock, sales, and purchase flows remain coherent.

Thus, by mastering UoM and Packaging in Odoo 19 Sales, you solidify the backbone of your order-to-delivery chain.

Key Changes in Odoo 19: Combined UoM & Packaging

Odoo 19 introduces a more unified model: Units of Measure (UoM) and packaging models are merged into a single, simplified structure.  

Here's what changes bring:

  • No separate UoM categories or packaging models in the old sense, you now manage things more fluidly.
  • You can define multi-level packages and let Odoo apply conversion logic automatically.
  • When creating a sales order, you can pick packaging options directly on the line, and Odoo will compute how many base units are needed.

These changes make Odoo 19 packaging setup and Odoo 19 sales packaging management much more intuitive, provided you set things up correctly.

Even Retail Stores can easily manage sales and Inventory with Odoo ERP.

Step-by-Step: How to Change UoM and Packaging in Odoo 19 Sales

In this section, we'll walk through the exact steps. Use these subtitles to jump:

  1. Activate UoM & Packaging in settings
  2. Configure base UoMs
  3. Define packaging types
  4. Assign packaging to products
  5. Using packaging in sales orders (i.e., change UoM in sales)
  6. Validate and adjust

1. Activate UoM & Packaging in Settings

To begin with, you must enable the features:

  • Go to Inventory → Configuration → Settings
  • Under the Products section, tick Product Packagings (or UoM & Packaging / Packagings)
  • Click Save

With packaging enabled, Odoo unlocks the packaging configuration fields on product forms and in the sales order lines.

2. Configure Base UoMs

Though Odoo 19 simplifies the model, you still need to define base units and conversion logic:

  • Direct to Inventory → Configuration → Units & Packagings.
  • Here, you'll see a simplified list rather than categories; you can create new UoMs
  • When you define a unit, you specify its ratio relative to the base reference unit (e.g., "Box of 20" = 20 × base unit)
  • Because UoM and packaging are unified, every unit you define can act both as a simple unit measure or a package unit.
  • Use rounding precision to control the smallest increment for that UoM.

This step ensures Odoo knows how to convert between different units when needed.

3. Define Packaging Types

This is where you tie packaging options to your products:

  • Open Inventory → Products → Product Packagings OR you can define packaging inside the product form.
  • Create a new packaging record:
  • • Name (e.g., "Pack of 6")
  • • Contained quantity (e.g. 6)
  • • Unit of Measure (select the UoM you defined)
  • • Sales checkbox (if you want this packaging in sales orders)
  • • Purchase checkbox (if supplier packaging)
  • Optionally, define the barcode, company, or specific routes if the packaging has its own logistics flow.
  • Save the packaging record.

These packaging definitions will appear later when you assign them to products or select packaging in a sales order.

4. Assign Packaging to Products

Next, assign the packaging options to individual products:

  • Go to Inventory → Products → Products
  • Open a product (or create a new one)
  • Under the Inventory tab, scroll to the Packaging section
  • Click Add a line
  • Choose your packaging (e.g., "Pack of 6"), set the Contained Quantity, and indicate whether it's for sales or purchase use.
  • If needed, expand "additional options" to show fields like routes, barcode, company, etc.
  • Save the product

Now that the packaging options are tied to the product, they'll appear in sales and purchase lines automatically.

5. Using Packaging in Sales Orders (Changing UoM in Sales)

This is the crucial step where changing the product UoM in the sales order in Odoo 19 comes alive:

  • Go to Sales → Orders → Quotations / Sales Orders.
  • Create a new SO or open an existing one.
  • Add a product line in Order Lines.
  • You will see a Packaging field next to or under the product line, select the packaging option (e.g., "Pack of 6")
  • The Quantity you enter will now be interpreted in packaging units, and Odoo will automatically compute the number of base units. For example, 3 * Pack of 6 = 18 base units
  • Pricing may be adjusted automatically based on packaging vs unit pricing.
  • You can change the packaging or revert to the base unit if desired.

This is how UoM and Packaging in Odoo 19 Sales come into active use; you essentially change the unit representation in the sales flow by picking the packaging.

6. Validate, Deliver & Adjust

After confirming the sales order:

  • The Delivery Order generated will reflect the correct number of base units and packaging mix
  • You can reserve either complete or partial packaging, depending on your current stock levels.
  • Validate the delivery, and Odoo will track the movement correctly
  • On the accounting side, the invoice will reflect the correct quantities and unit prices

If you ever need to change UoM mid-process, you can go back to the line and adjust packaging or units; Odoo will recalculate accordingly.

Common Scenarios & Tips

Scenario: Selling in Bulk but Storing in Single Units

You might sell in "Box of 12" but store and track in single units. In Odoo 19, you can:

  • Define "Box of 12" packaging
  • In the sales order, set packaging = “Box of 12,” quantity = 5 → Odoo will deliver 60 units
  • Internally, your inventory always remains in base units.

Scenario: Mixed Packaging & Partial Deliveries

Odoo 19 supports partial packaging reservation:

  • If only 20 units are available but your packaging is 24, you can still deliver 20 units if Reserve Partial Packagings is enabled in product categories.

Best Practices & Tips

  • Always maintain your base unit (e.g., "Unit / pc") as the core reference and let packaging build up from that.
  • Use rounding precision cautiously to avoid ending with fractional quantities.
  • When defining pricing, define both unit price and packaging price (if applicable)
  • Use barcodes on packaging types so scanning a package pulls the correct quantity.
  • Test with dummy products and sales orders before switching to live.
  • Train your sales & warehouse teams on the difference between quantity and packaging units.

A community tip:

"Keep the base UoM as pcs but use the packaging feature. Create a package case with its quantity. Then, in POS or Sales, scanning the package pulls the correct quantity."

Troubleshooting & Common Pitfalls

  

Issue

Cause

Solution

The packaging field is not visible on the sales order

Feature not enabled in settings

Go to Inventory → Settings → enable Product Packagings

UoM conversion appears wrong

Unit ratios or rounding are misconfigured

Check your units of measure definitions and ratios

Packaging is not showing on the product

Packaging not assigned to that product

Edit product → Inventory tab → add packaging lines

Sales order shows weird quantities

Mixing incompatible UoMs

All UoMs must be convertible (in the same measure)

Delivery shows the wrong count

Packaging reservation logic

Enable or adjust Reserve Partial Packagings in product categories

 

If you encounter unexpected behaviour, review your unit definitions and packaging assignments first; almost 90% of issues stem from misaligned UoMs or missing packaging links.

At Netilligence, we've configured UoM and Packaging for many clients across Oman, the UAE, and beyond. We understand the subtle pitfalls and best practices when implementing UoM and Packaging in Odoo 19 Sales.

  • We train your team so they get the difference between the base unit and the packaging
  • We provide ongoing support for sales, inventory, and reporting
  • We optimise workflows so your sales packaging management and product UoM configuration always stay accurate

When you choose us, you're not just getting a consultation; you're getting a partner who ensures your ERP drives real business value.

Summary & Final Advice

Mastering UoM and Packaging in Odoo 19 Sales pays dividends across your inventory, sales, and logistics. By following these steps:

  1. Enable features in settings
  2. Define base UoMs
  3. Create packaging types
  4. Assign packaging to products
  5. Use packaging in sales orders (changing UoM)

Title: What Is Odoo 18 PLM Module & How Does It Benefit Manufacturers?

What Is the Odoo 18 PLM Module?

The Odoo-18 PLM Module (Product Lifecycle Management) is part of Odoo's manufacturing suite, helping companies manage the full lifecycle of their products, from design and engineering to production and maintenance.

This module enables real-time collaboration between engineering, manufacturing, and quality departments. By centralising product information and tracking changes with a complete version history, it ensures that everyone is constantly working with the latest data.

Unlike traditional Product Lifecycle Management systems, which require expensive integrations, the Odoo-18 Product Lifecycle Management Module is fully integrated into the Odoo ecosystem. That means you can connect it directly with Odoo Manufacturing, Inventory, and Quality modules without leaving the same platform.

Key Benefits at a Glance:

  • Whole integration with Odoo Manufacturing
  • Real-time product updates and document synchronisation
  • Complete version control for the manufacturing Odoo process
  • Clear traceability of all engineering changes
  • Enhanced collaboration and faster approvals

Along with the Odoo-18 Product Lifecycle Management Module, manufacturers can also benefit from other advanced Odoo-18 applications. Learn more in our post on Odoo 18 Modules Every Manufacturing Company Should Use.

Core Odoo 18 PLM Module Features

The Odoo 18 PLM Module features are designed to make life easier for engineers, production teams, and managers. Below are the standout functions that make it one of the most valuable tools in Odoo 18's manufacturing environment.

1. Centralised Product Data Management

With Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) in Odoo-18, all product details, including technical specifications, drawings, CAD files, and notes, are stored in a unified database. Teams can access or update the same information from anywhere, ensuring consistency.

This not only improves transparency but also reduces the risk of using outdated product information in production.

 2. Engineering Change Orders (ECOs)

The Odoo-18 engineering change order system is one of the most powerful tools in the Product Lifecycle Management module. It allows you to propose, review, and approve product design changes systematically.

Each ECO tracks:

  • The reason for the change
  • The affected Bill of Materials (BOM)
  • The responsible team or engineer
  • Approval history and comments

With built-in stage management (such as "New," "In Progress," and "Approved"), your change process remains transparent and traceable. This makes the Odoo-18 Product Lifecycle Management Module invaluable for manufacturers working under strict compliance requirements.

3. Version Control in Manufacturing

Manufacturing often requires multiple design versions before reaching the final approved product. The version control feature in Odoo lets you manage these iterations effortlessly.

Every update, from materials to component design, is tracked as a new version. You can always compare past versions, restore earlier configurations, or view who made the last modification. This reduces production mistakes and guarantees consistency across product releases.

4. Odoo 18 BOM Versioning

The Odoo-18 BOM versioning feature lets you maintain multiple versions of your Bill of Materials. When a design change occurs, you can create a new BOM version instead of replacing the existing one.

This ensures:

  • Smooth product transition from old to new models
  • Historical tracking of materials used
  • Precise cost analysis for each version

Combined with ECO tracking, the Odoo-18 Product Lifecycle Management Module provides complete lifecycle visibility from design to Manufacturing.

  • Product specifications
  • Manufacturing process sheets
  • Compliance certificates

1. Obtain Faster Approval  

The system enables users to create change requests and add designs, which then proceed to approval without needing email or spreadsheet management. The ECO thread maintains all communication records while managers receive immediate alerts about new updates.

2. Synchronized BOM and Routing

The approval of an ECO triggers automatic updates to both the BOM and routing information. The system eliminates the need for manual duplication work, thereby reducing coordination time and minimising production errors.

3. Better Team Collaboration

Odoo-18 uses Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) to connect engineers with production staff and quality control personnel through a unified system. Real-time system updates enable teams to work more efficiently, which results in shorter production times and improved product accuracy.

4. Real-Time Version Tracking

Since every product design version is recorded, you always have a digital trail of what changed, when, and why. This is essential for industries that must comply with ISO or FDA regulations.

5. Improved Quality and Compliance

With controlled engineering changes and full version traceability, production quality improves naturally. Manufacturers can prove compliance and respond quickly to audits or customer inquiries.
