What’s more, you can set up the system to automate feedback requests Odoo, so no one forgets to ask clients for their thoughts. And with Odoo customer satisfaction tracking, you have everything in one place to monitor results and see the bigger picture. That’s why learning how to collect customer ratings in Odoo is not just a technical step; it’s a practical move that changes how you understand your projects.

Understanding Odoo 18 Customer Ratings

When we talk about Odoo 18 customer ratings, we are referring to a simple way of gathering opinions directly from clients inside the same platform where you manage your projects. Instead of relying on random emails or separate surveys, ratings are built into the project flow. Clients can rate their experience quickly, and the results show up for managers to review.

This process matters because it adds clarity. With ratings, project managers know how satisfied the client is at every stage. When you collect customer ratings in Odoo, you bring consistency to the feedback process, and the data is available whenever you need it.

Project Feedback in Odoo and Why It Matters

Feedback is often the bridge between what was delivered and how it was received. With project feedback in Odoo, you are not waiting until the end of a contract to ask if the customer is happy. Instead, you ask along the way. If something is not going well, you find out earlier, not later.

By doing this, businesses reduce misunderstandings and improve trust. When you collect customer ratings in Odoo, the message to clients is clear: “Your opinion is important, and we want to hear it.” That kind of interaction makes relationships firmer and projects smoother.

How to Use & Enable the Customer Ratings Project Module in Odoo

To start using ratings, you first need to enable the customer ratings feature of the project module in Odoo. Direct to the Project App.

Then, click on the Configuration > Settings.

In the analytics section, locate the ‘‘Customer Ratings’’ option. Check (✔) the box and click on Save.

Go to the Project dashboard and click on New.

Enter the project name, and enable time tracking if needed. Select the Billable option, fill in the customer field and then click on the ‘‘Create Project’’.

Stages can be added manually or chosen from ready-made examples. Click on the ‘‘See examples’’ to open a new window with stage templates.

Select the one best fit for your project and then click on the ‘‘Use This For My Project’’.

The selected stages will be automatically added to your project, and you can edit or reorder them as needed. To create a task, click on the plus (+) icon.

Enter the task name and assign it to a responsible person, and then click on the ‘‘Add’’ to finalize the creation of a task.

Suppose you want to collect the feedback at the ‘‘Done’’ stage. Open the settings for this stage and click ‘‘Edit’’.

Select the rating email template and tick (✔) the Automatic Kanban Status, and click on the Save & Close.

Next, open the existing task.

In the task form, find a customer field and select the client you want linked to this task. Once selected, click Save to apply the changes.

Then, go back to the main project view, locate the task in its current stage and drag it to the ‘‘Done’’ stage.

This transition will trigger the feedback process. Since the rating email template is set, the client automatically receives an email, and from the email, the client can leave a rating. 

The email includes three smiley (🙂, 😐, 🙁) options, green for satisfied, orange for okay and red for dissatisfied. After selecting one, the clients are redirected to a new page where they can leave feedback in the form of a text message in the provided field and click ‘‘Send Feedback’’.

Back in the task, you will see the rating and the kanban status automatically changed to approved, along with a green indicator.

This way, Odoo 18 allows you to quickly gather feedback, monitor client satisfaction and respond promptly to their needs. This improves transparency, project quality and client trust.

One of the most valuable features is the ability to automate feedback requests in Odoo. Instead of sending manual reminders to clients every time you want feedback, the system can do it for you. When a task is marked as complete or a stage is finished, the system can automatically ask the client for a rating.

This automation saves time, but more importantly, it ensures that feedback is always requested at the right moment. When you consistently collect customer ratings in Odoo, you start to see patterns. This kind of insight is only possible when feedback collection is steady and reliable.

You can see average scores across different projects, notice if one type of work tends to get higher ratings than others, and spot areas that may need extra attention. Tracking results over time shows if the steps you are taking to improve are actually working.

When you collect customer ratings in Odoo and track them regularly, you gain a clear picture of your performance. It becomes easier to make decisions because they are based on actual client opinions rather than assumptions.

Another interesting part of this system is the Odoo project stage feedback. By linking feedback to project stages, you make sure that clients are asked for their opinion when it is most relevant.

For example, after the design stage is complete, you can ask the client if they are happy with the design before moving to the development stage. This prevents misunderstandings from growing into bigger problems later. When you collect customer ratings in Odoo at each stage, you are not only measuring satisfaction, you are guiding the project in the right direction as it happens.

Practical Example of Collecting Ratings in Odoo 18

Imagine you are managing a software development project. The client is involved in multiple stages: design, coding, testing, and delivery. You decide to enable the customer ratings project module in Odoo and set feedback requests at the end of each stage.

After the design stage, the client gives their rating. If it’s high, you know the team is on the right track. If it’s low, you can ask questions and fix the issues before moving on. Later, after coding and testing, the client provides more ratings. By the time you deliver the final product, you already know if they are satisfied. This is only possible because you decided to collect customer ratings in Odoo at every critical step.

Why Every Business Should Collect Customer Ratings in Odoo

The habit of asking for feedback is not just about numbers; it is about building better projects and better relationships. Businesses that utilize Odoo 18 often experience improvements in communication and delivery, as indicated by customer ratings. When customers notice that their feedback leads to changes, they are more likely to trust the team and return for future work.

With project feedback, Odoo automates feedback requests and customer satisfaction tracking, making the process part of everyday work. You no longer need separate tools or extra systems. Everything happens inside Odoo, making it easier to manage.

Most importantly, when you regularly collect customer ratings in Odoo, you create a culture where feedback is regular. This culture encourages teams to strive for excellence and clients to share openly.

Collect Customer Ratings in Odoo for Lasting Results

In the end, learning how to collect customer ratings in Odoo is about more than just turning on a feature. It is about listening. With Odoo 18 customer ratings, businesses can ask for and record opinions directly inside their projects. By combining this with project feedback, companies can configure the Odoo system to enable the customer ratings project module, set up automated feedback requests, and analyze results using Odoo customer satisfaction tracking. This approach allows them to enhance both their projects and client relationships.

Adding Odoo project stage feedback ensures that opinions are gathered at the right time, making them more valuable and accurate. The process keeps teams focused, clients involved, and projects on track. That is why the ability to collect customer ratings in Odoo is becoming such an essential part of project management in Odoo 18.

The Odoo 19 financial reports module simplifies this process by providing a dynamic, real-time financial overview. By learning to analyse the balance sheet in Odoo, you gain visibility into:

In short, the Odoo 19 balance sheet helps you make informed financial decisions, ensuring you maintain a healthy financial position and stay compliant with accounting standards.

Getting Started with Odoo 19 Accounting Module 2025

2. Configuring Chart of Accounts

3. Using Filters and Date Ranges

Users of Odoo 19 can access balance sheet data via specific date ranges, journal selections, and tag applications. The system provides complete flexibility for users to perform exact financial period-based analysis through its Odoo accounting system.

Step-by-Step Guide to Analyse Balance Sheet in Odoo 19

Let's break down how to analyse the balance sheet effectively in Odoo to understand your organisation's financial pulse.

Step 1: Open the Balance Sheet Report

Go to Accounting → Reporting → Balance Sheet.

Here you'll see a structured report divided into Assets, Liabilities, and Equity.

Step 2: Understand Each Section

Assets

Assets represent what your company owns, both tangible (like machinery, cash, and inventory) and intangible (like patents and goodwill).

In Odoo 19, the balance sheet automatically classifies assets into Current Assets and Non-Current Assets.

Liabilities

Liabilities reflect what your company owes. These are also grouped into Current Liabilities (due within a year) and Long-Term Liabilities (loans and deferred taxes).

Equity

Equity represents the owner's stake in the business. It includes retained earnings and capital investments.

By exploring these three sections in Odoo 19 accounting, users can quickly determine whether the company is growing sustainably or over-leveraged.

Comparing Odoo Profit and Loss vs Balance Sheet

One of the most common confusions among new Odoo users is the distinction between Odoo profit and loss and the balance sheet.

Here's the distinction:

Aspect

Profit & Loss Statement

Balance Sheet

Purpose

Shows the company's performance over a period

Shows the financial position at a specific date

Focus

Revenue, expenses, and profit

Assets, liabilities, and equity

Frequency

Snapshot view (as of date)

Deep Odoo Accounting Analysis

The true strength of Odoo lies in its analytics. When you analyse the balance sheet in Odoo, you're not just reading numbers, you're decoding your business's financial DNA.

1. Ratio Analysis

The system uses Odoo's reporting features to generate three financial ratios.

  • The Current Ratio equals Current Assets divided by Current Liabilities.
  • The Debt-to-Equity Ratio equals Total Liabilities divided by Total Equity.
  • The Return on Assets (ROA) ratio equals Net Income divided by Total Assets.
  • These ratios help you evaluate liquidity, leverage, and profitability in a few clicks.

2. Comparative and Trend Analysis

The dynamic dashboard in Odoo 19 enables users to view their balance sheets across different time periods, including monthly and yearly comparisons. The system allows users to track financial patterns by showing how assets change while liabilities decrease and equity values rise.

The process of handling employee hours and leaves, together with payroll management, continues without end. Most businesses dedicate extensive time to spreadsheet updates, error correction, and verification of leave records against timesheet data. The process is both tedious and risky because minor errors can trigger payroll disputes and employee dissatisfaction, and result in wasted time. This is why the ability to automate timesheets with Odoo is getting so much attention.

With Odoo 18, companies can finally say goodbye to the old way of managing timesheets and leave data separate. The new features allow a complete flow from leave requests to timesheet updates. What this means is simple: when an employee takes a leave, the system automatically updates their timesheet without you lifting a finger. That's the magnificence of Odoo 18 timesheet automation.

In this blog, we'll explore how businesses can use Odoo time off integration to save time, reduce errors, and keep employees happy. We'll also explore the role of Odoo 18 HR management in restructuring the process and why timesheet software automation is a must-have tool for modern organizations. Why Automate Timesheets with Odoo for Better HR Flow

This chain of work can easily break if one person forgets to update a detail. But when you automate timesheets with Odoo, all of this happens automatically.

This isn't just about saving time; it's about building trust. Employees want to feel confident that their leave records are properly counted, and managers wish to have accurate timesheet data for payroll. With Odoo 18 timesheet automation, both sides win. The system handles everything in the background, leaving no room for missed entries or confusion.

When companies use Odoo time off integration, the flow of data becomes smoother. Leaves and absences are automatically linked with the timesheet, and you don't need to chase down HR staff for updates. The result is a transparent and reliable process, which is exactly what every modern workplace needs.

Step-by-Step Guide on How to Automate Timesheets with Odoo 18 Time Off

Odoo has a feature that automatically fills in timesheets for you when your Time off request is approved. This means you don't have to enter those days as Time off on your timesheet manually. It's very easy, so let me show you some simple steps on how to request it and how it appears in the timesheet. First, we need to inform Odoo about which type of Time off we are taking. Open the Time Off module to request Time off.

Before requesting time off, let me show you the different kinds of time off. Just go to the Configuration > Time Off Types.

Here, you can see the dashboard of time off types, such as paid time off, sick time off, unpaid time off, and extra time off. To create a new one, click the New button. You can also view the pre-created one. So, I am taking the pre-created time off from here that is Paid Time Off.

After clicking on the paid time off, another form appears. Under the Time Off Requests section, you'll find an option called Approval. I select No Validation (indicating no approval is needed) and then click Save.

Go back to the previous page and click My Time > Dashboard.

Now, I'll determine my paid leave date, so let's click on 28 August 2025.

After clicking on the date, a new wizard appears. Fill out the details and then click Save.

Now you can see in the screenshot below that 28 is highlighted in cream color.

Let’s go back to your Odoo dashboard and open the Timesheets module.

Here, you can see the incredible view of the timesheet, and when you check on the specified date, you can see that 8 hours of time off we requested.

That's how we can easily request time off and automate timesheets with the Odoo 18 Time Off module.

The best part is that it connects all these elements, so when one action happens in the system, it reflects everywhere it needs to.

If an employee applies for annual leave, the approval doesn't just stop at the HR desk. Instead, through Odoo leave to timesheet automation, the timesheet automatically updates to show the absence. Later, payroll also picks up this information without anyone needing to re-enter it. That's how Odoo time off automated entries removes repetitive manual tasks.

This setup ensures that timesheets are never out of sync with leave records. Businesses save hours of work every week, reduce the chances of payroll errors, and build a more organized HR system. The more you dive into Odoo 18 HR management, the more you realize it's not just software, it's like having a reliable HR assistant working silently in the background.

What makes this exciting is that there is no delay. If an employee takes a sick day today, their timesheet already knows about it. The HR team doesn't need to remember to add that absence later. By using Odoo time off integration, you are connecting two critical parts of HR into one smooth system.

This flow makes payroll simpler, too. When you automate timesheets with Odoo, salaries are based on accurate data. No more double-checking if someone's leave was included, no more explaining to employees why their payslip looks wrong. It's all automatic, and it builds confidence in the payroll process.

Title: How to Manage a Sales Team in Odoo 18 CRM?
Content:
Handling a sales team is not just about giving targets or pushing people to close deals. It's about guiding the team, creating wise systems, and using the right tools to make their work easier and more effective. And that's where Odoo 18 CRM shines. If you've ever wondered how to manage a sales team in Odoo, you're about to discover a system that converts scattered sales efforts into organized, goal-driven teamwork.

Odoo has always been known for simplifying business processes, but with version 18, it becomes even more effective. From assigning leads to tracking every deal in real time, Odoo 18 CRM gives you all the tools you need for CRM sales team management. Whether you're a startup, a growing business, or a large organization, managing your sales team through Odoo can save time, reduce stress, and increase profits.

Let's explore the real magic behind sales team management in Odoo, and how this excellent tool can help you make a stronger, more focused, and highly productive sales force.

Why Odoo 18 CRM is Perfect for Sales Team Management in Odoo

The most prominent challenge in managing a sales team is visibility. You often don't know which deals are moving forward, which ones are stuck, and who needs help. But Odoo 18 CRM solves this problem at the root. It offers a clear, easy-to-use dashboard where you can see all leads, opportunities, and team activities in one place.

When you use Odoo 18 CRM, your sales team gets their own space with specific targets, assigned leads, and a pipeline to manage their deals. You, as the manager, can easily track performance without asking for daily updates. You can set up automated reminders, score leads based on behavior, and assign opportunities based on location or industry.

This system makes CRM sales team management more innovative and more human at the same time. You're not just pushing numbers; you're guiding your team with real-time data and supporting them where they need help.

Sales Team Management in Odoo

Build Your Team, Set Your Rules

Odoo allows you to create different sales teams depending on how your business operates. You can have teams based on geography (like UAE Sales, Europe Sales), product lines (like Software Sales, Hardware Sales), or customer types (like B2B, B2C). Setting up a team in Odoo is quick. To set up your team, go to the CRM configuration, click "Sales Teams," and then set your team’s name, team leader, and members.

This structure is the first step to sales team management in Odoo, as it provides clarity. You know who is working on what, and you can assign tasks more wisely. You can also enable email labels for each team, so leads automatically land in the right inbox.

The best part is that each team can have its own pipeline stages, targets, and workflows. So, one team can focus on high-ticket B2B deals, while another can chase quick retail sales all within the same CRM.

How to Manage a Sales Team in Odoo 18 CRM: A Step-By-Step Guide

Let's break down exactly how to manage a sales team in Odoo, step by step, so that your team stays focused, your leads don't fall through the cracks, and your results improve week after week.

The first step in sales team management in Odoo is creating and organizing your teams.

Open your CRM from your Odoo dashboard.

Go to Configuration → Sales Teams.

This displays all your currently configured sales teams, including sales, website, and point of sale. So, to create a new team, click on New.

The first step is to give your team a clear name and description. So, I'm giving it the name Demo Team. Then, you have both checkboxes, such as Pipeline & Leads. If you want them to get involved in both, you have to make sure you enable both.

Next, you need to enter the team details, including Team Leader, Email Alias, Accept Emails from & Company. Then, add the members to your team by clicking on the Add button.

Once you click on add a window pops up. Here, you can choose how many members you want from the checkbox. So, whichever member is necessary, you can tick (✔) the checkbox and click on Select.

In Odoo, you even have the option to add new members. If you click on the Add button again, you see the option called New.

Clicking on that will create a new salesperson. It's exactly like building a new contact. If not necessary, you can click on Discard.

Now, the Demo Team has three members. So, this is how a team is created by clicking Save.

If you want to assign the same salesperson to multiple teams, you can’t do that before the correct settings are enabled. For that, go to the Configuration → Settings.

Enable Multi Teams and click Save. It allows you to assign salespersons to multiple sales teams. So, that’s how the creation works.

Now, let’s explore how robust the sales team dashboard is. For that, go to the Sales → Teams.

Here, you will see a Kanban card for every sales team you are a member of, giving you an immediate snapshot of their performance. Each card provides a quick overview. So, if you take a look at the Sales Teams Card, you can see the number of open opportunities, the quotations, how many sessions are running for this particular team, etc. And if you set a target or a goal for your team, that can also be found here. It also displays the invoicing progress graph. If you want a detailed view, click on the Pipeline button.

So, this will directly take you to the Sales Teams Pipeline. This gives you a clear idea about the team. 

If you need to view or edit a sales team's settings quickly, you can click on the (፧) dropdown menu, and it will offer you a menu called Configuration, along with some other menus. Click on the Configuration.

It opens the creation form for that specific team, prefilling all the details. If you want to perform any edits, you can do it here.

That’s how you manage the Sales team in Odoo 18 CRM. By organizing your sales force effectively, you’ll gain clear insights, improve lead distribution and drive better results.

This feature is a must-have for any business aiming to manage a sales team in Odoo more efficiently.

Odoo Sales Pipeline

Your Visual Map to Success

Suppose you walk into your office and instantly see what's happening with every lead and deal in your CRM. That's precisely what the Odoo sales pipeline gives you. It uses a simple Kanban board where every lead moves from one stage to another, like New → Contacted → Proposal Sent → Won.

This visual flow helps both the sales representatives and the manager. Representatives know where to focus each day, and managers can spot where deals are getting stuck. You can even color-code deals by priority or add tags to organize them better.

With the Odoo sales pipeline, your team doesn't have to guess what to do next. Everything is in front of them: deadlines, contact info, notes, emails, and calls, all linked to each opportunity. You can even automate some of the movements, so when a client replies, the deal automatically moves to the next stage.

This way, managing the team becomes more about coaching and less about micromanaging. And when you manage a sales team in Odoo using the pipeline, everything clicks into place.

CRM Sales Team Management

Lead Smarter, Not Harder

One of the most frustrating things in sales is when leads go cold because nobody followed up. It often happens when leads are randomly assigned or forgotten in the system. But with CRM sales team management in Odoo, you can set up rules that take care of this.

You can define how leads should be assigned by location, product, team, or even by score. For example, leads from the UAE can automatically go to Team A, while high-value leads (based on lead scoring) go to your senior team.

The lead assignment feature in Odoo is beneficial here. You can automate the entire lead routing process so that no lead is missed and every sales representative gets a fair workload. If a lead isn't touched in 48 hours, Odoo can even escalate it or reassign it.

This smart assignment helps you balance your team's efforts and gives every lead the attention it deserves. Your customers are happier, your team performs better, and you spend less time doing manual work.

Lead Assignment in Odoo

The Art of Speed and Accuracy

Speed matters in sales. The faster you respond to a lead, the higher your chances of converting it. But speed must come with structure. That's where lead assignment in Odoo shines.

Instead of dumping all leads into one pool, you can use automated rules to distribute them based on any criteria you like: industry, location, deal size, or even custom fields. And it's not just about assigning. You can set reminders for follow-ups, automate email responses, and track every step your sales team takes.

For example, if a lead comes from your website, it can be scored as "Hot" and immediately go to your top performer. Or if a lead hasn't been contacted in 3 days, Odoo can send a friendly reminder to the representative or escalate it to the manager.

This innovative workflow ensures no opportunity slips through the cracks, helping you manage your Odoo sales team like a professional.

Odoo CRM Reporting

Real-Time Insights for Real Decisions

One of the biggest strengths of Odoo 18 CRM is its reporting ability. With just a periodic click, you can develop real-time reports on almost everything, including lead conversion rates, deal stages, sales by team, win/loss ratios, and more.

Odoo CRM reporting isn't just for the end of the month. It's for daily use. You can monitor which team is hitting their targets, which representative is lagging, which region is performing better, and how long your deals usually take to close.

You can also create customized dashboards with graphs and pivot tables that update live. Need to see how many deals are stuck in the "Proposal Sent" stage? Just filter your view. Want to compare performance across different teams? It's all there.

This kind of visibility helps you manage your team not just reactively, but proactively. You can run coaching sessions, update goals, and spot trends early, all thanks to the insights from Odoo CRM reporting.

CRM Sales Team Management with Real Results

When you bring all of this together, team structure, pipeline, lead assignment, and reporting, you create a complete ecosystem for CRM sales team management. Your team knows their responsibilities, your customers get faster responses, and you, as a manager, can focus on improving the strategy instead of fixing daily chaos.

One of the great things about Odoo is that it doesn't force you into one system. You can customize almost everything, including fields, workflows, rules, and dashboards, to match how your team works. Whether your sales cycle is 3 days or 3 months, Odoo adapts.

And the more your team uses the system, the better the data becomes. You can forecast revenue, plan your hiring, and refine your marketing, all based on the live numbers coming from your Odoo sales pipeline.

The Future of Sales Team Management in Odoo 18 CRM

Sales are changing fast. Customers expect instant replies, personalized offers, and smooth experiences. To keep up, your sales team needs tools that are just as smart. With Odoo 18 CRM, you're not just getting a CRM; you're getting a complete command center for your sales team.

From managing opportunities to assigning leads, from automating tasks to tracking reports, everything works together in a straightforward interface, eliminating the need to switch between tools, lose leads, or deal with endless spreadsheets.

The way you manage a sales team in Odoo is different from traditional CRMs because it blends automation with flexibility. It helps your team do their job better and enables you to lead them with clarity and confidence.

It's Time to Manage Your Sales Team in Odoo Like an Expert

Sales management doesn't have to be stressful or messy. With Odoo 18 CRM, it becomes transparent, efficient, and even enjoyable. You can finally stop chasing reports, stop guessing who's doing what, and start focusing on growth.

So, if you're looking to manage a sales team in Odoo, now is the perfect time. Set up your teams, build your Odoo sales pipeline, use smart lead assignment in Odoo, and track progress with influential Odoo CRM reporting. Whether you're just getting started or scaling up fast, Odoo 18 CRM gives you everything you need to win in sales.

What is the Trial Balance Report in Odoo 18?

The Trial Balance Report in Odoo is a financial report that displays every account along with its debit and credit balances. It serves as a checkpoint to ensure that total debits are equal to total credits. If they do not match, it means there is an error somewhere in your books.

The trial balance feature in Odoo 18 has been designed to rationalize this process, making it fast and simple. Instead of manually checking accounts, you can generate the report instantly. This not only saves time but also gives you peace of mind that your numbers are accurate.

The Odoo trial balance accounting report is also a helpful starting point before preparing financial statements, such as the profit and loss statement or balance sheet. Without this check, those statements could present an inaccurate picture.

If you are new to this report, here is a simple Odoo 18 trial balance report tutorial that shows you how to use it.

First, log in to your Odoo 18 account and go to the Accounting module.

The next step is to review the numbers. This is where you need to carefully analyze the trial balance in Odoo to make sure that the totals are equal. Finally, once you are satisfied, you can export the trial balance report in Odoo 18 as a PDF or Excel file.

The Odoo trial balance accounting report also facilitates the preparation of other financial documents. Since it displays all accounts in one place, you can quickly verify whether your profit and loss statement or balance sheet is accurate.

How to Analyze Trial Balance Odoo 18

When you run the Trial Balance Report in Odoo, the most crucial step is analysis. To analyze the trial balance in Odoo, start by verifying that the total debit equals the total credit. If they are equal, it means your books are balanced. If not, you will need to investigate further.

Next, look at individual accounts. Does the balance of each account make sense? For example, if you see a negative balance in an expense account, that could mean something was entered incorrectly. If you notice unusually high balances in certain accounts, it may indicate that you should review those transactions.

Comparing the trial balance with previous periods is another good way to analyze it. This allows you to notice trends or sudden changes. For example, if your advertising expenses have doubled compared to last month, the trial balance will help you identify this quickly.

Trial Balance vs General Ledger Odoo

It is essential to understand the distinction between a trial balance and a general ledger in Odoo, as many people often confuse these two concepts.

The trial balance is a summary. It displays the ending balance of each account, along with debit and credit totals. It does not show every transaction but only the final balances. The purpose is to make sure debits and credits are equal.

The general ledger, on the other hand, is detailed. It lists every single transaction for each account. While the trial balance gives you a snapshot, the general ledger tells you the whole story of how you reached that balance.

The Trial Balance Report in Odoo serves as a checkpoint to confirm accuracy, while the general ledger is used for detailed investigation. Both are needed, but they serve different purposes.

You can generate it for a single month if you want to check the monthly performance. You can generate it for a quarter if you are preparing quarterly reports. This flexibility means the report adapts to your business needs, rather than forcing you to follow a fixed format. It also means you can quickly answer questions from managers or auditors without needing to prepare separate reports.

Using the Trial Balance Report in Odoo 18 for Better Accounting

The Trial Balance Report in Odoo is one of the most reliable tools for checking the accuracy of your books. With Odoo 18, it has become even easier to use. You can follow the Odoo 18 trial balance report tutorial to learn how to set dates, apply filters, and generate a trial balance Odoo 18 in just a few clicks. When your team uses the CRM just for capturing leads, you're missing a huge opportunity. The magic happens when you schedule tasks in Odoo 19 proactively, including calls, meetings, emails, and follow-ups, and then track those activities to ensure they're completed, escalated, or triggered next. Want to strengthen your foundation before getting into Odoo 19 activity tracking? Read our comprehensive article on How to Track & Manage Leads Effectively in Odoo 18 CRM to learn essential lead management workflows.

Setting Up Activity Types for Tracking

Before you get into live scheduling, define your activity types. In the world of Odoo CRM activity tracking, activity types are the building blocks. In Odoo 19, you'll navigate to:

CRM app → Configuration → Activity Types.

There, you can create or edit activity types such as:

  • Email
  • Call
  • Meeting
  • To-Do
  • Upload Document
  • Request Signature
  • These types appear when you schedule tasks in Odoo 19.

Additionally, note that in Odoo 19, there are enhancements (compared to earlier versions) to make this process smoother, including one-click meeting scheduling, clearer icons, and improved workflow.

How to Schedule Activities in Odoo 19 CRM

Now comes the action: how do you actually Schedule and Track Activities in Odoo 19 CRM on leads or opportunities?

Step-by-step:

  • Open the lead or opportunity record in the CRM app.
  • In the chatter or top right, click the Activity button (in Odoo 19, it's now labelled "Activity" for clarity).
  • Choose "+ Schedule An Activity". In the form, pick the Activity Type, enter a Summary, select a Due Date, and choose the Assigned To user. Optionally add a note.
  • If you select 'Meeting' or 'Call', you may see a button to open the calendar. In Odoo 19, this flow is optimised: selecting 'Meeting + Schedule' opens the calendar directly.
  • Click "Schedule" (or "Save") to confirm. The activity now appears under the "Planned Activities" section in the chatter.
  • In the Kanban view of the pipeline, you'll see a clock icon (or the specific type icon) on the card. The colour indicates status: green = upcoming, orange = due today, red = overdue. This is how you visually track tasks in Odoo 19 CRM.

Useful Tips During Scheduling

  • Always set the due date and user assignment; this ensures proper tracking and accountability.
  • Encourage your team to add concise notes ("Log a note" field) so context is preserved.
  • Use the "Schedule & Mark as Done" or "Done & Schedule Next" buttons where appropriate (especially when chaining tasks).
  • Use filters like "My Activities", "Due Today", and "Overdue" to maintain high visibility.
  • Train your team to click the clock icon in Kanban so they never skip scheduling an activity.

Tracking Activities and Ensuring Follow-Ups

Scheduling is one side; tracking is equally crucial. To schedule and Track Activities in Odoo 19 CRM, you need to build a mindset and dashboard that makes follow-ups automatic and reliable.

Visual Tracking in Pipeline

As noted above, in the Kanban view for opportunities, you'll see icons representing scheduled activities. Colour coding flags those items that are due or overdue.

This gives your sales managers a quick "at a glance" sense of pipeline health: how many opportunities have no next activity, how many are overdue, etc.

Activity View & My Activities Dashboard

The CRM module also provides a dedicated Activities (clock) view, where you can see all planned tasks across records, including those due today, upcoming, or late.

In your tracking toolkit, make sure you use:

  • A "My Activities" filter for each salesperson.
  • A "Team Activities" view for managers to monitor assignments and statuses.
  • Export or report of overdue activities so action can be taken.

Automating Follow-Ups (CRM Follow-Ups)

One of the most potent aspects of Odoo 19 schedule activities is built-in automation for follow-ups. Through activity plans and chaining, you can define a sequence: call → meeting → quote → follow-up email. When the prior task is done, the next is suggested or triggered.

For example:

  • After the initial birth-lead, schedule a "Demo meeting" within 2 days.
  • After the meeting is done, auto-schedule "Send Quote" 1 day later.
  • Then, "Follow-up email" 5 days later if no response.

This is how you build consistent, high-quality CRM follow-ups in Odoo 19. And once that is live, your tracking becomes hands-free: nothing is skipped.

Reminders & Notifications in Odoo 19

One of the most common holes in a sales process is forgetting tasks. When you schedule and Track Activities in Odoo 19 CRM, you want reminders and notifications to help close that gap.

How Reminders Work

When you schedule an activity, the assigned user will see it:

  • In their chatter under the record.

Title: What Is the Closest Location Removal Strategy in Odoo 18 Inventory?
Content:
Inventory management is at the heart of every business that deals with products. Whether it’s a warehouse, retail chain, or distribution center, the way stock is picked directly impacts time, cost, and efficiency. Odoo 18 has refined its inventory system to provide advanced features that enable companies to select more intelligent picking methods. Among these, the Closest Location Removal Strategy in Odoo has gained attention for its practical approach in minimizing movement within the warehouse.

When businesses handle large stock volumes spread across multiple shelves or storage units, the key challenge is identifying the right removal strategy. The Odoo 18 closest location removal strategy solves this by allowing items to be picked from the nearest available stock location. This strategy is part of Odoo 18’s inventory picking methods, helping teams save effort, reduce walking time, and increase overall productivity.

With the closest location removal warehouse setup in Odoo, businesses can ensure that employees pick goods from the shortest path instead of roaming across the warehouse. When you configure removal strategies in Odoo 18, you gain the flexibility to define rules that guide your warehouse operations. Whether it’s a small store or a significant distribution hub, Odoo ensures that picking from the nearest location reduces time and effort.

Additionally, Odoo offers support for multi-step routes in the warehouse, which allows you to manage complex workflows that involve receiving, storing, and delivering stock through multiple stages. Combined with the Odoo 18 picking optimization feature, these strategies provide a clear advantage for businesses seeking to enhance their operational efficiency.

In this blog, we’ll take a closer look at the Closest Location Removal Strategy in Odoo, including its functionality in Odoo 18, its significance for businesses, and how to configure it for your warehouse.

Understanding the Closest Location Removal Strategy in Odoo 18

The Closest Location Removal Strategy in Odoo is one of the most innovative methods for picking goods in a warehouse. Instead of randomly choosing a location or following a strict first-in-first-out approach, Odoo allows you to set rules that prioritize stock based on its proximity to the operator.

For example, imagine a warehouse where the same product is stored in three different places: near the entrance, in the middle section, and at the far end. Without the right system, your team may end up picking items from the farthest shelf, wasting both energy and time. With the Odoo 18 closest location removal strategy, the system guides workers to select stock from the nearest point.

This method is not only about convenience but also about reducing operational costs. Shorter travel distances within the warehouse result in faster order fulfillment, ultimately improving customer satisfaction.

The Role of Odoo 18 Inventory Picking Methods

Odoo offers multiple inventory picking methods to cater to various business requirements. While FIFO (First In, First Out) or LIFO (Last In, First Out) might work for perishable items or specific financial reporting needs, the closest location removal warehouse Odoo strategy is practical for fast-moving products where speed is more critical than stock age.

The flexibility to configure removal strategies in Odoo 18 ensures that each company can select the most effective method, custom-made to its specific products and operations. For warehouses that handle thousands of movements daily, relying on the Odoo 18 closest location removal strategy can significantly simplify picking tasks for staff.

How to Configure Removal Strategies in Odoo 18

Setting up the Closest Location Removal Strategy in Odoo doesn’t require complex steps. The process in Odoo 18 is straightforward and user-friendly. Here’s a simple outline of how you can configure it:

Open the Inventory App from your Odoo dashboard.

Go to Configuration > Settings.

Enable the Storage Locations & Multi-Step Routes, then click Save.

Direct to Configuration > Locations.

Here, Odoo decides which location is closest based on the alpha-numeric order of the location names. To make this work properly, we should name our locations in a way that reflects the real distance from the packing area. In this example, we have Shelf 1 as the closest shelf and Shelf 2 a little further away.

That way, Odoo understands a picking sequence in a way that matches the real-world layout of our warehouse. Now that our shelves are appropriately named, we need to apply the removal strategy. We can either set it on the parent location. In this case, WH/Stock applies; however, please note that if we do so, the closest location strategy will be used for all shelves within the warehouse to stock.

Alternatively, we can apply it to each shelf individually. This way, Odoo will always suggest picking from the nearest shelf first for those specific locations, while other warehouse areas continue their default removal strategy.

Now, let’s check the on-hand stock at each storage location. To do that, I'll go to the Products > Products.

And click on the Cable Management Box.

Under the Product Form, click the "On Hand" smart button at the top.

Here, we can see the product stored across shelves. You will also notice the on-hand quantity column, which shows precisely how much stock is available at each shelf.

Let’s move to the Sales App and create a sales order to see the strategy in action.

Click New and create a new quotation.

Select the Customer, add the Product, and click Confirm.

Click the Delivery smart button.

Inside the Operations tab, click the details button on the product line to open the stock move information.

Here, Odoo suggests picking first from Shelf 1, then from the following nearest location, Shelf  2, until the full demand is covered.

With the closest location removal strategy, Odoo ensures products are always picked from the nearest available shelf. This not only saves time but also makes the picking process smoother, keeping warehouse operations running efficiently. 

By learning how to configure removal strategies in Odoo 18, businesses can experiment with various setups and determine what works best for their specific environment. The best part is that these settings can be applied to both small warehouses and extensive multi-level facilities.

Odoo 18 Picking Optimization with Nearest Location Strategy

The ability to choose the closest storage area is one of the most effective Odoo 18 picking optimization techniques. Workers save steps, orders are processed faster, and the overall flow of products improves significantly.

The picking from the nearest location Odoo strategy is especially beneficial for industries such as retail, wholesale, e-commerce, and manufacturing, where speed plays a crucial role in meeting demand. Every second saved in the warehouse adds up to significant improvements when scaled across thousands of transactions.

By integrating multi-step routes warehouse Odoo 18 with the closest location strategy, companies can create a fine-tuned system where each product moves through a structured process while still being picked from the most efficient point.

Why Businesses Prefer Closest Location Removal in Odoo 18

The Closest Location Removal Strategy in Odoo has gained popularity because it directly addresses one of the most common problems in warehouse management: unnecessary movement. Picking goods from random or distant places leads to inefficiency and frustration for warehouse staff.

With the Odoo 18 closest location removal strategy, businesses can:

  • Reduce walking time inside warehouses.
  • Improve picking accuracy.
  • Shorten delivery preparation cycles.
  • Lower labor fatigue and increase staff efficiency.
  • Speed up operations in high-demand seasons.

When companies adopt Odoo 18 inventory picking methods with this strategy, they experience smoother processes that improve overall productivity.

Multi-Step Routes and Closest Location Removal in Odoo 18

Complex warehouses often require more than just simple stock picking. The multi-step routes warehouse feature in Odoo 18 is designed for such setups. It enables you to manage receipt, storage, internal transfers, and deliveries with multiple checkpoints.

By combining these routes with the closest location removal warehouse Odoo, companies get the best of both worlds: structured workflows and optimized picking. This combination ensures that products follow a clear path through the warehouse while workers save time by always choosing the nearest available stock location.

Final Thoughts on Closest Location Removal Strategy in Odoo 18

The Closest Location Removal Strategy in Odoo is not just another option in the system; it’s a practical way to make warehouse tasks more efficient. With Odoo 18's closest location removal strategy, companies can focus on reducing wasted effort and ensuring that employees pick items from the nearest possible location.

When you combine this with Odoo 18 picking optimization, multi-step routes for warehouse Odoo 18, and other Odoo 18 inventory picking methods, you create a warehouse that runs smoothly and meets customer needs on time. By learning how to configure removal strategies in Odoo 18, businesses can effectively manage their stock operations without unnecessary complications.

Title: How to Do Bank Reconciliation in Odoo 19 Accounting?
Content:
Manage Finances with Bank Reconciliation in Odoo 19 Accounting

Managing finances can be complex, especially when it comes to matching every transaction with your bank statement. That's where Bank Reconciliation in Odoo 19 Accounting becomes essential.

This feature enables businesses to verify that the records in their books accurately reflect the balances in their actual bank accounts. Whether you're a small startup or a growing enterprise, mastering Odoo 19 bank reconciliation keeps your accounts transparent, accurate, and stress-free.

In this Odoo bank reconciliation tutorial, we'll guide you through the complete process, from setup to automation. You'll learn how to reconcile bank statements in Odoo, use Odoo reconciliation models, handle manual bank reconciliation in Odoo, and even automate the entire process with Odoo auto bank reconciliation.

At Netilligence, a trusted Odoo Partner, we believe smart accounting isn't just about recording numbers, it's about building financial confidence. With the proper setup, Odoo Accounting reconciliation can save you hours every month, enabling you to make faster and more intelligent business decisions.

Let's break it all down step by step and see how Bank Reconciliation in Odoo 19 Accounting can completely transform the way you manage your finances.

What is Bank Reconciliation in Odoo 19 Accounting?

Simply put, Bank Reconciliation in Odoo 19 Accounting means comparing your company's accounting records with your bank statements to ensure everything matches.

Think of it as your financial "truth check." Every payment received, bill paid, or fee deducted is verified in detail. If there's any mismatch, you'll identify and correct it before it causes more significant problems.

Odoo 19 makes this process smoother than ever. It allows you to import statements, automatically match transactions, and review everything from a clean dashboard.

Why It Matters:

  • Saves Time: Reconcile hundreds of transactions in minutes.
  • Ensures Accuracy: No more guessing or manual errors.
  • Improves Visibility: Track real-time cash flow with precision.
  • Supports Audits: Maintain clean and compliant records.
  • Simplifies Accounting: Odoo's built-in tools handle complexity for you.

In short: Reconciliation is the backbone of healthy accounting, and Odoo 19 gives you all the tools to make it effortless.

Step-by-Step: How to Do Bank Reconciliation in Odoo 19 Accounting

Now, let's go step by step through the process. Whether you prefer automation or manual control, Odoo 19 gives you both options to ensure nothing slips through the cracks.

Step 1: Set Up Your Bank Journal

Everything starts with configuring your bank journal correctly.

Go to:

Accounting → 

Configuration → Journals → Create (or Edit your existing Bank Journal).

Add:

  • The Bank Account Number
  • Bank Name
  • Currency
  • And enable Bank Feeds (if supported)

This setup connects Odoo to your bank account, allowing it to fetch statements directly or import them manually at a later time.

Step 2: Import Your Bank Statements

Next, bring your actual transactions into Odoo.

Head to Accounting → Bank → Import Statement and choose the format (CSV, OFX, or QIF). Odoo will read your file and display all transactions neatly.

If your bank supports it, you can connect it directly for Odoo auto-bank reconciliation, which means your statements will automatically appear inside Odoo, eliminating the need for uploads.

Pro Tip: Utilize this feature on a weekly or monthly basis to keep records up-to-date and error-free.

Step 3: Let Odoo Match Transactions Automatically

This is where the magic happens.

Once the statement is imported, Odoo automatically tries to match each line with invoices, payments, or journal entries, thanks to its innovative Odoo reconciliation models.

To do this:

  • Open your reconciliation dashboard.
  • Click Auto Match.
  • Review the suggested matches.
  • Validate when you're satisfied.

Odoo learns from your previous reconciliations, making future ones even faster. That's the power of AI built into Odoo Accounting reconciliation.

Step 4: Handle Manual Bank Reconciliation in Odoo

Automation is great, but sometimes, human review is essential.

If Odoo can't find a match, you can handle it manually:

  • Select the unmatched transaction.
  • Click Create or Match Manually.
  • Select the correct entry (such as an expense, invoice, or adjustment).
  • Confirm to validate.

You might use manual bank reconciliation in Odoo when:

  • The customer paid a slightly different amount.
  • The bank charged unexpected fees.
  • A reference or label is missing.

Manual review ensures no transaction is left unrecorded.

Step 5: Review and Validate Your Reconciliation

Once all matches are confirmed, you can validate and close the reconciliation.

Double-check that:

  • The bank balance equals your journal balance.
  • All statements are marked as reconciled.
  • No pending entries remain.

That's it! You've completed your Bank Reconciliation in Odoo 19 Accounting, clean, quick, and reliable.

You can check our detailed guide on How to Record Expenses in Odoo 18 Accounting Module to learn how expense management connects smoothly with your reconciliation process.

Advanced Tips to Get More Out of Odoo 19 Bank Reconciliation

Odoo 19 isn't just efficient, it's intelligent. Here's how you can unlock more advanced features:

1. Use Odoo Reconciliation Models for Speed

Reconciliation models in Odoo are like templates or rules that automate repetitive matching tasks.

For example, if you always incur a $10 monthly bank charge, you can create a model that automatically recognizes and reconciles it.

How to do it:

  • Go to Accounting → Configuration → Reconciliation Models
  • Click Create
  • Set conditions (like amount, partner, or label)
  • Assign an account
  • Save and apply

From then on, Odoo will automatically reconcile all similar transactions.

2. Enable Auto Bank Reconciliation in Odoo 19

If you're ready to save significant time, enable Odoo auto bank reconciliation.

This feature automatically matches transactions using your defined models and machine learning.

It learns patterns, identifies recurring payments, and suggests likely matches; you approve them.

Why It's Important:

  • Reduces manual effort by up to 80%
  • Improves accuracy over time
  • Speeds up month-end closings
  • Keeps your cash position constantly updated

No more spending hours on spreadsheets, Odoo handles it for you.

Common Mistakes to Avoid During Bank Reconciliation

Even with great tools like Odoo, small mistakes can lead to significant confusion later. Here are common ones to avoid:

  1. Ignoring minor mismatches: Tiny differences add up; always investigate.
  2. Not checking auto-matches: Odoo's smart, but human verification matters.

Title: How Can a Company Measure the Return on Investment (ROI) After Implementing Odoo ERP?
Content:
When a company decides to integrate Odoo ERP into its business, one key question always arises: "How can we measure the return on investment after implementing Odoo ERP?"

It's a fair question, and honestly, it's something every business owner should think about. You spend money, time, and energy on implementation, and it's natural to want to know whether it's worth it. That's where Odoo ERP ROI measurement becomes essential.

Measuring the return on investment isn't just about comparing costs; it's about understanding how much your company has grown, saved, or improved as a result of implementation. Many people get confused about where to start, but if you know how to measure ERP ROI, what metrics to track, and how to apply the ERP ROI formula, you can easily see how Odoo is paying off.

In this blog, I'll speak to you as I would with a friend who has just implemented Odoo ERP and now wants to see whether it's truly working. We'll guide you through everything, from understanding ERP implementation ROI metrics to conducting an Odoo ERP cost savings analysis, utilizing an Odoo ROI calculator, and tracking key ERP performance indicators. By the end, you'll know exactly how to measure the return on investment and get clarity on the results your ERP is delivering.

Why Measuring the Return-on-Investment Matters?

Imagine spending a significant amount on a project without knowing whether it actually helped your business. That's what happens when companies don't measure their ROI. You might feel things have improved, but without numbers, it's only a guess.

Measuring the return on investment after implementing Odoo ERP provides proof. It tells you if the system is working, where it's saving money, and how it's improving your daily operations. Consider that Odoo ERP impacts nearly every aspect of your business, including finance, inventory, sales, HR, and even customer service. If you don't measure the results, you'll never know where it's making a difference.

With proper Odoo ERP ROI measurement, you can identify which areas have shown the most improvement and which still require attention. It also helps justify your investment to management or partners, showing them the actual business value generated.

ERP Implementation ROI Metrics: Setting the Right Foundation

Now, when we talk about ERP implementation ROI metrics, we're talking about the specific areas that reflect your ERP's performance. These are the signs that show whether Odoo ERP is helping your business grow or not.

Here are a few key ones you should focus on:

  • Operational Efficiency: Is your team completing tasks faster now? Are order or payment cycles shorter?
  • Cost Reduction: Has automation reduced manual work, errors, or unnecessary expenses?
  • Inventory Management: Are you holding fewer products in stock while still meeting customer demand?
  • Employee Productivity: Are your employees spending less time on manual reports and more on valuable work?
  • Customer Satisfaction: Are clients happier because of better order tracking or quicker responses?

These are all strong indicators of ROI. When you track them regularly, you'll notice how Odoo ERP impacts your operations daily.

Using the ERP ROI Formula to Measure Success

When it comes to numbers, you don't need to make things complicated. The basic ERP ROI formula is simple:

ROI = (Total Benefits – Total Costs) ÷ Total Costs × 100%

This formula helps you calculate the percentage return on your investment. However, to achieve the right results, you need two key elements: accurate benefits and complete cost details.

Costs include everything you have invested in, such as software licenses, implementation, training, support, and even the time your team spent learning the new system.

Benefits include cost savings, increased revenue, faster processes, and improved productivity that Odoo ERP has brought.

Once you fill in those numbers, you'll have a clear picture of your ROI. Even if the percentage isn't huge in the first year, don't worry. The ROI grows over time as your team becomes more comfortable with Odoo ERP and utilizes it more effectively.

Odoo ERP Cost Savings Analysis: Finding the Real Value

To accurately measure the return on investment, you need to conduct a cost savings analysis using Odoo ERP. This is where you look closely at all the ways your ERP has helped save money or reduce waste.

Start by asking yourself:

  • Are there fewer manual errors now?
  • Has the company reduced duplicate work between departments?
  • Are we saving time in financial reporting or inventory updates?
  • Do employees spend less time on paperwork and more on actual business growth?

Every minute saved has a cost value. For example, if Odoo ERP saves your team 10 hours every week, calculate the total salary cost for those hours and count that as part of your savings. Similarly, if your inventory is now managed better, you're saving storage costs and freeing up working capital.

When you add all these figures, you'll see how much your company is truly gaining from Odoo ERP. This Odoo ERP cost savings analysis becomes the backbone of your ROI measurement.

How to Use an Odoo ROI Calculator for Better Clarity

To make things even easier, you can create or use an Odoo ROI calculator. Think of it as a tool that gathers all your input costs, benefits, time, and savings and gives you a precise ROI figure.

You can build one using Excel or an online calculator. Just make sure to include:

  • Implementation costs (software, setup, training)
  • Annual maintenance or support
  • Operational savings
  • Productivity gains
  • Additional revenue from faster processes or improved accuracy

When you fill in these details, the calculator instantly shows your ROI. It's a quick and practical way to track how much your ERP is benefiting you over the months or years.

Most companies find it motivating to see the numbers. It helps them realize that Odoo ERP is not just a software expense, it's an investment that continues to pay off.

Measure ERP ROI with Real Performance Indicators

Once your ERP system is running smoothly, the next step is to regularly track ERP performance indicators. These are the numbers that tell you how well your business is performing after implementation.

A few key performance indicators include:

  • Order-to-cash cycle time (how quickly you receive payments after orders)
  • Purchase-to-pay cycle time (how efficiently you handle supplier payments)
  • Inventory turnover rate (how fast products move through stock)
  • Revenue per employee (how much output each employee delivers)
  • Customer satisfaction ratings or repeat purchase rates

Tracking these indicators on a monthly or quarterly basis helps you spot trends early. If a particular metric is improving, you'll know your ERP is working well. If it's falling behind, you can investigate and fix the issue before it grows.

By consistently measuring these ERP performance indicators, you're not only tracking ROI but also improving business efficiency step by step.

Measure the Return on Investment Through Real Improvements

When companies start tracking results, they're often surprised by the kind of improvements they see. For instance, they realize that processes that once took hours now take minutes. Teams that struggled with reports in the past can now receive real-time updates through dashboards.

These small improvements may seem minor individually, but collectively, they represent significant growth. That's why Odoo ERP ROI measurement isn't just a one-time task. It's something you do continuously to see how your investment continues to add value over time.

And the best part is this approach keeps your team motivated. When employees see measurable progress, they feel their efforts are paying off, and that's something every business owner wants.

ERP Implementation ROI Metrics That Help in Decision-Making

When you measure ERP ROI correctly, you start seeing patterns in your business. You understand what's working, what's not, and where more focus is needed. These insights help inform decision-making, whether it's adding new Odoo modules, expanding operations, or investing in additional training.

For example, suppose your ERP implementation ROI metrics indicate that most savings are coming from inventory control. In that case, your next focus may be on automating sales or HR to gain further benefits.

This data-driven mindset ensures that every step you take is based on facts, not assumptions, when implementing Odoo ERP. Over time, this consistency helps you make smarter choices and grow more quickly.

Seeing the Results Beyond Numbers

When you start to measure the Return on Investment, it's not always about financial reports or charts. The real value of Odoo ERP often becomes apparent in daily operations, faster approvals, fewer mistakes, smoother communication, and more effective planning. These minor yet constant improvements make teams more confident in their work and enable managers to make informed, timely decisions.

So, even though your Odoo ERP ROI measurement may begin with figures, the long-term impact is felt through increased efficiency, enhanced satisfaction, and improved control over your processes. Companies that focus on these non-financial ERP performance indicators often realize that Odoo ERP does much more than what can be calculated; it builds the foundation for smarter, data-driven growth.

Is Your Odoo ERP Paying Off?

If you've already implemented Odoo ERP or are planning to do so, now is the right time to measure its performance. Use your ERP ROI formula, run an Odoo ERP cost savings analysis, or explore an Odoo ROI calculator, but don't stop there. Look deeper into how your teams are working, how much time is saved, and how decisions are improving. That's where your real ERP implementation ROI metrics begin to show results.

Step 2: Set Up Employees in Odoo

Go to Manufacturing > Operations > Manufacturing Orders.

Select the product and quantity. Choose the BoM that includes routing. Click Confirm to generate work orders.

Step 6: Open the Work Order

In the confirmed MO, click the Work Orders tab.

Open the generated work order.

Step 7: Assign Multiple Employees

In the work order form, look for the field labeled Assigned Employees. Choose multiple employees then Save the work order.

Title: How to Configure the Chart of Accounts in Odoo 19
Content:
Accounting with the Chart of Accounts in Odoo 19

Business accounting requires both a structured organization and clear presentation methods to function correctly. Configuring the Odoo 19 Chart of Accounts requires knowledge, as it enables both precise financial reporting and streamlined business operations.

If you're looking for an Odoo accounting setup tutorial that's simple, practical, and aligned with real business needs.

✅ Configure the Chart of Accounts in Odoo 19

✅ Customize account types for better financial tracking

✅ Import an existing chart of accounts Odoo ERP file

At Netilligence, as an Odoo Partner, we've helped hundreds of businesses set up their Odoo accounting systems. Our experts ensure that your Odoo 19 chart of accounts is not just technically configured, but also optimized for your unique business processes.

What is a Chart of Accounts in Odoo 19?

Before configuring, let's understand what a Chart of Accounts actually means in the Odoo accounting module.

The Chart of Accounts in Odoo 19 encompasses all financial accounts, assets, liabilities, income, expenses, and equity of your company. Your accounting system depends on this fundamental structure to handle all monetary transactions with exactness.

In simpler words, it's like your business's financial dictionary; every debit or credit entry passes through it.

Each account has:

  • A unique code
  • A name describing its purpose
  • An account type (Asset, Liability, Expense, etc.)
  • A related journal (Sales, Purchase, Bank, etc.)

This modular approach sets Odoo apart from other ERP systems, as it is easy to use, flexible, and compliant with international accounting standards.

Why Configure the Chart of Accounts in Odoo 19 Matters

Setting up your Chart of Accounts correctly in Odoo 19 on the first day of operation will provide you with precise financial data, simplify audit processes, and enhance operational efficiency.

The following reasons explain why this process stands as a critical step.

Accurate Financial Tracking:

The system automatically links all financial transactions to their designated accounts for customer invoices and vendor bills.

Simplified Tax Reporting:

The system ensures tax authority compliance through its automated reporting system, which generates precise, real-time reports.

Data Consistency:

The implementation of standardized account codes prevents both duplicate entries and account confusion.

Time Savings:

The automated setup process in the Odoo accounting setup tutorial enables your finance team to dedicate their time to analysis instead of performing manual data entry.

Scalability:

The chart of accounts system in Odoo adapts to business expansion by supporting operations across multiple branches.

Step-by-Step: How to Configure the Chart of Accounts in Odoo 19

We will begin by configuring the Chart of Accounts in Odoo 19 from scratch.

The process will be divided into smaller sections, enabling users to understand each step better.

Step 1: Activate the Accounting Module

First, ensure that the Accounting module is installed in your Odoo 19 instance.

  • Go to Apps → search for "Accounting."
  • Click Install.

This section is where all your financial accounts will live.

Step 2: Create Accounts Odoo 19

If you need to add custom accounts, Odoo makes it easy:

  • Go to Accounting → Configuration → Chart of Accounts
  • Click Create New".
  • Fill in these fields:
    • Code: A unique number (e.g., 1010000 for Cash)
    • Account Name: e.g., Cash in Hand
    • Type: Select from predefined categories (Asset, Liability, Income, Expense, etc.)
    • Allowed Journal: Choose journals related to this account (Bank, Sales, Purchase, etc.)
  • Click Save

You've now successfully added a new account to your Odoo 19 chart of accounts!

Step 3: Use Predefined Templates

One of the best features in Odoo 19 accounting setup is that it comes with predefined templates based on localization (country-specific rules).

For instance, if you select "United States – Chart of Accounts" or "Oman – Chart of Accounts," Odoo automatically loads standard account codes and types.

To use templates:

  • Go to Settings → Accounting → Fiscal Localization
  • Select your country and install the localization package.
  • Odoo automatically imports standard accounts.

This feature saves hours of manual setup and ensures compliance with local accounting laws.

Step 4: Import the Chart of Accounts Odoo

Do you already have your company's chart of accounts in Excel or CSV format? Odoo makes importing it simple.

  • Go to Accounts→ Select Favorites → Import Records from the menu.
  • Choose the file you want to upload from the following steps, which show how to import the chart of accounts into Odoo:
  • Access Accounting → Configuration → Chart your system (CSV/XLSX format).
  • Ensure your file columns match the corresponding fields in Odoo (e.g., Account Code, Name, Type).
  • Start the import process by clicking Import.

The method enables users to transfer their data from previous ERP systems and accounting software systems.

Step 5: Configure Default Accounts

You can assign default accounts for specific financial operations. For example:

  • Receivable Account → Customer Invoices
  • Payable Account → Vendor Bills
  • Expense Account → Purchase transactions

To set defaults:

  • Go to Accounting → Configuration → Settings
  • Under Default Accounts, assign the relevant accounts for each function

This ensures Odoo automatically selects the correct account every time a transaction occurs.

Once your chart is configured correctly, you can also deepen your financial insights by leveraging invoice-level analytics. For a step-by-step guide on how to perform invoice analysis in Odoo 19, see our detailed blog post How to Perform Invoice Analysis in Odoo 19 Accounting.

Step 6: Group and Classify Accounts

To maintain a clean and structured chart of accounts, Odoo ERP groups accounts.

For example:

  • Assets (1000–1999)
  • Liabilities (2000–2999)
  • Revenue (4000–4999)
  • Expenses (5000–5999)

This logical structure facilitates quick reporting and informed decision-making.

Step 7: Verify Your Chart of Accounts Setup

Once your configuration is done, review your setup:

✅ Go to Accounting → Reporting → General Ledger

✅ Generate a few sample invoices and payments

✅ Check if the correct accounts are being used automatically

If all looks good, congratulations! You've completed your Odoo accounting module configuration.

Best Practices for Managing the Chart of Accounts in Odoo 19

After setting up your Chart of Accounts in Odoo 19, follow these best practices to maintain accuracy and efficiency:

1. Avoid Redundant Accounts

Please don't avoid creating multiple accounts for the same purpose, as this can complicate reporting.

2. Use Meaningful Codes

Choose codes that reflect hierarchy or function, such as 1000 for "Cash," 1100 for "Bank," etc.

3. Regularly Review Accounts

Conduct quarterly audits to identify and close accounts that are unused or inactive.

4. Odoo Reports

Utilize built-in reports, such as Trial Balance, Balance Sheet, and Profit and Loss (P&L), to ensure accuracy.

5. Use Localization Packages

Always install the correct localization for your country to ensure compliance with local regulations.

  • Dedicated post-implementation support

Build a Strong Financial Foundation with Odoo 19

Configuring the Chart of Accounts in Odoo 19 is not just a technical step; it's a strategic investment in your company's financial clarity and transparency.

With proper setup, you'll experience:

  • Real-time insights into business performance

Odoo 19 makes it easier than ever to transform accounting into a growth-driven process.

Understanding the Cash Flow Statement in Odoo 19 Accounting

The Cash Flow Statement in Odoo 19 Accounting provides a clear view of your organization's liquidity, helping you make informed strategic financial decisions.

Unlike traditional methods that require manual data entry and calculations, Odoo 19 automates most of the process. With its updated cash flow tags, financial statement setup, and cash flow automation features, it ensures accuracy and saves hours of manual work.

At Netilligence, as an Odoo Partner, we help businesses implement, customize, and optimize their Odoo accounting cash flow processes, making financial management effortless, accurate, and growth-driven.

How to Generate a Cash Flow Statement in Odoo 19 Accounting (Step-by-Step Tutorial)

Step 1: Enable the Accounting Module

First, ensure the Accounting app is installed in your Odoo 19 instance. Navigate to Apps > Accounting and click "Install."

Once installed, you'll gain access to all financial management tools, including cash flow statements, balance sheets, and profit & loss reports.

Step 2: Configure Your Chart of Accounts

Before generating any reports, ensure your chart of accounts is configured correctly.

Go to Accounting > Configuration > Chart of Accounts.

Here, review and edit your account types; each one determines how transactions appear in financial statements.

For example:

  • Cash and Bank accounts → Operating activities
  • Loan accounts → Financing activities
  • Investments → Investing activities

This setup ensures accurate categorization in the Odoo 19 cash flow statement.

Step 3: Set Up Cash Flow Tags

In Odoo 19, cash flow tags play a vital role. These tags define how each account contributes to the cash flow report.

You can configure them via Accounting > Configuration > Accounts and select the correct cash flow tag for each account.

For example:

  • Receipts → Inflow
  • Payments → Outflow

This mapping enables Odoo accounting cash flow reports to separate transactions automatically.

Step 4: Record Transactions

Record your invoices, bills, and payments as usual in Odoo. Every transaction affects your cash flow.

Odoo 19 automatically updates your cash flow report based on real-time data.

Step 5: Generate the Cash Flow Report

Now, go to Accounting > Reporting > Cash Flow Statement.

Here, you can:

  • Choose a date range.
  • Filter by journal or company.
  • Click "Generate Report."

Within seconds, you'll have a detailed Cash Flow Statement in Odoo 19 Accounting, clearly showing cash inflows and outflows categorized into:

  • Operating Activities
  • Investing Activities
  • Financing Activities

Step 6: Analyze and Export

Odoo allows you to export the cash flow statement in PDF or Excel format for sharing or presentation.

Analyze your liquidity trends, identify areas for improvement, and plan future expenditures accordingly.

How Odoo 19 Makes Cash Flow Automation Simpler

Automated Report Updates

The cash flow automation feature in Odoo updates your financial statements automatically whenever new transactions are recorded, saving manual effort and ensuring accuracy.

Scheduled Reports

You can schedule automatic cash flow reports to be sent on a weekly, monthly, or quarterly basis. These reports are emailed directly to finance managers and stakeholders.

Smart Filters & Dashboards

Title: RFQ Workflow in Odoo 19: Complete Step-by-Step Purchase Guide

Understanding the Odoo 19 RFQ Process

When you create an RFQ in Odoo 19, you're starting a conversation with your vendors. You list the products you want, add quantities, and Odoo automatically organizes everything for you. You can even send the same RFQ to multiple vendors at once, compare their offers, and choose the best deal all without switching tabs or doing manual work.

This is what makes RFQ work in Odoo 19 Purchase so assertively; it's not just about requesting prices, it's about saving time, improving communication, and making wise purchase decisions.

How the Odoo 19 Request for Quotation Works (Step-by-Step)

Let me walk you through it step by step as if we're doing it together.

You open Odoo → Go to Purchase

Click New RFQ.

Now, suppose you want to buy 100 units of Apple Pie for your business. You add them to your RFQ form. You can either choose a specific vendor or leave it blank for now.

Then, Odoo helps you move forward smoothly. It allows you to:

  • Add multiple products.
  • Set delivery dates.
  • Add notes for vendors.
  • Feel free to attach files if needed.

Once that's done, you hit Send RFQ, and your vendor instantly receives a professional quotation request.

Then, click on Confirm Order.

After clicking on the confirm order button, the RFQ instantly turns into a Purchase Order.

That's the magnificence of the Odoo 19 request for quotation. It looks simple, but it's smart, fast, and built for real business scenarios.

Exploring the RFQ Workflow in Odoo 19 Purchase

Now comes the part you'll really want to see. The RFQ workflow in Odoo 19 Purchase is similar to a journey that spans from requesting quotes to finalizing the purchase.

Draft Stage: You start by creating your RFQ.

Sent Stage: Once you send it to the vendor, Odoo updates its status automatically.

Waiting Stage: Now, you wait for the vendor's response.

Negotiation Stage: You can communicate, adjust terms, and ask questions right inside Odoo.

Confirm Stage: Once you're satisfied with a vendor's quote, you convert it into a purchase order.

The best part is that all of this is tracked, including every email, change, and update. You never lose any information.

The system keeps everything in one place, providing full RFQ status tracking in Odoo, so you always know which quotation is pending, which vendor has replied, and which deal you've confirmed.

Send RFQ to Multiple Vendors in Odoo 19 The Smart Way

Have you ever wished you could send one RFQ to multiple vendors without duplicating the effort?

Well, Odoo 19 makes that wish come true.

Here's how: you create one RFQ, then click Duplicate and choose a different vendor. Odoo will automatically copy your details and resend them. You can do this for as many vendors as you want.

Suppose three vendors receive your RFQ simultaneously. One offers a better price, another promises faster delivery, and the third gives an extended warranty.

All these options are now visible side by side on your Odoo screen. You can compare, analyze, and decide which one fits your business needs.

That's how the Send RFQ to multiple vendors feature in Odoo 19 simplifies a complex task into a few clicks, saving you hours and enabling data-driven decisions.
