You know that anxious feeling when you've sent a quotation and don't know what's happening next? Odoo 19 eliminates that.

The system tracks your RFQ status from start to finish. You can instantly see whether:

  • Your RFQ is still a draft.
  • It has been sent to vendors.
  • A vendor has responded.
  • It's late.
  • Or it's been converted into a purchase order.

This RFQ status tracking in Odoo gives you complete visibility, eliminating confusion and follow-up chaos.

You can also use filters to view all "waiting" or "late" RFQs, which helps you prioritize and stay organized.

That's one reason many companies appreciate how RFQs function in Odoo 19 Purchase. It makes tracking effortless.

Now let's talk about one of my favourite parts, vendor negotiation in Odoo 19 purchase.

When your vendors send back their quotations, you don't just have to accept them as they are. Odoo gives you the flexibility to negotiate professionally and transparently.

Here's how it works:

  • You can reply directly to vendor emails through Odoo's built-in chatter system.
  • You can ask for discounts, request changes in delivery dates, or even add comments for clarification.
  • Every message and reply is automatically recorded in the RFQ.

So, the next time you open that record, you'll see the whole conversation, with no lost emails and no missing details.

This makes negotiation easier and smarter. You build better relationships with vendors while ensuring your company gets the best value.

And honestly, that's what the Odoo 19 RFQ process is all about: making purchasing efficient and human.

The Final Step is to Convert RFQ to Purchase Order in Odoo 19

After comparing all offers and finalising your deal, convert the RFQ to a purchase order in Odoo 19.

This step is as simple as it sounds. You open your selected RFQ, click Confirm Order, and boom, your RFQ becomes a confirmed purchase order.

You don't need to re-enter details or duplicate any data. Odoo carries forward all vendor information, products, pricing, and terms, ensuring everything stays intact.

And here's something even better:

  • If you have sent the RFQ to multiple vendors, Odoo will prompt you to either cancel the alternative quotations or keep them open for later. That's clean, smart, and practical.
  • From this point, your Purchase Order becomes part of your inventory workflow, ready for receiving, billing, and payment.

That's the complete cycle of how RFQs work in Odoo 19 Purchase, from requesting prices to completing the deal.

You open Odoo, create a new RFQ, and add all the product details.

Then, with just a few clicks, you send the same RFQ to three suppliers.

Within a day, you start getting responses:

  • Vendor C gives you a bulk discount.

Now, you use Odoo's Compare Product Lines feature to see all three offers side by side. You like Vendor C's discount, but you ask for a faster delivery using the vendor negotiation in the Odoo 19 purchase feature.

Vendor C agrees, and you click Confirm Order. Odoo automatically converts RFQ to purchase order in Odoo 19, updates the status, and marks the other two RFQs as cancelled. Everything is tracked, transparent, and unified.

That's how prevalent and practical the RFQ workflow is in Odoo 19 purchase.

The Real Influence Behind RFQ Work in Odoo 19 Purchase

Here are a few little secrets that can help you get even more out of it:

  • Use alternatives wisely. Send RFQs to multiple vendors only when necessary; this helps keep your workflow clean.
  • Use notes and chatter. Communication inside Odoo keeps things transparent.
  • Check status daily. Don't let "Waiting" RFQs stay unattended.

These simple habits will keep your RFQ workflow in Odoo 19 purchase running smoothly and efficiently.

Wrapping It All Up — What You've Learned

By now, you know precisely how RFQs work in Odoo 19 Purchase from creating your first quotation to finalizing your order.

Title: How to Perform Internal Inventory Transfers in Odoo 19
Content:
Internal Inventory Transfers in Odoo 19

If you're looking to optimise your warehouse operations, streamline stock movements, and eliminate confusion around product movement, learning Internal Inventory Transfers in Odoo 19 is essential. Understanding Internal Inventory Transfers in Odoo 19

Internal transfers refer to moving products inside your own warehouses, from one location to another, such as:

  • Stock to Quality Control
  • Warehouse A to Warehouse B
  • Picking Area to Packing Zone
  • Manufacturing Input Stock to Production Floor

These movements do not involve customers or vendors. Instead, they help maintain operational flow and keep your internal stock levels accurate.

Odoo 19 makes this process easy and user-friendly, thanks to improved location mapping, updated routing logic, and enhanced multi-warehouse capabilities.

This guide to Internal Inventory Transfers in Odoo 19 shows you how to achieve flawless stock movement in just a few clicks.

Efficient inventory movement is at the heart of any successful warehouse operation. Poor tracking or manual processes often lead to:

  • Reduced customer satisfaction

With Odoo's move stock warehouse functionality, organisations ensure that every internal movement is documented, timed, and traceable.

Key benefits:

  • Real-time stock accuracy
  • Improved warehouse staff productivity
  • Zero manual errors
  • Smoother order fulfilment
  • Clear visibility across multiple warehouses

Odoo's automated workflows and smart rules make it simple to execute Odoo 19 stock transfer operations at scale.

Prerequisites Before Performing Internal Inventory Transfers in Odoo 19

Before performing Internal Inventory Transfers in Odoo 19, you must complete some basic configurations.

These include:

1. Enable Multi-Locations

Go to:

Inventory → 

Configuration → Settings → 

Warehouse → Storage Locations

Turn on "Storage Locations".

This enables internal routing inside the warehouse.

2. Enable Multi-Warehouse (if needed)

Go to:

Inventory → Configuration → Settings → Warehouse → Multi step routes

This helps you activate multi-warehouse management in Odoo.

3. Check Product Tracking Settings

Verify if your product uses:

  • Lots
  • Serial numbers
  • Units of measure

Correct product settings ensure accurate Odoo 19 stock transfer speeds and traceability.

Odoo's streamlined configuration steps make it ready for scalable operations within minutes.

Step 1 – Navigate to Internal Transfers Menu

Go to:

Inventory → Operations → Transfers

Here, you can view:

  • Incoming shipments
  • Outgoing deliveries
  • Internal transfers
  • Other stock movements

Click "New" to create a fresh internal transfer record.

Step 2 – Select Operation Type (Internal Transfer)

Choose the operation type as Internal Transfer. This ensures that Odoo understands the movement is occurring within your organisation, not outside it.

Step 3 – Select the Source Location

Choose the location where the product currently exists, such as:

  • Stock
  • Finished Goods
  • WH/Stock/Shelf 1
  • WH2/Stock

This allows accurate tracking and prevents errors.

Step 4 – Select the Destination Location

Choose where the stock should move to:

  • Quality Check
  • Return Area
  • Production Floor
  • Packing Zone

H2: Step 5 – Add Products to the Transfer

Enter:

  • Quantity
  • Lot or Serial Number (if required)

Step 6 – Validate the Transfer

Once all details are added:

  1. Click "Mark as To Process"

2. Then click "Validate"

Your stock now moves instantly from source to destination.

4. Enable Real-Time Inventory Alerts

Odoo can notify you when:

  • Stock falls below a minimum level

5. Train Warehouse Staff on the Odoo App

Odoo 19's mobile interface lets staff perform:

Directly from handheld devices.

Real-World Use Cases of Internal Inventory Transfers in Odoo 19

24/7 traceability ensures quality and efficiency.

Retail

Transfer items between:

This improves store availability and reduces lost sales.

E-Commerce

All of these scenarios rely heavily on Internal Inventory Transfers in Odoo 19 for accuracy and operational efficiency.

Common Mistakes and How to Avoid Them

Without enabling locations, you cannot perform internal transfers.

Always turn it on first.

  Mistake 2 – Incorrect Location Mapping

Double-check every new location added.

Avoid inconsistent stock data by ensuring:

They are always correct before transfers are validated.

Ensure all staff know this step.

Create SOPs for:

  • Stock movement
  • Transfer creation
  • Location updates

This ensures consistent inventory movement in Odoo 19.

Mastering Internal Inventory Transfers in Odoo 19 is vital for businesses that want complete control over their stock movement. From simple shelf-to-shelf transfers to complex multi-warehouse logistics, Odoo provides powerful tools to streamline operations.

Every time someone tops up, their balance automatically updates. As a business owner, you don't have to track it manually. What's great about this is its flexibility. You can use Odoo 19 customer loyalty features to connect these gift cards to loyalty programs, offer special rewards, or use them as part of promotions. Enable ‘‘Promotions, Loyalty & Gift Card’’ and click Save.

Then, click  Products > Gift cards & eWallet.

Click Orders > Quotations.

Create a New quotation.

First, specify the customer as ‘‘Abigail Peterson’’, add the product, and select the product quantity.

Now, let me show you how to use the coupon code. Scroll down and click on Coupon Code.

Paste the copied coupon code and click Apply.

Choose your reward, then click Apply again.

After applying the coupon card, you can see the amount deducted here.

From here, you can easily send or share this with your customer.

Select the customer and add the product.

Scroll down and click on the Reward button.

Then, choose your reward and click Apply.

After clicking apply, you will receive an eWallet and the amount. And that amount will be deducted from our total amount.

Then, click Orders > Vendors.

Title: How to Lock Confirmed Purchase Orders in Odoo 19?
Content:
If you use Odoo for managing your company's purchases, you already know how easy it is to create and confirm purchase orders. But have you ever noticed that sometimes, even after an order is confirmed, someone might edit it again? It could be a slight change in price, a quantity, or a vendor detail, but that one edit can cause confusion between your accounts, stock, and vendor agreements. That's why it's so important to learn how to lock confirmed purchase orders in Odoo 19.

In Odoo 19, there's a simple and effective way to keep your confirmed purchase orders safe from any unwanted changes. This feature is not just about control; it's about maintaining clean records, accurate data, and respected approvals. When you lock confirmed purchase orders in Odoo 19, you ensure that once an order is finalized, it remains that way unless someone with the necessary permission decides otherwise.

This blog will guide you through the process, explain how to restrict purchase order editing in Odoo, and discuss why the Odoo purchase order lock feature can make your daily purchase management easier and more reliable. We'll also discuss purchase order approval controls in Odoo and how you can utilize them to ensure that every confirmed order remains exactly as your team approved it.

If you've ever dealt with last-minute order changes or inconsistent data, this is something you'll definitely want to read until the end.

Why You Need to Lock Confirmed Purchase Orders in Odoo 19

Let's talk about what happens when confirmed purchase orders remain open for editing. Imagine your purchase manager confirms an order for 100 items, and later someone unknowingly changes that number to 80. Now your inventory team expects 100, but your vendor only ships 80. Accounting books one thing, and the warehouse receives another.

That's precisely why you should secure a purchase order in Odoo 19: it's about keeping everyone on the same page. Once an order is confirmed, it should stay untouched unless there's a valid reason to reopen it.

The Odoo purchase order lock feature enables this. Once you use it, Odoo automatically prevents any edits to confirmed purchase orders. You can still view all the information, but you won't be able to change it unless you deliberately unlock it, and only authorized users can do that.

This simple rule helps you avoid mistakes, miscommunication, and unnecessary back-and-forth between teams. It also helps your audit and approval process stay easy to track.

How to Lock Confirmed Purchase Orders in Odoo 19: Step-By-Step

Now that we understand why it matters, let's examine how to lock confirmed purchase orders in Odoo 19 in a few straightforward steps. You don't need to be a developer to do this; you need access to the settings.

Open your Odoo dashboard and head to the Purchase module.

Click on Configuration → Settings inside the Purchase app.

In Odoo 19, you'll find an option called ‘‘Lock Confirmed Orders’’. Enable the setting that mentions locking or preventing editing after confirmation. Once enabled, save your settings. Now, whenever you confirm a purchase order, Odoo will automatically restrict further changes.

Go to Orders → Requests for Quotation.

Click New.

Create a test purchase order, confirm it, and then attempt to edit it.

You'll notice the editing options are disabled. This confirms that your Odoo setup for purchase order editing restrictions is working.

From now on, no one can modify confirmed orders without the necessary access, ensuring your purchase data remains consistent and trustworthy.

Restrict Purchase Order Editing Odoo: Why This Step Is So Useful

When you restrict purchase order editing in Odoo, you set a clear rule for your purchase process. Once something is confirmed, it's considered final. This eliminates confusion about which version of an order is the valid one.

Your finance team doesn't have to worry about numbers being changed after approval. Your warehouse team knows precisely what to expect from suppliers. And your procurement manager can relax, knowing that no one will alter confirmed data.

This simple purchase order editing restriction in Odoo also facilitates a more efficient workflow. Everyone focuses on new orders or approvals instead of double-checking old ones. It builds trust across teams because everyone can rely on the data they see.

Understanding the Odoo Purchase Order Lock Feature

The Odoo purchase order lock feature is not just a setting; it's a control system that strengthens how your business handles purchase approvals.

Here's how it works behind the scenes:

When a purchase order is in "Draft" state, all fields are editable. You can change the vendor, quantity, prices, or any other details as needed. However, once you confirm the order, Odoo updates it to a "Locked" or "Confirmed" state. In this state, you can only view the order; you cannot edit it.

If someone tries to make changes, they'll notice the fields are disabled. This ensures that the order details stay exactly as approved.

This feature helps you secure purchase order data in Odoo 19 by protecting it from accidental edits or unauthorized updates. It's like sealing a document after signing; everything stays as it was agreed upon.

How to Lock Purchase Order Odoo 19 and Control Who Can Edit It

Sometimes, businesses still need flexibility. For example, a senior manager or an admin might need to correct a vendor reference or change a date after confirmation. Odoo 19 allows this in a controlled way.

You can define user permissions so that only specific roles can unlock or modify confirmed purchase orders. This balance gives your company the right mix of control and flexibility.

So, if you're wondering how to lock a purchase order in Odoo 19 without blocking your workflow, the answer is permissions. Limit editing rights for regular users and allow higher-level staff to make necessary corrections as needed. This keeps your purchase order approval controls in Odoo active, ensuring a consistent process.

Purchase Order Editing Restriction Odoo Keeps Data Consistent

When you add a purchase order editing restriction in Odoo, you're not just stopping people from editing. You're maintaining consistency across all your business data from procurement to accounting and stock.

Every confirmed order becomes a fixed reference point. Your reports stay accurate. Your stock levels match your purchase records. Your accounting entries remain correct.

And if any changes are needed, they go through a proper approval process. This adds a layer of responsibility to your team, as they now know that every confirmed order represents an approved, unchangeable agreement.

This approach reduces human errors and helps your business run smoothly with fewer purchase discrepancies.

Secure Purchase Order Odoo 19 That Builds Trust and Accuracy

To secure a purchase order, Odoo 19 means to protect your company's agreements with vendors. Every confirmed purchase is a commitment to an official record of what you've agreed to buy and at what price.

By securing these orders, you avoid awkward vendor disputes or internal confusion about "who changed what." You also save time during audits because every purchase record remains unchanged since it was approved.

In daily business life, these small details make a huge difference. Teams spend less time resolving data issues and more time focusing on actual work.

Purchase Order Approval Controls Odoo

Approval control is another crucial aspect of maintaining an organized purchase system. With purchase order approval controls in Odoo, you can determine who can confirm an order and who must approve it before it is confirmed.

For example, you might want:

  • Regular staff to create draft orders only.
  • Managers are responsible for confirming orders with a value below a specific threshold.
  • Directors to approve larger orders.

When you combine Odoo's purchase order approval controls with the Odoo purchase order lock feature, you create a workflow that's clear, reliable, and free from confusion. Every order follows a structured path from draft to approval to confirmation, and once confirmed, it remains fixed.

Real-Life Example of Why You Should Lock Confirmed Orders

Let's say your purchasing team confirms an order for 50 office chairs at $100 each. Later, someone from another department changes the quantity to 40 or updates the price by mistake.

When your supplier delivers 50 chairs and sends an invoice for $ 5,000, your accounts team will be surprised to see that the PO states $ 4,000. You'll spend hours trying to figure out what went wrong.

However, if you had used the method to lock confirmed purchase orders in Odoo 19, none of this would have happened. The confirmed data would stay the same, your records would match, and your finance, procurement, and stock teams would all stay aligned.

This is why this feature is not just technical; it's practical and saves time for everyone involved.

How Odoo 19 Makes Purchase Management More Reliable

Odoo 19 places a strong emphasis on data control and process accuracy. The Odoo purchase order lock feature is a small yet significant improvement for businesses that frequently place orders.

By adding these controls, you're making your Odoo setup more reliable and easier to manage. Every confirmed purchase order becomes a solid record that reflects a clear business decision, with no surprises and no confusion.

When you utilize purchase order editing restrictions in Odoo, secure purchase orders in Odoo 19, and implement purchase order approval controls in Odoo, you create a stable purchasing process that supports your business growth with confidence.

Final Thoughts on How to Lock Confirmed Purchase Orders in Odoo 19

When it comes to managing purchases, accuracy is everything. Minor edits after confirmation can lead to big problems later, and fixing them always takes time. That's why learning how to lock confirmed purchase orders in Odoo 19 is so important.

It's not just about control; it's about clarity. It's about keeping your team aligned, your vendors satisfied, and your financial data accurate and up to date. The Odoo purchase order lock feature gives you precisely that.

Once you utilize purchase order approval controls and purchase order editing restrictions in Odoo, you'll notice that your purchase process becomes more organized and dependable.

Your team will have fewer misunderstandings, your approvals will carry weight, and your confirmed orders will remain precisely as they should be final, approved, and secure.

If you haven't tried it yet, take a few minutes today to secure your purchase order in Odoo 19. You'll see how much smoother your purchase management becomes once you implement this simple control.

Title: How to Manage User Types & Access Rights in Odoo 19 Accounting?

Access Rights in Odoo 19 Accounting: Why It Matters More Than Ever

Access Rights in Odoo 19 Accounting play a decisive role in securing your company's most sensitive financial data. From invoices and vendor bills to tax reports and journals, accounting information must be accessible only to the right people at the right time with the correct permissions.

In modern businesses, accounting teams are no longer limited to a single bookkeeper or accountant. CFOs, auditors, finance managers, sales teams, and even operations staff may require partial access to financial records. Without structured Access Rights in Odoo 19 Accounting, businesses risk data leaks, fraud, errors, and compliance violations.

Odoo 19 introduces improved and more flexible access rights management, allowing companies to define clear accounting roles, control user permissions, and enhance accounting security without complexity.

Whether you are a startup, SME, or enterprise, mastering Access Rights in Odoo 19 Accounting ensures:

  • Strong financial security
  • Error-free bookkeeping
  • Regulatory compliance
  • Smooth internal workflows

In this guide by Netilligence - Odoo Partner, you will learn how to manage accounting user types, roles, and permissions effectively using Odoo 19.

How to Manage User Permissions in Odoo 19 Accounting (Step-by-Step)

Step 1: Enable Developer Mode

Go to Settings → Activate Developer Mode.

Step 2: Configure User Groups

  • Navigate to Settings → Users & Companies → Groups
  • Select Accounting groups
  • Edit permissions as needed

Step 3: Assign Roles to Users

  • Open Users
  • Assign correct accounting groups
  • Save changes

Step 4: Test Access Rights

Always test with a sample user to confirm:

  • Correct visibility
  • No unauthorised access

Proper setup ensures error-free Access Rights in Odoo 19 Accounting.

 

Understanding User Types in Odoo 19 Accounting

Before configuring Access Rights in Odoo 19 Accounting, it is essential to understand how Odoo categorises users.

Odoo 19 Accounting User Types Explained

Odoo uses role-based access control (RBAC), where users are assigned to predefined or custom groups.

Common accounting-related user types include:

  • Accountant
  • Billing User
  • Accounting Manager
  • Read-Only User
  • Auditor
  • Administrator

Each user type comes with preset permissions that determine what they can view, create, edit, approve, or delete within the accounting module.

Why User Types Are Critical for Accounting Security

Without clearly defined user types:

  • Unauthorized users may modify financial data
  • Sensitive reports may be exposed
  • Internal fraud risks increase

Proper Access Rights in Odoo 19 Accounting ensure accountability and transparency across departments.

 

Access Rights in Odoo 19 Accounting: Core Structure

How Access Rights Work in Odoo 19

Odoo controls accounting access through three key layers:

  1. User Groups
  2. Access Control Lists (ACLs)
  3. Record Rules

Together, these elements form the foundation of Access Rights in Odoo 19 Accounting.

1. User Groups in Odoo 19

User groups define what users can see and do.

Examples:

  • Accountant → Can manage invoices and payments
  • Billing Clerk → Can create customer invoices only
  • Accounting Manager → Full control over accounting

Assigning users to the correct group is the first step in managing access rights in Odoo 19.

2. Access Control Lists (ACLs)

ACLs define permissions such as:

  • Read
  • Write
  • Create
  • Delete

For example:

  • An accountant may read & write
  • An auditor may read only

Well-configured ACLs prevent unauthorized actions in accounting workflows.

3. Record Rules

Record rules decide which records a user can access.

Example:

  • A branch accountant sees only branch-specific invoices
  • A group CFO sees consolidated records

This granular approach strengthens Odoo accounting access control.

Standard Accounting Roles Available in Odoo 19

Odoo 19 provides predefined accounting roles:

Billing User

  • Create customer invoices
  • View payment status
  • No access to financial reports

Accountant

  • Manage vendor bills
  • Reconcile bank statements
  • Handle taxes and journals

Accounting Manager

  • Full accounting control
  • Approve journals
  • Lock fiscal periods

Each role is designed to maintain secure Access Rights in Odoo 19 Accounting while promoting efficiency.

Custom Accounting Roles for Your Business

Every business is unique. Odoo 19 allows you to create custom roles based on your internal structure:

  • Junior accountant
  • External auditor
  • Finance executive

Custom roles ensure flexible access rights management without compromising security.

Best Practices for Odoo 19 Accounting Security

Follow the Principle of Least Privilege

Give users only what they need.

Separate Accounting Duties

Split responsibilities between:

  • Invoice creation
  • Payment approval
  • Reporting

Regularly Audit User Access

Remove unused or outdated permissions.

Use Multi-Level Approval Workflows

Reduce fraud and prevent single-user control.

Strong Odoo accounting security protects your financial integrity.

  • Ignoring audit trails
  • Not revoking access of ex-employees

Title: How to Create Pricelist in Odoo 19 Sales?
Content:
Suppose you're running a business where pricing varies from one customer to another, or you offer discounts, special offers, or bulk pricing. In that case, setting up a pricelist in Odoo 19 Sales can make your life much easier.

In this guide, I'll explain everything you need to know about creating a price list in Odoo 19 in a simple, practical way. We'll go through how to manage multiple prices per product in Odoo, how to set up your Odoo price rules setup, and how to handle Odoo 19 discount pricing effectively. You'll also learn how to configure product pricelists in Odoo and how to use dynamic pricing in Odoo 19 for real business situations.

By the end, you'll be confident about creating your own price lists and setting prices that make sense for your customers and your business goals.

Why You Need a Pricelist in Odoo 19 Sales

Every business owner has faced this challenge: how to sell the same product at different prices to different customer types without getting confused or losing track. This is where the pricelist in Odoo 19 Sales helps. It's a simple feature that allows you to set specific prices for each customer, region, or situation.

For example, you can sell your product at one price to retail customers and another to distributors. Or you may want to give discounts when someone buys in bulk. Instead of manually adjusting prices each time, you can let Odoo handle it with Odoo 19 pricelist creation.

Once you understand how this works, pricing stops being a headache. You'll have complete control and clarity over who gets what price, and your sales team will save time and effort.

Odoo 19 Pricelist Creation – The First Step to Organized Pricing

To start your Odoo 19 pricelist creation, the first thing you need to do is enable the pricelist feature in your Odoo settings. Here's how:

Go to the Sales app in Odoo.

Open Configuration → Settings.

Under the Pricing section, enable the Pricelists option and click Save.

Now you've unlocked the core feature that lets you manage different prices for different products or customers.

This step is essential because Odoo offers two approaches: fixed prices or flexible rules. If you only need to assign different prices per product, use the multiple prices per product option in Odoo. But if your business requires discounts, date-based pricing, or quantity-based offers, you'll prefer to work with Odoo's price rule setup.

Odoo Sales Price List Tutorial – Setting Up Your Pricelist

Once the pricelist feature is active, go to the Sales app.

 Direct to Products → Pricelists.

Click New.

Here's what you need to do next:

Give your pricelist a clear name, like "International Customer". Select the currency and company (if applicable) and click on Add a line.

Select the Product, apply price rules and click Save & Close.

Now, I want to add this price list under customer sale order. So, let’s move to Orders → Orders.

Create a New order.

Select the Customer and click on Add a product.

Specify the attributes of the product and click on Confirm.

As you can see an option called Pricelist and under the drop-down menu find the pricelist which we created above (International Customer).

Specify the product quantity and click on Confirm.

Then, click on the Delivery smart button.

Let’s Validate.

And move to the sale order.

Now, Create an Invoice based on the product.

Select regular invoice and click on Create Draft.

Let’s Confirm the invoice.

Click on Pay button.

The Customer is ready for the payment. So let’s Create Payment for this product.

Just in few clicks we are done with the pricelist and we successfully sold our product to the customer.

That’s how you can create a pricelist inside the Odoo 19 Sales app and you can apply that on different kinds of customers as per your requirements.

How Multiple Prices Per Product in Odoo Work

The concept of multiple prices per product in Odoo is simple: it means you can sell the same item at different prices without duplicating your product entries.

Let's say you have a single product called "Organic Apple Juice." You might want to set:

  • $5 per bottle for retail buyers
  • $4 per bottle for distributors
  • $3.5 per bottle for large quantity purchases

All of this can be done from one product record using different pricelists. So, when your sales team creates a quotation, Odoo automatically selects the correct price based on the customer they're selling to.

This not only saves time but also reduces mistakes. You'll never have to remember which customer gets which discount; Odoo handles that for you.

Adding Flexibility to Your Pricing with Odoo Price Rules Setup

Now, let's talk about Odoo price rules, which are the heart of smart pricing.

Price rules let you define how prices are calculated. You can set them based on:

  • A fixed amount
  • A discount percentage
  • A formula (for advanced pricing logic)

For example, suppose you want to apply a 10% discount to a product category or set a new price for a specific quantity. In that case, you can create a rule that automatically adjusts prices when those conditions are met.

You can also control the start and end dates of each rule. So, if you're running a New Year's sale or a festive discount, Odoo can handle it without you having to change the price back later manually.

The Odoo price rules setup is beneficial when you're managing extensive product catalogs or frequently changing your pricing strategy.

Odoo 19 Discount Pricing that Gives Smart Offers Without Extra Work

Discounts are part of almost every business strategy. But managing them manually often leads to confusion. With Odoo 19 discount pricing, you can automate discounts directly through your pricelist.

You can create percentage-based discounts or special offers that only apply to certain products, customers, or order quantities.

For example:

  • "Buy 10, get 10% off"
  • "20% discount for premium customers"
  • "Flat $2 off on each item during the weekend"

These discounts can be visible on customer invoices or hidden depending on how you configure them. It gives you control over how transparent you want to be with your clients.

This feature ensures you never miss applying a discount and keeps your promotions consistent across all sales channels.

Product Pricelist Configuration in Odoo – Keeping Everything Organized

The product price list configuration in Odoo helps you manage your pricing structure efficiently. Once you've created your price lists and rules, you can assign them directly to customers.

Here's how:

Go to Sales → Customers.

Select the customer you want.

In the "Sales & Purchase" tab, set the pricelist that applies to them.

Now, whenever this customer places an order, Odoo automatically applies the correct pricing without any manual changes.

This step ensures consistency and saves your sales team time. You don't have to worry about applying the wrong discounts or sending incorrect quotes anymore.

Dynamic Pricing in Odoo 19 – Real Pricing Flexibility

Now, this is where Odoo starts to feel truly helpful. Dynamic pricing in Odoo 19 lets your prices change automatically based on predefined logic such as cost, season, or customer segment.

For example, if your product cost changes, you can configure Odoo to calculate the sales price by adding a fixed margin to the cost. So even if your cost fluctuates, your profit margin stays safe.

This approach gives you pricing flexibility while keeping everything organized. Instead of manually updating prices whenever costs change, Odoo's dynamic setup handles it for you.

Dynamic pricing is also ideal for businesses that operate across multiple regions or run frequent promotions. You can maintain consistency while remaining competitive across different markets.

A Simple Example of How It Works

Let's say you run a small company that sells both online and offline. You have retail customers, wholesale buyers, and seasonal promotions.

Here's how you can use a pricelist in Odoo 19 Sales to handle all of it:

Title: How to Create Work Centers in Odoo 19 Manufacturing?
Content:
Whenever someone begins using Odoo for manufacturing, one of the first questions is how to create work centers in Odoo 19 that accurately reflect their production flow. This question makes complete sense. If your work centers are not set up correctly, your planning becomes confusing, your production orders don't behave as you expect, and your team ends up relying on guesswork rather than a proper system.

That is why, before anything else, we need to understand the purpose of work centers and how they support real manufacturing. When you know how to create work centers in Odoo, you finally start controlling your production instead of just reacting to problems.

Odoo 19 Work Centers – Understanding What They Truly Mean in Your Factory's Everyday Life

Before you even start clicking around in the system, it's essential to understand what Odoo 19 work centers represent inside your factory. Think of them as the digital version of your real machines, real people, or real workstations. If something happens on your shop floor, your work centers should reflect that inside Odoo. Many companies start using work centers without understanding them, and then later they feel the system is confusing or inaccurate.

But the truth is that Odoo only knows what you tell it, and if you do not define work centers properly, Odoo cannot plan your production correctly. When I speak to manufacturing teams, they often say they know their machines well but are unsure how to convey that to the system. And this is where Odoo 19 work centers serve as the link between your physical factory and your digital workspace. Once you understand the meaning behind each section of a work center, your entire production flow starts making more sense.

Odoo Manufacturing Work Center Setup – The Real Beginning of Everything

Whether you are starting from scratch or correcting an old setup, the first step in Odoo manufacturing work center setup is enabling the right features. Users often jump straight into configuration screens without activating work orders. And without work orders, Odoo cannot use work centers correctly. Once work orders are active, Odoo opens up the full manufacturing flow for you.

But let me explain why this step matters: your manufacturing depends on proper structure. When the system knows you want to work with step-by-step operations, it starts guiding your production according to the real machines and real timings you define. This is why your Odoo manufacturing work center setup should begin with the right switches turned on. It sets the stage for everything you will do afterward, and it ensures the system behaves the way your production team needs.

How to Configure Work Centers in Odoo – The Step Where Most People Get Confused

Now, we can move on to understanding how to configure work centers in Odoo correctly. And trust me, this is the part where most users feel a little lost because they see a lot of fields and don't know what each one means for their real shop floor. When you create a work center, the first thing you decide is its name. This may sound simple, but many teams choose vague names that later confuse everyone. If your machine is a cutting station, call it Cutting Station. If it's an assembly table, call it Assembly Table. Clear names help your team understand exactly what step happens where.

Once you add the name, you see options for capacity, costing, efficiency, OEE, and working hours. And this is where users usually stop thinking and start guessing. But you don't need to guess. You only need to describe your real production inside Odoo. Whatever happens in your factory every day is exactly what you enter here. That's how you learn to configure work centers in Odoo with confidence, not fear.

Step-by-Step Guide to Create Work Centers in Odoo 19 Manufacturing

Now this is the part you came for. Follow these steps in order, and you'll have your work centers ready in just a few minutes.

The moment you enter Odoo, click on the Manufacturing app from your dashboard. This is the home base for everything related to your production process. Once you're inside, you'll instantly feel the entire workflow layout in front of you.

A lot of people miss this part and then wonder why they can't find work centers. Just go to:

Configuration → Settings.

Enable Work Orders, then click Save. This will activate all features related to work centers and operations.

Now that everything is activated, go to:

Configuration→ Work Centers

Here you'll see an empty list if you're setting up for the first time. Click New.

A clean form will pop up, and this is where your real setup begins. Enter basic details:

Work Center Name (e.g., Cutting Machine A, Assembly Line 1, Packing Station)

Code (short identifier)

Working Hours (crucial for scheduling)

Think of this page as a way to describe your real-life workplace, but digitally.

Now, tell Odoo how strong and capable your work center is.

Time Efficiency: how fast this center works

Setup Time / Cleanup Time: so Odoo calculates accurate production time

When you add these details, Odoo automatically optimizes your production. Add Costing Information. This section helps you understand how much each production step costs you.

Once this is added, Odoo will show you the real manufacturing cost based on actual work center usage. This is super helpful when you want to improve profit margins.

Your work center is ready. But it won't work until you link it to an operation. Go to:

Operations → Work Orders

Choose the operation and select your new work center (Packing Station).

Now your production workflow becomes complete. The final step is to test it. Create a new Manufacturing Order, Confirm it.

And then click on Work Orders. You'll now see your new work center assigned and active.

 This is where everything comes alive, tracking time, performance, and actual production movement.

Odoo 19 Manufacturing Tutorial – Capacity, Timing, and Why They Matter More Than You Think

If you follow any Odoo 19 manufacturing tutorial, you will repeatedly see one thing: capacity matters. This one value directly affects how Odoo schedules your production. If your machine handles one item at a time, your capacity is 1. But if you have four identical stations that work together, your capacity might be 4. Setting the capacity wrong is one of the biggest reasons why planning goes off track.

People often set everything to 1, even when their machine can handle more, and Odoo starts planning everything slowly. Then they think the system is the issue, but the setup is the real problem. When you genuinely understand your factory, you know exactly what to enter here. That is why a proper Odoo 19 manufacturing tutorial always explains that your work center should reflect your actual daily capacity, not what you assume or guess.

Odoo Work Centers Manufacturing – Working Hours: Decide Your Entire Planning Flow

Another misunderstood area in Odoo work centers manufacturing is working hours. If your team works from 9 am to 6 pm, Odoo should know that. If your machine works two shifts, Odoo should know that. If your operator only uses a machine during the first half of the day, Odoo should know that too. When working hours are wrong, Odoo starts planning tasks when no one is actually working.

This creates stress, confusion, and a last-minute rush. But when working hours match reality, Odoo guides your production in a predictable rhythm. And this is what good manufacturing feels like. It feels like your system is walking with you, not pulling you in the wrong direction. That is the real value of understanding Odoo work centers and manufacturing, and of correctly defining your calendar.

Work Center Configuration Odoo MRP – Costing and the Clarity It Brings to Your Product Pricing

Once you reach the costing section in Odoo MRP work center configuration, many users stop paying attention. They think costing is optional. But the truth is that costing tells you how much it actually costs to manufacture a product. If your machine consumes electricity, needs labor, or requires regular maintenance, all of this affects your product cost. And Odoo can only calculate real cost if you enter realistic values here.

You don't need complicated calculations. Just enter the hourly cost of that machine or the labor charge connected to that workstation. Over time, this helps you understand which part of your production costs more and where your money is being used. Without costing, you may end up selling a product without realizing how much you spent making it. That is why the Odoo MRP work center configuration helps you see the financial side of manufacturing in a simple, honest way.

How to Create Work Centers in Odoo – Connecting Work Centers with Your Bill of Materials

Now that your work center is ready, the next step in learning how to create work centers in Odoo is linking them to your BoM operations. Many users don't know this step is necessary, and then they wonder why their production orders don't show any operations. When you open your BoM and add operations, you choose which work center performs which step.

This connection is vital because it tells Odoo how your product is actually made. Without this link, work centers have no role in your production. But once linked, everything changes. Your production orders become detailed, realistic, and easier to follow. You can see which step happens first, which machine is involved, how long it takes, and when the next step starts. This is the moment when the effort you put into work center setup finally shows results inside your manufacturing flow.

Odoo 19 Work Centers – The Small Mistakes That Cause Big Manufacturing Confusion

Every manufacturing team I've worked with repeats the same mistakes when dealing with Odoo 19 work centers, and I want to share them so you don't fall into the same issues. The first mistake is incorrect capacity. The second mistake is unrealistic working hours. The third mistake is ignoring costing. And the fourth mistake is failing to connect operations in the BoM.

These four things may look small, but they create major planning problems. Once you fix them, everything becomes clearer. Production orders feel more accurate. Timelines make sense. And your team stops guessing and starts trusting the system. This is the difference a properly configured work center makes.

Odoo Manufacturing Work Center Setup – How It Helps You Feel More In Control of Your Factory

When you complete your Odoo manufacturing work center setup, you begin to see your factory differently. You feel more aware of where delays occur, which machines are overloaded, which operations take longer, and how your planning behaves.

Odoo gives you simple dashboards that show machine usage, performance, and timing. You don't need complicated reports. These small insights tell you everything you need to know about your production line. This is why I always say that work centers are not just technical settings. They are the digital heartbeat of your factory. When they are set correctly, the rest of your manufacturing flow becomes easier to manage.

Your Clarity Begins When You Learn How to Create Work Centers in Odoo

Now that you understand how work centers behave, how they are created, and how they guide your production planning, you can move forward with a clearer mind. You now understand the real purpose of knowing how to set up work centers in Odoo. You know why capacity matters, why working hours shape your planning, why costing brings financial clarity, and why linking operations is necessary for actual production flow.

This entire guide was written as if I were sitting right in front of you, helping you fix these issues step by step. If you ever felt confused or unsure about Odoo's manufacturing module, I hope this gave you the confidence you needed.

Step-by-Step: How to Create a Commission Plan in Odoo 19 Sales

So, let's get practical. Here's how you can easily create a commission plan in Odoo using the Odoo 19 Sales app.

First, go to your Odoo Sales app.

Head over to Configuration > Settings.

And look for "Commissions” under the Invoicing section. Please enable it and click Save. This step activates the commission management module in Odoo 19, allowing you to start building your plans.

Once enabled, go to Commissions > Commission Plans.

Click on New. Here, you'll define the structure of your Odoo 19 ERP commission plan, including its name, description, and plan type. Let’s specify the commission name, and in this example, I am going to create a Target based commission plan and set a target for each salesperson. This means each salesperson will have a target to hit, and the commission will be calculated accordingly. Now, set the Effective period and Target Frequency to monthly, quarterly, or yearly, as per your requirements.

The important part, called a 'Payslip input', you cannot see in Odoo 18 because it's a new feature in Odoo 19. If you check the ‘‘Payslip input’’ box, Odoo will automatically push the commission amount into the employee’s payroll as an input line. And every time you use the Odoo 19 events app, your confidence grows. This is how event management becomes enjoyable instead of stressful.

I wrote this entire blog as if I were standing beside you, showing you where to click, how to think, and how to move step by step. If you follow this guide, your first event using the Odoo 19 events app will feel simple, clear, and entirely achievable. Title: How to Create & Manage Tickets in Odoo 19 Helpdesk?
Content:
If you’re handling customer queries daily and still depending on emails, WhatsApp messages, or random notes, I know exactly how messy it feels. One message gets missed, another customer follows up again, and suddenly, your team looks busy, but nothing feels under control. This is precisely where learning to manage tickets in Odoo 19 Helpdesk starts to make sense.

In this blog, I’m not going to talk in complicated system language. I’ll talk to you like we’re sitting together and solving a real problem. I’ll show you how tickets are created, how they move, how teams work on them, and how nothing slips through the cracks when you properly manage tickets in Odoo 19 Helpdesk.

Why Businesses Struggle Before They Manage Tickets in Odoo 19 Helpdesk

Most businesses don’t fail at customer support because they don’t care. They fail because everything is scattered. Emails are in one place, calls are somewhere else, and follow-ups depend on memory. When you don’t have a clear system, customers feel ignored even when your team is trying hard.

The moment you decide to manage tickets in Odoo 19 Helpdesk, things start to become visible. You know who raised the issue, what the problem is, who is handling it, and what stage it is at. That clarity alone removes half of the daily stress.

Every Customer Story Begins with Odoo 19 Helpdesk Ticket Creation

Every support issue starts with a straightforward action: creating an Odoo 19 helpdesk ticket. Think of a ticket as a written version of what your customer is trying to tell you. When a customer sends an email, fills a form, or contacts your team, Odoo turns that message into a ticket so nothing gets lost.

With Odoo 19 helpdesk ticket creation, you don’t have to worry about searching emails or WhatsApp chats anymore. Everything comes into one system where the issue, customer name, and request are clearly visible. This is where support teams feel relief because now they can focus on solving the problem instead of finding it.

Create Customer Ticket Odoo So No Issue Is Ever Ignored

Many customers don’t complain loudly; they just leave silently when they don’t get a response. This is why it is essential to create a customer ticket as soon as a request comes in. When you make a customer ticket in Odoo, you are basically telling your customer, “Yes, we have received your issue and we are working on it.”

In Odoo 19, creating a ticket is quick and straightforward. Once the ticket is created, it stays there until it is resolved. This gives both your support team and your customers peace of mind, as nothing is forgotten or ignored. To create customer tickets in Odoo, follow these steps:

Direct to Helpdesk Module.

Go to the Tickets > My Tickets.

Click on New.

Enter the ticket subject, select the customer, assign priority, and team, then Save the ticket.

There are 5 stages for a ticket: New, In Progress, On Hold, Solved, and Cancelled. After creating the ticket, you can move it to the In Progress stage. If you want to hold it, click the On Hold button.

And when the problem is solved, you can move this ticket to the Solved stage; if it is cancelled, you can move it to the Cancelled stage.

Now, go back to Tickets > My Tickets, remove all default filters, and click the Kanban view.

In the Kanban view, you can find all the tickets, including the one we just created and moved to the solved stage.

This simple process ensures every customer concern is documented and tracked efficiently.

Manage Helpdesk Tickets Odoo 19 Without Confusion

Once tickets start coming in, the real challenge begins. This is where businesses usually get stuck. If tickets are not appropriately handled, support teams feel overwhelmed. That is why it is vital to manage Odoo 19 helpdesk tickets in a clear, organized manner.

When you manage helpdesk tickets in Odoo 19, you always know which ticket is new, which one is being worked on, and which one is waiting for customer feedback. This clarity helps your team respond faster and with more confidence. Instead of asking each other what to do next, everyone can see the status directly in Odoo.

Odoo Helpdesk Ticket Workflow That Makes Daily Work Easier

The Odoo helpdesk ticket workflow is like a clear path that every ticket follows. From the moment a ticket is created until it is closed, it progresses in steps. This helps your team understand exactly where the ticket stands at any moment.

With a proper Odoo helpdesk ticket workflow, there is no guessing. A ticket is either new, in progress, waiting for information, or resolved. This helps managers see delays early and helps agents stay focused on what needs attention right now.

Odoo 19 Ticket Assignment Stages That Reduce Team Pressure

One common issue support teams face is uneven workload. Some agents get too many tickets while others wait. Odoo 19 ticket assignment stages solve this problem by clearly defining who is responsible for what.

How Odoo Discount Without Losing Profit Becomes Practical

Many people think that avoiding loss during discounting is complicated. In reality, it becomes simple when the system thinks for you. An Odoo discount that doesn't erode profit works when every discount is measured against cost and margin.

In Odoo 19 Sales, you can see precisely how a discount affects profit. When sales teams know this information, they start making better decisions. Instead of blindly pushing discounts, they focus on deals that make sense for both the customer and the business.

Let’s see how innovative businesses offer discounts inside Odoo 19 sales without killing their profits. For that, let’s open the Sales module from your Odoo 19 dashboard.

Go to Configuration > Settings.

Under the Pricing section, enable the Discounts option and click Save.

Then go to Orders > Quotations.

Click New.

Specify the Customer.

Then add products. After adding the products, you can find an option called Discounts, but no discount is applied here.

And to give discounts without killing profits, we have an option under the Order lines tab. So click on the Discount Smart button.

Now, you will see a small wizard; here, you can see the discounts and three options, so you can either apply a discount or use one of the three options. So, let’s choose the first one, On All Order Lines. It’s basically mentioned that the same discount percentage is applied to every product line in the sales order. Provide the discount percentage and click on Apply.

As you can see below, you will get a 5% discount on each product.

Now, select the second option, Global Discount, enter 10% as the discount percentage, and click Apply.

After that, you can see another line, which means the global discount that is 10%, and you can find the unit price is and the total amount that is deducted as 10% from the total amount of the product.

Let’s move on to the last one: Fixed Amount. It is basically a fixed value being deducted. So, apply a fixed $5 discount and click Apply.

As you can see below, it is also showing a third line, which means a $5 deduction from the total amount of your product.

Title: How to Transfer Data from Odoo 17 to Odoo 18 Using XML-RPC?
Content:
Integrating and migrating data between different Odoo instances is a common requirement during upgrades, testing, or multi-database setups. One of the most reliable methods to achieve this is Odoo 17 to Odoo 18 using XML-RPC, a remote procedure call protocol that allows external applications to communicate with Odoo using XML over HTTP.

Odoo exposes its models and operations through a powerful XML-RPC API, allowing you to authenticate, read records, create new ones, and perform complete data migrations programmatically. In this blog, we will walk through a real-world example of migrating CRM Lead records from Odoo 17 to Odoo 18 using XML-RPC and Python. The guide is written to be practical, easy to follow, and suitable for developers and functional consultants alike.

Why XML-RPC Is Ideal for Odoo Data Migration

XML-RPC (Extensible Markup Language, Remote Procedure Call) is a protocol that allows one system to call methods on another system remotely using HTTP. Odoo exposes its models and business logic via XML-RPC, enabling external access to its databases.

Using XML-RPC for Odoo integration offers several advantages:

✔ Works across different Odoo versions

✔ Supports full CRUD operations (Create, Read, Update, Delete)
✔ Enables communication between completely separate servers
✔ Allows selective migration of specific models
✔ Ideal for automation, upgrades, and integration testing

Unlike manual exports or one-time imports, XML-RPC provides repeatability and control, which is especially important in production environments.

Prerequisites Before You Begin Transfer Data From Odoo 17 to Odoo 18 Using XML-RPC

Before Transfer Data From Odoo 17 to Odoo 18 using XML-RPC Make sure the following requirements are met:

  • Python 3 is installed on your system
  • CRM module is installed on both Odoo 17 and Odoo 18
  • You have admin or API access to both databases
  • Both Odoo servers are accessible via HTTP
  • Basic understanding of Odoo models and Python scripting

Note: This guide focuses on simple fields. Relational fields such as many2one, one2many, and many2many may require ID mapping, which should be handled separately.

Migration Overview

We will perform the migration in five logical steps:

  1. Import the required Python library
  2. Connect to the Odoo 17 (source) server
  3. Connect to the Odoo 18 (target) server
  4. Fetch CRM Lead data from Odoo 17
  5. Insert the fetched data into Odoo 18

Step-by-Step Guide to Transfer Data From Odoo 17 to Odoo 18 Using XML-RPC

Step 1: Import Required Python Library

Python includes xmlrpc.client by default, so no additional installation is required.

				
					import xmlrpc.client as xmlrpclib

This module enables Python to communicate with Odoo’s XML-RPC endpoints.

Step 2: Configure Odoo 17 Server Connection (Source Database)

Here we define the connection details for the Odoo 17 instance:

				
					# version 17
url_common="http://localhost:8017//xmlrpc/2/common"
url_object="http://localhost:8017//xmlrpc/2/object"
sock_common = xmlrpclib.ServerProxy(url_common)
dbname="new_practice"
username="admin"
pwd="admin"
uid = sock_common.authenticate(dbname, username, pwd, {})
sock = xmlrpclib.ServerProxy(url_object)

What’s Happening Here?

  • common endpoint: used for authentication
  • object endpoint: used for CRUD operations
  • authenticate() returns uid, proving successful login

Step 3: Configure Odoo 18 Server Connection (Target Database)

Same process, but for the destination Odoo 18 instance:

				
					# version 18
url_common18="http://localhost:8018/xmlrpc/2/common"
url_object18="http://localhost:8018/xmlrpc/2/object"
sock_common18 = xmlrpclib.ServerProxy(url_common18)
dbname18="trial"
username18="admin"
pwd18="admin"
uid18 = sock_common18.authenticate(dbname18, username18, pwd18, {})
sock18 = xmlrpclib.ServerProxy(url_object18)

At this point, both Odoo instances are authenticated and ready for data transfer.

Step 4: Fetch CRM Lead Data From Odoo 17

We use search_read() to fetch all CRM lead records with selected fields:

				
					crm_leads = sock.execute_kw(
dbname, uid, pwd,
'crm.lead', 'search_read',
[[]],
{'fields': ['name','contact_name','email_from','phone','mobile','type','priority','description','expected_revenue']}
)
print("Total CRM Leads:", len(crm_leads))

Why search_read() Is the Best Choice

  • Combines search + read in a single call
  • Returns clean dictionaries ready for insert
  • Prevents double looping / duplication issues

Step 5: Insert Data Into Odoo 18

Loop through the fetched records and create them in Odoo 18:

				
					for rec in crm_leads:
   # rec is already a dict, so send directly
   new_id = sock18.execute_kw(
       dbname18, uid18, pwd18,
       'crm.lead', 'create',
       [rec]
   )
   print("Created lead:", new_id)

The Odoo 18 CRM lead page is empty before transferring the data.

Before running the script, the CRM Leads page in Odoo 18 is empty.

After execution, all leads from Odoo 17 will appear in Odoo 18.

How to Run the Script

  1. Save your Python script (the XML-RPC migration code) as:
				
					crm_lead.py

Now, you can run the migration using:

				
					python3 -m crm_lead.py

After running the python script go to the Odoo 18 CRM lead page then we can see all leads from the Odoo 17 will be transferred to Odoo 18.

Important Considerations and Best Practices

  • Relational Fields: Many2one fields may require ID mapping
  • Large Data Volumes: Use batch processing for better performance
  • Error Handling: Wrap create calls in try/except blocks
  • Duplicate Records: Apply filters or uniqueness checks if required
  • Access Rights: Ensure the user has permission to create records

For production migrations, always test the script in a staging environment first.

Transfer Data From Odoo 17 to Odoo 18 Using XML-RPC

Migrating data between Odoo versions does not have to be complex. With XML-RPC, you gain a powerful, flexible, and repeatable method to transfer data across Odoo instances with precision.

This approach is particularly useful for:

  • Upgrading from older Odoo versions
  • Migrating selected models only
  • Synchronizing data across multiple servers
  • Automation and integration testing

By utilizingOdoo’s XML-RPC API and Python scripting, businesses can ensure smooth transitions while maintaining full control over their data.

Understanding Odoo 19 Overtime Calculation Attendance from the System’s Point of View

Let me explain Odoo 19 overtime calculation attendance in the simplest way possible. Odoo compares two things only:

what time the employee should work and what time the employee actually worked.

If Odoo does not know what “should work” means, it cannot decide what overtime means. This is where most issues start. People expect Odoo to automatically understand overtime, but Odoo needs clear instructions.

Overtime is not calculated just because someone stayed late. It is calculated only when extra hours cross the defined limits. This small detail explains why overtime sometimes shows zero even after long working days.

Why Working Schedules Decide How You Calculate Overtime in Odoo 19 Attendance

Before thinking about overtime, ask yourself one question: Does Odoo know my employee’s daily working hours? If the answer is no, overtime will never calculate correctly.

Working schedules specify when work starts and ends, and how many hours are considered normal. When you calculate overtime in Odoo 19 attendance, the system always checks the schedule first.

If an employee has no schedule or the schedule is wrong, Odoo has nothing to compare attendance with. As a result, overtime stays missing or inaccurate.

How to Configure Overtime Rules Odoo 19 So Extra Hours Are Counted Properly

Now we come to the most ignored step, overtime rules. Knowing how to configure overtime rulesin  Odoo 19 changes everything. Overtime rules decide:

  • After how many hours does overtime starts
  • Whether overtime is counted daily or weekly
  • Whether a minimum extra time is required

Many companies forget to define these rules and then wonder why overtime is not calculated. Odoo will not assume anything for you. Once rules are clearly defined, Odoo follows them exactly the same way every time. So, let’s dive into the Attendance module to configure overtime rules.

Go to the Configuration > Overtime Rulesets.

Click New.

Give the ruleset name, add the overtime rules, and click Save.

Overtime hours don’t go directly to payroll. First, they are converted into system records called overtime work entries in Odoo Attendance.

Connecting Attendance with Salary Using Odoo 19 Payroll Overtime Setup

Attendance can calculate overtime, but payroll must pay for it. This connection is made through Odoo 19's payroll overtime setup.

In payroll, overtime is defined as a separate salary component. It reads overtime work entries and calculates payment based on defined rates. If this step is skipped, overtime hours stay invisible on payslips.

Once the payroll overtime setup is complete, attendance and payroll start speaking the same language, and salary calculations become consistent.

What is a Contra Voucher Entry in Odoo 19?

Bank A

Inter-bank transfer

Odoo 19 Operation Types Inventory: The Rules That Control Stock Movements

Before any stock moves, Odoo needs to know how it should move. This is where Odoo 19's inventory operation types come into play.

Operation types tell Odoo what kind of movement is happening. Is it a receipt? Is it a delivery? Is it an internal transfer or scrap? Each operation type has its own source location, destination location, and workflow.

If these operation types are not set correctly, stock movements become confusing. You might receive items, but they end up at the wrong location. You might deliver items, but the stock does not reduce correctly. Understanding Odoo 19's inventory operation types helps you control how stock flows within your business, rather than reacting to errors later.

Now let’s talk about the types of inventory transfers Odoo 19 supports. These are the movements you deal with almost every day, even if you do not realise it.

The most common movements in any business are receiving goods, delivering goods, and handling damaged stock. In Odoo, these are clearly separated, so you always know what is happening.

When goods arrive from a supplier, Odoo treats this as a receipt. Stock moves from the vendor location to your warehouse. This movement increases your available stock. If something goes wrong here, your entire inventory starts showing incorrect numbers.

When you send goods to a customer, Odoo records the delivery. Stock moves from your warehouse to the customer location. This reduces your available stock. Late deliveries, partial deliveries, and backorders are all handled through this process.

Then there is scrap. Scrap is often ignored, but it can cause serious problems if not managed properly. In Odoo 19, receipts, deliveries, and scrap movements ensure that damaged or expired items are removed from available stock to prevent issues later.

Not every movement involves a supplier or a customer. Often, products move within your own warehouse. This is where the internal stock moves Odoo tutorial becomes important.

Maybe you are moving items from the receiving area to storage. Maybe you are shifting fast-moving products closer to the packing area. Maybe you are transferring stock from one warehouse to another. All of these are internal stock moves.

These movements do not change the total stock quantity, but they change where the stock is stored. If internal moves are not recorded properly, your system shows stock in one location, while it is physically somewhere else. For businesses working with multiple warehouses, types of inventory transfers in Odoo 19 become even more important. Stock may move between cities, branches, or storage facilities.

Odoo handles this by treating each warehouse as a location. When stock moves from one warehouse to another, it is still an internal transfer, but with tracking and documentation. This gives full visibility of where goods are and how long they take to move.

When you deliver products, the inventory value decreases, and the cost of goods sold is recorded. When you scrap products, value is written off.

When you manage scrap orders in Odoo 19 UAE, you create clear records of what was scrapped, why it was scrapped, and when it happened. This helps management understand loss reasons and helps finance teams keep clean records.

Scrap movements remove stock from usable inventory and move it to the scrap location. This ensures your available stock is always realistic.

Title: How to Add a New Button Next to the Create Button in Tree and Form Views in Odoo 18?
Content:
In Odoo 18, customizing the user interface is essential for enhancing usability and workflow efficiency. One common requirement is adding custom buttons next to the default “Create” button in Tree and Form views. This feature allows developers to add quick actions, such as importing data, launching wizards, or automating specific tasks, directly from the view. In this blog, we’ll explore how to add a new button beside the Create button using XML and Python in Odoo 18.

Add a New Button or Custom Button in List View

Sometimes, you may need to add a custom button to a specific tree view, such as the header of the Sales Order or Product list view.

Create the templates file inside the static/src/xml directory

The 'web.ListView.Buttons' template, which defines the list view buttons, must be inherited to add a button to the list view. The 'Create Order' button and associated 't-on-click' functionality will be included in this template.

				
					<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<templates id="template" xml:space="preserve">
<t t-name="button_on_tree_view.ListView.Buttons" t-inherit="web.ListView">
     <xpath expr="//Layout/t[@t-set-slot='control-panel-create-button']" position="inside">
        <button type="button" style="margin-right: 10px;" t-on-click="OnClickOrder">
            Create Order
        </button>
    </xpath>
</t>
</templates>

Create a JS file inside the static/src/js directory

We can add functionality to our template and the default ListController component. A new 'button_in_tree' item can then be added to the view register accordingly.

The "t-on-click" function of the button can be defined in the JavaScript file. This is where we may use the "doAction" method to launch a sale order wizard. There is no need to import the action from the hook again because it has already been added to the default ListController.

				
					/** @odoo-module */
import { ListController } from "@web/views/list/list_controller";
import { registry } from '@web/core/registry';
import { listView } from '@web/views/list/list_view';
export class ProductController extends ListController {
 setup() {
     super.setup();
 }
 OnClickOrder() {
     this.actionService.doAction({
        type: 'ir.actions.act_window',
        res_model: 'sale.order',
        name:'Sale Order',
        view_mode: 'form',
        view_type: 'form',
        views: [[false, 'form']],
        target: 'new',
        res_id: false,
    });
 }
}
ProductController.template = "button_on_tree_view.ListView.Buttons";
export const CustomProductController = {
  ...listView,
  Controller: ProductController,
};
registry.category("views").add("button_in_tree", CustomProductController);

Create the view file for the list inside the view directory

This particular JS class should now be included in the Product template's treeview.

				
					<odoo>
  <record id="product_template_tree_view" model="ir.ui.view">
      <field name="name">product.template.view.tree.inherit.button.on.tree.view</field>
      <field name="model">product.template</field>
      <field name="inherit_id" ref="product.product_template_tree_view"/>
      <field name="arch" type="xml">
          <xpath expr="//list" position="attributes">
              <attribute name="js_class">button_in_tree</attribute>
          </xpath>
      </field>
  </record>
</odoo>

The 'Create Order' button is now visible in the product list view, and clicking it launches our wizard.

Custom Button in Form View

Now, let's look at how to add a custom button to the product form view.

Add the form_button.xml file to the static/src/xml directory

In this instance, we use the XPath expression to add our button to the "web.FormView" template, which we extend by inheriting it. The word "Create Order" is contained within an element, which will be displayed as the button's label.

				
					<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<templates xml:space="preserve">
  <t t-name="button_on_tree_view.FormView.Buttons" t-inherit="web.FormView">
      <xpath expr="//t[@t-set-slot='layout-buttons']" position="inside">
          <button type="button"
             t-on-click="OnFormClickOrder">
             Create Order
         </button>
      </xpath>
  </t>
</templates>

Add the form_button.js file to the static/src/js directory

In this instance, we can add our template and the default FormController component. After that, we can add a new "button_in_form" item to the view register. Additionally, provide the "Create order" button functionality.

This involves importing an action from the "useService" hook.

				
					/** @odoo-module */
import { FormController } from "@web/views/form/form_controller";
import { useService } from "@web/core/utils/hooks";
import { registry } from '@web/core/registry';
import { formView } from '@web/views/form/form_view';
export class ProductFormController extends FormController {
 setup() {
     super.setup();
     this.actionService = useService("action");
 }
 OnFormClickOrder() {
     this.actionService.doAction({
        type: 'ir.actions.act_window',
        res_model: 'sale.order',
        name:'Sale Order',
        view_mode: 'form',
        view_type: 'form',
        views: [[false, 'form']],
        target: 'new',
        res_id: false,
    });
 }
}
ProductFormController.template = "button_on_tree_view.FormView.Buttons";
export const CustomProductFormController = {
  ...formView,
  Controller: ProductFormController,
};
registry.category("views").add("button_in_form", CustomProductFormController);

Create the view file for Form inside the view directory

The new class must now be specified in the view to make this new button appear in the product template model's form view. We can do so by using the "js_class" attribute in the view's form tag.

				
					<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<odoo>
   <record id="product_template_only_form_view" model="ir.ui.view">
       <field name="name">product.template.view.form.inherit.button.on.tree.view</field>
       <field name="model">product.template</field>
       <field name="inherit_id" ref="product.product_template_only_form_view"/>
       <field name="arch" type="xml">
           <xpath expr="//form" position="attributes">
               <attribute name="js_class">button_in_form</attribute>
           </xpath>
       </field>
   </record>
</odoo>

The "Create Order" button is now shown next to the "Create" button in the product form view.

The do_action method defines a specific wizard that opens when the newly added button is clicked in both the form and tree views. A sale order creation wizard is used in this example.

Build Smarter UI with Custom Buttons

Adding a custom button next to the “Create” button in Odoo 18 enhances user efficiency and provides quick access to frequently used actions. By inheriting the web.ListView.By extending the buttons template with custom functionality, developers can seamlessly integrate new features without disrupting the existing UI. This approach not only improves workflow automation but also creates a more intuitive, user-friendly experience in Odoo.

Title: What is the Difference Between Credit Notes and Debit Notes in Odoo 19 Accounting?

Credit Notes and Debit Notes in Odoo 19 Accounting Explained for Daily Business Use
