The credit notes and debit notes in Odoo 19 accounting help you keep a clear link between the original invoice and the correction. That is why the Odoo 19 credit note vs debit note matters so much.

If you know the difference between credit and debit notes in Odoo Accounting, you will never panic when a customer asks for a refund or when you need to add a missed charge. The right tool is already available in Odoo 19, accounting for credit and debit notes.

This Odoo Accounting credit debit notes guide is written in a simple way, so you can relate it to what happens in your office every day.

Odoo 19 Credit Note vs Debit Note – What They Really Mean

A credit note is used when you owe something back to the customer. A debit note is issued when the customer owes you more. Understanding the differences between Odoo 19 credit notes and debit notes is essential for accountants and finance managers.

Feature

Credit Note

Debit Note

Purpose

Reduces customer balance

Increases customer balance

Issued When

Refunds or returns

Extra charges or underbilling

Impact

Lowers revenue

Increases revenue

VAT Effect

VAT is reduced

VAT is increased

The difference between credit and debit notes in Odoo Accounting lies mainly in whether the invoice value increases or decreases.

Credit Note Refund Odoo 19 UAE and Why It Is Used

In many UAE businesses, product returns are common. A customer may receive damaged goods or send back items that were not needed. In this case, you must issue a credit note refund in Odoo 19 UAE instead of deleting the invoice.

In Odoo 19 accounting, credit and debit notes keep the original invoice and adjust the amount. This keeps your VAT records clean. When you issue a credit note refund in Odoo 19 UAE, Odoo also adjusts the tax, so you do not overpay VAT.

This is why understanding credit notes and debit notes in Odoo 19 accounting is so important in the UAE. VAT reporting depends on it.

When to Use Debit Note Odoo 19 in Real Situations

Many people think debit notes are rare, but in real life, they are very common. You should know when to use the Odoo 19 debit note to avoid losing money.

If you delivered extra items after the invoice was sent, you use a debit note. If transport or handling charges were missed, you use a debit note. If the price was wrong and should be higher, you use a debit note.

This is part of credit notes and debit notes in Odoo 19 accounting that many businesses ignore, and then they wonder why revenue does not match the work they did.

How to Create a Credit Note in Odoo 19

Creating a credit note is just as simple. Open the Accounting module.

Go to the Customers → Invoices.

Click New to create a new invoice.

Select the customer, add a product, and click Confirm.

Now, you can see that it will be moved to the posted stage. But we learned that one of the products is damaged. So, we want to reduce the amount of the damaged product by creating a credit note. Let’s click on the Credit Note button.

Give the Reason, then click Reverse.

Since we only want to reverse the one quantity, you can set it here and click Confirm.

Now, you can see that the amount has been paid back to the customer, and that will be marked under the credit note.

We have just made a partial payment; we can also make a full payment by following the same steps.

This is how you process a credit note refund Odoo 19 UAE in a VAT-compliant way.

Odoo 19 Debit Note Creation Tutorial for Daily Work

Let us walk through the Odoo 19 debit note creation tutorial so you can understand how easy it is.

Go to Accounting → Vendors → Bills.

Click New.

Select the Vendor, choose the bill date, add a product, and then click Confirm.

At this moment, we came to know that we have not added the extra charges for that, just click on the Debit Note.

Here, you can add the extra charges as transportation, and if you just want to add the product (Corner Desk Right Sit) in the debit note, you can check (✔) the copy lines option, and you can also specify the journal and then click Create Debit Note.

Add the $100 transportation charge and click Confirm.

As you can see below, we have successfully added the debit note.

Odoo will automatically post the journal entries and link the debit note to the original invoice.

When you follow the Odoo 19 debit note creation tutorial, all entries remain linked to the original invoice, which is very helpful during audits.

Important Note: Many people think a credit note is used to manage customer invoices and a debit note is used to manage vendor bills, but this is a misconception. A credit note is used to reduce the amount, and a debit note is used to make corrections and add the amount. So, you can use both credit and debit notes in customer invoices as well as in vendor bills.

Difference Credit Debit Notes Odoo Accounting in Reports

One thing I always explain to finance teams is how these notes affect reports. In the difference between credit and debit notes, Odoo Accounting, a credit note reduces revenue and VAT. A debit note increases revenue and VAT.

So, when you look at your Profit and Loss report or VAT report, you will see the correct numbers only if you use credit and debit notes correctly in Odoo 19 accounting.

Once you configure debit and credit notes in Odoo 19, Odoo handles all calculations for you. That is why many companies rely on credit and debit notes in Odoo 19 accounting rather than spreadsheets.

The Odoo 19 credit note vs. debit note system provides a clear way to handle all adjustments. The difference in credit and debit notes in Odoo Accounting helps you decide what to do without confusion.

  • Interbank transfer charges

  • POS transaction fees
  • Cheque processing charges
  • Foreign exchange conversion fees
  • Monthly account maintenance fees

Individually, these charges appear small. Collectively, they represent a recurring cost that impacts net profitability.

Without a proper structure for Bank Fees in Odoo 19 Accounting, businesses typically face the following issues:

  • Bank balance in Odoo does not match the actual bank balance
  • Reconciliation takes excessive manual effort
  • Profit and loss statements understate expenses
  • Audit trails become unclear
  • Finance teams spend time on low-value corrections

For any organisation that processes a high volume of bank transactions, structured handling of Odoo accounting bank service charges is essential.

Understanding Bank Fees in Odoo 19 Accounting

In Odoo, bank fees are treated as expense transactions linked to bank journals. They are typically identified during bank statement import or bank synchronisation and must be posted to a dedicated expense account.

Common examples of Bank Fees in Odoo 19 Accounting include:

  • Banks deduct NEFT/RTGS charges
  • Payment gateway fees are deducted before settlement
  • International wire transfer charges
  • Currency conversion fees
  • POS machine rental or per-transaction charges

These transactions should always be mapped to a specific bank fees expense account to ensure financial transparency.

How to Record Bank Charges in Odoo 19

There are two primary methods for recording bank charges in Odoo 19: manual entry and automated reconciliation.

Manual Recording (Basic Method)

This method is suitable for very small businesses with low transaction volumes.

Steps:

  • Go to Accounting → Vendors → Bills
  • Create a bill with the bank as the vendor.
  • Add a line for bank charges.
  • Select the bank fees expense account
  • Post the bill

While this method works, it is neither efficient nor scalable for organisations that process frequent bank transactions.

Odoo 19 Bank Fees Expense Account Setup

Before automating anything, the first requirement is to configure a dedicated expense account.

Go to:
Accounting → Configuration → Chart of Accounts → Create

Set the following:

  • Account Name: Bank Fees / Bank Charges
  • Account Type: Expenses
  • Code: As per your chart of accounts structure

This account becomes the foundation for all Bank Fees in Odoo 19 Accounting.

Without a dedicated account, bank fees get mixed with general expenses, making financial analysis and audits difficult.

Odoo 19 Bank Statement Fees Handling

Most businesses use bank statement import or live bank synchronisation in Odoo. This process brings all transactions directly into the system.

Typical bank statement lines look like:

  • "Service Fee – 10 USD"
  • "Transfer Charge – 5 USD"
  • "Gateway Commission – 3 USD"

These entries must be classified correctly.

This is where handling bank statement fees in Odoo 19 becomes important.

Instead of manually assigning each line, Odoo allows you to use reconciliation models to classify them automatically.

Configure Reconciliation Model Bank Fees Odoo 19

A reconciliation model is a rule-based mechanism that enables Odoo to automatically recognise and classify transactions.

This is the core feature behind automatic bank fees reconciliation in Odoo.

Steps to Configure:

  • Go to Accounting Dashboard
  • Open the Bank Journal
  • Click Reconcile
  • Select a bank fee transaction line
  • Click Create Rule
  • Define conditions like:
  • Label contains: fee / charge / commission
  • Set the counterpart account as Bank Fees Expense Account
  • Save the rule

Automatic Bank Fees Reconciliation Odoo in Practice

Once the reconciliation model is active, the workflow becomes highly efficient.

Process:

  1. Import or sync bank statement
  2. Odoo scans transaction labels
  3. Matching lines are identified as bank fees
  4. The system suggests the reconciliation model
  5. User validates the entry
  6. The transaction is posted automatically

The result is a consistent classification of Bank Fees in Odoo 19 Accounting without manual intervention.

This significantly reduces reconciliation time and eliminates repetitive accounting work.

Handling Payment Gateway Fees

Payment gateway fees are one of the most common use cases.

Example scenario:

  • Customer pays: 1,000
  • Payment gateway deducts: 30
  • Bank receives: 970

In accounting terms:

  • Revenue = 1,000
  • Bank balance increase = 970
  • Expense (bank fee) = 30

Using automatic bank fees reconciliation in Odoo, the System splits the transaction and posts the difference to the bank fees expense account.

This ensures:

  • Customer ledger remains accurate
  • Revenue is not understated
  • Expenses are correctly recorded
  • Bank reconciliation balances perfectly

This is one of the strongest practical benefits of Bank Fees in Odoo 19 Accounting.

Best Practices for Odoo Accounting Bank Service Charges

1. Always Use Dedicated Expense Accounts

Never post bank fees to generic expense or miscellaneous accounts.

2. Use Separate Reconciliation Models per Bank

Different banks use different transaction labels.

3. Review Bank Fees Monthly

Analyse the amount paid to banks and gateways.

4. Automate as Much as Possible

Manual reconciliation increases the risk of errors.

5. Maintain Audit Trails

Ensure every bank fee is traceable to a statement line.

How to Use Batch Payments in Odoo 19 Accounting

A batch payment in Odoo 19 is typically used to pay multiple invoices or bills at once. Imagine you have several vendor bills due on the same day, or multiple customers have paid you, and you need to reconcile these payments. Instead of handling each one separately, you can create a batch payment.

With batch payments, Odoo allows you to select all the invoices you want to pay and make a single transaction through your bank. This makes it easier to reconcile your bank statements later and reduces the risk of missed or duplicate payments.

To use a batch payment, go to the Accounting module.

Select Customers > Batch Payment.

Pick the invoices or bills you want to pay together, validate the payment, and export it to your bank.

Once the bank confirms the transaction, you can complete Odoo 19 customer payment batch payment reconciliation quickly without checking each invoice manually. Batch payments save time, reduce errors, and simplify the bank reconciliation process. This is especially useful for businesses that process many invoices each month.

How to Use Group Payments in Odoo 19 Accounting

Group payments are slightly different. When you create a group payment, you are not combining bank transactions. Instead, you are grouping several invoices or bills into a single accounting entry. This makes your books easier to read and your reporting cleaner.

Group payments are mostly used for vendor bills. If your company receives multiple invoices from the same supplier and you want to record them together, you can select all these bills and create a group payment. This produces a single journal entry rather than multiple entries for each invoice.

In Odoo 19, to use a group payment, go to Accounting > Customers >  Invoices.

Select the invoices you want to combine, and click Pay.

Enable the Group Payment option and then click Create Payment.

Validate the entry, and all the selected invoices will appear as a single entry in your accounting records.

This is what Odoo 19 customer invoices group payment is all about. It keeps your books organized and simplifies reporting, even if you pay each invoice separately via your bank later.

Practical Example of Using Batch and Group Payments

Now, if you want your accounting team to have cleaner records, you can use a group payment first to combine these six invoices into a single journal entry. Then, you can process the batch payment for the bank. This way, both your accounting records and bank reconciliation stay organized.

Subtotal + Taxes = Total $42.15

Step 2: Click on Split Option

Inside the payment screen, Odoo provides a Split Bill option by clicking on 3 vertical dots.

The cashier simply selects it.

This opens the bill-splitting interface.

Step 3: Select Items to Split

The POS allows splitting in multiple ways:

  • By product
  • By quantity
  • By customer

For example:

Customer 1 → Chicken Curry Sandwich + Pasta

Then, click on the split order button

Once items are selected:

Odoo automatically creates separate bills.

  • Card
  • Mobile wallet

Understanding Odoo Sales Order Numbering Setup Before You Change Sequence Number SO and PO in Odoo 19

Before we directly jump into technical steps, let’s understand how numbering works in Odoo. In Odoo 19:

Sales Orders (SO) automatically get a sequence like:

  • S00001, S00002

Purchase Orders (PO) may look like:

  • P00001, P00002

These numbers are generated using Odoo’s built-in sequence mechanism. Every time you create a new document, Odoo picks the next number from a predefined sequence. This is part of the Odoo sales order numbering setup and purchase order configuration inside the system.

Now the question is what if your company needs:

  • SO-2026-0001
  • PK-LHR-SO-001
  • PO-RAW-0001

Different numbering for different branches? That’s where you need to change the sales order sequence in Odoo 19 and apply proper customization.

Why Businesses Want to Modify SO PO Sequence in Odoo 19

Every business has its own documentation standards. Here are common reasons why companies choose to modify the SO PO sequence in Odoo 19:

Companies operating in multiple cities want branch codes in order numbers.

Example:

  • KHI-SO-0001
  • LHR-SO-0001

2. Financial Year Based Numbering

Some organizations reset numbering every year:

  • SO-2026-001
  • SO-2027-001

3. Department-Based Prefix

Manufacturing or trading companies may use prefixes like:

  • SO-TRD-0001
  • PO-IMP-0001

4. Compliance and Audit Requirements

In some industries, legal authorities require structured numbering formats. That’s why learning how to change sequence number SO and PO in Odoo 19 is not just a technical task; it’s a business necessity.

Step-by-Step Guide to Change Sequence Number SO and PO in Odoo 19

Now I will guide you practically on how to do Odoo 19 change SO sequence number. To access sequence settings:

Go to Settings App.

Scroll down and click on Activate Developer Mode.

Save the settings by clicking on Save. Developer Mode allows you to see technical configurations like sequences.

After enabling Developer Mode, click on Technical > Sequences & Identifiers > Sequences.

Here, you will find all sequences available in the system.

To perform Odoo 19 change SO sequence number:

Search for “Sales Order”.

Open the Sales Order sequence.

You will see fields like:

  • Prefix
  • Suffix
  • Next Number
  • Sequence Size
  • Step

If you want to change the sales order sequence in Odoo 19, you can modify:

  • Prefix → Example: SL-%(year)s-%(month)s-
  • Next Number → Reset or adjust
  • Sequence Size → Number of digits (e.g., 4 digits: 0001)

This is the core part of the Odoo sales order numbering setup.

Click Save after updating.

Now, create a new Sales Order and check the updated numbering. Go to Sales app > New > Select Customer > Add Product > Confirm.

Here, you can see that you have now successfully customize sales order number in the Odoo process.

Now, let’s do Odoo 19 PO sequence customization.

Go back to Sequences. Search for “Purchase Order”.

Open it.

To customize purchase order number Odoo, update:

  • Prefix → Example: PO-%(y)s-%(day)s-
  • Next Number → Set desired starting point
  • Sequence Size → Set digit length

Save changes.

Create a new Purchase Order to test. Go to Purchase app > New > Select Vendor > Add Product > Confirm Order.

You have now successfully done customize purchase order number Odoo process.

Now I want you to think about your own company. Do you need branch-based numbers like:

  • LHR-SO-0001
  • KHI-SO-0001

  • NT-SO-2026-001

To change the sales order sequence in Odoo 19, you just need to modify the prefix carefully. Inside the prefix field, you can write text like:

  • LHR-SO-
  • KHI-SO-
  • NT-SO-%(year)s-

Odoo 19 also supports dynamic values like year and month. This is part of the Odoo 19 sequence prefix sales purchase functionality. But before changing anything in a live system, please check:

  • Are there already confirmed orders?
  • Will resetting numbers create confusion?

Planning is important before you modify the SO PO sequence in Odoo 19.

Many companies want numbering like:

This is possible using Odoo 19 sequence prefix sales purchase options. In prefix field, you can use:

  • %(year)s

Now your Sales Order will look like:

This is very helpful for reporting and tracking. But I always suggest one thing: keep numbering simple. If you add too many elements, it becomes difficult for staff to read quickly. So, when you configure Odoo 19 sequence prefix sales purchase, think from a practical daily use perspective.

Sometimes small configuration looks simple, but it affects reporting and audits later. So, always think before you modify SO PO sequence in Odoo 19.

Title: How to Add a Text-Based Watermark in Odoo 18 PDF Reports?
Content:
Text-Based Watermark in Odoo 18 PDF Reports

If you are new to Odoo or ERP systems, you might be wondering what this blog is actually about.

Whenever a business creates documents like quotations, sales orders, invoices, or purchase orders in Odoo, those documents are usually downloaded or shared as PDF files. Sometimes, these PDFs need a visible label such as “DRAFT”, “CONFIRMED”, or “CONFIDENTIAL” to clearly show the document’s current status.

That visible label placed behind the content of a PDF is called a watermark.

In simple terms, this blog will teach you how to automatically display a large, light text (like “DRAFT”) in the background of a PDF report in Odoo 18, without changing any core system files or writing complex backend code.

We will use a practical example of a Sales Order to show how the watermark text can change automatically based on the document’s status. Even if you are implementing Odoo customization for the first time, this guide will walk you through the process step by step in an easy and understandable way.

By the end of this article about Text-Based Watermark in Odoo 18 PDF Reports, you will clearly understand:

  • What a text-based watermark is
  • Why businesses use it
  • How Odoo generates PDF reports
  • And how you can safely add dynamic watermarks using QWeb and CSS

Let’s get started.

What Is a Text-Based Watermark?

A Text-Based Watermark in Odoo 18 PDF Reports is semi-transparent text displayed behind the main content of a PDF report. It acts as a visual status indicator while keeping the document readable.

In Odoo 18, PDF reports are generated using QWeb templates and rendered through the wkhtmltopdf engine. Because reports are HTML-based before conversion to PDF, we can use CSS styling to insert and design watermarks easily.

Unlike image watermarks, Text-Based Watermark in Odoo 18 PDF Reports are:

  • Lightweight
  • Dynamic
  • Easy to maintain
  • Fully customizable
  • Upgrade-safe

That’s why they are generally the recommended approach for Odoo report customization.

Why Businesses Use Watermarks in Odoo Reports

Text-Based Watermark in Odoo 18 PDF Reports aren’t just about aesthetics, they serve practical business purposes.

Common use cases include:

  • Marking quotations as DRAFT
  • Showing CONFIRMED on finalized sale orders
  • Labeling internal documents as CONFIDENTIAL
  • Indicating CANCELLED records
  • Showing PAID or OVERDUE on invoices

These indicators reduce miscommunication and add a layer of operational clarity.

Text-Based Watermark vs Image Watermark

When customizing Odoo PDF reports, you have two main options:

Text-Based Watermark (Recommended)

  • Uses HTML and CSS
  • Fully dynamic (changes based on record state)
  • No need for image files
  • Easier to modify later

Image-Based Watermark

  • Uses a background image
  • Less flexible
  • Harder to manage across different states

In this guide, we focus exclusively on Text-Based Watermark in Odoo 18 PDF Reports because it is cleaner and more scalable.

Example Use Case: Sale Order PDF (Odoo 18)

Let’s implement a dynamic watermark for Sale Orders.

We want:

  • DRAFT when the quotation is in draft or sent state
  • CONFIRMED when the order is in sale or done state

This ensures the PDF reflects the exact document status automatically.

Step 1: Inherit Sale Order Report Template

The first rule of proper Odoo customization is simple:

Never modify core files.

Instead, inherit the original Sale Order report template.

				
					<template id="sale_order_watermark" inherit_id="sale.report_saleorder_document">

By inheriting the template, we extend it safely without breaking future upgrades.

This approach ensures your Text-Based Watermark in Odoo 18 PDF Reports customization remains stable even when Odoo updates.

Step 2: Add Text-Based Watermark (QWeb)

Watermark Logic (Text Only)

Now we inject the Text-Based Watermark in Odoo 18 PDF Reports inside the page container.

				
					<xpath expr="//div[@class='page']" position="inside">
       <t t-if="doc.state in ['draft', 'sent']">DRAFT</t>
       <t t-if="doc.state in ['sale', 'done']">CONFIRMED</t>
</xpath>

What’s Happening Here?

  • We locate the main page container using XPath.
  • We insert a new div called o_watermark.
  • We use QWeb conditional statements.
  • The watermark text changes dynamically based on doc.state.

No Python code is required. Everything is handled within the QWeb template.

That’s the beauty of Odoo’s reporting system.

Step 3: Add CSS Styling for Text Watermark

Text-Based Watermark Style

Now we style the watermark so it looks professional and subtle.

				
					<style>
   .o_watermark {
       position: fixed;
       top: 45%;
       left: 10%;
       width: 80%;
       text-align: center;
       font-size: 90px;
       font-weight: bold;
       color: rgba(150, 150, 150, 0.25);
       transform: rotate(-30deg);
       z-index: 0;
       pointer-events: none;
   }
</style>

Why This Styling Works Perfectly

  • position: fixed ensures the watermark appears on every page.
  • rgba(..., 0.25) makes it semi-transparent.
  • rotate(-30deg) creates a classic watermark angle.
  • pointer-events: none prevents interference with report layout.

The result is clean, readable, and professional.

What the Final Output Looks Like

After implementation:

  • Draft quotations show a large, subtle “DRAFT” watermark.
  • Confirmed orders automatically show “CONFIRMED”.
  • The watermark stays behind the content.
  • The document remains fully readable.
  • Layout integrity is preserved.

The watermark enhances clarity without affecting usability.

Extending This to Other Odoo Reports

Once you understand the logic, you can apply it anywhere.

This approach works for:

  • Customer Invoices
  • Vendor Bills
  • Purchase Orders
  • Delivery Orders
  • Custom reports
  • Internal HR documents

You simply inherit the respective report template and adjust the state conditions.

Best Practices for Odoo PDF Customization

To ensure clean implementation:

  1. Always use template inheritance.
  2. Avoid editing original Odoo files.
  3. Keep watermark opacity subtle.
  4. Test across multiple document states.
  5. Validate layout on multi-page reports.

Following these practices ensures upgrade safety and professional output.

Why This Matters for Odoo Developers

If you are offering Odoo development or ERP customization services, learning how to implement a text-based watermark in Odoo 18 is a small but powerful skill.

Clients often request:

  • Document status indicators
  • Custom PDF layouts
  • Report branding adjustments
  • Compliance labeling

Being able to implement dynamic watermarks quickly increases your development efficiency and client satisfaction.

Final Thoughts About Text-Based Watermark in Odoo 18 PDF Reports

Adding a Text-Based Watermark in Odoo 18 PDF Reports is a simple yet powerful customization that enhances document clarity and professionalism.

By utilizing QWeb inheritance and CSS styling, you can dynamically display document status without writing complex backend logic.

This method is:

  • Clean
  • Upgrade-safe
  • Flexible
  • Scalable
  • Developer-friendly

Small improvements like this elevate your Odoo system from functional to professional.

And in business, clarity is everything.

That is why businesses need to manage user permissions in Odoo 19 in a structured way from day one.

A smart setup of Odoo 19 user roles and groups helps you control who can view, create, edit, or delete data. It also helps answer a very common question: how to set access rights in Odoo without making the system too open or too hard to use. On top of that, understanding Odoo record rules and access rights gives you even deeper control over what users can do with specific records. This becomes even more useful when you want to manage permissions by groups in Odoo 19 instead of assigning rights one by one. A strong Odoo security group configuration saves time, reduces mistakes, and keeps your ERP secure as your team grows.

If you want your Odoo system to run smoothly, securely, and professionally, learning how to Manage Group Access Rights in Odoo is not optional anymore. It is a core part of building a reliable business system.

What Does It Mean to Manage Group Access Rights in Odoo?

Before configuring permissions, it is important to understand the security architecture used in Odoo.

The security system in Odoo mainly consists of three major components:

1. User Roles

Users represent individuals who access the system.

2. Groups

Groups define roles and determine access permissions.

3. Access Rights and Record Rules

These control what users can do and which records they can access.

When businesses manage user permissions in Odoo 19, they mainly work with groups. Instead of assigning permissions individually to each user, administrators assign users to groups. This makes system administration much easier.

This approach allows businesses to manage permissions by groups rather than individually managing every user.

What Are Odoo Group Access Rights?

Odoo group access rights determine what actions users can perform within the system.

These rights generally include:

  • Read Access – Users can view records
  • Write Access – Users can modify records
  • Create Access – Users can create new records
  • Delete Access – Users can remove records

How to Set Access Rights in Odoo Step by Step

If you are wondering how to set access rights in Odoo, Odoo provides a clear interface for it. According to the official Odoo 19 user documentation, administrators can go to the user form, open the Access Rights tab, and set permission levels for each installed application. The options vary by app, but common levels include none, own documents, all documents, and administrator. Only an administrator can change access rights, and Odoo warns that poor changes can seriously affect the database.

Step 1: Review the user type

Odoo 19 works with different user types such as Internal User, Portal, and Public. Portal users are more restricted and usually do not follow the normal internal group structure. This is important because many companies accidentally confuse portal access with internal access.

First, enable developer mode.

Settings → Activate Developer Mode

Developer mode allows you to configure advanced security settings.

Step 2: Open the Access Rights tab

Go to:

Settings → Manage Users → Select User → Access Rights

From there, choose the right permission level for each app. This is the fastest way to control standard app access like Sales, Inventory, Accounting, or Project.

Step 3: Use groups instead of random manual control

The best long-term method is not to configure every user from scratch. Instead, create logical groups and assign people to those groups. This is the heart of Odoo 19 manage permissions by groups. It gives your business consistency and makes onboarding much faster.

Go to:

Settings → Users & Companies → Groups

Here you will see all available Odoo 19 user roles and groups.

Step 4: Add record rules where needed

If users need limited visibility, such as seeing only their own leads, branch data, or company records, you should use record rules. Odoo’s security model clearly separates model-level access rights from record-level restrictions.

You can either:

  • Modify an existing group
  • Create a new group

For example:

Sales Manager

HR Officer

Inventory Supervisor

Each group can be customized according to business needs.

Step 5: Assign Access Rights

Once inside the group settings, define module permissions such as:

  • CRM
  • Accounting
  • Inventory
  • Sales
  • HR

For example:

Sales User Group

Module

Access

CRM

Read, Write

Sales

Full Access

Accounting

No Access

This ensures employees only access the modules they require.

Step 6: Assign Users to Groups

After creating groups, assign users.

Go to:

Settings → Users

Select the user and assign the appropriate group.

This automatically applies the permissions defined in the group.

Step 7: Test before going live

This step is often skipped. But it matters a lot. Log in as a test user and verify what they can really see and do. Odoo even notes that menus connected to models without access may disappear for users, which is a helpful way to validate your setup.

Odoo 19 User Roles and Groups: A Practical Business Setup

A clean permission structure should match the way your business actually works. That is where Odoo 19 user roles and groups become valuable. Instead of assigning rights by person, build a role-based structure.

Common internal groups businesses use

Sales Team

Sales users usually need access to leads, quotations, customers, and sales orders. Some can create and edit. Managers may need approval and reporting access.

Accounts Team

This group may need invoice access, payment registration, journal visibility, and reporting features. They usually should not touch warehouse or HR records.

Inventory Team

Warehouse users need stock moves, receipts, deliveries, and inventory adjustments, but they may not need pricing or payroll access.

HR Team

HR staff need employee data and attendance tools, while only selected users should access payroll or sensitive employee files.

Management

Managers often require cross-app visibility, approvals, and reports. But even they should not always receive full administrator control.

This is exactly why Odoo security groups configuration should be designed around duties, not just job titles. A “manager” in sales is different from a “manager” in finance. When groups are mapped to real responsibilities, the system becomes easier to use and far safer.

Odoo’s developer documentation also explains that an empty access control group can apply rights to everyone, including portal or public users, depending on context. That is why group design must be done carefully. A small mistake can open access much wider than intended.

Odoo Record Rules and Access Rights: The Difference You Must Understand

Many Odoo users know about roles and app permissions, but fewer understand Odoo record rules and access rights. This is where advanced security becomes truly powerful.

Access rights are broad. They decide whether someone can read, create, write, or delete records in a model. Record rules are more precise. They decide which specific records a user can work with. Odoo describes record rules as conditions checked record by record after access rights are evaluated. Odoo also notes that if access rights allow the action and no record rule applies, access is granted by default.

Real example 1: Salesperson visibility

You may want all salespeople to access the CRM module, but only see their own leads. In that case:

  • Access rights allow CRM usage
  • The record rules filter leads to only the assigned salesperson

Real example 2: Multi-company protection

In multi-company setups, users should not see data from companies they are not allowed to work in. Odoo’s multi-company guidance explains that security rules often use company_ids to keep access limited to the companies selected for the current user. The user form also includes Allowed Companies and Default Company fields.

Real example 3: Protecting sensitive models

You may want a group to read a document type, but never delete it. Odoo’s access rights model supports separate read, create, write, and delete permissions, so you can allow operational work without giving destructive power.

This is why companies that want serious control over data must go beyond basic roles. To truly Manage Group Access Rights in Odoo, you need both layers working together.

Best Practices to Manage User Permissions in Odoo 19 Without Risk

To manage user permissions in Odoo 19 the right way, you need a strategy, not just settings. Below are the best practices that experienced Odoo consultants follow.

1. Start with the least access needed

Do not give broad permissions first and reduce them later. Start small. Give only what a person needs to do their job. This lowers risk and makes audits easier.

2. Build roles around real tasks

Your groups should reflect real business functions such as Sales User, Sales Manager, Inventory Operator, Accounts Executive, or HR Admin. Avoid vague groups that mix unrelated permissions.

3. Do not overuse administrator access

Odoo clearly states that only administrators can change access rights and warns that bad changes can cause serious issues, including situations where no one can properly manage rights. Admin access should stay limited to trusted people only.

4. Use groups for scale

If your company is growing, one-by-one permission control becomes a nightmare. Odoo 19 manages permissions by groups, which is the smarter path because it keeps access structured and repeatable.

5. Add record rules for precision

Groups alone are not enough for branch-based access, salesperson ownership, or multi-company separation. Add record rules where the business needs narrower control.

6. Review menus and hidden access

Odoo notes that menus may not display if the user lacks access to the underlying model and has no visible submenu. This is useful for both security and a cleaner user experience.

7. Audit user access regularly

As teams grow, roles change. A person who moved from sales to operations may still have old access. Regular audits prevent security gaps and reduce confusion.

8. Be careful with the portal and public exposure

Odoo distinguishes internal, portal, and public users. If you misconfigure global rights, external access can become riskier than expected.

These best practices are not just technical tips. They directly affect productivity, compliance, privacy, and trust.

Common Mistakes Businesses Make With Odoo Group Access Rights

Even smart teams make mistakes with Odoo group access rights. Here are the most common ones:

Because access rights are additive, one extra group can silently expand what a user can do.

Relying only on app-level permissions

App access alone does not control data visibility deeply enough. Record rules are often needed.

Creating too many custom groups too early

Over-customization makes the system hard to maintain. Start with a clean structure first.

Ignoring multi-company rules

If your business has more than one company, failing to control company access can expose the wrong records.

Forgetting testing

Title: How to Manage Partial Goods Receiving & Backorders in Odoo 19?
Content:
Understanding Partial Goods Receiving and Backorders in Odoo 19

Running a business means managing a lot of moving parts – inventory, orders, suppliers, and customers. One of the most common challenges businesses face is dealing with Manage Partial Goods Receiving and backorders.

In simple terms, partial goods receiving happens when a business orders items from a supplier but receives only part of the order. Backorders occur when some items from a purchase order are not available at the time of delivery, and the remaining items are put on hold until they are back in stock.

Odoo 19, a comprehensive business management software, makes managing these challenges easy and efficient. It helps businesses streamline the process of partial goods receiving and backorder management. In this guide, we’ll explain how to manage partial goods receiving in Odoo 19, ensuring that your inventory is always accurate and that your customers stay happy. We’ll break down the steps in a way that’s easy for anyone, even beginners, to understand.

What is Partial Goods Receiving in Odoo 19?

Partial goods receiving occurs when a supplier delivers only a portion of the ordered items instead of the full quantity. This situation is very common in supply chain operations due to reasons such as:

  • Supplier stock shortages
  • Transportation delays
  • Large order quantities delivered in batches
  • Production scheduling by suppliers

Instead of waiting for the complete shipment, businesses can record the received items immediately using Odoo 19's partial goods receiving.

This allows companies to start using available products while tracking the remaining items separately.

Why Businesses Need Partial Goods Receiving

Businesses benefit significantly when they Manage Partial Goods Receiving efficiently.

Some major advantages include:

1. Faster Warehouse Operations

Warehouse teams can process received items immediately instead of waiting for the full order.

2. Accurate Inventory Tracking

Using partial goods receipt in Odoo 19, stock levels remain accurate and updated in real time.

3. Better Supplier Tracking

Businesses can easily identify pending shipments and follow up with suppliers.

4. Improved Production Planning

Manufacturers can start production using available materials without delays.

5. Clear Backorder Management

With Odoo 19 inventory backorder management, pending quantities are tracked automatically.

How Odoo 19 Handles Partial Goods Receipt and Backorders

One of the strongest advantages of Odoo is its intelligent inventory workflow. The system automatically manages pending quantities when partial deliveries occur.

Using Odoo 19 GRN partial receipt and backorder, the system performs several tasks automatically:

  • Records received products in inventory
  • Updates stock levels instantly
  • Creates a backorder for the remaining items
  • Links the backorder with the original purchase order

This automation helps businesses maintain transparency in their purchasing process.

For example:

Purchase Order: 100 units ordered

Received: 60 units

Odoo will automatically:

  • Accept the 60 units into inventory
  • Create a backorder for the remaining 40 units

This is part of the Odoo 19 purchase order partial delivery workflow, making inventory tracking much easier.

Step-by-Step Guide: How to Manage Partial Goods Receiving in Odoo 19

1. Creating a Purchase Order in Odoo 19

The first step in managing partial goods receiving is creating a purchase order in Odoo 19.

  • Go to the Purchase module in Odoo.
  • Click on Create to start a new purchase order.
  • Select the Supplier, and then add the products and quantities you want to purchase.
  • Confirm the purchase order by clicking on Confirm Order.

Once you confirm the order, Odoo will automatically create a purchase receipt for the items you ordered.

2. Receiving Partial Goods in Odoo 19

When part of the order arrives, follow these steps to receive the goods:

  • Go to the Purchase Order that you created.
  • Under the Receipts tab, you will see an option to receive the goods.
  • Click on Receive, and Odoo will prompt you to enter the quantity you’ve received.
  • If only 10 out of 20 items have arrived, enter 10 in the quantity field.

Once the partial goods are received, Odoo updates the inventory and the purchase order to show that part of the order has been fulfilled. The remaining items will automatically be placed on backorder.

3. Automatically Generating Backorders in Odoo 19

When you receive partial goods in Odoo 19, the system will automatically create backorders for the items that were not delivered.

Here’s how the backorder process works:

  • After you receive the partial goods, Odoo will check the quantity ordered versus the quantity received.
  • The system will automatically generate a backorder for the unfulfilled items. This backorder is linked to the original purchase order and tracks the remaining quantity.
  • You can view and manage the backorder just like a regular purchase order. Once the supplier delivers the remaining goods, the backorder is updated.

4. Managing Backorders in Odoo 19

Managing backorders is essential to ensure that your inventory remains accurate and your business operations continue smoothly.

To manage backorders in Odoo 19:

  • Go to the Purchase Order or Backorder linked to the original purchase order.
  • Odoo will automatically show the status of the backorder, so you can track when the goods are expected to arrive.
  • Once the remaining items are delivered, go back to the purchase order and receive the goods, just like you did with the partial delivery.
  • The backorder will then be marked as complete.

Best Practices for Managing Partial Goods Receiving & Backorders in Odoo 19

Here are some best practices to ensure smooth management of partial goods receiving and backorders in Odoo 19:

1. Keep Your Purchase Orders Updated

When receiving partial goods, always make sure to update the purchase order with the quantities you’ve actually received. This ensures that your inventory and backorders are correctly updated in the system.

2. Set Up Notifications for Backorders

Odoo 19 allows you to set up notifications for backorders. You can receive an email alert whenever a backorder is created, when an item is shipped, or when the backorder is fulfilled. This ensures you’re always aware of the status of your orders.

3. Use Odoo’s Reporting Tools

Odoo offers powerful reporting tools to track the status of your backorders and partial goods receiving. You can generate reports to analyze supplier performance, monitor order fulfillment, and manage inventory levels effectively.

Benefits of Managing Partial Goods Receiving & Backorders in Odoo 19

Odoo 19 offers several benefits when it comes to handling partial goods receiving and backorders:

  • Accurate Inventory Management: By updating your inventory as soon as goods are received, even partially, Odoo ensures that your stock levels are always up-to-date.
  • Enhanced Order Fulfillment: With backorder management in Odoo 19, you can easily track outstanding items and fulfill customer orders as soon as the goods arrive.
  • Better Supplier Communication: Managing backorders gives you a clear overview of what items are still pending, allowing you to follow up with suppliers effectively.
  • Updated Business Operations: Odoo automates the partial goods receiving and backorder process, saving you time and reducing errors compared to manual tracking.

Lead Partial Goods Receiving & Backorders with Odoo 19

Managing partial goods receiving and backorders can be a complex task, but with Odoo 19, it becomes a smooth and efficient process. Odoo’s purchase order management system allows you to receive partial deliveries, automatically generate backorders, and keep track of your inventory all in one place.

By following the simple steps outlined in this guide, you can manage partial goods receiving and backorders with ease, ensuring smooth operations and satisfied customers. Whether you’re dealing with small orders or large shipments, Odoo 19 has the tools you need to stay organized and efficient.

With its automated workflows and comprehensive reporting tools, Odoo 19's inventory backorder management is a game-changer for businesses looking to streamline their supply chain. Start using Odoo 19 today and take control of your inventory, improve your backorder management, and boost your customer satisfaction.

Title: How to Change Messaging Icon in Odoo 18 (Mail Systray Customization)
Content:
Easily Change Messaging Icon in Odoo 18

When working in Odoo 18, users often rely on the messaging feature to receive notifications, internal messages, and system updates. This feature is represented by a small icon located in the top-right corner of the Odoo interface, commonly known as the systray. By clicking this icon, users can quickly view conversations, alerts, and important notifications without navigating to another page.

By default, Odoo displays this messaging feature using a chat bubble icon (💬). While this works well for general communication, some businesses prefer to customize the icon to reflect their internal communication style better or match their company’s interface design. For example, organizations that use messaging primarily for notifications or email-like communication may find a mail or envelope icon more intuitive for their users.

Fortunately, Odoo allows developers to customize many parts of the interface without modifying the core system. Using QWeb template inheritance, you can replace the default chat icon with a different one while keeping the rest of the functionality unchanged.

In this blog, we will walk through a simple method to change the messaging icon in Odoo 18 from the default to a mail envelope icon. Even if you are new to Odoo customization, this guide will help you understand the concept and implement the change step by step.

Objective of This Customization

The main goal of this customization is straightforward:

  • Replace the default chat icon (fa-comments)
  • Display a mail or envelope icon (fa-envelope)
  • Maintain compatibility with the existing Odoo interface
  • Implement the change safely without modifying core Odoo files

To achieve this, we will extend the existing messaging template using QWeb inheritance, the recommended method for customising Odoo’s frontend components.

Technical Overview

Odoo 18 uses a combination of OWL (Odoo Web Library) and QWeb templates to render user interface components. These templates define how different parts of the UI are displayed, including menus, icons, buttons, and widgets.

The messaging icon that appears in the systray is rendered through the template:

mail.MessagingMenu

Instead of editing this core template directly, we will create a custom XML file that inherits from it to Change Messaging Icon in Odoo 18. This allows us to modify only the specific element we want, the messaging icon, while keeping the rest of the system unchanged.

This approach offers several benefits:

  • Keeps the customization upgrade-safe

  • Avoids modifying core Odoo files

  • Allows developers to extend functionality easily

By using an XPath expression, we can locate the existing chat icon and replace its class attribute with a mail icon.

Code Implementation

To implement this customization, create an XML file inside your custom module.

The recommended file location is:

static/src/xml/messaging_menu.xml

Then add the following code:

				
					<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<templates xml:space="preserve">
   <t t-name="sale_report_watermark.MessagingMenuInherit" t-inherit="mail.MessagingMenu" t-inherit-mode="extension">
       <xpath expr="//i[contains(@class, 'fa-comments')]" position="attributes">
           <attribute name="class">fa fa-lg fa-envelope</attribute>
       </xpath>
   </t>
</templates>

This code extends the existing messaging menu template and modifies the icon displayed in the systray.

How This Code Works

Let’s break down the code step by step to understand how the customization works.

1. Template Inheritance

t-inherit="mail.MessagingMenu"
 

This line tells Odoo that our template should extend the original messaging menu template instead of replacing it entirely.

Using template inheritance ensures that the customization integrates smoothly with the existing UI.

2. XPath selector

				
					 //i[contains(@class, 'fa-comments')]

The XPath expression is used to locate the icon element that contains the default chat icon.

In the original template, the messaging menu uses the Font Awesome class fa-comments to display the chat bubble icon.

By targeting this element, we can modify its properties.

3. Modifying the Attribute 

				
					position="attributes"
 	→ Replaces only the class attribute

This instruction tells Odoo to update the attributes of the selected element rather than replacing the entire element.

This is a safer approach because it preserves the rest of the messaging component’s functionality.

4. Applying the New Icon 

				
					   fa fa-lg fa-envelope

Here we replace the existing icon class with a Font Awesome envelope icon.

This simple change updates the visual representation of the messaging menu in the systray.

User Interface Result

After implementing the customization and updating the module, the icon displayed in the Odoo systray will change.

Before the Customization

➡ Chat bubble (💬) icon shown in systray

🔹 After Change
➡ Envelope (✉️) icon shown in systray

 This subtle change improves visual clarity, especially for users who associate notifications with email rather than chat.

Practical Use Cases

Although the customization to change the messaging iconin Odoo 18 is small, it can be particularly useful in several real-world scenarios.

1. UI Branding Customization

Many companies customize their Odoo interface to align with their internal design guidelines or branding standards. Changing icons is one of the easiest ways to personalize the interface.

2. Improved User Experience

Some users find the envelope icon more intuitive when the messaging system is used primarily for notifications, alerts, or email-like communication.

3. Client-Specific Customization

When implementing Odoo for clients, developers often tailor the interface according to client preferences or workflow requirements.

4. Cleaner Backend Interface

Replacing icons with more meaningful visuals can make the interface cleaner and easier to understand, especially for new users.

Best Practices for Odoo UI Customization

When making UI changes in Odoo, it is important to follow certain best practices to ensure system stability and maintainability.

  • Always use template inheritance instead of modifying core files to change the messaging iconin Odoo 18

  • Keep customizations modular and organized

  • Use XPath expressions carefully to avoid breaking templates

  • Test changes across different modules to ensure compatibility

  • Document customizations for future maintenance

Following these practices helps ensure that your customizations remain upgrade-safe and easy to manage.

Change Messaging Icon in Odoo 18

Change Messaging Icon in Odoo 18 is a simple yet effective way to improve the user interface and align the system with your organization’s design preferences.

By using QWeb template inheritance, developers can safely modify the default chat icon and replace it with a more suitable icon, such as a mail envelope. This approach avoids changes to core Odoo files while ensuring compatibility with future updates.

Although the modification only Change Messaging Icon in Odoo 18, small UI enhancements like this can significantly improve usability and make the system feel more tailored to business needs.

Odoo’s flexible architecture makes it easy to implement such improvements, allowing organizations to create a more intuitive and visually consistent ERP environment for their teams.

Title: Where is Stock Input and Stock Output Accounts Go in Odoo 19?
Content:
Understanding Stock Input and Stock Output Accounts in Odoo 19

If you have worked with inventory accounting in previous versions of Odoo, you probably remember the stock input and stock output accounts. These accounts played a very important role in tracking the movement of products between purchasing, inventory, and accounting.

But when businesses started exploring Odoo 19, many users noticed something surprising. They could not easily find the stock input and stock output accounts the way they used to. This led to a common question among accountants and ERP users: where is the stock input account in Odoo 19, and where is the stock output account in Odoo 19?

In earlier versions of Odoo, these accounts were commonly known as interim accounts. They temporarily recorded the value of goods received or delivered before the accounting process was fully completed. However, many users noticed that Odoo 19 interim stock accounts removed the traditional structure and introduced a different approach.

Because of this change, businesses now want to understand the Odoo 19 replacement for stock input and output and how inventory transactions are recorded in the new system. Another important concern is how the inventory valuation account in Odoo 19 works and how it connects with accounting entries.

In this guide, we will clearly explain how stock input and stock output accounts work in Odoo 19, what replaced them, how the stock variation account in Odoo 19 functions, and how the Odoo 19 stock valuation accounts mapping works in the new inventory accounting system.

By the end of this article, you will have a complete understanding of inventory accounting changes in Odoo 19.

Understanding Inventory Accounting in Odoo

Before we talk about the changes in Odoo 19, it is important to understand how inventory accounting works in general. Inventory accounting connects three main business operations:

  • Purchasing products
  • Storing products in inventory
  • Selling products

When goods move in or out of the warehouse, their financial value must also move in accounting. For example:

  • When you receive goods from a vendor, the inventory value increases.
  • When you deliver goods to a customer, the inventory value decreases.

To track these financial movements, accounting entries are automatically created in Odoo. These entries are linked with different accounts, including:

  • Inventory valuation accounts
  • Cost of goods sold
  • Stock input accounts
  • Stock output accounts

In earlier versions, the stock input and stock output accounts acted as temporary accounts between purchasing, inventory, and sales processes.

What Were Stock Input and Stock Output Accounts in Previous Odoo Versions?

Before Odoo 19, inventory accounting used two important interim accounts:

Stock Input Account

The stock input account was used when goods were received from a vendor, but the vendor bill had not yet been recorded. Process example:

  • The purchase order is confirmed
  • Goods are received in the warehouse
  • Inventory value increases
  • Accounting entry posts to the stock input account

Later, when the vendor bill was validated, the value moved from the stock input account to accounts payable. This helped businesses maintain accurate accounting even if invoices were received later.

Stock Output Account

The stock output account worked in the opposite direction. It was used when goods were delivered to a customer, but the customer's invoice had not yet been created. Process example:

  • Sales order confirmed
  • Products delivered to the customer
  • Inventory value decreases
  • Accounting entry posted to stock output account

Later, when the invoice was validated, the value moved to cost of goods sold. These accounts were essential for businesses using real-time inventory valuation.

Why Odoo 19 Changed Inventory Accounting

Many businesses noticed that Odoo 19 interim stock accounts removed the traditional configuration that earlier versions used. The reason for this change was mainly to simplify inventory accounting. Many users found the earlier structure confusing because:

  • Too many interim accounts were involved
  • Accounting flows were difficult to understand
  • Configuration mistakes were common

Odoo redesigned the system so that inventory accounting becomes easier to manage and understand. Instead of depending heavily on stock input and stock output accounts, Odoo 19 focuses more on inventory valuation accounts mapping and simplified financial flows.

Where is Stock Input Account in Odoo 19?

In Odoo 19, the traditional stock input account is no longer configured the same way as before. The system now manages inventory accounting using direct valuation mapping and product category accounts.

Instead of assigning separate interim accounts manually, Odoo now relies on the inventory valuation account in Odoo 19 combined with automated journal entries. When goods are received:

  • Inventory valuation account increases
  • Vendor liability or bill entries are recorded later
  • The system handles adjustments automatically

This means the traditional stock input account behaviour is now integrated within the inventory valuation structure. This is one of the major parts of the Odoo 19 replacement for stock input output accounts.

Where is Stock Output Account in Odoo 19?

Just like the input account, the stock output account is also not configured as a separate interim account in many Odoo 19 setups. Instead, inventory reduction and accounting entries now rely on:

  • Inventory valuation account
  • Cost of goods sold account
  • Automated accounting rules

When products are delivered:

  • Inventory value decreases
  • Accounting entry posts to cost of goods sold
  • The inventory valuation account is credited

Because of this simplified flow, the stock output account may not appear the same way as it did in earlier versions. This is another key change introduced in the Odoo 19 stock valuation accounts mapping system.

Understanding Inventory Valuation Account in Odoo 19

The inventory valuation account in Odoo 19 is now the central account for managing inventory value. This account represents the financial value of all products stored in your warehouse. Whenever inventory moves, Odoo automatically updates this account. Examples:

Receiving Products

  • Debit: Inventory valuation account
  • Credit: Purchase related account

Delivering Products

  • Debit: Cost of goods sold
  • Credit: Inventory valuation account

Because of this structure, the inventory valuation account in Odoo 19 replaces several accounting steps that previously involved stock input and output accounts.

Odoo 19 Stock Valuation Accounts Mapping

Another important concept introduced in the new system is Odoo 19 stock valuation accounts mapping. This mapping defines how inventory transactions connect with accounting accounts. The configuration usually happens in Product Categories.

Inside product categories, businesses can define:

  • Inventory valuation account
  • Expense account
  • Income account
  • Cost accounts

Once these accounts are mapped correctly, Odoo automatically posts accounting entries whenever stock moves. This automation reduces the need for manually configuring stock input and stock output accounts.

Stock Variation Account in Odoo 19

Another account that often appears in inventory accounting is the stock variation account in Odoo 19. This account records changes in inventory value caused by:

  • Inventory adjustments
  • Stock corrections
  • Cost updates
  • Valuation differences

For example, if the physical quantity in the warehouse does not match the system quantity, an inventory adjustment is performed.

When this happens:

  • Inventory value changes
  • Accounting entry is created
  • Difference recorded in stock variation account Odoo 19

This helps businesses track financial differences between recorded and actual inventory.

Odoo 19 Replacement for Stock Input Output

Many businesses ask about the Odoo 19 replacement for stock input and output accounts. The replacement is not a single account. Instead, Odoo introduced a simplified inventory accounting structure that includes:

  • Inventory valuation account
  • Cost of goods sold
  • Expense accounts
  • Automated accounting entries

The system automatically manages the movement of values without requiring dedicated stock input and stock output accounts. This makes the accounting process easier, especially for companies that want a simpler setup.

How Inventory Transactions Work in Odoo 19

Let’s understand how inventory accounting flows now work in Odoo 19.

Purchasing Products

When products are received from a vendor:

  • Inventory valuation account increases
  • Vendor bill records the liability

This removes the need for separate stock input accounts.

Selling Products

When products are delivered:

  • Inventory valuation account decreases
  • Cost of goods sold increases

This replaces the traditional stock output account structure.

Inventory Adjustments

When inventory differences occur:

  • Stock variation account records the change
  • The inventory valuation account adjusts accordingly

This ensures accounting always reflects the real value of inventory.

Benefits of the New Odoo 19 Inventory Accounting System

The changes introduced in Odoo 19 provide several benefits.

Simpler Accounting Configuration

Businesses no longer need to configure multiple interim accounts. The inventory valuation account in Odoo 19 handles most inventory value tracking.

Fewer Accounting Errors

With fewer accounts involved, the chances of configuration mistakes are reduced. This is especially helpful for small and medium-sized businesses.

Clear Financial Reporting

The Odoo 19 stock valuation accounts mapping structure ensures that financial reports remain accurate and easier to understand.

Better Automation

Odoo now handles accounting entries automatically when stock moves, reducing manual work.

Common Mistakes Businesses Make in Odoo 19 Inventory Accounting

Even with the simplified structure, some mistakes still happen.

Incorrect Product Category Setup

If the product category accounts are not configured correctly, inventory entries may not post correctly.

Wrong Inventory Valuation Method

Businesses must select the correct valuation method, such as:

  • FIFO
  • Average cost

This affects accounting entries.

Ignoring Stock Variation Accounts

The stock variation account in Odoo 19 is important for tracking inventory differences. Ignoring this account can create confusion in financial reports.

Best Practices for Managing Inventory Accounting in Odoo 19

To ensure smooth inventory accounting, businesses should follow a few best practices.

Configure Product Categories Carefully

Always review the Odoo 19 stock valuation accounts mapping inside product categories.

Monitor Inventory Valuation Reports

Regularly check inventory valuation reports to ensure accounting matches stock levels.

Perform Regular Inventory Counts

This helps reduce large differences in the stock variation account in Odoo 19.

Train Accounting and Inventory Teams

Teams should understand how the Odoo 19 replacement for stock input output works so they can interpret financial reports correctly.

What You Should Remember About Stock Input and Output Accounts in Odoo 19

By now, it should be clear why many users get confused when they try to find stock input and stock output accounts in Odoo 19. In earlier Odoo versions, these accounts worked as interim accounts that temporarily recorded the value of goods moving between purchasing, inventory, and sales processes.

However, the structure has changed in Odoo 19. Instead of relying on multiple interim accounts, the system now focuses more on the inventory valuation account in Odoo 19, along with improved Odoo 19 stock valuation accounts mapping inside product categories. This change came after Odoo 19 interim stock accounts removed the traditional configuration that many users were familiar with.

Now, when products are received or delivered, Odoo automatically creates accounting entries using the inventory valuation account and cost-related accounts. Any differences caused by stock adjustments or valuation updates are handled through the stock variation account in Odoo 19. Because of this updated structure, the Odoo 19 replacement for stock input output works automatically behind the scenes and simplifies the overall inventory accounting process.

In simple terms, businesses no longer need to worry about manually managing stock input and stock output accounts like before. Once the product category accounts and the inventory valuation account in Odoo 19 are configured correctly, Odoo manages most of the accounting entries automatically, helping companies maintain accurate inventory values and financial records.

Once you understand the logic for managing your accounting firm using the firm's mode in Odoo 19, handling multiple companies within a single system becomes more organized and controlled.

If you have been searching for a clear way to manage your accounting firm using the firm's mode in Odoo 19, this guide is for you.

Odoo 19 Accounting Firms Mode Explained – What Is It and Why Should You Care?

Let me explain the Odoo 19 accounting firms mode in simple terms. Firms mode is specially created for accounting firms that manage multiple client companies. Instead of treating your accounting firm like a single company, Odoo allows you to operate as a service provider managing many businesses.

In simple terms, Odoo 19 accounting firms' mode explained means:

  • Your firm becomes the main controller
  • Your clients are added as separate companies
  • You can switch between them easily
  • Their financial data stays separate

You do not have to log in and out repeatedly. You do not need different software for each client. Everything stays under one system, but properly organized. For any growing accounting firm, this structure is not optional. It is necessary.

How to Manage Your Accounting Firm Using Firms Mode in Odoo 19 – A Step-by-Step Guide

If you are an accounting firm handling both sales and purchase entries for clients, you can simply select customer invoices and vendor bills and click Save. This is where managing accounting firm operations in Odoo 19 truly begins. You are no longer managing one company; you are managing a structured portfolio of clients.

Let’s move to the Customers > Invoices.

Once you enable that option when you create an invoice or a vendor bill inside the Odoo 19 accounting module, it will help you to simplify the invoicing process very easily. Instead of manually configuring every line, you can simply let Odoo set it up by default. So, let’s create a new invoice by clicking on New.

I only want to provide the customer's name here. You can now see that the invoice date is auto-populated, the accounting date and due date are present, and you can also enter the total product amount, which is tax-inclusive.

doo 19?

Convert Manufactured Products into Fixed Assets in Odoo 19

In modern manufacturing businesses, not every product you create is meant for sale. Some items are produced for internal use, such as machines, tools, equipment, or even infrastructure components. This is where businesses need to Convert Manufactured Products into Fixed Assets in Odoo 19 to maintain accurate financial and operational records.

If you’ve ever wondered how to create fixed assets from manufacturing in Odoo 19, you’re not alone. Many companies struggle with managing manufactured products as fixed assets in Odoo 19, especially when production, inventory, and accounting are not aligned properly.

Odoo 19 solves this problem by offering a connected system where you can easily manage in-house manufacturing and fixed asset Odoo 19 without relying on manual processes. Instead of keeping internally used products in inventory, you can convert them into assets and track their value over time.

When you properly Convert Manufactured Products into Fixed Assets in Odoo 19, you ensure:

  • accurate financial reporting
  • proper asset tracking
  • automated depreciation
  • better decision-making

In this guide, we’ll walk through the complete process, including converting Odoo 19 storable product to fixed asset, correcting Odoo 19 inventory to fixed asset journal entry, and automating fixed asset creation from production Odoo 19.

Why Converting Manufactured Products into Assets is Important

At first glance, it may seem like a small accounting adjustment, but in reality, it has a big impact.

When a manufactured product is used internally but still sits in inventory, your financial data becomes misleading. Inventory appears inflated, and your company’s asset value is understated.

By choosing to Convert Manufactured Products into Fixed Assets in Odoo 19, you bring clarity to your system. Your inventory reflects only sellable goods, while your assets represent long-term value.

This also helps management make smarter decisions. Instead of guessing what resources are available, you get a clear picture of what your business actually owns and uses.

Understanding the Workflow: From Manufacturing to Fixed Asset

The process itself is not complicated; it’s more about understanding the flow.

It usually follows this path:

  • You create a product
  • You manufacture it
  • It enters inventory
  • You decide to use it internally
  • You convert it into a fixed asset

This complete journey is what we call in-house manufacturing for the fixed asset Odoo 19.

The key moment is when the product shifts from being “stock” to becoming “value.” That’s exactly when you need to Convert Manufactured Products into Fixed Assets in Odoo 19.

Step-by-Step Process in Odoo 19

Let’s go through the steps practically and easily.

Go to Accounting > Settings and under valuation set perpetual (at invoicing) & Inventory cost method as “Average Cost (AVCO).

Then, check the product categories inventory valuation method as Perpetual (at invoicing) and set the expense account as cost of goods sold.

Then we have to change the accounts to the location of production.

For this, go to the locations.

Go to the Production.

And, set the account as the cost of production.

1. Create a Storable Product

Everything starts with product setup. In Odoo, the product must be defined as a storable product. This allows it to move through inventory and later be converted into an asset.

At this stage, you also define costing methods and basic configurations. This forms the base of the Odoo 19 storable product to fixed asset process.

  • Go to Inventory → Products → Products.

  • Click Create.
  • Enter Product Name (e.g., “Internal Machine”).
  • Under Product Type, select Goodst.
  • Scroll to the Inventory tab and make sure Track Lots or Serial Numbers is enabled if needed.

  • Click Save.

✅ Now your product is ready for manufacturing.

Create a Bill of Materials (BoM)

  • Go to Manufacturing → Products → Bills of Materials.
  • Click Create.
  • Select your Product (the one created in Step 1).

  • Add components required to manufacture the product under Components.
  • Define quantities.

  • Optional: Add routing operations if needed.
  • Click Save.

This step ensures Odoo can calculate production cost automatically.

2. Manufacture the Product

Next comes production.

You create a Manufacturing Order, define the Bill of Materials, and complete the process. Once done, the system calculates the total cost based on materials and operations.

Now the product is available in your inventory, but it’s not meant for sale.

Before manufacturing, we will buy this product by going to the purchase app, selecting the vendor, choosing the product and its quantity, then receiving that product, uploading the bill, and confirming it. 

  • Go to Manufacturing → Operations → Manufacturing Orders.

  • Click Create.
  • Select the product and Quantity you want to manufacture.

  • Confirm the order.

  • Produce all.

  • Click Mark as Done once production is completed.

💡 Tip: You can see the Total Cost calculated automatically from BoM and operations.

3. Move the Product to an Internal Location

Instead of leaving the product in your main stock, you should move it to a dedicated internal location like “Assets.”

This step is simple but important because it clearly separates:

  • sellable inventory
  • internally used items

It also prepares the system for handling manufactured products as fixed assets in Odoo 19 properly.

  • Set Destination Location as “Assets” (you may need to create this location first in Inventory → Configuration → Locations → Create).

  • Go to Inventory → Operations → Manufacturing.

  • Click on transfers.

  • Then, click on validate.

✅ Now your manufactured product is in the “Assets” location.

4. Create the Fixed Asset

This is the stage where you officially Convert Manufactured Products into Fixed Assets in Odoo 19.

  • Go to Accounting → Journal entries

  • To convert this into a fixed asset, we have to pass one journal entry. click Create.

  • Enter the Asset Name (e.g., “Internal Machine #001”). And enter values for accounts, Inventory Valuation ( $ 31,200.00) Cr. & internal machine ($ 31,200.00) Dr, and post it.

  • And then if we check the balance sheet, then we see that 31200 was converted into a fixed asset instead of an inventory valuation.

Now you move to the Accounting module and create a fixed asset.

Here, you define:

  • asset name
  • value (based on production cost)
  • asset category
  • depreciation method

And under the bill, also configure the related bill that we have set earlier.

And now, if we again check the balance sheet and fixed asset head, then we see that under fixed assets, our internal machine account comes. 

✅ Product is now officially a fixed asset.

6. Start Depreciation

Once the asset is created, Odoo automatically handles depreciation based on your configuration.

Over time, the asset’s value reduces systematically, giving you a realistic view of its worth.

Automation: Taking It to the Next Level

Manual processes work, but automation makes everything better.

Instead of repeating these steps every time, Odoo allows you to automate the flow. For example, you can trigger asset creation as soon as a manufacturing order is completed.

With proper configuration or customization, you can:

  • automatically create assets
  • link them to manufacturing orders
  • generate journal entries instantly

This is exactly how businesses automate fixed asset creation from production in Odoo 19.

And once implemented, it saves hours of manual work and eliminates human errors.

Best Practices for Better Results

Even with the right process, small improvements can make a big difference.

For example, maintaining separate locations for inventory and assets keeps your system clean and organized. Similarly, defining clear asset categories ensures correct depreciation.

It also helps to keep an eye on the costing. If production costs are inaccurate, your asset values will also be incorrect.

A few key things to remember:

  • Always use the correct production cost
  • Keep inventory and assets separate
  • review journal entries regularly
  • automate wherever possible

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Many businesses follow the process, but still face issues due to small mistakes.

One common problem is leaving internally used products in inventory. This leads to confusion and incorrect reporting.

Another issue is skipping proper journal entries. Without them, your financial data won’t reflect reality.

Some companies also ignore depreciation settings, which affects long-term asset tracking.

Avoiding these mistakes ensures your conversion of manufactured products into Fixed Assets in the Odoo 19 workflow runs smoothly.

Real-Life Example

Imagine your company manufactures a machine for internal use.

You produce it, complete the manufacturing process, and it appears in your inventory. Instead of selling it, you move it to an internal location and create a fixed asset.

After recording the journal entry and starting depreciation, your system now shows:
