Title: A Complete Practical Guide to ORM Methods in Odoo 18
Content:
Odoo development heavily relies on ORM (Object Relational Mapping) to interact with the database. Odoo ORM (Object Relational Mapping) is the backbone of backend development. Instead of writing raw SQL, Odoo provides powerful Python methods to interact with the database safely, efficiently, and cleanly.

This guide explains core ORM methods and advanced recordset operations with real examples used in daily Odoo development.

What is ORM in Odoo?

ORM (Object Relational Mapping) is a programming technique that connects Python objects with database tables.

ORM allows developers to:

  • Treat database rows as Python objects

  • Perform CRUD operations without SQL

  • Automatically handle security, access rights, and multi-company rules

Because of these advantages, ORM forms the foundation of backend development in Odoo.

Core ORM Methods in Odoo

create()

The create() method inserts a new record into the database and returns a recordset.

				
					partner = self.env['res.partner'].create({
   'name': 'Satya',
})

This method is commonly used when creating new customers, products, sales orders, or any custom model records.

write()

The write() method updates existing record(s) in the database.

				
					partner.write({'email': 'test@example.com'})

This method is frequently used when updating information such as customer emails, order statuses, or product details.

unlink()

The unlink() method permanently deletes record(s) from the database.

				
					partner.unlink()

Since this action removes data permanently, developers must ensure proper access rights and business rules before using it.

search()

The search() method fetches record(s) from the database based on a domain.

				
					partners = self.env['res.partner'].search([('is_company', '=', True)])

Domains allow developers to filter records using logical conditions such as equality, inequality, or pattern matching.

browse()

The browse() method creates a recordset for given IDs without querying the database immediately.

				
					partner = self.env['res.partner'].browse(10)

It is useful when you already know the record ID and want to interact with it directly.

onchange()

The onchange() dynamically updates field values in the UI without saving to the database.

				
					@api.onchange('product_id')
def _onchange_product(self):
   self.price_unit = self.product_id.list_price

This method improves the user experience by automatically updating fields when related fields change.

@api.constrains

Constraints validate data integrity before committing changes to the database.

				
					@api.constrains('credit_limit')
def _check_limit(self):
   if self.credit_limit < 0:
       raise ValidationError("Invalid credit limit")

If validation fails, Odoo prevents the record from being saved.

Advanced ORM Recordset Methods

Beyond basic CRUD operations, Odoo provides several advanced recordset methods to manipulate data more efficiently.

filtered()

The filtered() method returns a subset of records that satisfy a Python condition.

				
					companies = partners.filtered(lambda p: p.is_company)

This is useful when working with recordsets that require additional filtering logic.

mapped()

The mapped() method extracts field values from a recordset into a list.

				
					names = partners.mapped('name')

It is commonly used for collecting field values quickly.

sorted()

The sorted() method returns records ordered using a Python key.

				
					partners.sorted(lambda p: p.name)

This helps developers organize records based on specific fields.

exists()

The exists() method removes non-existing (deleted) records from a recordset.

				
					records = records.exists()

This ensures that the recordset only contains valid records.

sudo()

The sudo() method executes ORM operations with superuser privileges.

				
					self.env['res.partner'].sudo().create({'name': 'Admin'})

Developers should use this method carefully because it ignores access rights.

with_context()

The with_context() method passes temporary context values to ORM operations.

				
					self.with_context(skip_check=True).write({'state': 'done'})

Context values help modify behavior during execution.

ensure_one()

The ensure_one() method ensures that the method is called on exactly one record.

				
					self.ensure_one()

If the recordset contains multiple records, Odoo raises an error.

read()

The read() method fetches field values of an existing recordset.

				
					partner.read(['name', 'email'])

It returns the values in dictionary format.

search_read()

The search_read() method combines search and read into a single optimized call.

				
					self.env['res.partner'].search_read([], ['name'])

This method improves performance when both searching and reading records are required.

copy()

The copy() method duplicates an existing record with optional changes.

				
					partner.copy({'name': 'Copy of ' + partner.name})

This is useful when creating templates or cloning records.

name_get()

The name_get() method controls how records are displayed in many2one fields.

				
					def name_get(self):
   return [(rec.id, rec.name) for rec in self]

Developers customize this method to display additional information with record names.

name_search()

The name_search() method customizes search behavior in many2one fields.

				
					def name_search(self, name, args=None, operator='ilike', limit=100):
   return self.search([('name', operator, name)], limit=limit).name_get()

This improves record searching within relational fields.

read_group()

The read_group() method performs grouped queries similar to SQL GROUP BY.

				
					self.env['sale.order'].read_group(
   [], ['amount_total'], ['state']
)

It is useful for reports, dashboards, and aggregated data.

flush()

The flush() method forces pending ORM operations to be written to the database.

				
					self.flush()

It ensures that unsaved changes are committed when required.

Why Learning ORM Methods is Essential for Odoo Developers

Understanding ORM methods is essential for building efficient and scalable Odoo modules. These methods allow developers to interact with the database in a structured and secure way without relying on raw SQL queries.

Mastering ORM methods is mandatory for:

  • Writing clean Odoo modules
  • Handling complex business logic
  • Building scalable ERP solutions

This guide gives you both the basics and advanced ORM techniques used in real Odoo 18 projects. For anyone working with Odoo 18 development, strong knowledge of ORM methods is not just useful; it is a fundamental skill that directly impacts the quality and performance of the ERP system.

Title: What Is the Difference Between an Expense and a Vendor Bill in Odoo 19 Accounting?
Content:
If you are using Odoo for your business accounts, you have probably asked yourself about the difference between an expense and a vendor bill in Odoo 19 accounting. Many business owners, accountants, and even employees get confused when deciding whether to record something as an expense or as a vendor bill.

The difference between an expense and a vendor bill in Odoo 19 accounting is not just about which button you click. It directly affects how Odoo 19 records expenses in accounting, how payments are processed, and how your financial reports look at the end of the month.

In this blog, we will clearly explain the difference between an expense and a vendor bill in Odoo 19 accounting, break down the Odoo 19 expense vs vendor bill difference, and help you understand when to use an expense or a vendor bill in Odoo 19. By the end, you will confidently know how to record company expenses, Odoo 19 vendor bill or expenses without confusion.

Odoo 19 Accounting Expense vs Supplier Bill – Why Two Different Options?

When we talk about Odoo 19 accounting expense vs supplier bill, we are actually talking about two different situations. Both are related to company costs, but the flow is different.

An expense in Odoo is usually connected to an employee. It is used when an employee spends their own money for company work. For example, travel, fuel, food during a client meeting, or small office items. The employee pays first, and then the company reimburses.

A vendor bill is used when a supplier sends an invoice to your company. In this case, the company has not paid yet. The bill is recorded, and the company will pay the supplier later according to payment terms.

So, the difference between the expense app and vendor bills Odoo starts from one simple question: who paid first? If the employee paid first, it is an expense. If the supplier is waiting for payment, it is a vendor bill.

Vendor Bill vs Employee Expense Odoo – Who Paid and Who Is Waiting?

Let’s understand the vendor bill vs employee expense Odoo more virtually. Imagine your employee goes for a business trip. He pays for fuel and lunch using his own cash. Later, he submits a claim in Odoo. This is clearly an expense. The company now owes money to the employee.

Now, imagine your office receives an internet bill from your service provider. The company has to pay this bill within 15 days. This is a vendor bill. The company owes money to the supplier.

This is the core difference between an expense and a vendor bill in Odoo 19 accounting. In one case, the employee needs reimbursement. In the other case, the supplier needs payment.

When people don’t understand this, they start using vendor bills for employee claims or expenses for supplier invoices. That creates confusion in reports and payables.

Difference Between an Expense and a Vendor Bill in Odoo 19 Accounting

Understanding the difference between an expense and a vendor bill in Odoo 19 accounting is very important if you want clean reports and correct payables. Both are related to company costs, but the flow, purpose, and accounting impact are different.

Basis of Comparison

Expense (Employee Expense)

Vendor Bill (Supplier Bill)

Who Pays First

Employee pays from personal money

The supplier provides goods/services, but the company has not paid yet

Main Purpose

Employee reimbursement

Recording supplier invoice

Module Used

Expense App

Accounting App (Vendor Bills)

Payable Created

Payable to Employee

Accounts Payable (Supplier)

Payment Flow

Usually reimbursed after approval

Paid based on payment terms and due date

Approval Process

Goes through the Odoo 19 expenses approval workflow

Usually validated by an accountant (no employee-style approval)

Reporting Impact

Affects employee expense reports

Affects vendor aging and supplier balances

Example

Fuel, travel, meals paid by employee

Rent invoice, utility bill, and inventory purchase

Accounting Entry

Expense account debit, Employee payable credit

Expense/Asset debit, Accounts Payable credit

Used When

Employee already paid

The company needs to pay the supplier

So, in simple words, if the employee has already spent money on company work, use an expense. If the company has received a bill and needs to pay a supplier, use a vendor bill. Keeping this difference clear in Odoo 19 accounting will help you avoid confusion in reports and payment tracking.

Odoo Expense Creates Direct Payment vs Vendor Bill Payable: What Happens in Accounting?

Now, let’s talk about the accounting side, because this is where Odoo expense creates direct payment, vs a vendor bill payable becomes important.

When you approve an employee expense in Odoo, the system records the expense and creates a payable to the employee. Once you register the payment, it clears the payable. In many cases, Odoo expense creates a direct payment vs va endor bill payable because it is designed for quick reimbursement.

On the other hand, when you create a vendor bill, Odoo records it under Accounts Payable. That amount stays there until you make the payment. It shows in your vendor aging report and affects your outstanding liabilities.

So, in Odoo 19, vendor bill journal entry vs expense, the structure is slightly different. A vendor bill clearly creates a liability in Accounts Payable. An expense creates a payable to the employee, which is often processed quickly. This difference might look small, but during audits or financial reviews, it matters a lot.

Odoo 19 Vendor Bill Journal Entry vs Expense

Let’s go a little deeper into Odoo 19 vendor bill journal entry vs expense. When you post a vendor bill, Odoo debits the expense or asset account and credits Accounts Payable. That means your company officially owes money to the supplier.

When you post an employee expense, Odoo debits the expense account and credits a payable account linked to the employee. After reimbursement, the payable is cleared.

So technically, both create payables, but the nature of the payable is different. Vendor bills affect supplier balances. Expenses affect employee reimbursements.

This is an important part of the Odoo 19 expense vs vendor bill difference. If you mix them, your supplier statements and employee balances will not match reality.

Difference Between Expense App and Vendor Bills Odoo – Functional Side

Now, let’s talk about the difference between the expense app and vendor bills Odoo from a functional point of view.

The Expense App is more HR-focused. It is designed for employees to submit claims. It includes expense categories, attachments of receipts, and approval steps. It is built around the idea of reimbursement.

Vendor Bills are part of the Accounting module. They are designed to manage supplier invoices, due dates, taxes, and payment terms. They are built around liability management.

This is why the Odoo 19 accounting expense vs supplier bill is not just about posting entries. It is about using the correct module for the correct purpose. If you try to record all costs using only vendor bills or only expenses, you will miss the proper workflow and tracking features.

Odoo 19 Expenses Approval Workflow vs Vendor Bills – Control and Process

Another major part of the Odoo 19 expenses approval workflow vs vendor bills is how approvals work. In the Expense App, an employee submits an expense. It goes to the manager for approval. Then, accounting reviews and processes the payment. This creates internal control. You can decide who approves what, and up to what limit.

Vendor bills usually do not go through the same employee-style workflow unless you configure custom approval rules. Most of the time, the accountant records and validates the bill directly.

So, if you want proper control over employee spending, you should not record it as a vendor bill. The Odoo 19 expenses approval workflow vs vendor bills clearly shows that each tool has a different purpose. Understanding this helps you decide when to use an expense or a vendor bill in Odoo 19 without second-guessing.

When to Use Expense or Vendor Bill Odoo 19 – Simple Rule You Can Follow

You don’t need to overthink when to use an expense or a vendor bill in Odoo 19. Just remember this simple rule.

  • If an employee used personal money for company work, use Expense.
  • If a supplier sent you an invoice and your company will pay them, use the Vendor Bill.

For example, if your employee buys office stationery from a local shop and pays cash, that is an expense. But if you have a monthly contract with a supplier who sends you an invoice, that is a vendor bill. This one rule will solve most of your confusion about record company expenses, Odoo 19 vendor bill, or expense.

How Odoo 19 Records Expenses in Accounting – Why It Matters for Reports

Many people don’t think about how Odoo 19 records expenses in accounting until something goes wrong in reports.

If you record supplier invoices as expenses in the Expense App, your vendor aging report will not show the correct outstanding amounts. You will not see what you actually owe to suppliers.

If you record employee claims as vendor bills, your supplier list will start showing employees as vendors. That makes your reports messy and hard to understand.

So, how Odoo 19 records expenses in accounting directly affects your Profit and Loss statement, Accounts Payable report, and even cash flow planning. This is why the difference between an expense and a vendor bill in Odoo 19 accounting is not just a technical topic. It is connected to the accuracy of your financial data.

Odoo 19 Expense vs Vendor Bill Difference – Why Getting It Right Saves You Trouble

The Odoo 19 expense vs vendor bill difference might look small when you are entering a single transaction. But imagine hundreds of entries every month. Small mistakes repeated many times can create big confusion.

If your team understands vendor bill vs employee expense Odoo clearly, your accounting will stay clean. Your approvals will work properly. Your reports will make sense. And when auditors ask questions, you will not struggle to explain why employees are listed as vendors or why supplier balances don’t match.

So, take this seriously. Train your team. Set clear internal rules. Decide how to record company expenses in Odoo 19 vendor bill, or expense from day one.

Still Confused? Here’s What You Should Do Next

By now, you clearly understand the difference between an expense and a vendor bill in Odoo 19 accounting. It all comes down to one simple thing: who paid first and who needs to be paid. But in real business life, things don’t always look this simple. Sometimes entries are already mixed, reports are not matching, and your team is not sure when to use expense or vendor bill in Odoo 19.

If you ignore this confusion, it slowly creates bigger issues. Your vendor balances may not match. Employee reimbursements may get delayed. Your Profit and Loss report may not reflect the correct picture. And during audits, small mistakes can raise unnecessary questions.

That’s why understanding the Odoo 19 expense vs vendor bill difference is not enough. You also need to implement it correctly in your system. Your Expense app, vendor bills, journal entries, and approval workflow should all be properly configured so that how Odoo 19 records expenses in accounting stays accurate from day one. Title: How to Setup Cash Discounts in Odoo 19 Accounting?
Content:
If you are managing finances in Odoo, then understanding how to setup cash discounts in Odoo 19 can make a real difference in your cash flow. Many businesses struggle with late payments, and this is exactly where cash discounts become useful.

When you properly learn how to setup cash discounts in Odoo 19, you give your customers a strong reason to pay earlier. This not only improves liquidity but also builds better financial discipline in your business.

In this guide, I will walk you through how to setup cash discounts in Odoo 19, explain how early payment discounts work, and show you how to manage gain/loss accounts in a way just like you would expect in a real business scenario.

What Are Cash Discounts in Odoo 19 Accounting?

Cash discounts are incentives offered to customers when they pay their invoices before the due date.

For example:

Invoice total = $1000

Payment term = 2% discount if paid within 10 days

Customer pays early → Pays only $980

In Odoo 19 accounting, this feature is fully automated when configured properly. You can easily manage:

  • Odoo 19 cash discount on invoices
  • Customer early payment discounts
  • Discount gain/loss accounting entries

Odoo 19 Setup Cash Discounts in Accounting – What Actually Happens Behind the Screen

When you give a discount to your customer for early payment, you are actually accepting less money than your invoice amount. That means there is a small loss on your side.

And when your supplier gives you a discount, you are paying less. That means it becomes a gain for you.

This is where the early payment discount gain or loss in Odoo 19 comes in. Odoo doesn’t just reduce the amount; it also records that difference properly in your accounts.

So, when we talk about Odoo 19 setting up cash discounts in accounting, we are not just setting a discount; we are also telling Odoo how to handle that difference in accounting.

Odoo 19 Payment Terms with Cash Discount – The Real Place Where Everything Starts

In Odoo, cash discounts are controlled through payment terms. So, if you are thinking about Odoo 19 payment terms with a cash discount, just remember this is where everything begins.

You are basically telling Odoo something like this:

  • If the customer pays early → give a discount
  • If the customer pays late → take the full amount

For example:

2% discount if paid in 10 days

Otherwise, full payment in 30 days

This is how Odoo 19 customer early payment discount is defined in the system.

How to Setup Cash Discounts in Odoo 19 Step by Step Without Confusion

Let’s now go step by step on how to set up cash discounts in Odoo 19. First, open the Accounting app.

Go to Configuration > Payment Terms.

Click New and create a new one.

Give it a name that is easy to understand, like “2/7 Net 30 OR 2% in 7 Days Net 30”. Now add two lines. In the first line, define the discount percentage and the number of days. In the second line, define the full payment due date.

This is the core setup of Odoo 19 payment terms with cash discount. Take your time here. If this part is correct, everything else becomes easy.

Configure Discount Gain Loss Accounts Odoo – The Step Most People Skip

Now, I want you to focus carefully here, because this is where most people make mistakes. When a discount is applied, Odoo needs to know where to record that difference. That’s why you need to configure discount gain loss accounts in Odoo.

Go to your Chart of Accounts and create two accounts:

  • One for cash discount loss
  • One for cash discount gain

After that, go back to settings and link these accounts.

This step connects your discount with proper accounting. Without this, your reports will not show correct values. So, if you really want to understand how to set up cash discounts in Odoo 19, don’t skip this part.

Odoo 19 Customer Early Payment Discount – How It Works When You Create Invoices

Now let’s see what happens when you actually create an invoice. You select your customer and apply the payment term you created. Your Odoo 19 customer's early payment discount is now active.

When the invoice is sent, the customer sees:

  • Pay early → get a discount
  • Pay later → full amount

This is how Odoo 19's cash discount on invoices works from the customer side.

Early Payment Discount Gain Loss Odoo 19 – What Happens When Payment is Received

Let’s say your invoice is 1000, and the discount is 2%. If a customer pays early, they pay 980.

Odoo will:

Odoo 19 Credit Card Journal Setup for Accurate Tracking

A well-configured system always starts with the right setup. The same applies to your Odoo 19 credit card journal setup.

The credit card journal acts as a dedicated space where all card-related transactions are recorded. It is usually created as a bank-type journal, but it represents a liability, since the amount spent through the card is payable to the bank.

When the Odoo 19 credit card journal setup is done correctly, every transaction has a clear place in the system. This reduces confusion later, especially during reconciliation. Without this structure, even correctly recorded expenses may not reflect properly in reports.

Taking a few minutes to configure the journal properly saves a significant amount of time when reviewing accounts later. The first step is to go to: Accounting → Configuration → Journals → New.

Now configure:

Journal Name: Company Credit Card

Type: Bank

Account: Credit Card Liability Account

This is your Odoo 19 credit card journal setup, and it’s important because:

  • It tracks what you owe to the bank
  • It records all credit card transactions in one place

Now, configure Default Accounts and make sure:

Recording expenses correctly is one of the most important parts of managing credit cards. In Odoo 19, each transaction should reflect both the nature of the expense and the source of payment. One of the most frustrating things in perishable inventory is losing track of expiration dates. With Odoo 19's expiration dates for inventory, you can assign an expiry date to each batch. The system will alert you before a product expires, giving you enough time to sell or use it.

Think about it: no more last-minute panic when a batch of yogurt or medicine is about to expire. You can plan promotions, use it in production, or prioritize it for shipping.

Odoo 19 Lot Tracking for Perishables

Lot tracking is like giving each batch a unique passport. Odoo 19 lot tracking for perishables lets you see exactly where a product came from and where it’s going.

This is especially important for:

  • Food products (to meet health and safety regulations)
  • Pharmaceuticals (for compliance and recalls)
  • Chemicals (to prevent mixing incompatible batches)

With this system, you can track products from the supplier to the customer, ensuring safety, quality, and transparency.

FEFO Removal Strategy in Odoo 19

FEFO stands for First Expired, First Out, and it’s the smartest way to manage perishable products in Odoo 19

. You don’t want to sell the freshest batch first while older stock goes to waste.

With Odoo 19, you can set FEFO rules so the system automatically prioritizes items with the earliest expiration date. It’s a simple step that drastically reduces losses and keeps your inventory fresh.

  • Simplify recalls

For example, if one batch of chocolate melts during transport, you’ll know exactly which lot is affected. That’s inventory traceability in action.

FEFO ensures older stock moves out first. Odoo 19 can:

Title: What Is the Difference Between Trial Balance and General Ledger in Odoo 19 Accounting?
Content:
If you are working in Odoo 19 accounting and still feel confused while checking reports, you are not alone. Many business owners and accountants ask the same question again and again: What exactly is the difference between trial balance and general ledger in Odoo 19?

You open the accounting reports section, you see both reports there, and you think, “Aren’t they showing the same thing?” But when you start reviewing numbers, you realize they are not the same at all. The difference between the trial balance and the general ledger in Odoo 19 directly affects how you check errors, prepare reports, and understand what is really happening in your accounts.

In this blog, I am going to explain the difference between the trial balance and the general ledger in Odoo 19 in simple words. We will talk about Odoo 19 trial balance vs general ledger report, trial balance meaning in Odoo 19 accounting, and also Odoo 19 trial balance migration with general ledger. By the end, you will not only understand the concept, but you will feel confident using both reports in your daily work.

Trial Balance Meaning in Odoo 19 Accounting – What Is It Really Showing You?

Let me explain the trial balance meaning in Odoo 19 accounting in the simplest way possible. A trial balance is a summary report. It shows all your accounts with their total debit and total credit balances for a specific period. That’s it. It does not show individual transactions. It does not show invoice numbers. It does not show journal details. It only shows totals.

When you open the trial balance in Odoo 19 accounting, you will see:

  • Account name
  • Total debit
  • Total credit
  • Balance

Now here is something important. A trial balance helps you check one main thing: are your total debits equal to total credits? If yes, your books are balanced mathematically. If not, there is an issue somewhere.

But this is where many people get confused. Balanced does not always mean correct. It only means there is no calculation mistake in the totals. This is why understanding the trial balance meaning in Odoo 19 accounting is very important before moving ahead.

General Ledger Report in Odoo 19 Explanation – What Is Hidden Behind the Totals?

Now, let’s talk about the general ledger report in Odoo 19. If the trial balance is a summary, then the general ledger is the full story. It shows every single transaction posted to an account. When you open the general ledger in Odoo 19, you can see:

  • Date
  • Journal entry number
  • Description
  • Debit
  • Credit
  • Running balance

So, imagine your Sales account shows 1,000,000 in the trial balance. That is only a total. But when you open the general ledger, you see all the invoices that made up that 1,000,000. You see which customer, which date, and what amount.

This is where the Odoo 19 trial balance vs general ledger report becomes very clear. Trial balance shows totals. The general ledger shows details behind those totals. When someone asks for a general ledger report in Odoo 19, this is the real answer: it is a detailed record of all financial movements inside each account.

Difference Between Trial Balance and General Ledger in Odoo 19

Now, let’s directly talk about the difference between the trial balance and the general ledger in Odoo 19, so there is no confusion left.

Basis of Comparison

Trial Balance in Odoo 19

General Ledger in Odoo 19

Purpose

Used to check whether total debits and total credits are equal.

Used to review and verify individual transactions posted to each account.

Level of Detail

Summary report showing total balances of accounts.

Detailed report showing every transaction with date, journal, and description.

Information Shown

Account name, total debit, total credit, and final balance.

Date, journal entry number, description, debit, credit, and running balance.

Usage Timing

Mostly reviewed at month-end or year-end for closing accounts.

Used daily or whenever you need to investigate specific entries.

Error Detection

Helps identify if debits and credits are not matching.

Helps identify wrong postings, duplicate entries, or incorrect accounts.

Role in Financial Statements

Forms the base for preparing Profit & Loss and Balance Sheet.

Supports financial statements by providing transaction-level evidence.

Reporting Type

Part of Odoo 19 accounting reports trial balance summary vs ledger detail as the summary layer.

Part of Odoo 19 accounting reports trial balance summary vs ledger detail as the detailed layer.

During Migration

Used for importing opening balances in the Odoo 19 trial balance migration with the general ledger.

Used when migrating the full transaction history along with balances.

When to Use

When you need a quick overview of account balances.

When you need to understand how a balance was created.

This table clearly explains the difference between the trial balance and the general ledger in Odoo 19, so you can easily decide which report to use and when.

Odoo 19 Trial Balance vs General Ledger Report – A Practical Situation

Let’s say you are closing your month. You open the trial balance, and you see that your Expense account looks higher than usual. Now you are worried. You think something is wrong. A trial balance only shows you the total expense amount. It does not tell you why it increased.

Now, you open the general ledger report in Odoo 19. You filter the expense account. You check entries one by one. You find out that there were two extra vendor bills posted under the wrong account.

This is the real difference between the trial balance and the general ledger in Odoo 19. The trial balance shows you that something changed. The general ledger shows you why it changed. In real business life, you need both. One alerts you. The other explains.

How to Use Trial Balance and General Ledger in Odoo 19 in Daily Work

Now, let me explain how to use the trial balance and the general ledger in Odoo 19 properly, because this is where many teams struggle. At the end of every month, first open the trial balance. Check totals. Confirm that debit equals credit. Review major accounts like cash, payables, receivables, revenue, and expenses. If something looks unusual, do not guess. Do not assume. Immediately open the general ledger.

When you want to check customer balances, open a general ledger for a receivable account. When you want to verify vendor postings, open a ledger for a payable account. This is how to use the trial balance and general ledger in Odoo 19 correctly. A trial balance is your overview tool. The general ledger is your checking tool. If you mix them up, you will feel confused. If you use them properly, accounting becomes clearer.

Odoo 19 Accounting Reports Trial Balance Summary vs Ledger Detail – Why Both Are Important

Inside Odoo 19, accounting reports are designed in a structured way. When we talk about Odoo 19 accounting reports, trial balance summary vs ledger detail, we are talking about two layers of reporting. The trial balance summary gives management a quick look at financial health. It is compact and easy to review.

Ledger detail gives accountants the ability to track every entry. It is longer and more detailed. If your company is growing, you cannot rely only on a summary. You also need details for audits, tax checks, and internal reviews.

Understanding Odoo 19 accounting reports, trial balance summary vs ledger detail, helps you avoid mistakes that happen when people only check totals without verifying transactions.

Odoo 19 Trial Balance Migration with General Ledger – What You Must Know

Now let’s talk about something important: if you are shifting from another system, Odoo 19 trial balance migration with the general ledger. When businesses migrate to Odoo 19, they usually bring opening balances using trial balance data. This means they import total balances of each account.

But here is the issue. If you migrate only trial balance totals and not general ledger details, you lose historical transaction records. That means you will not see old invoice-level entries in the ledger. This can create problems later during audit or reconciliation.

So, during the Odoo 19 trial balance migration with a general ledger, it is always better to plan properly. If possible, migrate both opening balances and detailed transaction history. This way, your new system does not feel incomplete.

Many companies ignore this step and later realize they cannot trace past entries. That is why understanding Odoo 19 trial balance migration with the general ledger is very important before system implementation.

Why Many People Still Confuse These Two Reports

Even after working for years, some accountants still mix up the trial balance and the general ledger. The reason is simple: both show account names and balances.

But the difference between the trial balance and the general ledger in Odoo 19 becomes clear when you ask one question: “Do I need totals or do I need transaction details?”

  • If you need totals, open the trial balance.
  • If you need to see who posted what and when, open the general ledger.

Once you remember this simple rule, Odoo 19 trial balance vs general ledger report confusion will disappear.

Real Impact on Financial Statements

The trial balance is directly used to prepare the profit and loss statement and the balance sheet. It acts as a base report. The general ledger supports that base by providing evidence of each number.

If your trial balance is correct but ledger entries are posted to the wrong accounts, your financial statements will still look wrong.

So, the difference between the trial balance and the general ledger in Odoo 19 is not just technical knowledge. It directly impacts reporting accuracy.

Use the Right Report at the Right Time

Now you clearly understand the difference between the trial balance and the general ledger in Odoo 19. Trial balance meaning in Odoo 19 accounting is about summary and balance checking. The general ledger report in Odoo 19 explains is about detailed tracking of transactions.

Odoo 19 trial balance vs general ledger report is not about which one is better. It is about when and why you use them. How to use the trial balance and general ledger in Odoo 19 depends on what you are trying to review. And if you are planning an Odoo 19 trial balance migration with the general ledger, planning properly will save you from future confusion.

Title: How to Use Reservation Methods in Odoo 19 Inventory Effectively?
Content:
If you are working with inventory in Odoo, you already know that managing stock is not only about quantities. The real challenge is deciding when to reserve that stock. This is where understanding how to use reservation methods in Odoo 19 inventory becomes essential.

In many businesses, inventory issues do not come from a lack of stock. They come from incorrect reservation timing. Stock gets reserved too early and blocks other orders, or it gets reserved too late and delays deliveries. In both cases, operations become difficult to manage. That is why learning how to use reservation methods in Odoo 19 inventory is not just a technical step; it is an operational decision.

In this Odoo 19 reservation methods guide, we will go through each option in a clear and structured way so you can apply it based on how your business actually works. Once you understand how to use reservation methods in Odoo 19 inventory, you will notice better control, fewer delays, and more clarity in your workflow.

Understanding the Core Concept of Odoo 19 Reservation Methods Guide

Before going into different options, it is important to understand what a reservation really means in Odoo. Reservation is the process by which Odoo allocates available stock to a specific order. Once a product is reserved, it is no longer available for other orders.

This decision directly affects:

  • Order fulfillment
  • Stock availability
  • Warehouse operations

If the reservation is done at the wrong time, it can create unnecessary pressure on your system. That is why choosing the right method is important. This Odoo 19 reservation methods guide focuses on helping you make that decision based on your workflow rather than assumptions.

Odoo 19 At Confirmation vs Manual Reservation – Choosing Between Speed and Control

One of the most important decisions in Odoo inventory is selecting between Odoo 19 at confirmation vs manual reservation.

When you use the confirmation, Odoo automatically reserves stock as soon as the order is confirmed. This approach is straightforward and works well in stable environments where stock levels are predictable.

It helps your team move quickly because:

  • Reserved stock is immediately visible
  • Picking operations can start without delay
  • There is less manual involvement

However, this method can become difficult to manage if your stock changes frequently. Early reservations may block stock that could be used for more urgent orders.

On the other hand, manual reservation gives you complete control. Stock is only reserved when you decide to reserve it.

This is useful in situations where:

  • Stock is limited
  • Orders need prioritization
  • Availability is uncertain

When comparing Odoo 19 at confirmation vs manual reservation, the decision depends on your business needs. If your priority is speed and simplicity, automatic reservation works well. If your priority is control and flexibility, manual reservation is more suitable.

Before Scheduled Date Reservation Odoo 19 – Managing Stock with Better Timing

In many businesses, there is a gap between order confirmation and delivery. Reserving stock immediately in such cases may not be the right approach. This is where, before the scheduled date, Odoo 19 becomes useful.

With this method, Odoo delays reservation until closer to the scheduled operation date. This allows stock to remain available for other orders during that time.

This approach is particularly effective when:

  • Stock is continuously moving
  • Incoming shipments are expected
  • Delivery timelines are planned in advance

Using before the scheduled date in Odoo 19 helps maintain balance. It reduces unnecessary stock blocking while still ensuring that products are available when needed.

Reserve Only Full Packagings Odoo 19 – Maintaining Structured Inventory Handling

For businesses dealing with bulk quantities or packaged goods, handling stock at the packaging level is often necessary. By enabling reserve-only full packagings in Odoo 19, Odoo will only reserve stock if complete packages are available. It avoids splitting packages into smaller quantities.

Title: How to Use Cash Rounding in Odoo 19 Accounting?
Content:
Why Cash Rounding in Odoo 19 Accounting Matters in Daily Transactions

If you work with invoices every day, you already know how small decimal values can create confusion in cash payments. Suppose you generate an invoice for 10.02 or 15.03. When the customer pays with cash, giving or receiving those tiny coin values can be inconvenient. In many countries, these small coins are rarely used anymore. This is exactly why cash rounding in Odoo 19 accounting becomes an important feature for businesses that deal with cash transactions.

Cash rounding in Odoo 19 accounting allows the system to automatically adjust invoice totals to a practical number. Instead of handling amounts like 10.02 or 10.03, Odoo can round the invoice to 10.00 or 10.05, depending on the rule you define. This small adjustment makes daily billing easier for cashiers and keeps accounting records accurate.

The Odoo 19 cash rounding feature helps companies avoid manual calculations. When you enable it, Odoo automatically rounds off the invoice total based on the rules you configure. This means your accounting team does not need to manually adjust invoices or worry about mismatched totals.

Another important part of cash rounding in Odoo 19 accounting is that the system records the rounding difference in the background. That difference is posted to the Odoo 19 cash rounding gain loss account, so your financial reports remain correct. Nothing is lost, and everything is properly recorded.

In this guide, I will walk you through how to configure cash rounding in Odoo 19, how the Odoo 19 invoice cash rounding setting works, and how the Odoo 19 cash rounding methods nearest up down affect your invoices. By the end of this blog, you will clearly understand how to manage cash rounding inside Odoo without confusion.

Understanding the Odoo 19 Cash Rounding Feature in Real Business Scenarios

Before we talk about configuration steps, it is important to understand how the Odoo 19 cash rounding feature works in real business situations.

Think about a retail store where hundreds of small cash transactions happen daily. If every invoice contains amounts like 0.01 or 0.02, cashiers will constantly struggle with small change. Over time, this creates delays at the counter and unnecessary confusion.

With cash rounding in Odoo 19 accounting, the system automatically adjusts the invoice total to the nearest acceptable value. The cashier simply receives or gives cash based on the rounded total.

For example:

  • If the invoice total is 12.02, the system may round it to 12.00.
  • If the invoice total is 12.03, it may be rounded to 12.05.

This rounding happens according to the Odoo 19 cash rounding methods nearest up and down that you define in the configuration. At the same time, Odoo records the difference and sends it to the Odoo 19 cash rounding gain loss account so that your accounting remains balanced.

Configure Cash Rounding Odoo 19: A Step-by-Step Guide

Now let’s talk about the practical part. If you want to start using this feature, you need to configure cash rounding in Odoo 19 inside the accounting settings.

First, open the Accounting module in Odoo.

From there, go to the Configuration menu and open Settings.

Inside the accounting settings page, you will see the option related to the Odoo 19 cash rounding feature. Once you enable this option and save the settings, Odoo will allow you to create rounding rules.

After enabling the feature, the next step to configure cash rounding in Odoo 19 is to create a rounding rule. For this, go to Accounting → Configuration → Cash Roundings.

Here, you can create a new rule that defines how the system should round off the invoice total in Odoo 19.

Now, create our first rule, which is Half Up. When creating the rule, you will define several important values, such as rounding precision, rounding method, and the accounts used to record rounding differences, and click save.

Let’s move on to the second option, which is Half Down. Fill in the details and click save.

And later on, I would like to create a third cash rounding rule as Nearest. Set the rounding precision, strategy, and methods, etc., and click save.

Here, you can see all the created cash roundings. These settings tell Odoo exactly how to handle invoice totals during cash payments.

Once the rule is saved, the system is ready to apply rounding adjustments to invoices. So, go to the Customers > Invoices.

Click New.

Select the customer, add the product, and set the price of the product.

Currently, you can see that the price of the product is $749.30.

Now, let’s move to the Other Info tab. In this tab, you would be able to see the Cash Rounding Method. 

First, we select the Half Up method and click Save. With this method, the invoice total is always rounded up. Businesses may use this method to avoid losing small amounts.

Now, if we move on to the Invoice Line tab and scroll down, you can see it is just rounded up, and it’s set as $749.50. We have just rounded 0.20 here.

Let’s change this into the second cash rounding method, which is Half Down, and save the changes. Some businesses prefer this approach for customer satisfaction.

Now, you can clearly see the changes showing here, and we have subtracted -0.30. The loss has taken place here, and we are just collecting the $749.00 from the customer.

So, let’s change to the last cash rounding method, which is Nearest, and click save. The system rounds to the closest value, and this is the most commonly used rounding method.

When you set it as the nearest method, you can see it will be going with the precision, and that will be converted to $749.40 and rounded to just $0.10.

This is how the system automatically rounds off the invoice total in Odoo 19 based on the defined rule.

Odoo 19 Cash Rounding Methods Nearest Up Down Explained

While configuring the rounding rule, one important decision you need to make is selecting the rounding method. The Odoo 19 cash rounding methods nearest up or down determine how invoice totals are adjusted.

The first method is Nearest Rounding. In this method, the system rounds the invoice total to the closest value based on the rounding precision you defined. For example, if the rounding precision is 0.05, then an invoice amount like 10.02 will be rounded to 10.00, while 10.03 will be rounded to 10.05. Many businesses prefer this method because it keeps the rounding balanced between customers and the company.

The second option is Round Up. In this method, the invoice total always increases to the next rounding value. For example, 10.01, 10.02, or 10.03 would all become 10.05. Some businesses choose this option to avoid losing small amounts in cash transactions.

The third option is Round Down. With this method, the invoice total always decreases to the lower rounding value. For example, 10.04 or 10.03 may become 10.00. Some companies use this method to keep customers satisfied by slightly reducing the payable amount. Each business chooses the method that fits its financial policy and local currency practices.

Odoo 19 Invoice Cash Rounding Setting and How It Works on Invoices

Once you create the rounding rule, the next step is understanding the Odoo 19 invoice cash rounding setting and how it works when creating invoices.

When you generate a customer invoice in the accounting module, you will see an option to select a cash rounding rule. After selecting the rule, Odoo automatically checks the invoice total and applies the rounding adjustment.

For example, you create an invoice with a total of 25.02. If the selected rule rounds to 0.05, the system will automatically round off the invoice total in Odoo 19 and adjust the amount to 25.00.

Inside the invoice, Odoo also adds a small rounding line showing the adjustment amount. This ensures that the customer invoice remains transparent and your accounting entries stay correct. This Odoo 19 invoice cash rounding setting works quietly in the background but saves a lot of time for accounting teams.

Odoo 19 Cash Rounding Gain Loss Account and Why It Is Important

Whenever an invoice total is rounded, a small financial difference appears. This difference must be recorded somewhere in the accounting system. That is where the Odoo 19 cash rounding gain loss account comes into play.

When you configure cash rounding in Odoo 19, you define two accounts: one for gains and one for losses. If rounding increases the invoice amount, the difference goes to the profit account. If rounding decreases the invoice amount, the difference goes to the loss account.

For example, suppose an invoice total is 18.02, and the system rounds it down to 18.00. The difference of 0.02 will be recorded in the loss account. On the other hand, if an invoice total of 18.03 is rounded up to 18.05, the difference of 0.02 goes to the gain account.

This is why the Odoo 19 cash rounding gain loss account is necessary. It ensures that even the smallest financial differences are properly recorded in your accounting reports.

How Odoo Automatically Round Off Invoice Total Odoo 19

One thing many Odoo users appreciate is that once everything is configured, the system handles the rounding automatically.

After you configure cash rounding in Odoo 19, every time an invoice is created with the rounding rule selected, the system calculates the adjustment and updates the total. The accountant does not need to calculate anything manually.

Odoo checks the rounding precision, applies the selected option from Odoo 19 cash rounding methods nearest up or down, adjusts the amount, and posts the difference to the Odoo 19 cash rounding gain or loss account. Because of this automation, companies can easily round off the invoice total in Odoo 19 without affecting accounting accuracy.

Practical Example of Cash Rounding in Odoo 19 Accounting

Let me explain this with a simple example. Suppose you run a retail shop and a customer buys items worth 32.02. Your rounding rule is set to 0.05 with nearest rounding. When the invoice is generated, Odoo checks the amount and applies cash rounding in Odoo 19 accounting. The system adjusts the total from 32.02 to 32.00.

The difference of 0.02 is automatically recorded in the Odoo 19 cash rounding gain loss account. The customer pays 32.00, the cashier handles a clean cash amount, and your accounting records remain accurate. This small process makes daily transactions much easier for businesses that handle cash payments frequently.

Start Using Cash Rounding in Odoo 19 Accounting for Better Invoice Control

If you work with invoices every day, even small decimal values can create confusion in cash transactions. This is why understanding cash rounding in Odoo 19 accounting becomes important for businesses that handle regular cash payments.

Once you configure cash rounding in Odoo 19, the system automatically rounds off the invoice total Odoo 19 according to the rule you define. Whether you use the Odoo 19 cash rounding methods nearest up, down or a specific rounding precision, Odoo manages the calculation in the background and keeps your invoices accurate.

At the same time, any rounding difference is recorded in the Odoo 19 cash rounding gain or loss account, which keeps your accounting records balanced and transparent. The Odoo 19 invoice cash rounding setting also ensures that the rounding adjustment appears clearly on the invoice, so both your accounting team and your customers can easily understand the final amount.

In short, once the Odoo 19 cash rounding feature is properly configured, handling cash invoices becomes much simpler and more organized.

Title: How to Generate Inventory Stock Report Using Custom Commands in Odoo 18 Command Palette?
Content:
Modern ERP systems are all about speed, efficiency, and reducing unnecessary clicks. With Odoo 18, one prevailing yet often underutilised feature is the Command Palette, a smart interface that allows users to instantly access actions, menus, and even custom developer tools.

In this blog, we’ll walk through how to create a custom command that generates an inventory stock report, directly from the Command Palette, without navigating through multiple menus.

What is the Command Palette?

Odoo 18 provides a useful feature called the Command Palette. You can open it using the keyboard shortcut:

  • Ctrl + K

This palette allows users to quickly search menus, users, channels, and other items. Developers can also extend this feature by adding custom commands that execute backend logic. In this example, we create a command that opens a filtered inventory report.

Step 1: Create the Module Manifest

Create the module manifest file __manifest__.py.

				
					{
   'name': 'Inventory Stock Report using Command Palette',
   'version': '1.0',
   'summary': 'Add custom command palette actions',
   'category': 'Tools',
   'depends': ['web','product'],
   'data': [],
   'assets': {
   	'web.assets_backend': [
       	'smart_commands/static/src/js/command_provider.js',
   	],
   },
   'installable': True,
}

Step 2: Backend Python Method

First, extend the product.product model and create a method that returns an Odoo action. product.py

				
					from odoo import models, api, _
class ProductProduct(models.Model):
   _inherit = 'product.product'
   @api.model
   def generate_report(self):
   	return {
       	'name': _('Monthly Inventory Report'),
       	'type': 'ir.actions.act_window',
       	'res_model': 'product.product',
       	'view_mode': 'list,form',
       	'views': [[False, 'list'], [False, 'form']],
       	'domain': [('qty_available', '>=', 0)],
       	'target': 'current',
   	}

This method returns an action that opens the product list view filtered by available quantity.

Step 3: Add JavaScript Command

Next, create a JavaScript file to register the command in the Command Palette.

Your_module/static/src/js/command_provider.js

				
					/** @odoo-module **/
 import { registry } from "@web/core/registry";
import { _t } from "@web/core/l10n/translation";
const commandSetupRegistry = registry.category("command_setup");
const commandProviderRegistry = registry.category("command_provider");
// 1. Setup the visual header
commandSetupRegistry.add("smart_dev_actions", {
   name: _t("Developer Smart Actions"),
});
// 2. Define the search logic
commandProviderRegistry.add("smart_report_provider", {
   async provide(env, options) {
   	return [{
       	name: _t("Generate Monthly Developer Report"),
       	searchValues: ["smart", "report", "health"],
       	category: "smart_dev_actions",
       	action: async () => {
           	try {
               	// Call the Python method using ORM service
               	const action = await env.services.orm.call(
                   	"product.product",
                   	"generate_report",
                   	[] // Ensure this empty array is closed correctly
               	);
               	// If Python returns the action dictionary, execute it
               	if (action && action.type) {
                       env.services.action.doAction(action);
               	}
                   env.services.notification.add(_t("Report Generated Successfully!"), {
                   	type: "success",
               	});
           	} catch (error) {
               	console.error("Smart Command Error:", error);
           	}
       	},
   	}];
   },
});

This code registers a custom command inside the Command Palette.

Step 4: Using the Command

  1. Open Odoo.
  2. Press: Ctrl + K

Step 5: Search the Command

Type: Report

Select: Generate Monthly Developer Report.

Step 6: Execute the Command

Click on the Generate Monthly Developer Report. Odoo will open a product report where the Quantity Available ≥ 0.

 When the command is executed:

  •     The product list view opens.
  •     Only products with available quantities greater than or equal to 0 are displayed.
  •     A success notification appears on the screen.

This approach allows developers to create quick tools that execute backend actions directly from the Command Palette.

Boost Productivity with Smart Commands

Custom commands in the Odoo 18 Command Palette provide a fast and efficient way to execute actions directly from the interface. By combining a simple backend method with a JavaScript command, developers can quickly trigger reports or other operations. This approach improves productivity by reducing the need to navigate through multiple menus.

Start implementing your own custom commands today and turn Odoo into a faster, more efficient system personalised to your business needs.

Title: How to Set Up Make-to-Order (MTO) in Odoo 19
Content:
How to Set Up Make-to-Order (MTO) in Odoo 19

If you’re searching for a smarter way to manage inventory without overstocking or losing sales, then learning how to Set Up Make-to-Order (MTO) in Odoo 19 can completely change the way your business operates.

Holding too much inventory blocks your cash, and holding too little costs you customers. This is exactly where the Odoo 19 MTO setup becomes a powerful solution. Instead of guessing how much stock you need, Odoo allows you to replenish products only when a customer actually places an order.

In this blog, we’ll guide you through how to set up MTO in Odoo 19 in a very simple and practical way. You’ll understand the concept of Make to Order Odoo 19, learn the exact Odoo 19 MTO step-by-step process, and see how to configure MTO in Odoo 19 inventory without confusion.

We will also explore how the Odoo 19 MTO route works, how to combine the Odoo 19 buy route and MTO, and how the system can automatically generate purchase orders using Odoo 19 automatic purchase order from sales order.

By the end of this guide, you won’t just understand the theory, you’ll be confident enough to implement a complete Odoo 19 make-to-order configuration for your business.

What is Make-to-Order (MTO) in Odoo 19?

A Simple Explanation Anyone Can Understand

Make-to-Order (MTO) is an inventory method where you don’t keep products in stock. Instead, you only purchase or manufacture a product after receiving a confirmed customer order.

Think of it like this:

No unnecessary stock. No wasted money.

Why Businesses Love Make to Order Odoo 19

Businesses today want flexibility and efficiency, and that’s exactly what Make to Order Odoo 19 offers.

Here’s why it works so well:

  • You don’t invest money in unsold products
  • You avoid warehouse clutter
  • You only buy what is actually needed
  • You reduce financial risk
  • You automate your operations

For growing businesses, this is not just helpful, it’s essential.

Why You Should Use Odoo 19 MTO Setup

Real Problems MTO Solves

Let’s talk about real-life issues businesses face:

  • “We have too much stock sitting idle.”
  • “We run out of products when demand increases.”
  • “Manual purchasing is time-consuming.”

With the Odoo 19 MTO setup, these problems are minimized because the system responds directly to customer demand.

Automation That Feels Like Magic

Once you properly configure MTO in Odoo 19 inventory, something amazing happens:

  • A sales order is confirmed
  • Odoo instantly creates a purchase order
  • Vendor gets notified
  • The product is delivered

This is the beauty of Odoo 19: automatic purchase order from sales order, no manual follow-ups, no delays.

Step-by-Step Guide: How to Set Up Make-to-Order (MTO) in Odoo 19

Now let’s get into the practical part. Don’t worry, we’ll keep it simple and easy to follow.

Step 1: Activate Required Settings

Go to:

Inventory → Configuration → Settings

Enable:

  • Multi-Step Routes
  • Storage Locations

These settings are required to activate the Odoo 19 MTO route.

Step 2: Enable MTO Route

Navigate to:

Inventory → Configuration → Routes

  • Find Make To Order (MTO)
  • Activate it

This route ensures that products are replenished only when needed, also known as Odoo 19 replenish on order.

Step 3: Configure Product for MTO

Go to:

Inventory → Products → Products

Open your product and:

Under Inventory Tab:

  • Enable Routes
  • Select:
  •  
    • Make To Order (MTO)
    • Buy Route

This combination is very important. It tells Odoo:

“Whenever this product is sold, purchase it from a vendor.”

This is what we call Odoo 19 buy route and MTO.

Step 4: Add Vendor Details

Inside the product form:

  • Go to the Purchase tab
  • Add vendor name
  • Set price and delivery time

Without this step, Odoo 19 automatic purchase order from sales order will not work.

Step 5: Create and Confirm Sales Order

Go to:

Sales → Orders → Create

  • Select customer
  • Add MTO product
  • Confirm the order

Once confirmed, Odoo automatically:

  • Creates procurement
  • Generates a purchase order

That’s the power of Odoo 19 replenish on order in action.

Step 6: Process Purchase Order

Go to:

Purchase → Orders

  • Open the purchase order
  • Confirm it
  • Receive products

After receiving, the system will automatically prepare delivery to the customer; you just need to validate it.

Add approval from the designated person and make it done.

How Odoo 19 MTO Works in Real Life

Let’s make this even easier to understand with a real example.

Scenario:

You run a furniture business.

  • Customer orders a custom sofa
  • You don’t keep it in stock
  • Odoo creates a purchase order
  • The vendor manufactures and sends it
  • You deliver it to the customer

Simple. Efficient. No risk.

Combining Buy Route and MTO for Best Results

Title: How to Copy Chatter from Sale Order to Delivery Order in Odoo 18?
Content:
Copy Chatter from Sale Order to Delivery Order in Odoo18

In any business workflow, communication is everything. Whether it's internal coordination between teams or external interaction with customers, having the right information at the right time can make all the difference.

In Odoo 18, the copy chatter from Sale Order feature serves as a centralized communication hub. It keeps track of messages, emails, log notes, system notifications, and activities related to a specific document. While this functionality is powerful, it comes with a limitation chatter messages created in a Sale Order are not automatically transferred to the corresponding Delivery Order.

This gap can create confusion, especially for warehouse teams who rely on delivery orders to fulfill shipments accurately. Missing context can lead to delays, errors, or unnecessary back-and-forth communication.

In this blog, we’ll walk you through two practical approaches to solve this issue:

  • Copying the entire chatter history
  • Copying only internal log notes

By the end, you’ll be able to choose the approach that best fits your business workflow.

Understanding Copy Chatter from Sale Order in Odoo

Before getting into the solution, let’s briefly understand what chatter includes in Odoo.

Chatter is more than just a messaging tool, it acts as a timeline of all activities related to a record. It includes:

  • Log Notes (Internal Notes):
    These are used for internal communication within teams. They are not visible to customers and often include operational instructions or updates.
  • Emails:
    These represent communication sent to or received from customers directly from the document.
  • System Notifications:
    Automatically generated updates such as status changes, order confirmations, or automated alerts.
  • Activities:
    Tasks, reminders, and follow-ups assigned to users.

While all this information is useful in a Sale Order, not all of it is always relevant for a Delivery Order. That’s why choosing the right approach for copying chatter becomes important.

Case 1: Copy Entire Chatter

In the first approach, we copy all chatter messages from the Sale Order to the Delivery Order without any filtering.

When should you use this?

This method is ideal when:

  • You want complete transparency
  • Your delivery team needs full context, including customer communication

You prefer not to miss any detail, even if it includes extra information

Python Implementation (sale_order.py)

				
					from odoo import models, fields, api
class SaleOrder(models.Model):
   _inherit = 'sale.order'
   def action_chatter_copy(self):
       """
       Copies Chatter messages from the sale order to the first
       non-cancelled delivery order.
       """
       messages_sale = self.env["mail.message"].search(
           ["&", ("res_id", "=", self.id),
            ("model", "=", "sale.order")], order='create_date asc')
       for chat in messages_sale:
           delivery_id = [x.id for x in
                          self.picking_ids.filtered(
                              lambda l: l.state != 'cancel')]
           chat.copy({"model": "stock.picking", "res_id": delivery_id[0]})

How It Works

This method follows a straightforward logic:

  • It fetches all messages from the message model linked to the Sale Order
  • No filters are applied, so it includes:
    • Emails
    • Log notes
    • System-generated messages
  • It then identifies the first valid Delivery Order (excluding cancelled ones)
  • Finally, it copies each message to the Delivery Order

Pros and Cons

Advantages:

  • Complete communication history is preserved
  • No risk of missing important messages
  • Useful for audit trails and customer-related queries

Limitations:

  • Can clutter the Delivery Order with unnecessary information
  • Includes external emails that may not be relevant for warehouse operations

Sale Order Chatter

2️⃣ Copy Chatter Button

3️⃣ Delivery Before Copy

4️⃣ Delivery After Copy

Case 2: Copy Only Log Notes

The second approach focuses only on internal communication, ensuring that the Delivery Order remains clean and relevant.

When should you use this?

This approach is best when:

  • You want only actionable internal notes
  • Your warehouse team does not need customer emails
  • You prefer a clean and focused chat view
				
					def action_chatter_copy(self):
   """
   Copies only Log Notes (internal notes) from Sale Order
   to the first non-cancelled Delivery Order.
   """
   messages_sale = self.env["mail.message"].search([
       ("res_id", "=", self.id),
       ("model", "=", "sale.order"),
       ("message_type", "=", "comment")  # ✅ Only Log Notes
   ], order='create_date asc')
   delivery = self.picking_ids.filtered(lambda l: l.state != 'cancel')[:1]
   if not delivery:
       return
   for chat in messages_sale:
       chat.copy({
           "model": "stock.picking",
           "res_id": delivery.id
       })

📝 Explanation

This approach is similar to the first one but introduces one key difference:

  • It filters messages using:
    message_type = 'comment'

This ensures that only Log Notes (internal notes) are selected. As a result:

  • Emails are excluded
  • System notifications are ignored
  • Only relevant internal communication is transferred

Pros and Cons

Advantages:

  • Keeps the Delivery Order clean and clutter-free
  • Ensures only relevant information is shared
  • Improves efficiency for warehouse teams

Limitations:

  • Customer communication is not included
  • Some context might be lost if notes are not detailed

Adding a “Copy Chatter” Button in a Sale Order

To make this functionality user-friendly, you can add a button directly in the Sale Order form view.

XML Code

sale_order.xml

				
					<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<odoo>
   <record id="view_order_form_inherit_chatter_copy_in_sale" model="ir.ui.view">
       <field name="name">sale.order.form.inherit.copy.chatter.sale</field>
       <field name="model">sale.order</field>
       <field name="inherit_id" ref="sale.view_order_form"/>
       <field name="arch" type="xml">
           <xpath expr="//button[@name='action_draft']" position="after">
               <button name="action_chatter_copy"
                       string="Copy Chatter"
                       type="object"/>
           </xpath>
       </field>
   </record>
</odoo>

Why This Matters

Adding a button simplifies the process by allowing users to copy chatter with a single click. This reduces dependency on technical users and ensures that the feature is easily accessible during daily operations.

Screenshots that show only log notes

The log chatter note is transferred to the corresponding delivery order when the "Copy Chatter" button is clicked

Best Practices for Implementation

To get the most out of this feature, consider the following:

  • Choose the right approach based on your workflow
    Not every business needs full chatter visibility
  • Train your team to use Log Notes effectively
    Clear internal notes improve communication
  • Avoid unnecessary duplication
    Too much information can be as harmful as too little
  • Test before deployment

Title: How Do FIFO and LIFO Removal Strategies Work in Odoo 19 Inventory?
Content:
How FIFO and LIFO Removal Strategies Work in Odoo 19

If you are managing inventory in a growing business, one question always comes up:

“Which product should go out first?”

And, this small decision can affect your costs, profits, and even customer satisfaction. This is exactly where FIFO and LIFO removal strategies work in Odoo 19 and bring structure to your inventory flow.

In Odoo 19 inventory removal strategies, you don’t have to manually decide which product to pick during a delivery. The system follows a rule. You define that rule once, and Odoo applies it automatically every time.

You can choose between:

  • Odoo 19 FIFO removal strategy
  • Odoo 19 LIFO removal strategy

But many businesses still feel confused when it comes to:

  • How FIFO works in Odoo 19
  • How LIFO works in Odoo 19
  • And the real difference in FIFO vs LIFO in Odoo inventory

So, in this guide, I’ll walk you through everything in a practical way so you can actually use it in your system without second-guessing your setup.

Understanding Odoo 19 Inventory Removal Strategies

In Odoo 19 inventory removal strategies, a removal strategy defines: Which product lot or quantity should be picked first when fulfilling an order.

For example, you have 3 batches of the same product in your warehouse:

  • Batch A (received first)
  • Batch B (received second)
  • Batch C (received last)

Now, when an order comes in, Odoo needs to decide:

  • Should it pick from Batch A first or Batch C?

This decision is handled by:

  • FIFO (First In First Out)
  • LIFO (Last In First Out)

What is FIFO in Odoo 19 Inventory?

The Odoo 19 FIFO removal strategy follows a very simple rule: The first product that comes into inventory is the first one to go out. This is the most commonly used method in real-world businesses.

How FIFO Works in Odoo 19

Let’s break it down in a simple example. You receive:

  • 100 units on Jan 1
  • 100 units on Jan 10
  • Now you sell 50 units.

Odoo will pick from the Jan 1 stock first, not the latest one. That’s exactly how FIFO and LIFO removal strategies work in Odoo 19, but FIFO focuses on older stock.

Why FIFO Makes Sense for Most Businesses

FIFO is widely used because it matches how most businesses operate in real life. If your products have any kind of shelf life, like food, cosmetics, or pharmaceuticals, this method helps you avoid losses. Older stock moves first, so nothing stays unused for too long.

It also keeps your warehouse organized. Instead of random picking, there is a clear flow. Your team doesn’t have to guess which stock to use. And when it comes to reporting, FIFO gives you a clearer representation of inventory value because it follows the actual movement of goods.

Odoo 19 LIFO Removal Strategy – How LIFO Works in Odoo 19

Now, let’s talk about the second method: Odoo 19 LIFO removal strategy.

LIFO stands for:

  • Last In, First Out

This means that the most recently received stock is picked first. To understand how LIFO works in Odoo 19, let’s use the same example.

You receive:

  • 100 units on January 1
  • 100 units on January 10
  • Now you sell 50 units.

Odoo will pick stock from January 10. So, instead of clearing old stock first, it prioritizes the newest stock.

When LIFO is Used in Real Situations

LIFO is not as common as FIFO, but it can still be useful depending on your business. If your products do not expire, and your focus is more on cost tracking, LIFO may help. For example, if purchase prices are changing frequently, LIFO reflects more recent costs in your outgoing stock.

Some businesses also use LIFO for specific accounting or reporting preferences. But it’s important to understand one thing clearly:

If you use LIFO without proper planning, older stock may stay in your warehouse longer than expected.

FIFO vs LIFO in Odoo Inventory

Now comes the comparison that most people are looking for: FIFO vs LIFO in Odoo inventory, which one should you choose? Let’s make it super simple:

Stock Flow

  • FIFO → Old stock goes first
  • LIFO → New stock goes first

Best For

  • FIFO → Expiry-based products
  • LIFO → Non-perishable goods

Inventory Accuracy

  • FIFO → More realistic physical flow
  • LIFO → Useful for cost-based decisions

Risk Level

  • FIFO → Low risk (less waste)
  • LIFO → Higher risk (old stock may stay longer)

If your priority is:

  • Stock rotation
  • Avoiding waste
  • Operational clarity

Then FIFO is usually the better choice.

If your priority is:

  • Recent cost tracking
  • Specific financial approach

Then LIFO might work for you.

How to Set FIFO Strategy in Odoo 19

In Odoo, removal strategies are not set on individual products. They are applied at the product category level.

You simply go to the Inventory → Configuration → Product → Categories.

From there, select your category.

Choose FIFO (First In First Out) and click Save.

Once you save it, Odoo starts applying FIFO automatically to all products in that category. There is no need for manual selection during deliveries. The system handles it in the background.

How to Set LIFO Strategy in Odoo 19

If your business requires LIFO, you can also set the LIFO strategy in Odoo 19 using the same process.

Go to product categories, open the category you want, and select:

LIFO (Last In First Out) and click Save. 

After saving, Odoo will follow LIFO rules whenever stock is reserved for orders. Again, everything runs automatically once the rule is defined.

How Odoo 19 Applies Removal Strategies in Real Time

Once you configure either FIFO or LIFO, Odoo takes care of the rest. When a delivery order is created:

  • Odoo checks the available stock
  • Applies the selected removal strategy
  • Reserves the correct quantities

This happens instantly, without any manual effort. That’s how FIFO and LIFO removal strategies work in Odoo 19 in real business operations.

Common Issues Businesses Face with Removal Strategies

Even after setting up FIFO or LIFO, some businesses still face confusion. This usually happens because of small gaps in the setup or process.

One common issue is not organizing product categories properly. If categories are not structured, removal strategies won’t work as expected.

Another issue is the lack of tracking. If your stock is not properly recorded, the system cannot apply rules accurately.

And sometimes, the warehouse team follows a different process than the system, which creates a mismatch between physical stock and system data.

Why Understanding Removal Strategies is Important

Most people think inventory is just about stock in and stock out. But actually, the order in which stock moves matters a lot.

Because it affects:

  • Cost calculation
  • Stock value
  • Expiry management
  • Customer satisfaction

That’s why understanding FIFO vs LIFO in Odoo inventory is not optional; it’s necessary.

Choosing the Right Strategy for Your Business

At this point, the question becomes simple. Which strategy should you use?

If your business deals with products that can expire or become outdated, FIFO is the safer and more practical choice.

If your products do not expire and your focus is more on financial tracking, then LIFO can be considered. The important thing is not just choosing a strategy but applying it consistently.

Make Odoo Work the Way Your Business Needs

Inventory issues don’t always come from a lack of stock. Most of the time, they come from a lack of clarity.

When you don’t know:

  • Which stock is moving
  • Why is it moving
  • And in what order

Things start getting complicated. That’s why understanding how FIFO and LIFO work in Odoo 19 is so important.

Once your removal strategy is set correctly, your system starts behaving in a predictable way. Your team follows a clear process. And your reports begin to make sense. Title: How to Configure BoM and Create Manufacturing Orders in Odoo 19?

If you are planning to create manufacturing orders in Odoo 19, but you feel confused about BoM, routes, or MRP settings, then this guide is exactly for you. Many businesses install Manufacturing in Odoo and then get stuck at one simple point: how to connect everything properly so production runs smoothly.
