Title: How to Add Custom Fields to the Default Export List in Odoo 19
Content:
Add Custom Fields to the Default Export List in Odoo 19

Exporting data is one of the most common tasks performed in Odoo. Whether you're preparing reports, analyzing customer information, sharing records with another department, or migrating data between systems, the Export Wizard makes the process simple and efficient.

However, businesses that use custom fields often encounter a small but repetitive inconvenience. While Odoo allows custom fields to be exported, they are not included in the default Fields to Export list. Instead, users must manually search for each custom field and add it every time they perform an export.

Although this may seem like a minor task, it can become time-consuming for teams that regularly export data. Over time, these repetitive steps can reduce productivity and increase the likelihood that users will forget to include important business information in their exports.

Fortunately, Odoo 19 provides a simple way to make custom fields export-friendly through the default_export_compatible attribute. With a small enhancement, you can also ensure these fields remain selected regardless of whether the Import-Compatible Export option is enabled.

In this article, we'll walk through the complete implementation, explain how to Add Custom Fields to the Default Export List in Odoo 19, explain how the Export Wizard works behind the scenes, and show you how to provide a better export experience for your users.

What You'll Learn

By the end of this guide, you'll know how to:

  • Understand how the Odoo 19 Export Wizard selects fields.
  • Add custom fields to the default export list.
  • Use the default_export_compatible attribute correctly.
  • Understand why read-only fields behave differently during exports.
  • Prepare for a controller customization that keeps custom fields selected across all export modes.

Why This Matters

Every organization customizes Odoo to match its business processes. Customer records may include information not found in the standard Odoo database, such as tax identifiers, customer reference numbers, credit limits, loyalty information, or onboarding dates.

Imagine your sales or finance team exports customer data several times a day. In addition to standard customer details, they need business-specific information such as GST Number, PAN Number, Customer Code, Credit Limit, and Onboarding Date.

Without customization, users must manually search for these fields and add them to the export every single time. While this only takes a few clicks, repeating the same process every day is unnecessary and can lead to inconsistent exports if someone accidentally omits an important field.

Making these fields available by default not only saves time but also creates a smoother and more reliable workflow for everyone using the system.

Default Export Behavior

Before making any changes, it's important to understand how the Export Wizard behaves by default.

To export customer records:

  1. Open the Contacts module.
  2. Select one or more customer records.
  3. Click Action → Export.
  4. The Export Wizard opens.

You'll notice two separate sections:

  • Fields to Export – contains the fields that will be included in the exported file.
  • Available Fields – contains additional fields that can be added manually.

Standard Odoo fields usually appear automatically in the Fields to Export section. However, custom fields are generally listed under Available Fields, which requires users to click the "+" icon before they can be exported.

For businesses that frequently export data, this extra step quickly becomes repetitive.

Business Requirement

Let's consider a practical example.

A company frequently exports customer records for reporting and financial reconciliation. In addition to the standard customer information, they also need the following custom fields:

  • GST Number
  • PAN Number
  • Customer Code
  • Credit Limit
  • Onboarding Date

Since these are custom fields, users currently have to add them manually each time they export.

The goal is simple: whenever the Export Wizard opens, these fields should already appear in the Fields to Export section without requiring any manual action.

Adding Custom Fields Using default_export_compatible

Odoo provides a built-in field attribute that helps developers identify fields that should be available during export operations.

The attribute is:

default_export_compatible=True

When this attribute is added to a field definition, Odoo marks that field as suitable for export. This allows the Export Wizard to recognize it as an export-compatible field whenever it builds the list of available export fields. 

The following example creates multiple custom fields and enables them for default export:

				
					from odoo import fields, models
class ResPartner(models.Model):
   _inherit = 'res.partner'
   user_id = fields.Many2one(default_export_compatible=True)
   gst_number = fields.Char(
       string='GST Number',
       default_export_compatible=True,
   )
   pan_number = fields.Char(
       string='PAN Number',
       default_export_compatible=True,
   )
   customer_code = fields.Char(
       string='Customer Code',
       default_export_compatible=True,readonly=True,
   )
   credit_limit = fields.Float(
       string='Credit Limit',
       digits=(16, 2),
       default_export_compatible=True,
   )
   onboarding_date = fields.Date(
       string='Onboarding Date',
       default_export_compatible=True,
   )

After upgrading your custom module, Odoo recognizes these fields as export-compatible. Instead of being treated like ordinary custom fields, they become eligible to appear in the Export Wizard's default export configuration.

This approach works for different field types, including:

  • Char fields
  • Float fields
  • Date fields
  • Many2one fields
  • Many other standard Odoo field types

Simply adding this attribute is often enough to improve the export experience without writing any additional business logic.

Understanding Read-Only Field Behavior

One of the custom fields in our example is defined as follows:

				
					customer_code = fields.Char(
   string='Customer Code',
   default_export_compatible=True,readonly=True,
)

At first glance, you might expect this field to always appear in the default export list because it has been marked as export-compatible.

However, that's not always the case.

When users enable the Import-Compatible Export option, Odoo prepares an export file that can be imported back into the system later.

Since import-compatible exports are designed to update existing records, Odoo primarily focuses on fields that can be updated during the import process. As a result, read-only fields may not always remain selected by default, even if they have default_export_compatible=True.

This behavior often surprises developers because the field has already been marked as export-compatible.

Some common examples of read-only fields include:

  • Customer Codes
  • Internal Reference Numbers
  • Sequence Numbers
  • Automatically Generated Values

Although these fields are frequently required for reporting and auditing, they are generally not intended to be modified through imports.

Understanding this behavior is important because it explains why simply adding default_export_compatible=True may not always produce the expected result. In the next part of this guide, we'll explore why this happens and implement a small controller customization that ensures these fields remain selected regardless of the export mode.

Limitation of the Standard Behavior

While default_export_compatible=True helps Odoo identify export-friendly fields, the Export Wizard behaves differently depending on the Import-Compatible Export option's state.

Internally, Odoo uses logic similar to:

'default_export': import_compat and field.get('default_export_compatible')

When Import-Compatible Export is disabled, Odoo sets:

default_export = False

As a result, fields marked with default_export_compatible=True may no longer appear in the default export selection.

Users would again need to add those fields manually.

Extending the Export Controller

Rather than modifying Odoo's core files, the recommended approach is to inherit the existing Export Controller and override the get_fields() method.

This allows us to preserve Odoo's default functionality while making a small adjustment to how export-compatible fields are handled

				
					from odoo import http
from odoo.addons.web.controllers.export import Export
class ExportDefaultFields(Export):
   @http.route('/web/export/get_fields', type='jsonrpc', auth='user', readonly=True)
   def get_fields(self, model, domain, prefix='', parent_name='',
                  import_compat=True, parent_field_type=None,
                  parent_field=None, exclude=None):
       result = super().get_fields(
           model=model,
           domain=domain,
           prefix=prefix,
           parent_name=parent_name,
           import_compat=import_compat,
           parent_field_type=parent_field_type,
           parent_field=parent_field,
           exclude=exclude,
       )
       if not import_compat:
           Model = http.request.env[model]
           fields_meta = Model.fields_get(attributes=['default_export_compatible'])
           for field_dict in result:
               # field_dict['id'] is "prefix/field_name" or just "field_name"
               field_name = field_dict['id'].split('/')[-1]
               if fields_meta.get(field_name, {}).get('default_export_compatible'):
                   field_dict['default_export'] = True
       return result

Once this customization is added to your module and the module is upgraded, the Export Wizard continues to respect Odoo's standard behavior while ensuring that export-compatible fields remain selected, even when Import-Compatible Export is disabled. 

How the Customization Works

Although the code is relatively short, each step serves a specific purpose.

First, the method calls Odoo's original get_fields() function using super(). This preserves the default functionality and avoids replacing the existing export logic.

Next, the customization checks whether the export is not running in import-compatible mode.

If that's the case, it retrieves the metadata of all fields using fields_get(). Among the available attributes, we specifically look for default_export_compatible.

The controller then loops through every field returned by the Export Wizard.

For each field, it verifies whether the corresponding model field has been marked with:

default_export_compatible=True

If it has, the customization restores:

field_dict["default_export"] = True

As a result, the field remains selected in the Fields to Export section, regardless of whether the Import-Compatible Export option is enabled or disabled.

The overall flow can be summarized as follows: 

  1. Calls Odoo's original get_fields() method.
  2. Retrieves field metadata using fields_get().
  3. Checks whether the field has default_export_compatible=True.
  4. Restores default_export=True.
  5. Ensures the field appears in the Fields to Export section.
  6. Works in both export modes.

As a result, users no longer need to add these fields when exporting records manually.

Applying the Same Approach to Existing Odoo Fields

The same technique can also be applied to existing Odoo fields.

For example, to automatically include the Salesperson field in customer exports:

				
					class ResPartner(models.Model):
   _inherit = 'res.partner'
user_id = fields.Many2one(default_export_compatible=True)

In this case, we are not creating a new field. We are simply extending an existing Odoo field and modifying its export behavior.

All original field properties such as relation, label, domain, and business logic remain unchanged.

Testing the Implementation

Once the module has been upgraded, it's a good idea to verify that everything works as expected.

Test Case 1: Import-Compatible Export Enabled

  • Open Export Wizard.
  • Enable I want to update data.

Result:

The custom fields, such as GST Number, PAN Number, Customer Code, Credit Limit, and Onboarding Date, are already available in the Fields to Export section and do not require any manual selection. 

Test Case 2: Import-Compatible Export Disabled

  • Open Export Wizard.
  • Disable I want to update data.

Result:

Even though the export is no longer import-compatible, the same custom fields are still selected automatically due to the controller customization.

The user experiences the same export behavior in both modes, creating a more consistent and user-friendly workflow.

Benefits of This Approach

This small customization offers several practical advantages for both developers and end users.

Some of the key benefits include:

  • Eliminates the need to add custom fields to every export manually.
  • Saves time for teams that frequently export data.
  • Ensures consistent export files across different users.
  • Reduces the risk of accidentally omitting important business information.
  • Supports both custom fields and existing Odoo fields.
  • Works with read-only fields that are commonly required for reporting.
  • Preserves Odoo's standard functionality without modifying core files.
  • Makes future maintenance and upgrades easier.

Although the implementation is relatively small, it can significantly improve the daily experience of users who rely on exported data.

Add Custom Fields to the Default Export List in Odoo 19

The default_export_compatible attribute provides a simple and effective way to  Add Custom Fields to the Default Export List in Odoo 19. For many use cases, adding this attribute is enough to improve the export experience by allowing Odoo to recognize custom fields as export-compatible.

However, because the Export Wizard behaves differently depending on the Import-Compatible Export option, relying on this attribute alone may not always produce the expected results. Fields that should be available by default can disappear from the selected export list, requiring users to add them manually once again.

By extending the Export Controller and restoring the default_export property for fields marked with default_export_compatible=True, you can deliver a more consistent and user-friendly export experience. This approach works for custom fields, read-only fields, and even existing Odoo fields, all without modifying Odoo's core code.

For businesses that frequently export customer, sales, accounting, or inventory data, this small enhancement can eliminate repetitive manual steps, improve consistency, and make everyday operations more efficient.

Whether you're building custom Odoo modules for your organization or developing solutions for clients, this practical customization adds real value with minimal code.

Title: How to Create & Configure Stages on the Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline?
Content:
Build a Smarter Support Workflow with the Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline

Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline can make the difference between a support team that resolves tickets quickly and one that constantly struggles with delays. If your agents spend more time finding tickets than solving them, your workflow probably needs a better structure.

The good news? Odoo 19 lets you create custom helpdesk stages that match the way your business works. From organizing incoming tickets to automating updates and tracking progress, the right pipeline keeps your team productive and your customers happy.

In this guide, you'll learn how to:

  • Create custom Odoo 19 helpdesk stages
  • Configure the Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline for different teams
  • Understand Odoo helpdesk ticket stages
  • Improve your Odoo 19 helpdesk workflow
  • Learn the best practices to manage helpdesk stages in Odoo 19
  • Avoid common configuration mistakes

By the end of this article, you'll know how to configure Odoo 19 to create a faster, more organized, and customer-focused support process.

Understanding the Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline

Before configuring anything, it is important to understand what the Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline actually is.

The helpdesk pipeline is a visual workflow in which every customer support ticket moves from one stage to the next until it is fully resolved. Instead of searching through dozens of requests, support agents can immediately identify the current status of every ticket.

Think of the pipeline as a roadmap for customer support. Each ticket follows a predefined journey, allowing both agents and managers to track progress at every step.

For example, a typical workflow may look like this:

  • New
  • Assigned
  • In Progress
  • Waiting for Customer
  • Pending Internal Review
  • Solved
  • Closed

Each business can customize these stages according to its own requirements.

Unlike a fixed workflow, Odoo allows complete flexibility. A software company may require technical review stages, while a maintenance company may require site-visit or spare-part approval stages.

This flexibility makes the Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline suitable for almost every industry.

Why Is the Helpdesk Pipeline Important?

Without proper stages, support teams often experience problems like:

  • Tickets getting lost
  • Duplicate work
  • Delayed responses
  • Poor communication
  • Lack of visibility
  • Low customer satisfaction

A structured pipeline eliminates these issues by ensuring every ticket follows a defined process.

Some of the biggest advantages include:

Better Ticket Organization

Support teams can instantly identify open, pending, or completed tickets.

Improved Collaboration

Different team members know exactly which tickets require their attention.

Faster Resolution

Tickets move systematically instead of remaining idle.

Performance Tracking

Managers can monitor workloads and identify bottlenecks.

Better Customer Experience

Customers receive quicker responses because every ticket has a clear path toward resolution.

Why Proper Helpdesk Stages Matter in Odoo 19

Many businesses underestimate the importance of stage configuration.

Creating too few stages creates confusion, while creating too many makes the workflow unnecessarily complicated.

A well-designed Odoo helpdesk stage configuration should provide enough detail without making the process difficult to manage.

Let's understand why stage configuration is so important.

Better Workflow Visibility

When every ticket moves through clearly defined stages, managers can immediately identify where work is slowing down.

For example:

  • Are most tickets waiting for customer replies?
  • Is technical approval taking too long?
  • Are tickets staying in "In Progress" for several days?

These insights help improve operational efficiency.

Accurate Team Performance

Support managers can evaluate how quickly agents move tickets through the pipeline.

Instead of measuring only completed tickets, they can also analyze:

  • Average response time
  • Average resolution time
  • Ticket backlog
  • Team productivity

This data helps improve both individual and team performance.

Easier Ticket Prioritization

Not every support request has the same urgency.

Proper stages help agents identify:

  • High-priority issues
  • Tickets waiting for customers
  • Internal escalations
  • Completed requests

This reduces confusion during busy periods.

Automation Opportunities

One of the biggest benefits of configuring the helpdesk pipeline in Odoo 19 is automation.

Once stages are properly configured, Odoo can automate many repetitive tasks.

For example:

  • Send emails when tickets enter specific stages.
  • Assign tickets automatically.
  • Schedule activities.
  • Trigger reminders.
  • Notify managers.
  • Close inactive tickets.

Automation reduces manual work and helps maintain consistency.

How to Create Helpdesk Stages in Odoo 19

One of the strongest features of the Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline is its flexibility. Every business has a different customer support process, and Odoo lets you create stages that reflect your unique workflow rather than forcing you into a predefined structure.

Whether your team handles technical support, customer service, maintenance requests, or internal IT issues, you can easily create helpdesk stages in Odoo 19 that match your daily operations.

Step 1: Open the Helpdesk Module

Begin by logging into your Odoo 19 database with the necessary access rights.

Navigate to:

Helpdesk → 

Overview → Select a ticket from the card.

This section displays all the existing stages available in your helpdesk system.

If you're setting up the module for the first time, you'll likely see default stages such as:

  • New
  • In Progress
  • Solved

These can be edited, removed, or expanded based on your workflow.

Step 2: Create a New Stage

Click the New or Create button.

A form will appear where you can define the details of your new stage.

Or click the small settings icon over the stage, then click Edit, you will find a form.

Typically, you'll configure:

  • Stage Name
  • Applicable Helpdesk Team
  • Folded in Kanban View
  • Description
  • Sequence Order

Choose names that are easy for your support agents to understand.

Examples include:

  • Ticket Received
  • Initial Review
  • Assigned
  • Waiting for Customer
  • Waiting for Vendor
  • Testing
  • Ready for Closure
  • Closed

Simple stage names reduce confusion and improve consistency across teams.

You can also easily move the stage.

Step 3: Define the Stage Order

The sequence determines how tickets appear in the Kanban pipeline.

Arrange stages in the same order your support team normally follows.

For example:

  1. New
  2. Assigned
  3. Investigation
  4. In Progress
  5. Waiting for Customer
  6. Customer Replied
  7. QA Review
  8. Solved
  9. Closed

A logical sequence ensures that tickets move naturally from creation to completion.

Step 4: Assign Stages to Specific Teams

Not every support team needs identical workflows.

For instance:

Technical Support Team

  • Bug Investigation
  • Development
  • Testing

Customer Service Team

  • Complaint Received
  • Customer Verification
  • Resolution

Maintenance Team

  • Site Visit
  • Parts Ordered
  • Repair Completed

By assigning stages to individual teams, you keep each pipeline clean and relevant.

Step 5: Save the Configuration

After reviewing the settings, click Save.

Your newly created stage immediately becomes available in the Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline, allowing agents to move tickets through the updated workflow with ease.

How to Configure the Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline

After you create helpdesk stages in Odoo 19, the next step is to configure the pipeline to support your team's daily operations. A well-configured pipeline does much more than display tickets, it helps agents work efficiently, reduces delays, and keeps everyone informed about the status of every support request.

The Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline is highly flexible, allowing businesses to customize workflows based on their service processes. Whether you have one support team or multiple departments handling different types of tickets, proper configuration ensures that every ticket follows a structured path from creation to closure.

Organize Stages in a Logical Flow

A good pipeline should represent the natural journey of a support ticket.

For example:

  • New
  • Assigned
  • In Progress
  • Waiting for Customer
  • Waiting for Third Party
  • Under Review
  • Solved
  • Closed

When stages are arranged logically, support agents know exactly what action is required at every step.

Configure Stage Sequences

The sequence number assigned to each stage determines its position in the Kanban view.

Place frequently used stages in the correct order to make ticket movement smooth and intuitive.

For example:

Stage

Sequence

New

1

Assigned

2

In Progress

3

Waiting for Customer

4

Review

5

Solved

6

Closed

7

 

A properly ordered pipeline prevents confusion and helps agents update ticket statuses quickly.

Fold Completed Stages

Odoo allows you to fold completed stages such as Solved or Closed.

Folded stages remain accessible but take up less space on the Kanban board, making it easier for agents to focus on active tickets instead of completed ones.

This simple configuration keeps the workspace clean and organized.

Use Stage Descriptions

Each stage can include an internal description explaining when to use it.

For example:

Waiting for Customer

"Move tickets here when additional information is required from the customer."

These descriptions are especially useful for onboarding new support agents and maintaining consistency across teams.

Assign Stages to Helpdesk Teams

Different teams often follow different workflows.

For example:

IT Support

  • Investigation
  • Development
  • Testing
  • Deployment

Customer Service

  • Verification
  • Customer Follow-up
  • Resolved

Maintenance

  • Inspection
  • Parts Ordered
  • Repair in Progress
  • Completed

Assigning stages to specific teams keeps each pipeline relevant and prevents unnecessary stages from appearing where they are not needed.

Improve Your Odoo 19 Helpdesk Workflow with Automation

One of the biggest strengths of the Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline is its ability to automate repetitive tasks. Instead of relying on manual updates, businesses can configure automated actions that save time and reduce human error.

Automation allows support agents to focus on solving customer issues rather than performing routine administrative tasks.

Automatically Assign Tickets

Incoming tickets can be assigned automatically based on predefined rules such as:

  • Helpdesk team
  • Customer category
  • Product
  • Ticket type
  • Priority level

This ensures that tickets reach the right person without delay.

Send Email Notifications

Customers appreciate being informed about the progress of their requests.

You can configure automatic emails when tickets:

  • Are created
  • Change stages
  • Are assigned to an agent
  • Are resolved
  • Are closed

These notifications improve transparency and build customer trust.

Schedule Activities

Certain stages may require follow-up actions.

For example:

  • Contact the customer within 24 hours.
  • Schedule a technical inspection.
  • Request approval from a manager.
  • Follow up after issue resolution.

Odoo can automatically create these activities when a ticket enters a specific stage.

Trigger Internal Alerts

Managers can receive notifications whenever:

  • High-priority tickets remain unresolved.
  • SLA deadlines are approaching.
  • Tickets stay too long in one stage.
  • Critical customers submit new requests.

This helps prevent delays before they affect customer satisfaction.

Reduce Manual Errors

Automation minimizes mistakes such as:

  • Forgotten follow-ups
  • Incorrect ticket assignments
  • Missed deadlines
  • Inconsistent workflows

As a result, the entire Odoo 19 helpdesk workflow becomes more reliable and efficient.

Best Practices to Manage Helpdesk Stages in Odoo 19

Simply creating stages is not enough. To get the most value from the Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline, businesses should follow proven best practices that keep workflows simple, efficient, and easy to manage.

Keep Stage Names Simple

Avoid overly technical or confusing stage names.

Instead of:

  • Technical Escalation Level 2 Pending Internal Assessment

Use:

  • Technical Review

Simple names improve understanding across the team.

Avoid Creating Too Many Stages

More stages do not always mean better organization.

An overly complex pipeline can confuse support agents and slow down ticket management.

Most businesses perform well with around 6–10 clearly defined stages.

Review Stages Regularly

Business processes evolve.

Review your Odoo helpdesk stage configuration every few months to identify:

  • Unused stages
  • Duplicate stages
  • Bottlenecks
  • Opportunities for automation

Regular reviews keep the workflow efficient.

Train Your Support Team

Even the best pipeline is ineffective if employees use it incorrectly.

Ensure every support agent understands:

  • When to move tickets
  • Which stage to select
  • How automation works
  • Why accurate ticket updates matter

Proper training improves reporting accuracy and customer service.

Monitor Pipeline Performance

Use Odoo's reporting tools to analyze:

  • Average ticket resolution time
  • Number of tickets per stage
  • Agent productivity
  • Customer satisfaction
  • SLA compliance

These insights help managers continuously improve support operations.

Setting up the Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline is about more than creating stages. To get the best results, your helpdesk should align with your business processes, automate repetitive tasks, and provide complete visibility into customer support operations.

Build an Efficient Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline That Delivers Better Support

A well-organized Odoo 19 Helpdesk Pipeline is the foundation of excellent customer service. By creating meaningful stages, configuring a logical workflow, and automating repetitive tasks, businesses can manage support requests more efficiently and respond to customers faster.

The flexibility of Odoo 19 allows organizations to tailor helpdesk stages to their unique processes, whether they're handling technical support, customer service, maintenance requests, or internal IT operations. Title: How to Create a Custom Static Snippet in Odoo 18 Website
Content:
Odoo 18 Website Builder

The Odoo 18 Website Builder makes it simple to design professional websites using an intuitive drag-and-drop interface. With its collection of built-in snippets, users can quickly add banners, text blocks, images, buttons, forms, and other website elements without writing code. However, there are many situations where the default snippets are not enough to meet specific business requirements.

For example, you may want to display a custom promotional banner, a company introduction section, service highlights, product features, or a branded call-to-action that matches your organization's design. Instead of recreating these sections every time you build a new page, Odoo allows developers to create custom static snippets that can be reused anywhere on the website.

A static snippet contains fixed content that does not rely on database records or dynamic data. Once it has been registered in the Website Builder, website administrators can simply drag and drop it onto any page, making website management faster, more consistent, and easier to maintain.

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to create a custom static snippet in Odoo 18, register it in the Website Builder, and make it available for drag-and-drop use. Along the way, we'll also explain the purpose of each XML element, so you understand not just what to do, but why it works.

Why Create a Custom Static Snippet?

Many businesses display the same type of information across multiple pages of their website. These sections often include:

  • Company highlights
  • Service descriptions
  • Promotional banners
  • Customer testimonials
  • Contact information
  • Product features
  • Call-to-action sections

Recreating these sections manually for every page can be repetitive and time-consuming. It also increases the chances of inconsistent formatting or outdated content.

By creating a reusable Odoo 18 custom snippet, you only need to design the section once. After registering it in the Website Builder, content editors can simply drag and drop it wherever it's needed, ensuring a consistent design while saving valuable development time.

This approach is particularly useful for businesses that frequently update their website or publish new landing pages, as it allows non-technical users to build pages without modifying code.

Business Use Case

Businesses often need to display the same information across multiple website pages, such as:

  •       Company highlights
  •       Service descriptions
  •       Promotional banners
  •       Customer testimonials
  •       Contact information sections
  •       Product feature showcases

Instead of recreating the same content repeatedly, a custom snippet can be created once and reused across different pages. This improves consistency, reduces maintenance effort, and enables website administrators to build pages quickly using the drag-and-drop editor.

Step 1: Create the Snippet Template

Create a template that contains the HTML structure of the snippet.

File: basic_snippet_template.xml

				
					<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<odoo>
   <template id="basic_snippet_template" name="Basic Snippet">
   	<section>
                   	<h2>Basic Snippet</h2>
                   	<p>
                       	This is a simple static snippet created in Odoo 18.
                       	You can use it to display fixed content on your website.
                   	</p>
   	</section>
   </template>
</odoo>

Explanation

The snippet template defines the structure and content that will be displayed on the website. In this example, a section containing a heading and description is created using Bootstrap classes for responsive design.

Step 2: Register the Snippet in Website Builder

Now that the snippet template has been created, the next step is to register it with the Odoo 18 Website Builder. Without this step, Odoo knows the template exists, but it will not appear in the Website Editor for users to drag and drop onto a page.

Snippet registration connects your XML template with the Website Builder interface. Once registered, the snippet becomes available alongside Odoo's built-in snippets, making it easy for website administrators and content editors to use it without writing any code.

Create the following file: .

File: snippet_registry.xml

				
					<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<odoo>
   <template id="category_highlight_snippet" inherit_id="website.snippets" name="Category Highlight Snippet">
   	<xpath expr="//snippets[@id='snippet_groups']/*[1]" position="before">
       	<t snippet-group="basic_snippet"
          	t-snippet="website.s_snippet_group"
          	string="Basic Snippet"
          	t-thumbnail="/website/static/src/img/snippets_thumbs/s_text_image.svg"/>
   	</xpath>
   	<xpath expr="//snippets[@id='snippet_structure']/*[1]" position="before">
       	<t t-snippet="website_basic_snippet.basic_snippet_template"
          	string="Basic Snippet"
          	group="basic_snippet"/>
   	</xpath>
   </template>
</odoo>

Explanation

A new snippet group named Basic Snippet is created and the custom snippet template is registered under that group. Once registered, the snippet becomes available in the Website Builder sidebar.

Manifest Configuration

To load the custom snippet into Odoo, the module manifest file must include the required dependencies and XML files.

File: __manifest__.py

				
					{
   'name': 'Website Basic Snippet',
   'version': '18.0.1.0.0',
   'category': 'Website',
   'summary': 'Adds a static custom snippet to the website builder',
   'depends': ['website'],
   'data': [
   	'views/basic_snippet_template.xml',
   	'views/snippet_registration.xml',
   ],
   'installable': True,
   'auto_install': False,
   'license': 'LGPL-3',
}

Why Is the Manifest Important?

The manifest serves as the entry point for your module. It contains information such as the module name, dependencies, and the XML files that Odoo should load.

In this example:

  • The website module is listed as a dependency because snippet functionality belongs to the Website application.
  • Both XML files are included in the data section so Odoo can load the template and register it with the Website Builder.
  • Without these entries, your custom snippet will not appear in the Website Editor.

Step 3: Upgrade the Module

After creating the XML files and updating the manifest, you must load the changes into Odoo.

Follow these steps:

  1. Restart the Odoo server.
  2. Upgrade your custom module.
  3. Open the Website application.
  4. Open any website page.
  5. Click Edit to launch the Website Builder.

During the upgrade process, Odoo reads the XML files, creates the template, and registers the snippet so it becomes available in the editor.

Step 4: Verify the Snippet

Once the module has been upgraded successfully, it's time to test the implementation.

Open the Website Builder and check the snippets panel. You should now see a new category named Basic Snippet.

Select the category and drag the snippet onto any page.

If everything has been configured correctly:

  • The snippet will appear on the page.
  • The heading and paragraph will be displayed.
  • The Bootstrap layout will remain responsive across different screen sizes.
  • The snippet can be reused on any website page without creating it again.

This confirms that your custom static snippet has been successfully integrated into the Website Builder.

Best Practices for Creating Custom Snippets

As your website grows, following a few best practices will make your snippets easier to maintain and reuse.

  • Use meaningful template IDs and CSS class names to keep your code organized.
  • Follow Bootstrap's grid system to ensure responsive layouts.
  • Keep each snippet focused on a single purpose instead of combining multiple unrelated sections.
  • Store custom CSS and JavaScript in separate asset files instead of embedding styles directly into the XML template.
  • Group related snippets under custom categories to keep the Website Builder organized.
  • Use descriptive names so content editors can easily identify the correct snippet.

Following these practices improves maintainability and makes future enhancements much easier.

Instead of recreating the same sections across multiple pages, you can build a reusable component once and make it available through Odoo's intuitive drag-and-drop interface.

In this tutorial, we created a custom XML template, registered it in the Website Builder, configured the module manifest, upgraded the module, and verified that the snippet appeared correctly in the editor. Why Suggested Quantities Matter in Purchase Orders in Odoo

Purchase Orders in Odoo are designed to make purchasing faster, smarter, and more accurate. This saves time while reducing the chances of ordering too much or too little.

Ordering excess stock ties up cash and warehouse space, while ordering too little can result in delayed deliveries and unhappy customers. This is where Odoo purchase order suggestions become valuable. They help purchasing teams make informed decisions without spending hours analyzing stock reports.

What Are Suggested Quantities in Purchase Orders in Odoo?

Suggested quantities are recommendations generated by Odoo to help buyers determine how much inventory to purchase. Rather than entering numbers manually, the system analyzes inventory-related information and suggests appropriate purchase quantities.

The recommendations are not random. Odoo evaluates several business factors before making suggestions, including:

  • Current stock available
  • Forecasted inventory
  • Product demand
  • Purchase rules
  • Vendor information
  • Replenishment settings

These recommendations simplify purchasing decisions while helping businesses maintain healthy stock levels.

Instead of spending valuable time calculating inventory requirements, purchasing managers can simply review the suggested quantity and confirm or adjust it before sending the purchase order.

How Do Suggested Quantities Work in Odoo?

Understanding how suggested quantities work in Odoo is easier than many businesses think. Odoo gathers inventory information from multiple areas of the ERP and converts it into purchasing recommendations.

Current Stock Availability

The system first checks the available inventory for each product.

If enough stock already exists, Odoo may recommend purchasing nothing.

If inventory is running low, suggested quantities are automatically calculated.

Go to the Purchase Module, then click “New,” select the vendor, and click the cataloguing option.

Then turn on the suggestion options.

Forecasted Demand

Odoo doesn't only look at today's inventory.

It also considers expected outgoing quantities from:

  • Sales Orders
  • Manufacturing Orders
  • Delivery Orders
  • Reservations

This helps businesses prepare before inventory shortages happen. Replenishment Rules

Replenishment rules define when products should be reordered.

Businesses can configure:

  • Minimum stock levels
  • Maximum stock levels
  • Order multiples
  • Lead times

Once inventory falls below the minimum level, Odoo replenishment suggestions automatically recommend purchasing additional stock.

Historical Purchasing Data

One of the most useful features is Odoo historical demand purchase analysis.

The system reviews previous purchasing and sales activity to understand buying trends.

For example:

  • Seasonal products
  • Frequently purchased items
  • Fast-moving inventory

Historical demand helps businesses avoid shortages during busy periods.

When products are selected, Odoo can automatically display recommended quantities based on replenishment calculations.

  3. Send the RFQ to vendors.

This minimizes manual calculations and speeds up procurement.

Companies purchasing hundreds of products every week benefit greatly from this automation.

Using the Odoo purchase catalog to suggest quantities, buyers can quickly view products that require replenishment while placing orders.

Instead of searching product by product, the catalog displays recommended quantities alongside inventory information.

This provides several advantages:

  • Faster purchasing
  • Better purchasing decisions
  • Reduced ordering mistakes
  • Improved vendor communication

Buyers can simply review recommendations and confirm purchases within minutes.

Businesses avoid running out of popular products because replenishment recommendations are generated before shortages occur.

Lower Inventory Costs

Ordering only what is needed reduces unnecessary inventory carrying costs.

Companies save money on:

Faster Purchasing Process

Buyers spend more time approving purchases instead of analyzing spreadsheets.

Suggested quantities depend on accurate stock information.

Always ensure:

  • Inventory adjustments are completed.

  • Receipts are processed promptly.

Minimum and maximum stock levels should reflect actual business demand.

Review them regularly, especially during seasonal changes.

Monitor Historical Demand

Businesses should periodically analyze previous purchasing trends.

This allows Odoo's recommendations to match customer buying behavior better.

Review Suggestions Before Confirmation

Suggested quantities are intelligent recommendations, not mandatory values.

Purchasing managers should always review recommendations before approving purchase orders.

Employees should understand:

  • When adjustments are necessary
  • How replenishment settings affect recommendations

Proper training leads to better purchasing decisions.

Title: How Does Cross-Docking Work in Odoo 19 Inventory?
Content:
Introduction – What If Your Warehouse Never Had to Store Products?

Imagine paying for a huge warehouse... but the products inside barely stay there.

Sounds impossible?

Most businesses believe inventory must sit on shelves for days, or even weeks, before it's shipped. But what if your products could arrive in the morning and leave for customers just minutes later? No endless stacking. No unnecessary storage. No wasted warehouse space.

That's exactly what cross-docking makes possible.

Think about it: every extra hour a product spends sitting in storage costs money. More handling means more labor. More storage means higher expenses. More delays mean unhappy customers. So why let products collect dust when they could already be on their way to buyers?

This is where the cross docking process changes everything.

If you've ever searched for what is cross docking, you're about to discover why some of the world's fastest supply chains rely on it. Instead of moving products through multiple warehouse stages, cross docking inventory allows goods to flow almost directly from incoming trucks to outgoing deliveries.

The best part? You don't need complicated systems or manual coordination anymore. With Odoo inventory, businesses can automate the entire workflow. The latest Odoo 19 inventory features make it easier than ever to build a smart cross docking warehouse, reduce handling, and speed up deliveries without increasing operational costs.

So, how does warehouse cross docking actually work inside Odoo? How does inventory cross docking reduce storage costs while improving delivery speed? And is it the right strategy for your business?

Let's open the warehouse doors and find out. The answer might completely change the way you think about inventory management.

What Is Cross Docking and Why Does It Matter?

Many businesses keep inventory in storage until customer orders arrive. While this works for some industries, it also increases warehouse expenses, inventory holding costs, and handling time.

The answer to what is cross docking is much simpler than traditional warehousing. Products arrive from suppliers and are immediately sorted, packed if necessary, and loaded onto outbound vehicles for delivery.

Instead of following this process:

Supplier → Warehouse Storage → Picking → Packing → Shipping

Cross-docking follows this path:

Supplier → Receiving Dock → Sorting → Shipping Dock → Customer

This shorter workflow offers several advantages:

  • Faster order fulfillment
  • Lower warehouse storage costs
  • Reduced inventory handling
  • Better warehouse space utilization
  • Lower risk of product damage
  • Improved customer satisfaction

Businesses dealing with fast-moving products especially benefit from a well-organized cross docking warehouse.

How Does Cross-Docking Work in Odoo 19 Inventory?

Odoo 19 inventory includes advanced warehouse routing capabilities that make cross-docking easy to manage. Instead of manually deciding where products should go after receiving them, Odoo automatically follows predefined warehouse routes.

Here's how the process works.

Enable multi-step routes from settings

For this go to inventory module and then configuration:

Step 1 – Enable Cross-Docking for Your Warehouse

Before you can use cross-docking, you need to enable it in your warehouse settings.

Go to Inventory → Configuration → Warehouses

And open the warehouse where you want to use cross-docking. Under the warehouse configuration, enable the Cross-Dock route (or select the appropriate reception and delivery flow that supports cross-docking). Save your changes.

Once enabled, Odoo automatically creates the necessary routes and operation types required for cross-docking.

Step 2 – Create a Sales Order and Purchase Order

Cross-docking works when there is customer demand for a product that is not currently available in stock.

First, create and confirm a Sales Order for the customer. 

Since the product is unavailable, Odoo reserves the demand but waits for incoming stock.

For the product also add a vendor.

Also check the dropship option under inventory.

Next, create and confirm a Purchase Order for the same product. Odoo now understands that the incoming products are already needed for an existing customer order.

Step 3 – Validate the Incoming Receipt

After confirming the Purchase Order, Odoo generates an incoming Receipt.

Navigate to Inventory → Operations → Receipts, 

Open the receipt, verify the received quantities, and click Validate.

Instead of moving the products into the warehouse storage location, Odoo recognizes the cross-docking route and prepares the next stock movement automatically.

Step 4 – Process the Internal Transfer

Once the receipt is validated, Odoo automatically creates an Internal Transfer to move the products from the receiving dock to the Output or Shipping area.

Go to Inventory → Operations → Internal Transfers, open the generated transfer, review the quantities, and validate it.

This step is the heart of the cross docking process, allowing products to bypass storage and move directly toward shipment.

Step 5 – Validate the Delivery Order

After the internal transfer is completed, Odoo automatically prepares the Delivery Order linked to the customer's Sales Order.

Navigate to Inventory → Operations → Delivery Orders, 

Open the delivery, verify the product quantities, and click Validate.

The products are shipped to the customer, inventory levels are updated automatically, and complete traceability is maintained. By following this workflow, Odoo 19 Inventory helps businesses automate inventory cross docking, reduce warehouse handling, minimize storage costs, and deliver orders much faster.

Benefits of Cross-Docking in Odoo 19 Inventory

Implementing cross-docking inside Odoo offers both financial and operational advantages.

Lower Inventory Costs

Products spend less time sitting in storage.

Businesses reduce warehouse rental expenses, storage equipment costs, and inventory carrying costs.

Faster Deliveries

Customer orders are processed immediately after products arrive.

This helps companies meet growing customer expectations for same-day or next-day shipping.

Better Warehouse Space

A traditional warehouse requires large storage areas.

A cross docking warehouse needs far less storage space because inventory keeps moving instead of remaining on shelves.

Improved Inventory Accuracy

Because products move directly through the warehouse, there are fewer stock movements.

Fewer movements mean fewer opportunities for inventory mistakes.

Reduced Product Damage

Every time products are moved, there's a chance they may be damaged.

The cross docking process reduces handling, keeping products safer.

Increased Employee Productivity

Warehouse employees spend less time storing and retrieving products.

Instead, they focus on receiving and shipping activities that generate value.

Which Businesses Should Use Inventory Cross Docking?

Not every company requires cross-docking, but many industries benefit greatly from it.

Retail Distribution

Retailers often receive products that are already assigned to store orders.

Using inventory cross docking speeds up deliveries to multiple branches.

eCommerce Companies

Online businesses handling hundreds of daily orders can reduce delivery times while minimizing warehouse storage.

Food and Beverage

Fresh products have limited shelf life.

Cross-docking ensures products reach customers quickly.

Manufacturing

Manufacturers often receive raw materials needed immediately for production.

Cross-docking keeps production moving without unnecessary storage.

Wholesale Distribution

Wholesalers handling large quantities can move products directly to customers without filling warehouse shelves.

Best Practices for Successful Warehouse Cross Docking

Although Odoo automates much of the workflow, businesses should still follow best practices.

Configure Warehouse Routes Correctly

Proper routing rules are the foundation of successful warehouse cross docking.

Incorrect configurations may send products to storage instead of shipping.

Keep Real-Time Inventory Updated

Employees should validate receipts and deliveries immediately.

Real-time inventory keeps stock information accurate.

Train Warehouse Staff

Employees should understand the workflow and know which products are processed through cross-docking.

Forecast Demand

Cross-docking works best when customer demand is predictable.

Accurate sales forecasting helps businesses prepare incoming shipments.

Monitor Performance

Use Odoo reporting tools to measure:

  • Delivery speed
  • Warehouse efficiency
  • Inventory turnover
  • Order accuracy
  • Receiving performance

Regular analysis helps improve warehouse operations over time.

Title: How Do Invoice QR Codes Speed Up Payments in Odoo 19 Accounting?
Content:
Waiting for Customer Payments? There’s a Better Way

You’ve finished the project, delivered the product, and sent the invoice. Everything is done, except getting paid.

A few days pass. Then a week. You send a friendly reminder, but the payment still doesn’t arrive. Sound familiar?

For many businesses, delayed payments aren’t always because customers don’t want to pay. Sometimes the payment process itself creates unnecessary friction. Customers have to open their banking app, type long account numbers, enter the payment amount, copy the invoice reference, and double-check every detail before they can finally click "Pay." Even a small typing mistake can delay the transaction or send money to the wrong account.

This is where Invoice QR Codes make a real difference.

With Odoo 19 accounting, every invoice can include a QR code that contains all the payment information your customer needs. Instead of entering everything manually, they simply scan the code with their banking app, confirm the details, and complete the payment in seconds.

It sounds like a small feature, but it has a big impact. Businesses using QR code payments often spend less time chasing unpaid invoices and more time focusing on work that actually grows their business.

As companies continue moving toward digital invoice payment methods, features like the Odoo invoice QR code are becoming an important part of everyday accounting. They improve customer experience, reduce payment errors, support automated invoice payments, and contribute to the better accounting automation Odoo is known for.

If your goal is faster invoice payments, this is one feature you shouldn't overlook.

What Exactly Are Invoice QR Codes?

Think about the last time you paid a utility bill or transferred money using your banking app. There's a good chance you scanned a QR code instead of typing every payment detail yourself.

The same idea now applies to business invoices.

An Invoice QR Code is a small, scannable code printed directly on an invoice. It securely stores important payment details such as:

  • The amount due
  • Your company's bank account information
  • Payment reference
  • Invoice number
  • Currency

When customers scan the code, all of these details are automatically filled into their banking application. They simply review the information and approve the payment.

No copying.

No typing.

No worrying about entering the wrong account number.

This simple process makes QR code payments much more convenient than traditional bank transfers.

For businesses, it's equally valuable. Instead of answering customer questions about payment references or correcting payment mistakes, finance teams receive more accurate payments with much less effort.

How Does Odoo 19 Generate Invoice QR Codes?

One reason businesses enjoy working with Odoo 19 accounting is that many tasks happen automatically.

Invoice QR codes are no exception.

Once your payment information has been configured, Odoo automatically creates a QR code every time you generate a customer invoice. There is no need to visit another website, use a third-party QR code generator, or manually paste images into your invoices.

Everything happens inside Odoo.

When the invoice PDF is created, the QR code appears alongside the payment details, giving customers an easy way to complete their payment.

From the customer's perspective, the process feels incredibly simple.

They receive the invoice.

They open it on their phone or computer.

They scan the QR code using their preferred banking application.

The payment amount, account details, and reference are already filled in.

All that's left is confirming the payment.

What used to take several minutes now takes only a few seconds.

That convenience may seem small, but when you're sending dozens or even hundreds of invoices every month, it can significantly improve the speed at which customers pay.

How to Enable Invoice QR Codes in Odoo 19 Accounting

The good news is that you don't need a separate application to use Invoice QR Codes in Odoo 19 Accounting. Once your payment details are configured correctly, Odoo can automatically generate a QR code on customer invoices.

Here's how it works.

Step 1 – Open the Accounting Module

Log in to your Odoo 19 database and open the Accounting module.

From the dashboard, go to Configuration and then open Settings.

This is where you can manage payment-related options for your accounting system.

Step 2 – Configure Your Bank Account

Before Odoo can create a QR code, you must add your company's bank account.

Go to Configuration → Bank Accounts (or open your company record if your localization stores bank details there).

Make sure your bank account number, account holder name, and other required payment information are correct.

If any information is missing, Odoo won't be able to generate a valid QR code.

Step 3 – Select a Supported Payment Method

Different countries use different QR payment standards.

Odoo supports QR code generation based on your company's localization and payment method.

Choose the supported payment option for your region and save the configuration.

Once this is done, Odoo knows which payment information should be included in the QR code.

Step 4 – Create a Customer Invoice

Now create a new customer invoice as you normally would.

Add:

  • Customer
  • Products or services
  • Quantity
  • Price
  • Taxes
  • Payment terms

There is nothing different about creating the invoice.

The QR code is added automatically when all payment information is available.

Step 5 – Print or Send the Invoice

Validate the invoice and click Print or Send.

You'll notice a QR code on invoice documents near the payment section.

Customers can scan it using their banking or payment application without entering account details manually.

Step 6 – Customer Completes the Payment

When the customer scans the QR code:

  • Payment amount is filled automatically.
  • Bank details appear instantly.
  • Payment reference is already included.
  • The customer simply reviews the information and confirms the payment.

Because everything is pre-filled, payments are usually completed much faster and with fewer mistakes.

⚠️ One Important Note

The exact menu names and QR code options depend on your country's localization. For example, Swiss QR-bills, EPC QR codes (Europe), and other regional standards are available only when the corresponding localization package is installed. If your localization doesn't support invoice QR codes, you may need to enable the appropriate localization or use a compatible payment provider.

Why Customers Prefer QR Code Payments

Businesses often focus on making their own work easier, but successful companies also think about the customer's experience.

Imagine receiving an invoice after a busy workday.

One invoice asks you to manually copy account numbers, payment references, and invoice details before making a transfer.

Another invoice simply says:

"Scan the QR code below to pay instantly."

Most people won't think twice, they'll choose the easier option.

That's exactly why QR code on invoice documents are becoming more common.

Customers appreciate convenience.

The fewer steps involved, the more likely they are to complete payment immediately instead of postponing it.

This doesn't just improve customer satisfaction.

It also leads to faster invoice payments, which means healthier cash flow for your business.

For companies sending recurring invoices every month, even reducing the average payment time by a few days can make a noticeable difference.

More Than Faster Payments - A Smarter Accounting Process

Many people think Invoice QR Codes are only about collecting payments faster.

In reality, they improve your entire accounting workflow.

When payments arrive with the correct information attached, your finance team spends less time matching transactions with invoices. Instead of sorting through bank records and checking references manually, they can focus on reporting, planning, and other important financial tasks.

This is where Odoo 19 Accounting stands out.

Its built-in automation helps businesses reduce repetitive work without making the accounting process more complicated.

As your business grows, you naturally send more invoices every month. Without automation, that also means more manual work.

With the right setup, however, automated invoice payments and QR-enabled invoices help your accounting process grow with your business, not against it.

The result is a finance department that works faster, makes fewer mistakes, and spends more time adding value instead of fixing problems.

Is This Feature Right for Every Business?

Absolutely.

Whether you're a small business sending ten invoices a month or a growing company processing hundreds, Invoice QR Codes can make a noticeable difference.

They're especially useful for businesses such as:

  • Trading companies
  • Retail businesses
  • Manufacturers
  • Service providers
  • Consultants
  • Healthcare organizations
  • Educational institutions
  • Wholesale distributors

If your business sends invoices, you can benefit from making payments simpler.

You don't need to change the way you work, you simply make the final step of the customer journey much easier.

That small improvement often leads to quicker payments, fewer follow-up emails, and happier customers.

Why the Right Odoo Partner Makes All the Difference

Installing Odoo is one thing.

Getting the most out of it is something else entirely.

Many businesses use only a fraction of what Odoo 19 Accounting can actually do because their system wasn't configured properly from the beginning.

A trusted Odoo implementation partner can help you:

  • Configure secure payment methods
  • Enable Invoice QR Codes correctly
  • Customize invoice layouts to match your brand
  • Set up automated invoice payments
  • Connect accounting with sales and banking modules
  • Train your team to use the system effectively

At Netilligence, we don't just implement Odoo, we help businesses build accounting systems that save time, reduce manual work, and improve the overall customer experience.

Our goal is to ensure every feature, including Invoice QR Codes, works the way your business needs it to.

When technology is implemented properly, your team spends less time solving accounting issues and more time growing the business.

Make Every Invoice Easier to Pay

Getting paid shouldn't be the hardest part of doing business.

You can deliver great products, provide excellent service, and build strong customer relationships, but if the payment process is slow or complicated, your cash flow will still suffer.

That's why Invoice QR Codes are more than just a modern feature in Odoo 19 Accounting. They remove unnecessary steps, reduce payment errors, and make life easier for both businesses and customers.

Instead of asking customers to manually enter payment details, you give them a faster, simpler way to complete the transaction with a single scan.

It's a small change that creates a better experience, encourages faster invoice payments, and supports a more efficient accounting process.

If you're planning to upgrade your accounting system or want to make better use of Odoo 19 Accounting, now is the perfect time to explore what Invoice QR Codes can do for your business.

At Netilligence, we help businesses implement Odoo solutions that don't just work, they work smarter. From setup and customization to automation and ongoing support, our team ensures your accounting system is built to save time, improve accuracy, and help you get paid faster.

Because when getting paid becomes easier, growing your business becomes easier too.

Title: How to Create a Petty Cash Account in Odoo 19 Accounting?
Content:
Introduction: Why You Need to Create a Petty Cash Account in Odoo 19

If you want better control over daily expenses, the first step is to create a petty cash account in Odoo 19. Small business expenses like office supplies, tea, travel reimbursements, or minor repairs can quickly become unorganised without a proper system. That’s where petty cash management in Odoo 19 becomes essential.

When you create a petty cash account in Odoo 19, you get a structured way to track small cash transactions without mixing them into your main bank accounts. Many businesses struggle because they don’t properly set up Odoo 19 petty cash, which leads to errors during reconciliation.

Using the petty cash journal in Odoo 19, you can easily record and monitor every expense. The petty cash account setup in the Odoo process ensures transparency and control. Whether you're learning how to record petty cash in Odoo or improving your Odoo petty cash workflow, having a proper setup is critical.

With the right approach, petty cash management software Odoo helps reduce manual tracking, improve reporting, and save time. This guide will walk you through everything you need to know to create a petty cash account in Odoo 19 effectively and professionally.

What is Petty Cash in Odoo 19 Accounting?

Before you create a petty cash account in Odoo 19, it’s important to understand what petty cash actually means in an accounting system.

Petty cash refers to a small amount of physical cash kept in the office for minor day-to-day expenses. Instead of issuing bank payments for every small transaction, companies use petty cash for convenience.

In Odoo 19, accounting petty cash is handled through:

  • A dedicated account in the chart of accounts
  • A separate journal (cash-type journal)
  • Controlled entries for expenses

This ensures:

  • Accurate tracking
  • Clear reporting
  • Easy reconciliation

Without a proper petty cash account setup in Odoo, businesses often face:

  • Missing expense records
  • Difficulty in audits
  • Lack of transparency

Key Benefits of Petty Cash Management in Odoo 19

When you properly create a petty cash account in Odoo 19, you unlock several practical advantages.

1. Better Expense Control

Every small expense is recorded systematically using Odoo 19's petty cash, reducing the chances of untracked spending.

2. Organized Financial Records

With a proper petty cash journal in Odoo 19, all entries are centralized and easy to review.

3. Faster Reconciliation

You can easily match physical cash with system records, improving accuracy in Odoo's petty cash workflow.

4. Improved Accountability

Assigning petty cash responsibility ensures transparency and reduces misuse.

5. Automation & Efficiency

Using the petty cash management software Odoo, manual logs are replaced with digital tracking.

Step-by-Step Guide to Create Petty Cash Account in Odoo 19

Now let’s get into the practical part, how to create a petty cash account in Odoo 19.

Step 1: Enable Developer Mode (Optional but Recommended)

  • Go to Settings
  • Activate Developer Mode

This gives you full control during the petty cash account setup in Odoo.

Step 2: Create a Petty Cash Account

  • Go to Accounting → Configuration → Chart of Accounts.
  • Click Create

Fill in the following details:

  • Account Name: Petty Cash
  • Account Type: Current Assets
  • Allow Reconciliation: Enabled

This step is essential to create a petty cash account in Odoo 19 properly.

Step 3: Create Petty Cash Journal in Odoo 19

Next, you need a dedicated journal.

  • Go to Accounting → Configuration → Journals
  • Click Create

While creating a journal for petty cash, select the “Cash” option, as it is specifically designed to record physical cash movements and small day-to-day expenses. 

Enter:

  • Journal Name: Petty Cash
  • Type: Cash
  • Default Account: Select the petty cash account created earlier

This completes the petty cash journal in the Odoo 19 setup.

Step 4: Configure Opening Balance

To start using Odoo 19 petty cash, you need to define the initial cash amount.

  • Go to the Accounting Dashboard
  • Open Petty Cash Journal
  • Add opening balance

Example:

  • Debit: Petty Cash
  • Credit: Cash/Bank

Step 5: Define Expense Accounts

What Are Bank Reconciliation Models in Odoo 19?

Instead of reviewing every transaction one by one, you can create rules that automatically recognize specific transactions and suggest the appropriate accounting treatment.

For example, whenever your bank deducts monthly service charges, Odoo can automatically:

  • Identify the transaction
  • Select the correct expense account
  • Create the journal entry
  • Complete the reconciliation

This significantly speeds up Odoo accounting bank reconciliation while minimizing human errors.

Some common transactions that can be automated include:

  • Bank charges
  • Payment gateway fees
  • Loan installments
  • Interest income
  • Vendor payments
  • Customer receipts
  • Monthly subscriptions
  • Utility payments
  • Currency exchange differences

The more reconciliation models you create, the more intelligent your accounting process becomes.

Why Businesses Should Use Bank Reconciliation Models

Modern businesses process hundreds, or even thousands, of bank transactions every month. Reconciling each one manually consumes valuable time and increases the risk of mistakes.

Using Bank Reconciliation Models provides several advantages.

Save Time

Automation eliminates repetitive manual matching and allows accountants to focus on more strategic financial tasks.

Reduce Human Errors

Manual reconciliation often leads to incorrect account selection or duplicate entries. Reconciliation models minimize these mistakes.

Improve Financial Accuracy

Consistent rules ensure every similar transaction is handled the same way, improving reporting accuracy.

Faster Month-End Closing

When most bank transactions are automatically reconciled, month-end closing becomes much quicker.

Better Audit Trail

Each reconciliation follows predefined rules, making audits easier and ensuring financial transparency

Before learning how to use reconciliation models in Odoo, it's important to understand the overall Odoo 19 bank reconciliation workflow.

The process generally follows these steps:

Step 1: Import Bank Statements

Bank statements can be imported through:

  • CSV files
  • CAMT files
  • OFX files
  • Direct bank synchronization

Once imported, transactions appear in the bank journal.

Step 2: Odoo Analyzes Transactions

Odoo compares each transaction with:

  • Customer invoices
  • Vendor bills
  • Existing payments
  • Previous reconciliation rules

If a matching transaction is found, Odoo suggests reconciliation automatically

Step 3: Reconciliation Models Are Applied

If a transaction matches one of your configured Odoo 19 reconciliation models, Odoo automatically proposes the correct accounting treatment.

Examples include:

  • Monthly bank fees
  • Payment gateway commissions
  • Interest earned
  • Loan repayments

Step 4: Accountant Reviews Suggestions

The accountant only needs to review and confirm the suggested reconciliation.

This dramatically reduces processing time.

How to Create Bank Reconciliation Models in Odoo 19

Now let's look at the complete process of creating Odoo bank reconciliation models.

Navigate to Accounting Settings

Open:

Accounting → Cash → Reconciliation Models

Click New.

Give Your Model a Name

Choose a descriptive name such as:

  • Monthly Bank Charges
  • Stripe Fees
  • PayPal Commission
  • Interest Income
  • Utility Payments

Clear naming helps maintain your accounting system as more models are added.

Choose Matching Conditions

Define when the model should be applied.

Conditions may include:

  • The transaction label contains certain words
  • Transaction amount
  • Partner
  • Payment reference
  • Bank account
  • Journal

For example:

If the label contains:

Service Charge

then apply the model automatically.

Configure Accounting Entries

Specify:

  • Expense Account
  • Revenue Account
  • Taxes (if applicable)
  • Analytic Account
  • Partner
  • Journal

This tells Odoo exactly how the transaction should be recorded.

Enable Automatic Validation

If you're confident with the rule, enable automatic validation.

Odoo will then process matching transactions without manual approval.

This is one of the most powerful features for automatic bank reconciliation Odoo 19.

Practical Examples of Reconciliation Models

Let's explore some real-world examples.

Example 1 – Monthly Bank Charges

Suppose your bank deducts:

$25 every month.

Create a model:

Condition:

Label contains:

Bank Charges

Action:

  • Expense Account → Bank Charges
  • Automatically reconcile

Now every month, Odoo handles this transaction automatically.

Example 2 – Interest Income

If your bank pays monthly interest:

Condition:

Label contains:

Interest

Action:

  • Income Account → Interest Income

No manual journal entry required.

Example 3 – Payment Gateway Fees

Businesses using Stripe or PayPal often receive payments after commission deductions.

Create a model that:

  • Detects Stripe Fee
  • Posts commission expense
  • Reconciles payment automatically

This saves hours every month.

Example 4 – Loan Installments

Loan repayments typically include:

  • Principal
  • Interest

A reconciliation model can automatically allocate each portion to the correct account.

Recurring electricity or internet payments can also be automated.

Once configured, every payment follows the same accounting treatment.

Best Practices for Using Odoo 19 Reconciliation Models

To maximize the benefits of Odoo 19 reconciliation models, follow these recommendations.

Avoid broad rules that might match unrelated transactions.

Instead of:

Contains:

Payment

Use:

Contains:

Stripe Fee

or

Bank Charges

Always test new reconciliation models with sample transactions.

Verify:

  • Correct account selection
  • Tax application
  • Journal entries
  • Partner assignment

Group similar models together.

Examples:

This makes future maintenance easier.

Review Models Regularly

Banks sometimes change transaction descriptions.

Update your rules periodically to maintain accuracy.

The more specific the conditions, the better Odoo identifies the correct transactions.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Even though Bank Reconciliation Models are easy to configure, certain mistakes can create accounting problems.

Using Generic Keywords

A rule like:

Contains:

Payment

may incorrectly match many unrelated transactions.

Always verify the account assigned to each model.

Posting bank charges to the wrong expense account affects financial reports.

Never activate automatic validation without testing.

Run several sample reconciliations first.

Too Many Overlapping Rules

Multiple rules with similar conditions can confuse the reconciliation engine.

Keep rules simple and unique.

Forgetting Updates

As your business grows, review your reconciliation models regularly.
