Title: How Can Odoo ERP Help Businesses Identify Slow-Moving Products?
Content:
Understanding Slow-Moving Products and Their Impact on Your Business

Many businesses struggle with Slow-Moving Products because they do not have a clear picture of what is selling and what is sitting untouched. Without proper inventory visibility, it becomes difficult to identify Slow-Moving Products, understand why they are not selling, or decide what action should be taken.

This is where slow moving inventory management becomes essential. Businesses need accurate data to understand product movement, sales patterns, stock levels, and inventory age. Instead of manually checking spreadsheets and warehouse records, an ERP system can provide this information in one place.

With Odoo, businesses can monitor Slow-Moving Products more effectively by analyzing inventory movement and generating useful reports. Odoo helps managers identify which products have not moved for a specific period and which items are occupying warehouse space without generating revenue.

Proper management of Slow-Moving Products is not simply about removing unwanted stock. It is about understanding customer demand, improving purchasing decisions, reducing unnecessary inventory costs, and maintaining healthier stock levels.

By using the right technology, businesses can turn inventory data into meaningful insights. Odoo ERP gives companies the visibility they need to identify Slow-Moving Products before they become non-moving or obsolete inventory.

Why Slow-Moving Inventory Is a Serious Business Challenge

Inventory is an investment. Every product sitting in a warehouse represents money that has already been spent. When products do not move as expected, businesses face several operational and financial challenges.

Slow Moving Inventory can increase storage costs, reduce available warehouse space, and affect cash flow. Businesses may continue purchasing new products without realizing that older stock is still sitting unused.

Over time, slow-moving stock can become damaged, outdated, expired, or completely obsolete. This is especially important for businesses dealing with food products, electronics, fashion items, seasonal products, and other goods with a limited lifecycle.

Some common reasons behind slow-moving inventory include:

  • Incorrect demand forecasting
  • Changes in customer preferences
  • Overstocking
  • Seasonal demand changes
  • Poor purchasing decisions
  • Ineffective pricing strategies
  • Lack of product visibility
  • Limited sales promotions

The biggest challenge is that many businesses discover the problem too late. By the time managers manually review warehouse records, a product may have already remained in stock for several months.

A reliable slow moving stock report can help businesses identify these products earlier. However, manually creating and updating such reports can be time-consuming and prone to errors.

This is where Odoo ERP provides a practical advantage.

How Odoo ERP Helps Identify Slow-Moving Products

Odoo Inventory provides businesses with real-time visibility into their stock. Instead of relying on disconnected spreadsheets or manual stock checks, businesses can track inventory movements directly within the ERP system.

Every stock transaction can provide useful information about how products are moving through the business.

Real-Time Inventory Visibility

One of the biggest advantages of Odoo is centralized inventory management. Businesses can view stock levels across warehouses and locations from one system.

Managers can analyze:

  • Current stock quantities
  • Product movements
  • Incoming inventory
  • Outgoing deliveries
  • Sales activity
  • Warehouse locations
  • Replenishment requirements

This visibility makes it easier to identify products that have high stock quantities but low sales activity.

For example, a company may have 1,000 units of a product in stock but only sell 20 units per month. Without proper reporting, this issue may remain unnoticed. With Odoo, managers can analyze inventory and sales data together to identify products that are moving slower than expected.

Product Movement Analysis

Odoo records inventory transactions throughout the supply chain. Businesses can track when products enter the warehouse, when they are transferred, and when they leave through sales or deliveries.

This information helps businesses identify slow moving inventory based on actual movement rather than assumptions.

Managers can compare product movement over different periods and identify patterns such as:

  • Products with declining sales
  • Items that have not moved recently
  • Products with excessive stock
  • Seasonal items remaining after the season
  • Inventory with low turnover

By understanding these patterns, businesses can make informed decisions before inventory becomes a bigger problem.

Using Inventory Aging Reports for Better Stock Control

An inventory aging report is one of the most useful tools for understanding how long products have remained in stock.

Instead of only looking at current inventory quantities, inventory aging focuses on the age of stock. This helps businesses understand whether products are newly purchased or have been sitting in the warehouse for an extended period.

For example, inventory can be categorized based on age:

  • Stock available for less than 30 days
  • Stock available for 30 to 60 days
  • Stock available for 60 to 90 days
  • Stock available for more than 90 days

This information gives businesses a clearer picture of inventory health.

How Odoo Inventory Aging Supports Better Decisions

With proper Odoo configuration, customization, and reporting, businesses can use Odoo inventory aging insights to monitor how long products remain in stock.

This is particularly valuable for businesses managing large product catalogs. Instead of manually reviewing hundreds or thousands of products, managers can focus on items that require immediate attention.

An inventory aging analysis can help answer important questions:

  • Which products have been in stock the longest?
  • Which items are not selling as expected?
  • Which products are approaching expiration or obsolescence?
  • Which products should not be reordered?
  • Which products require discounts or promotions?

This level of visibility helps businesses move from reactive inventory management to proactive decision-making.

Creating a Slow Moving Stock Report in Odoo

A well-designed slow moving stock report can provide managers with the information they need to take action quickly.

Depending on business requirements, Odoo reports and dashboards can be customized to highlight products based on criteria such as stock age, sales frequency, stock turnover, and movement history.

Businesses can analyze products according to specific periods. For example, management may want to identify products that have not had any sales movement in the last 30, 60, or 90 days.

This makes Odoo slow moving inventory analysis more practical and actionable.

Important Data to Include in Slow-Moving Inventory Reports

An effective report may include information such as:

  • Product name
  • Product category
  • Current quantity on hand
  • Last sale date
  • Last inventory movement date
  • Number of days in stock
  • Sales quantity during a selected period
  • Inventory value
  • Warehouse location

When all this information is available in one report, managers do not need to search through multiple systems.

They can quickly identify problematic inventory and decide what should happen next.

For businesses with unique reporting requirements, Odoo can also be customized to create dashboards and reports based on specific inventory KPIs.

How Businesses Can Take Action on Slow-Moving and Non-Moving Inventory

Identifying the problem is only the first step. Businesses must also take action based on the insights they receive.

Once slow moving and non-moving inventory has been identified, companies can use several strategies to improve stock movement.

Offer Discounts and Promotions

Products that are not selling may benefit from targeted discounts or promotional campaigns.

Instead of applying discounts randomly, businesses can use inventory data to identify products that genuinely require action.

Bundle Products

Slow-moving items can sometimes be combined with popular products.

For example, a business can create product bundles or special offers to encourage customers to purchase older inventory.

Stop Unnecessary Reordering

One of the most important actions is preventing additional purchases of products that are already overstocked.

When purchasing and inventory data are connected through Odoo, businesses can make smarter replenishment decisions.

Improve Demand Forecasting

Historical sales data can help businesses understand future demand more accurately.

By analyzing which products sell quickly and which remain in stock, businesses can improve purchasing strategies and avoid repeating the same mistakes.

Transfer Stock Between Locations

A product may move slowly in one warehouse but have higher demand in another location.

Odoo’s multi-warehouse capabilities can help businesses review stock availability and transfer products where they are more likely to sell.

The Advantage of Connecting Inventory with Sales and Purchasing

One of the biggest benefits of Odoo ERP is integration.

Inventory does not operate independently. Product movement is connected with sales, purchasing, accounting, warehouses, and customer demand.

When these departments use separate systems, businesses may struggle to understand the complete inventory picture.

Odoo connects these processes within one platform.

For example:

A purchasing manager can see existing stock before creating a new purchase order.

A sales team can access product availability.

Warehouse teams can monitor stock movements.

Management can analyze inventory value and product performance.

This connected approach makes slow moving inventory management more accurate and efficient.

Title: How to Manage Month-End Closing in Odoo 19?
Content:
Introduction to Month-End Closing in Odoo 19

Month-End Closing in Odoo 19 becomes much easier when you know exactly where to look and what to verify inside Odoo. Instead of moving between spreadsheets and different systems, you can review sales, purchases, inventory, and accounting activities directly from Odoo.

In this practical guide, we will walk through Odoo 19 Month-End Closing step by step. You will learn how to check Odoo open purchase orders, review Odoo open sales orders, investigate Odoo 19 stock variation, verify Odoo 19 stock valuation, and use the Odoo inventory valuation report before finalizing the month.

The idea behind Month-End Closing in Odoo 19 is not simply to click a button and finish the month. You need to make sure transactions are complete, inventory records are accurate, and accounting information reflects what actually happened during the month.

This is especially important for companies using Odoo for inventory management, purchasing, sales, and accounting. A practical closing routine helps identify unfinished transactions and unusual stock movements before they create problems in financial reporting.

Let’s look at how you can actually perform these checks inside Odoo 19.

Step 1 - Check Your Accounting Activities

Start with the Accounting application.

From the Accounting dashboard, review the accounting activities for the month you are closing. Depending on your configuration, you may need to review customer invoices, vendor bills, payments, bank transactions, and journal entries.

Go to the relevant accounting menus and filter transactions by the month you are closing.

For example, if you are closing August, use the date filters to review transactions from August 1 through August 31.

Look for:

  • Customer invoices that are still in draft
  • Vendor bills waiting for confirmation
  • Payments that have not been reconciled
  • Unusual journal entries
  • Transactions recorded with incorrect dates

Do not immediately close the accounting period just because the month has ended. First, make sure the transactions that should belong to the month have actually been recorded.

This is one of the most important parts of Month-End Closing in Odoo 19 because incorrect dates or missing transactions can affect the final financial figures.

Step 2 - Review Odoo Open Sales Orders

Next, move to the Sales application.

Go to Sales → Orders → Orders and use the available filters to identify sales orders that are still open or not fully processed.

This is where you review your Odoo open sales orders.

An open order does not necessarily mean something is wrong. The customer may genuinely be waiting for delivery, or the order may have been partially fulfilled.

The important thing is to understand why the order is still open.

Check whether:

The order is waiting for delivery

If the products have not been delivered, confirm that the delivery operation is still valid and expected.

The order has been partially delivered

Check the delivery order and verify whether the remaining quantity is genuinely pending.

The order has been delivered

If the products have already been delivered, make sure the related workflow has been completed according to your company’s invoicing process.

The order is no longer required

If an old order was cancelled or is no longer expected, make sure it is handled correctly instead of leaving it indefinitely in an open state.

This simple review can prevent your month-end figures from being affected by old or incomplete sales transactions.

Step 3 - Review Odoo Open Purchase Orders

Now move to the Purchase application.

Go to Purchase → Orders → Purchase Orders and identify purchase orders that are still open.

This gives you an opportunity to review your Odoo open purchase orders before closing the month.

For every important open purchase order, check its status.

Was the purchase order confirmed?

Were the products received?

Was the receipt only partially completed?

Is the vendor still expected to deliver the remaining products?

Does the purchase order need to be cancelled?

You should also open the related receipt when necessary and verify the actual quantities received.

This matters because a purchase order itself does not necessarily mean inventory has been received. The receipt is what helps you understand what physically entered the warehouse.

For example, suppose a purchase order contains 500 units, but only 300 units were received before month-end. Your month-end review should reflect that reality rather than assuming all 500 units are already in stock.

This is where connecting purchasing with Odoo inventory management becomes valuable.

Step 4 - Check Inventory Operations

Now go to the Inventory application.

Before reviewing valuation, first check whether there are unfinished inventory operations.

Look at your inventory operations and identify receipts, deliveries, internal transfers, returns, and adjustments that may still require processing.

Pay particular attention to operations that occurred close to the end of the month.

For example, imagine goods physically arrived at your warehouse on August 31, but the receipt was not validated until September 1.

That timing can matter during month-end reporting.

Similarly, if products were shipped to a customer on August 31 but the delivery operation was not properly processed, the inventory position may not represent what actually happened.

This is why month-end closing should involve both the finance and warehouse teams.

Step 5 - Review Odoo 19 Stock Valuation

Once inventory operations have been reviewed, you can examine Odoo 19 stock valuation.

In Odoo, inventory valuation can be reviewed through the Inventory reporting and valuation features available in your database configuration.

Go to the Inventory application and open the relevant Reporting section. From there, access the inventory valuation information.

The exact options available can depend on your installed apps and inventory/accounting configuration.

The purpose here is to answer a simple question:

Does the value of inventory recorded in Odoo make sense for the stock you actually have?

Review the valuation for the month and pay attention to significant increases or decreases.

A major change could be completely normal. For example, perhaps you received a large shipment at the end of the month.

But if the valuation changed unexpectedly, investigate it before completing the closing process.

Step 6 - Use the Odoo Inventory Valuation Report

The Odoo inventory valuation report becomes particularly useful when you need to investigate why inventory value has changed.

Open the valuation report and review the relevant products, locations, quantities, and values available in your configuration.

You can investigate individual product movements when you notice something unusual.

For example:

Opening inventory: 10,000 units

Purchases during the month: 4,000 units

Sales and other outgoing movements: 3,500 units

If the ending quantity does not appear reasonable, do not simply accept the figure.

Trace the inventory movements behind it.

Check receipts.

Check deliveries.

Check returns.

Check internal transfers.

Check inventory adjustments.

This approach allows you to move from “the number looks wrong” to “this specific transaction caused the difference.”

That is exactly what makes Odoo useful during Month-End Closing in Odoo 19.

Step 7 - Investigate Odoo 19 Stock Variation

After reviewing valuation, look for unusual Odoo 19 stock variation.

Stock differences can come from several sources, including incorrect quantities, inventory adjustments, product returns, missing receipts, incorrect deliveries, or other inventory transactions.

If you find a variation, open the related product or inventory record and trace the underlying transactions.

Ask:

What changed?

When did it change?

Which transaction caused the change?

Was the transaction legitimate?

Does the quantity in Odoo match the physical stock?

For example, if a product suddenly shows a significant quantity increase, check whether a purchase receipt was validated.

If the quantity decreased unexpectedly, check customer deliveries, returns, or inventory adjustments.

Do not make an inventory adjustment simply to force Odoo to match an expected number. First understand the reason for the difference.

This is an important principle of good Odoo inventory management.

Step 8 - Reconcile Inventory With Accounting

Once operational inventory checks are complete, finance should compare the inventory information with the accounting records.

This is where the connection between Odoo Inventory and Accounting becomes particularly important.

Depending on your inventory valuation configuration, stock movements can have corresponding accounting impact.

Review the relevant journal entries and investigate unusual values.

If finance sees one inventory figure while the warehouse team expects another, stop and investigate the difference before finalizing the month.

A proper month-end process should bring these teams onto the same page.

Step 9 - Review Exceptions Before Closing

Before you consider the month complete, create a final exception list.

This can include:

  • Open sales orders requiring action
  • Open purchase orders requiring follow-up
  • Unvalidated receipts
  • Pending deliveries
  • Inventory discrepancies
  • Unusual stock valuation changes
  • Draft invoices or bills
  • Unreconciled transactions

The important part is not simply identifying these items. Each exception should have an owner and a clear next action.

For example:

Open Purchase Order → Purchasing team checks vendor status.

Pending Delivery → Warehouse confirms shipment status.

Stock Variation → Inventory team investigates the movement.

Unreconciled Payment → Finance team completes reconciliation.

This makes Month-End Closing in Odoo 19 a controlled process instead of a last-minute rush.

Make Month-End Closing Easier With Odoo Experts

Odoo provides the tools needed to bring sales, purchasing, inventory, and accounting information together. But the results depend heavily on how those workflows are configured.

If your team still spends hours exporting data from Odoo into spreadsheets, manually checking stock differences, or trying to understand why inventory valuation changed, your Odoo setup may need attention.

Netilligence can help businesses configure and optimize Odoo according to their actual workflows.

From Odoo inventory management and purchasing to sales, accounting, reporting, and custom workflows, our Odoo experts can help you build a system that makes operational and financial information easier to manage.

Instead of waiting until month-end to discover problems, you can establish processes that help your team identify issues earlier.

The result is a more controlled closing process, better visibility into inventory, and greater confidence in the information management uses to make decisions.

Final Checklist for Month-End Closing in Odoo 19

Before completing your monthly closing process, make sure you have reviewed:

✓ Accounting transactions

✓ Odoo open sales orders

✓ Odoo open purchase orders

✓ Pending receipts and deliveries

✓ Inventory movements

✓ Odoo 19 stock variation

✓ Odoo 19 stock valuation

✓ Odoo inventory valuation report

✓ Inventory-to-accounting reconciliation

✓ Outstanding exceptions

Once these checks are complete, your team can move forward with much greater confidence.

Right Odoo Setup Makes Month-End Closing in Odoo 19 Easier

Month-End Closing in Odoo 19 does not have to be a complicated spreadsheet exercise. When your Odoo database is properly configured, you can review the actual transactions behind your sales, purchases, inventory, and accounting figures.

The key is to work through the process systematically.

Check your open orders. Review inventory operations. Investigate stock variations. Analyze Odoo 19 stock valuation. Use the Odoo inventory valuation report to investigate unusual changes, and make sure your financial records reflect the operational reality of the business.

If your current closing process still involves too much manual work, Netilligence can help you get more from Odoo. With the right configuration, workflows, reporting, and expert support, your month-end process can become easier to control and much easier to trust.

Title: How Can You Manage Consignment Notes (CMRs) in Odoo Inventory?
Content:
Why Consignment Notes Matter in Modern Logistics

Consignment Notes are an important part of road transportation because they provide a clear record of what is being shipped, who is sending it, who is receiving it, and who is responsible for transporting it. For businesses that handle frequent deliveries, manually preparing Consignment Notes can be time-consuming and lead to unnecessary paperwork.

Odoo Inventory can make the process much easier. With Odoo’s dispatch and delivery management features, businesses can generate a CMR consignment note directly from a delivery order. The system uses information already available in Odoo, reducing the need to enter the same shipment details repeatedly.

With Odoo CMR, businesses can connect shipment documentation to their inventory operations. Odoo can generate a consignment note from a delivery order, and its Inventory CMR functionality helps prepare the required transport document for road shipments. This makes consignment notes in Odoo useful for companies that handle domestic or international road transportation.

If your business still prepares every CMR manually, manages separate documents, or copies information between systems, it may be time to consider a better approach. Understanding CMR in Odoo Inventory can help you build a more organized, reliable shipping workflow.

What Is a CMR Consignment Note?

A CMR is a standardized waybill used for international road carriage of goods. CMR stands for the Convention on the Contract for the International Carriage of Goods by Road. The document provides important shipment information for the sender, receiver, and carrier.

In practical terms, a CMR can contain information such as:

  • Sender details
  • Receiver details
  • Carrier information
  • Shipment and delivery information
  • Description of goods
  • Quantity and other transport details
  • Transport-related information
  • Required signatures or additional details

A traditional CMR typically has multiple copies for the various parties involved in the transportation process. Odoo’s documentation explains that the standard CMR contains copies for the sender, receiver, carrier, and a second carrier. Odoo can populate the form with information already stored in the system, and you can add additional information manually where needed.

This distinction matters: a consignment note is a transport document, whereas Odoo’s consignment inventory feature refers to stock owned by another party. These are two different concepts, even though they use similar terminology.

How Does Odoo CMR Work With Inventory?

The main advantage of Odoo CMR is that it integrates the consignment note into the delivery process rather than treating it as a separate document.

In Odoo Inventory, outgoing shipments are managed through delivery orders. Once the delivery order contains the relevant shipment information, the CMR can be generated from the delivery operation when the required dispatch management setup is available.

This creates a more connected workflow:

Sales Order → Delivery Order → Shipment Preparation → CMR → Delivery

Instead of creating a CMR from scratch, Odoo takes information from the relevant delivery operation. This reduces duplicate data entry and makes documentation easier to manage.

This is especially useful for companies with a high volume of deliveries. A logistics team can prepare shipment information in Odoo and then generate the corresponding transport document from the same system.

Odoo also supports batch delivery CMRs. When you group several delivery orders into a batch transfer, Odoo can generate a CMR for each delivery in that batch.

How to Create a CMR in Odoo Inventory

If you are wondering how to create a CMR in Odoo, start with the delivery order.

Step 1: Prepare the Delivery Order

First, make sure the relevant delivery order has been created in Odoo Inventory.

Go to:

Inventory → Operations → Deliveries

Open the delivery order for which you need a CMR.

The delivery order should include the relevant shipment information, such as the products being delivered and the customer or destination details.

A properly prepared delivery order matters because Odoo uses delivery operation information to complete the CMR.

Step 2: Review Shipment Information

Before generating the document, review the delivery order carefully.

Check:

  • Customer or receiver information
  • Delivery address
  • Products
  • Quantities
  • Shipment details
  • Carrier or delivery method, where applicable
  • Scheduled delivery information

This simple review can help prevent mistakes from appearing on the final Odoo delivery note, CMR, or related shipping documentation.

Step 3: Generate the CMR

Once the delivery order is ready, click the Actions menu.

Then select:

Print → Consignment Note (CMR)

Odoo generates the CMR based on the information available in the delivery order.

This is one of the biggest advantages of CMR in Odoo Inventory. Instead of preparing a separate document manually, Odoo generates the transport document from an existing operational record.

Step 4: Add Any Required Information

Although Odoo can automatically fill in information available in the system, not every detail will be available automatically.

Odoo notes that you may need to enter additional information manually on the CMR.

Therefore, your logistics team should review the generated document before sending it with the shipment.

Managing CMRs for Multiple Deliveries

Businesses that handle only a few shipments can generate a CMR individually. But what happens when dozens of deliveries need to leave the warehouse?

This is where batch processing becomes useful.

Odoo allows businesses to group delivery orders into batch transfers. From the batch transfer, users can generate a CMR for each delivery included in that batch.

To work with batch CMRs, navigate to:

Inventory → Operations → Batch Transfers

Open the relevant batch transfer and use:

Actions → Print → Consignment Note (CMR)

Odoo then generates a consignment note for each delivery within the batch.

For logistics teams, this can save considerable administrative effort. Instead of opening each shipment individually, preparing documents, and repeating the process, you can handle multiple delivery documents through a batch workflow.

Odoo Delivery Note CMR vs. Regular Delivery Documentation

Understanding the difference between a regular delivery slip and a CMR is useful.

A delivery slip primarily documents the goods being delivered to a customer. It can include product details, quantities, and other delivery information. Odoo also supports printing delivery slips from delivery orders, including relevant lot or serial information when the appropriate settings are enabled.

A CMR, on the other hand, is a transport document designed for road carriage.

Therefore, an Odoo CMR delivery note should not be treated simply as another name for a standard delivery slip. They serve related but different purposes.

For a logistics business, you may need both:

  • Delivery Slip: Helps document the goods being delivered.
  • CMR: Provides the road transport waybill.
  • Shipping Label: Helps identify the shipment or package.
  • Invoice: Handles the commercial and financial side of the transaction.

Keeping these documents connected through Odoo can give your team better visibility throughout the delivery process.

Benefits of Managing Consignment Notes in Odoo

Using Consignment Notes within a connected Odoo workflow can provide several practical advantages.

Less Manual Data Entry

Because Odoo can populate the CMR using information already available in the delivery operation, employees do not have to recreate every shipment detail from scratch.

Better Shipment Accuracy

Manual document preparation creates opportunities for typing mistakes. Connecting the CMR to the delivery order helps reduce unnecessary duplication.

Faster Documentation

For companies processing many shipments every day, even a few saved minutes per delivery can make a meaningful difference.

Better Coordination

Warehouse employees, logistics teams, carriers, and administrative staff can work from information stored within the same ERP environment.

Easier Batch Processing

Companies handling multiple deliveries can use batch transfers and generate CMRs for deliveries included in the batch.

Improved Traceability

Odoo Inventory already provides visibility into product movements, delivery operations, and shipment-related information. Connecting transport documentation to these workflows can make it easier to understand what was scheduled, processed, and delivered.

Important Difference: CMR vs. Consignment Stock

One common source of confusion is the word “consignment.”

In Odoo, consignment stock refers to products a business stores and sells, but another party still owns. Odoo provides a dedicated consignment feature for managing this type of inventory.

A CMR consignment note, however, is a transport document used for road freight.

These are not the same thing.

For example, a retailer might store products that belong to a supplier. That is consignment stock. If those products are later transported by road and require a CMR, the CMR is the transport document for that shipment.

Understanding this difference matters most when configuring Odoo for businesses involved in distribution, logistics, wholesale, or international trade.

How Netilligence Can Help With Odoo Inventory and CMR

Managing Consignment Notes may sound simple, but getting the complete workflow right can require more than enabling a feature.

Your business may need to connect sales, inventory, warehouse operations, delivery, transport management, and documentation in a way that matches your actual processes.

This is where an experienced Odoo implementation partner can add value.

At Netilligence, we help businesses assess their existing workflows, configure Odoo around their operational requirements, and reduce unnecessary manual work. Instead of forcing your logistics team to adapt to a complicated process, we build an Odoo environment that supports how your business works.

Whether you need help with Odoo CMR, delivery workflows, inventory configuration, warehouse operations, or broader Odoo implementation, professional configuration can help you get more value from your ERP.

Move Every Shipment Forward With Smarter Consignment Notes in Odoo

Managing Consignment Notes does not have to be a disconnected paperwork process. With Odoo Inventory, businesses can generate CMR documents for delivery operations and use batch transfers to handle multiple shipments. Odoo can automatically populate available information while allowing you to add details when needed.

For businesses in road transportation, distribution, and logistics, Odoo consignment note management can reduce repetitive data entry, improve documentation, and connect transport paperwork with inventory operations.

If your current process involves spreadsheets, manually prepared CMRs, repeated data entry, or disconnected shipping documents, it may be worth reviewing how Odoo can improve your workflow.

Title: How Can You Add a New Payment Method When Registering a Payment in Odoo?
Content:
Make Every New Payment Method Work for Your Business

A New Payment Method can make a noticeable difference when your business accepts payments through different channels. Whether customers pay by cash, bank transfer, cheque, or another supported option, configuring the right Odoo payment method helps your accounting team record transactions correctly. When you use Odoo to register a payment, the selected method determines how the transaction is recorded and connected to the relevant journal.

For businesses managing a large number of transactions, having the right Odoo payment methods available can save time and reduce accounting mistakes. Instead of manually adjusting every Odoo invoice payment, your team can select the appropriate option during the payment process. If a required option is missing, knowing how to add a payment method in Odoo becomes important.

The process of adding a New Payment Method is closely connected with journals. Odoo allows payment methods to be configured from the Incoming Payments and Outgoing Payments sections of a bank or cash journal. This means your Odoo register payment method should be configured according to the way your business receives or sends money.

In this guide, we will explain how to register a payment in Odoo, when you may need a New Payment Method, how to configure it, and how the Odoo invoice payment method works in the overall accounting workflow. If your business needs several Odoo payment methods, understanding this setup can help you create a cleaner and more reliable payment process.

Why Do You Need a New Payment Method in Odoo?

Businesses rarely use only one way to receive or send money. A company may receive customer payments through cash, bank transfers, cheques, or other payment channels. Similarly, vendor payments may be handled through different bank-based methods.

Odoo provides payment methods that can be configured for different types of transactions. These methods are associated with bank or cash journals and can be used when registering payments.

You may need a New Payment Method when:

  • Your business starts accepting a different payment type.
  • Your accounting team wants to identify a particular payment channel separately.
  • You want better visibility during reconciliation.
  • You need to distinguish cheques or specific manual payment types.
  • Your existing payment configuration does not match your business workflow.

For example, suppose your company receives customer payments through bank transfers and cheques. Instead of recording every cheque simply as a generic manual payment, you can create a specific payment method called “Cheque.” Odoo’s documentation gives this approach as an example for identifying customer cheque payments more easily.

This small configuration change can make payment records easier to understand and reconcile later.

How to Add a Payment Method in Odoo

Before using a New Payment Method during payment registration, you need to configure it in the appropriate journal.

In Odoo 19, payment methods can be configured from the Incoming Payments and Outgoing Payments tabs of a bank or cash journal.

Step 1: Open Accounting and Journals

Go to the Accounting application and open:

Accounting → Configuration → Journals

Find the bank or cash journal that should be used for the payment.

The journal is important because it determines where the payment transaction is recorded. Choosing the correct journal from the beginning helps maintain accurate accounting records.

Step 2: Open the Appropriate Payment Tab

Depending on the transaction, use the relevant tab:

  • Incoming Payments for money received from customers.
  • Outgoing Payments for money paid to vendors or other recipients.

If you are creating a method for customer invoice payments, you will generally work with the incoming payment configuration.

Step 3: Add a Payment Method

In the relevant payment section, click Add a line.

Odoo allows you to select an available payment method and give it a suitable name. For example, its documentation shows how a business can select Manual and name the new method Check for incoming cheque payments.

Your method name should be simple and recognizable.

Examples include:

  • Customer Cheque
  • Bank Transfer
  • Cash Collection
  • Corporate Card
  • Local Transfer

Avoid creating multiple methods with almost identical names. Clear naming makes it easier for accountants to select the right option later.

How to Register Payment Using the New Payment Method

Once your New Payment Method is configured, you can use it when recording a customer or vendor transaction.

For an invoice, open the relevant customer invoice and click Pay or Register Payment, depending on your Odoo interface and version.

The payment window allows you to select the journal and payment details. In Odoo 19, the standard flow includes selecting the journal and payment date, reviewing the payment amount, editing the memo if required, and then clicking Create Payment.

Step 1: Open the Customer Invoice

Go to:

Accounting → Customers → Invoices

Open the invoice for which you have received payment.

The invoice should be in the appropriate posted status before payment registration.

Step 2: Click Pay or Register Payment

Click the payment button available on the invoice.

Odoo opens the payment window.

Step 3: Select the Journal

Choose the bank or cash journal associated with your payment.

For example, if the customer paid through your business bank account, select the relevant bank journal.

Step 4: Select the New Payment Method

Now select your newly configured payment method.

This is where your New Payment Method becomes part of the actual Odoo invoice payment process.

Step 5: Review the Payment Details

Check:

  • Payment amount
  • Payment date
  • Journal
  • Payment method
  • Memo or reference
  • Customer details

If everything is correct, click Create Payment.

The invoice can then move to an In Payment status, depending on the accounting configuration. Odoo explains that the invoice is finalized as Paid after the relevant payment is reconciled with the bank transaction when outstanding accounts are being used.

What Happens After You Register the Payment?

Understanding what happens after Odoo register payment is just as important as knowing how to create it.

When a payment is linked to an invoice, Odoo uses the payment to reduce or settle the amount due on that invoice. Multiple payments can also be linked to the same invoice.

However, registering a payment and reconciling a bank transaction are not always the same thing.

For example, suppose a customer transfers PKR 100,000 to your bank account. Your accounting team registers the payment against the invoice. The invoice may show In Payment while the corresponding bank transaction is still waiting to be reconciled.

Once the bank transaction is matched with the registered payment, the invoice can be marked as Paid.

This is why the correct Odoo payment method and proper bank reconciliation work together.

Why Reconciliation Matters

Bank reconciliation confirms that the payment recorded in Odoo corresponds to the actual transaction appearing in the bank statement.

Without proper reconciliation, your accounting records can become difficult to review. Payments may appear to be registered while invoices remain in an intermediate status.

A well-configured Odoo register payment method therefore supports more than payment entry. It contributes to a complete accounting workflow.

Common Mistakes When Adding Payment Methods

Adding a New Payment Method is straightforward, but businesses can still run into problems if the configuration is not planned carefully.

Choosing the Wrong Journal

A payment method should be associated with the appropriate bank or cash journal. If the wrong journal is selected, transactions may be posted or reconciled against the wrong account.

Creating Too Many Similar Methods

Creating “Bank Transfer,” “Bank Payment,” “Bank Transfer 1,” and “Online Bank Transfer” without a clear reason can confuse users.

Use names that describe actual differences in your payment process.

Ignoring Reconciliation

Registering a payment does not necessarily mean the entire banking workflow is complete. If your configuration uses outstanding accounts, the payment may need to be reconciled with the corresponding bank transaction before the invoice becomes fully paid.

Using the Wrong Incoming or Outgoing Configuration

An incoming customer payment and an outgoing vendor payment serve different purposes. Make sure the method is configured in the correct section.

How Netilligence Can Help You Configure Odoo Payments

Payment configuration may look simple when you have only a few transactions. But as your business grows, accounting workflows become more complicated.

Different customers may use different payment channels. Multiple bank accounts may need separate journals. Your finance team may also need specific reconciliation rules, payment reporting, and controls.

This is where professional Odoo implementation can add real value.

At Netilligence, we help businesses configure Odoo according to their actual accounting processes instead of forcing teams to work around a generic setup. From configuring journals and payment methods to improving invoice workflows and reconciliation, the goal is to make Odoo easier for your finance team to use every day.

A properly configured New Payment Method can be a small change, but the wider accounting setup needs to work together. When journals, payment methods, invoices, outstanding accounts, and reconciliation are configured correctly, your team can spend less time fixing payment records and more time managing the business.

If your current Odoo payment workflow feels confusing, payments are regularly left unreconciled, or your team cannot find the right Odoo invoice payment method, it may be time to review the configuration rather than adding manual workarounds.

Build a Better Payment Workflow with Odoo

Adding a New Payment Method in Odoo allows businesses to record different types of payments in a more organized way. By configuring the appropriate journal, adding the payment method under Incoming or Outgoing Payments, and selecting it while registering a payment, your accounting team can create a more structured payment workflow.

The key is not simply knowing how to add payment method in Odoo. The real value comes from configuring the payment process around your business requirements.

Whether you need to manage customer payments, vendor payments, bank transfers, cheques, or reconciliation, Odoo provides the flexibility to support different accounting workflows.

If you want to get more from your Odoo Accounting setup, Netilligence can help you review your current configuration, identify workflow gaps, and implement a payment process that fits the way your business actually operates.

Title: How Can Odoo ERP Help Prevent Duplicate Customer Records?
Content:
Why You Need to Prevent Duplicate Customer Records

Preventing duplicate customer records is more important than it may seem when managing customer data in an ERP system. As a business grows, the number of customers, leads, suppliers, and contacts also increases. Without proper Odoo contact management, the same customer may accidentally be added more than once.

For example, one salesperson may create a customer record using the company name, while another employee creates the same customer using the contact person’s name. Over time, these Odoo duplicate contacts can make your database confusing and difficult to manage.

Duplicate records can affect sales activities, customer communication, reporting, invoicing, and overall Odoo customer management. A sales representative may contact the same customer twice, while another employee may unknowingly work on a separate record for the same company.

This is why businesses need a reliable way to Prevent Duplicate Customer Records before they become a bigger problem.

Odoo provides tools that help businesses identify and manage duplicate customer records. It also allows users to merge duplicate contacts and clean up existing customer data.

What Causes Duplicate Customer Records in Odoo?

Before learning how to Prevent Duplicate Customer Records, it is important to understand why duplicates happen in the first place.

In many businesses, customer information enters the system from different sources. A customer might contact the company via the website, email, phone, social media, or a sales representative. If employees don't check whether the customer already exists, they may create a new record unnecessarily.

Some common reasons for duplicate contacts in Odoo include:

  • Different employees creating the same customer record
  • Spelling variations in customer names
  • Different phone number formats
  • Customers being entered through different business processes
  • Importing customer data from external systems
  • Creating a new contact instead of searching for an existing one
  • Multiple employees maintaining customer information independently

For instance, one record may be created as ABC Trading LLC, while another employee enters ABC Trading. Both records may belong to the same business.

This creates an Odoo duplicate customer problem that can affect the entire customer lifecycle.

The solution is not simply deleting one record. Businesses need a structured process to identify, review, and manage duplicates.

How to Merge Duplicate Contacts in Odoo

Sometimes duplicate records already exist. In that situation, knowing how to merge duplicate contacts in Odoo becomes essential.

Odoo allows users to select duplicate contacts and merge them into a single record. According to the Odoo 19 documentation, users can open the Contacts application, switch to list view, select the duplicate records, and choose Actions → Merge.

Step 1: Open the Contacts Application

Go to the Contacts application in Odoo.

Switch to the list view to easily identify and select multiple records.

Step 2: Select the Duplicate Records

Find the customer records that appear to represent the same person or company.

Select the relevant records using the checkboxes.

Before merging, carefully compare details such as:

  • Name
  • Email
  • Phone
  • Company
  • VAT
  • Address
  • Customer history

This step is important because not every similar-looking contact is actually a duplicate.

Step 3: Select Merge

Once you have confirmed that the records belong to the same customer, go to:

Actions → Merge

Odoo opens a merge window where you can review the selected contact information before completing the process.

Step 4: Select the Destination Contact

Odoo allows users to select the destination contact. The system defaults to the first-created contact record, but users can choose another record if necessary.

Review the information carefully and confirm the merge.

Important: Merging contacts is irreversible, so businesses should merge records only when they are certain the contacts represent the same customer.

How Odoo Helps Prevent Duplicate Customer Records

Odoo’s Contacts application serves as a central place to store important customer and business information. Contact records can include names, email addresses, phone numbers, addresses, company relationships, and other details.

This centralized approach is a foundation of effective Odoo customer management.

1. Centralized Customer Information

Instead of keeping customer information across spreadsheets, emails, and separate systems, businesses can maintain customer records in Odoo.

With centralized customer information, employees can search the existing database before creating a new record.

This simple habit can significantly reduce duplicate Odoo contacts.

2. Consistent Contact Details

Odoo allows businesses to maintain structured information such as:

  • Customer name
  • Company
  • Email
  • Phone number
  • Address
  • VAT information
  • Parent company
  • Contact type

Consistent information makes it easier to identify whether two records belong to the same customer.

3. Duplicate Detection and Deduplication

One of Odoo's most useful features for preventing duplicate contact workflows is deduplication.

Odoo can search for possible duplicate records using criteria such as Email, Name, Is Company, VAT, and Parent Company. If you select multiple criteria, Odoo can suggest records that match all selected fields.

This gives businesses a practical way to identify potential duplicate Odoo customer records without manually checking the entire database.

Why Duplicate Customer Records Can Hurt Your Business

Many businesses underestimate the impact of duplicate customer records in Odoo.

A duplicate may look like a small data-entry issue, but when hundreds or thousands of records are involved, the consequences can become significant.

Poor Customer Communication

If two salespeople work from separate records for the same customer, the customer may receive multiple calls or emails about the same matter.

This can make your business look unorganized.

Inaccurate Sales Reports

Duplicate records can split customer activities between multiple profiles.

As a result, management may not get a complete picture of the customer’s sales history or value.

Repeated Manual Work

Employees may waste time updating the same customer information in different records.

Instead of working with one complete profile, teams have to check multiple records.

Inconsistent Customer Information

One contact may have the latest phone number while another contains an old email address.

This creates confusion and increases the chance of using outdated information.

Problems Across Business Operations

Customer records are not limited to the Contacts application. They can connect to other business processes such as sales, CRM, invoicing, and accounting.

That makes clean data an important part of effective ERP management.

Best Practices for Odoo Contact Management

Odoo’s deduplication tools help, but businesses should also establish strong Odoo contact management practices.

Make Search Before Create a Habit

Employees should search for a customer before creating a new record.

Searching by name, email, phone number, or company can help identify an existing record.

Standardize Customer Information

Create internal guidelines for entering customer information.

For example, decide how to record company names, phone numbers, addresses, and VAT numbers.

Review Imported Data

If you import customer information from spreadsheets or another system, review the data before importing it into Odoo.

Poor-quality imported data can quickly increase duplicate contacts in Odoo.

Schedule Regular Data Cleanup

Do not wait until your database becomes difficult to manage.

Regularly review customer records and use Odoo’s deduplication functionality to identify potential duplicates.

Train Your Team

Even the best ERP system cannot fully prevent poor data entry if employees do not know how to use it correctly.

Train employees to search for contacts, create records, update information, and handle duplicates.
